He was heard who said: I called to the Lord with my voice and he heard me from his holy mountain. He who asks outside this mountain does not expect to be heard in order to eternal life. Many are heard in many other things. But do not congratulate yourself for having been heard; The demons were heard asking to enter the swine. Let us long to be heard regarding eternal life, attending to the desire with which we say: Send your light and your truth. This light seeks the eye of the heart: Blessed, he says, are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Now we are on his mountain, that is, in his Church, in his tent or tabernacle. The tent is typical of pilgrims; the house, of those who live by seat. The tabernacle or tent is typical of pilgrims and soldiers. When you hear the word tabernacle or tent, remember the war, be on your guard against the enemy. What will the house be? Blessed are those who dwell in your house; forever and ever they will praise you. 5 [v.4]. Then brought to the tent or tabernacle and established on his holy mountain, what hope do we have? I will enter the altar of God. There is a sublime and invisible altar to which the unjust does not approach. Only he who safely approaches his holy mountain approaches this sublime altar. On this sublime altar he who distinguishes his cause on the holy mountain finds his life. I will enter the altar of God: from (the other altar), that is, from his holy mountain, from his tent, from his Church, I will enter the sublime altar of God. What sacrifice exists there? The same one who enters is taken as a burnt offering. I will enter the altar of God. What does it mean to the altar of God? To God who makes my youth happy. Youth means (Dan 2,35). In hoc monte se exauditum dicit, qui dicit: Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi, et exaudivit me de monte sancto suo (Ps 3,5). Quisquís praeter istum montem orat, non sese speret exaudiri ad vitam aeternam. Exaudiuntur enim multi ad fine. Nec sibi plaudant quod exaudiuntur: exauditi sunt daemones, ut in porcos mitterentur (Mt 8:32). Exaudiri ad vitam aeternam concupiscamus, propter desiderium quo dicimus: Emitte luzem tuam et veritatem tuam. Illa lux oculum cordis inquirit: Beati enim, inquit, mundi corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt (Mt 5,8). Mode in monte eius sumus, id est in Ecclesia eius, et in tabernacle eius. Tabernaculum peregrinantium est, domus cohabitantium: est et tabernaculum peregrinantium et militantium. Cum audis tabernaculum, bellum intellige, hostem cave. Domus autem quae erit?

Beati qui habitant in domo tua, in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). 5 {V.4]. Iam etgo perducti ad tabernaculum, et positi in monte sancto eius, quam spem gerimus? Et introibo ad altare Dei. Est enim quoddam sublime altare invisibile, quo non accessit iniustus. Ad illud altare ille solus accessit, qui ad istud securus accessit: illic inveniet vitam suam, qui in isto discetnit causam suam. Et introibo ad altare Dei: de monte sancto eius, et de tabernacle eius, de sancta Ecclesia eius, introibo ad altare Dei sublime. What ibi sacrificium est? Ipse qui intrat, assumitur in holocaustum. Introibo ad altare Dei. Quid est quod dicit,
An exile's desire to see the sanctuary

ca new thing; Therefore, it is as if he said: To God, who rejoices in my new thing. Rejoice in my new thing who saddens my old age. Now I walk sad in old age, then I will remain joyful in newness. I will praise you to the sound of my zither, oh my God! What does it mean to praise with the zither and the psaltery? It is not always praised with the zither nor always with the psaltery. These two musical instruments have different and different dispositions, worthy of being considered and entrusted to memory. Both are held and touched with the hands, and symbolize certain bodily works of ours. It is good to know how to play the psaltery and the zither. But since the psaltery is an instrument that has a concavity in the upper part, that is, it is a triangular instrument of wood and concave in which the sounding strings are supported, and the zither is a similar instrument, also made of wood, concave and sonorous in the lower part, for the same reason our works must be distinguished and know when they belong to the psaltery and when to the zither. Yet both are pleasing to God and sweet to his ears. When, moved by the precepts of God, we perform something by submitting to his commands and obeying him in the fulfillment of his precepts, by acting and not enduring external action, then we play the psaltery. This is how angels also act, since they do not suffer or are forced to act by something strange. When on earth we endure tribulations, temptations and scandals, by enduring them because of the inferior part, that is, because we are mortal, because we bring this baggage, coming from our first condition, and also because we endure many things from those who are inferior, enad altare Dei? Ad Deum qui laetificat iuventutem meam. Iuventus novitatem significat: tanquam diceret, Ad Deum qui laetificat novitatem meam. Laetificat novitatem meam, qui contristavit vetustatem meam. Incedo enim moda sadtis in vetustate, tune autem stabo gaudens in novitate. Confitebor tibí in cithara, Deus, Deus meus. Quid est in cithara confiteti, et in psalterio confiteri? Non enim semper in cithata, nec semper in psalterio. Duo haec organa musicorum habent inter se distinctam discretemque rationem, dignified considetatione et commendatione memoriae. Utrumque hoc manibus portatur et tangitur, et significat opera quaedam our corporalia. Utrumque bonum, si quis norit psallere, si quis norit citharizare.

Sed quia psalterium istud otganum dicitut, quod de superiore parte habet testudinem; illud scilicet tympanum et concavum lignum cui chordae innitentes resonant: cithara veto idipsum lignum cavum et sonorum ex inferiore parte habet: discetnenda sunt opeta nostra, quando in psalterio sint, quando in cithata, utraque tamen placita Deo et suavia eius auditui. Quando ergo ex praeceptis Dei aliquid agimus, iussis eius obtempetantes et obaudientes ad implenda praecepta eius; ubi facimus et non patimur, psalterium est. Faciunt enim ita et Angelí: non enim aliquid patiuntur. Cum autem aliquid patimur tribuíationum, tentationum, scandalorum in hac terra; quia non patimur nisi ex inferióte patte, id est ex eo quod mottales S.Ag. 20
^.narratives about the Psalms

then we play the zither. For in this circumstance comes the soft sound from the bottom; then we suffer and chant, or, rather, we play the zither. When the Apostle said that he evangelized and preached the Gospel throughout the earth according to the command of God, as he affirmed that he had not received that Gospel from men or through man, but through Jesus Christ, the strings sounded at the top. But when he said: We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation works patience; patience, test, and the test, hope, the zither sounded at the bottom, but without a doubt very pleasantly. Patience is pleasing to God. If you fail in these tribulations, you break the zither. Then why did he say now: I will praise you with the zither? Because of what I had said before: Why am I sad when the enemy afflicts me? He suffered somewhat due to inner affliction, and yet in this he wanted to please God, and he tried to give thanks to God by remaining strong in tribulation; and, as he could not be without tribulations, he offered patience to God: I will praise you with the zither, O my God! 6 [v.5]. Again, addressing his soul upon perceiving the sound of that sonorous and wooden instrument, he says: Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? I find myself in tribulations, in weakness, in anguish. Why do you trouble me, oh my soul? Who is speaking? Who are you talking to? We all know that the soul speaks; It is evident that he addresses his words to her: Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? He asks for the persosumus, ex eo quod primae nostrae causae quiddam tribulationum debenmus, et quia patimur tumba ab eis qui non sunt desuper, cithara est. Venit enim sonus suavis ex inferiore parte: patimur et psallimus, vel potius cantamus et citharizamus. Quando dicebat Apostolus evangelizare se, et praedicare Evangelium toto orbe terrarum ex praecepto Dei; quia illud Evangelium se non ab hominibus ñeque per hominem, sed per Iesum Christum accepisse dicebat (Gal 1,12), desuper sonabant chordae: cum vero dicebat, Gloriamur in tríbulationibus; scientes quia tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia probationem, proven spem (Rom 5,3 et 4); cithara sonabat ex inferiore quidem, sed tamen dulciter. Omnis enim patientia dulcis est Deo. Si autem in ipsis tríbulationibus defeceris, citharam fregisti. Quare ergo moda dixit: Confitebor tibí in cithara? Propter illud quod dixerat: Utquid tristis incedo, dum affligit me inimicus?

Patiebatur enim quiddam ex inferiore afflictione, et in eo ipso tamen volebat placeré Deo, et grafias gestiebat agere Deo, fortis in tríbulationibus: et quia sine tribulatione esse non poterat, patientiam Deo debenbat, Confitebor tibí in cithara, Deus, Deus meus. 6 [v.5}. Et rursus ad animam suam, ut ex inferiore illo sonoro ligno capiat sonum: Utquid tristis es, inquit, anima mea, et tttquid conturbas me? In tríbulationibus sum, in languoribus, in moeroribus, utquid conturbas me, or animate? What did you say? cui dicit? Animae dicit, omnes novimus; planum est enim, ad illam directus est sermo. Utquid tristis es, anima mea, et utquid trouble me? Quaeritur persona loquens. Numquid caro animae loquitur, cum caro sine anima non loquatur?
An exile's desire to see the sanctuary

na that speaks Does the flesh speak to the soul, since the flesh does not speak without the soul? It is more natural for the soul to speak to the flesh than for the flesh to speak to the soul. But since he did not say: Why are you sad, my flesh, but: Why are you sad, my soul?, and also, taking into account that, if one spoke to the flesh, perhaps it would not say: Why are you sad?, but: Why do you hurt?, since the pain of the soul is called sadness and the discomfort that the body feels can be called pain, but not sadness, although because of the pain of the body the soul is often saddened, that is why it is important to know what hurts and what saddens. The flesh hurts and the soul is saddened. Patent is the expression Why are you sad, my soul? Therefore the soul does not speak to the flesh, because it did not say: Why are you sad, my flesh?; nor the flesh to the soul, since it is absurd for the lower to speak to the higher. Therefore, we must understand that we have something where the image of God is, namely, the mind and reason. The mind calls upon the light of God and the truth of God. She is the one through which we perceive what is just and the unjust, she is the one through which we distinguish the true from the false. It is called understanding, which beasts lack. If anyone despises and postpones understanding to the other things he has and degrades it as if it did not possess him, listen to what is said in the Psalm: Do not be like the horse and the mule, in which there is no understanding. Then our understanding speaks to our soul. It is weak in tribulations, tired in anguish, cowed in temptations, sick in sufferings; but the mind, which perceives the truth from above, lifts it up and says: Why are you sad, my soul; why do you bother me? Proprium enim magis est, ut anima carnem alloquatur, quam ut caro alloquatur animam. Sed quia non dixit, Quare tristis es, caro mea, sed ait: Quare tristis es, anima mea? (Si enim carnem alloqueretur, fortasse non diceret: Quare tristis es; sed, Quare doles? Dolor enim animae tristitia dicitur: discomfort vero quae fit in corpore dolor dici potest, tristitia non potest. Sed ex dolore corporis plerumque anima contristatur. Interest tamen quid doleat, et quid contristetur. Dolet enim caro, tristis est anima; et apena ista vox est, Utquid tristis es, anima mea?) Non ergo anima alloquitur carnem; quia non dixit, Utquid tristis es, caro mea? nec caro, animam; quia absurdum est ut inferior alloquatur superiorem.

Ergo intelligimus habere nos aliquid ubi imago Dei est,mentem scilicet atque rationem. Ipsa mens invokebat luzem Dei et veritatem Dei. Ipsa est qua capimus iustum et iniustum; ipsa est qua discernimus verura to false; ipsa est quae vocatur intellectus, quo intellectu carent bestiae; quem íntellectum quisquís in se negligit, et postponit caeteris, et ita abiicit quasi non habeat, audit ex psalmo: Nolite esse sicut equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus (Ps 31,9). Intellectus ergo noster alloquitur animam nostram. Ista in tríbulationibus marcida est, fessa in angoribus, contracta in tentationibus, aegra in laboribus. Erigit eam mens desuper capiens veritatem, et dicit Utquid tristis es, anima mea, et utquid conturbas me?
Ennarrations on the Psalms

7. See if this is not the Apostle's speech in that conflict, in which, symbolizing in himself some, and perhaps us, he said: I am pleased with the law of God according to the inner man, but I see another law in my members, that is, certain carnal movements; and, being in this struggle and in desperation, he invokes the grace of God, saying: I am a miserable man; Who will free me from this body of death? The grace of God through our Lord Jesus Christ. The Lord himself also deigned to prefigure in himself those who fight in this way when he said: Sad is my soul until death. He knew what he had come for. Did he fear death who had said: I have the power to give up my life and take it up again? Nobody takes it away from me; I give it myself or I take it again. But he who said: My soul is sad until death, prefigured in himself certain members of his. Ordinarily, the mind already firmly believes and knows the wonders that man, according to its belief, must see himself in the bosom of Abraham. He believes this, and yet, when the danger of death comes, he is disturbed by the familiarity he has had with the world; then apply your ear to the inner voice of God, and hear inwardly the song of reason. Thus, in the midst of the silence something sounds from above, not to the ears, but to the mind; so that anyone who hears this melody is disgusted by the bodily noise and all this human life is a deafening uproar that prevents hearing the celestial sound, extremely delightful, incomparable and ineffable. When this happens due to some disturbance, the man suffers violence and says speaking to his lucta et quasi desperatione, invoket gratiam Dei, Miser ego homo, quis liberate me from corpore mortis buius? Gratia Dei per lesum Christum Dominum nostmm (Rom 7,22,25). Such ita pugnantes etiam ipse Dominus in se praefigurare dignitus est, cum ait: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem (Mt 26,38). Ule enim noverat ad quod venerat.

Ule passionem pavebat qui dixerat: Potestatem drool ponendi animam meam, et potestatem drool iterum sumendi eam; nemo tollit illam a me, sed ego ipse pono eam a me, et iterum sumo eam? (10,17,18). Sed, Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem, qui dixit, quaedam membra sua in se figuravit. Pletumque enim iam mens bene credit et bene novit futurum hominem secundum fidem suam in gremio Abrahae: credit hoc, et tamen cum venerit aliquis articulus mortis, turbatur ex familiaritate quadam saeculi huius; erigit auditum in illam vocem Dei internam, audit rationabile carmen intrinsecus. Ita enim desuper in siientio sonat quiddam, non auribus, sed mentibus; ut quicumque audit illud melos, taedio afficiatur ad strepitum corporalem, et tota ista ista vita humano tumultus ei quídam sit, impediens auditum superni cuiusdam soni nimium delectabilis, et incomparabilis, et ineffabilis. Et revera cum ita contingit ex aliqua per-
An exile's desire to see the sanctuary

soul: Why are you sad and why do you disturb me? Or is it perhaps that he is disturbed because it is difficult to find a purified life when he judges the One who knows how to judge even purity and cleanliness? Although a plausible life is led among men, so that they have no reason to reprove, yet, when the examination takes place in the eyes of God, when applying the rule that levels without deception, God finds in man some things to censure that men did not realize should be censured, nor did he who must be internally judged. Fearing these things, the soul is troubled, and therefore the mind speaks to it, as if to say: Why do you fear sins, since you cannot avoid them all? Wait on the Lord, for I will praise him. The present address cures certain faults; Faithful confession purges the rest. Be truly afraid if you proclaim yourself righteous, for here are the words of another psalm: Do not enter into judgment with your servant. Why do you say do not call your servant to judgment? Because your mercy is necessary to me, since if you come to judgment without mercy, where will I go? If you attend, O Lord, to iniquities, Lord, who will resist? Do not call your servant to judgment, for no living person will be justified in your presence. Therefore if no living person will be justified in your presence, whoever lives here, no matter how righteously he lives, woe to him if God enters into judgment with him! In this way he rebukes from time to time arrogant and arrogant men by another prophet, saying: Why do you want to argue with me? You all abandoned me, says the Lord. Do not argue with God; be just and, no matter how just you are, confess yourself a sinner; always wait for mercy. turbatione, vim patitur homo, alloquens animam suam: Utquid tristis es, anima mea, et utquid conturbas me? An forte ideo quia difficile purgata vita invenitur, cum ille iudicat qui novit ad purum et liquidum iudicare? Quia etsi probabilis iam vita est inter homines, ita ut nomines quid iam reprehendant iuste non habeant: procedit examination ab illius oculis, proceeda regula exaequans non fallaciter, et invenit in homine quaedam quae reprehendat Deus, quae homines reprehendenda non videbant, nec ille ipse intus qui iudicandus est.

Haec timens anima forte conturbatur: alloquitur eam mens, quasi dices, Quid times de peccatis, quia non potes omnia devitare? Spera in Dominum, quoniam confitebor Mi. Quaedam sanat praesens allocutio, reliqua purgat fidelis confessio. Plan time, if iusrum you say; si non habes illam vocem ex alio psalmo: Ne intres in iudicium cum servo tuo. Quare, Ne intres in iudicium cum servo tuo? Misericordia tua mihi opus est. Nam si iudicium exhibitueris sine mercy, quo ibo? If you iniquitates observe you will see Domine, Domine, quis sustinebit? (Ps 129.3). Ne intres in iudicium cum servo tuo, quia non iustificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivos (Ps 142,2). Ergo si non iustificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivos, quia quicumque hic vivit, quantumlibet iuste vivat, vae illi si cum illo in iudicium intraverit Deus. Nam ex alio propheta arrogant et superbos identidem sic obiurgat: Utquid vultis mecum iudicio contendere? Omnes dereliquistis me, dicit Do-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

And in this humble confession speak confidently to your soul, which troubles you and which is in an uproar against you, and say to it: Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Maybe you wanted to trust yourself: Wait in the Lord, not in yourself. In yourself, what are you? For your part, what are you? Let him who took the wounds for you be your health. “Wait,” he says, “in the Lord, for I will praise him.” How will I praise or confess him? Saying: Health of my face (is) my God. You are the health of my face; you will heal me. As a sick person I speak to you; I know the doctor, I do not boast of being healthy. What does it mean: I know the doctor, I don't boast of being healthy? What is said in another psalm: I said: Lord, have mercy on me, heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. 8. This supplication, brothers, is prudent, but pay attention to good works. Play the psaltery obeying the precepts. Play the zither enduring tribulations. Divide your bread with the poor, you have heard from the mouth of Isaiah. Well, don't think that fasting is enough for you. Fasting mortifies you, but it does not help your neighbor. Your deprivations will be profitable if you offer to your neighbor what you deprive yourself of. Look how you let your soul down. To whom will you give what you took away? Where will you put what you denied yourself? How many can you feed with today's fast? Fast in such a way that, because someone else has eaten, you rejoice that you have eaten through prayer, so that you may be heard. About this Isaiah says: Still speaking to you, I will tell you: I am present if you would willingly divide bread with the hungry, because most of the time it is given grumbling and with sadness, rather to avoid mominus (Ier 2,29). Noli ergo iudicio contendere: da operam esse iustus: et quantumcumque fueris, confitete te peccatorem; semper spera mercym: et in this humili confessione securas alloquere turbantem te, et tumultuantem adversus te animam mam. Utquid tristis es, anima mea, et utquid trouble me? Forte in te voiebas sperare: Spera in Dominum, noli in te. What enim is in te? what is it about tea? Ule sit sanitas in te, qui suscepit vulnera propter te. Spera, inquit, in Dominum, quoniam confitebor Mi. Quid illi confiteberis? Salutare vultus mei, Deus meus. Tu es salutare vultus mei, tu sanabis me. /Eger ad te loquor: agnosco medicum, non me iacto sanum. Quid est, agnosco medicum, non me iacto sanum? Quod in alio psalmo diritur: Ego dixi, Domine, miserere mei, sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibi (Ps 40,5). 8. Haec vox, fratres, tuta est: sed vigilate in operibus bonis.

Tangite psalterium, obeying praeceptis: tangite cithatam, tolerating passiones. Frange esurienti panem tuum, audisti ab Isaia: noli ieiunium putare sufficere. Ieiunium te punishes, non alterum reficit. Fructuosae erunt anguishe tuae, si alteri praestiteris latitudinem. Ecce fraudasti animam tuam: cui dabis quod tibi abstulisti? ubi put quod tibi denegasti? Quam multos pauperes saginare potest intermissum hodie prandium nostrum! Ita ieiuna, ut alio manducante prandisse te gaudeas, propter orationes, ut exaudiaris. Ibi enim ait: Adhuc loquente te dicam, Ecce adsum; si fregeris ex animo esurienti panem (Is 58,7.9 et 10): quia ple-
Lamentation for the state of oppression

Lesties of the one who asks to calm the hunger of the needy; but God loves him who gives cheerfully. If you give the bread while being sad, you lose the bread and the reward. Then give it with good courage, so that He who sees within, even while you are speaking, may say: Here I am. How quickly the prayers of those who do good are received in heaven! And this goodness of man in the present life is fasting, almsgiving, prayer. Do you want your prayer to fly to God? Give it two wings: fasting and almsgiving. May the Lord find us prepared in this way so that the light and truth of God will find us full of confidence when he who has already come to suffer death for us comes to free us from death. Amen.
[LAMENTATION FOR THE STATE OF OPPRESSION IN WHICH THE PEOPLE ARE FOUND} SERMON TO THE PEOPLE

1. This psalm speaks of the sons of Korah, as his title declares. Korah means bald head or skull, and we know from the Gospel that our Lord Jesus Christ was crucified in the place of the skull. Therefore it is evident that this psalm is sung to the children of his passion. We also have the very clear and solid testimony of the apostle Saint Paul on this, because, when the Church found itself involved in the persecutions of the Gentiles, he took rumque fit a tristibus et a murmutantibus, ut careant taedio interpellantis, non ut reficiant viscera indigentis: Hilarem autem datorem diligit Deus (2 Coi 9,7). Si panem dederis tristis, et panem et meritum perdidisti. Ergo ex animo fac: ut ille qui intus videt adhuc loquente te, dicat, Ecce adsum. Quam celeriter accipiuntur orationes bene operantium: et haec iustitia hominis in hac vita, ieiunium, eleemosyna, otatio. Vis orationem tuam volate ad Deum? Fac illi duas alas, ieiunium et eleemosynam. Such us inveniat, ut secutos inveniat lux Dei, et vetitas Dei, cum venerit liberae nos a morte, qui iam venit will rise pro nobis mortem. Amen.

1. Psalmus iste filiis Core dicitur, sicut eius titulus praefert. Interpretatut autem Core Calvitium vel Calvaría, et invenimus in Gospel Dominum Iesum Christum in loco Calvariae crucifixum (Mt 27,33). Etgo clarum est, quod filiis passionis eius cantetur hic psalmus. Habemus autem hinc evidentissimum et fitmissimum testimonium apostoli Pauli: quia tum cum in persecutionibus Gentilium laboratet Ecclesia, hinc
Emanations on the Psalms

from this psalm the verse that he introduces in his epistle to the Romans to exhort patience and console the faithful. In this psalm he said what he included in his epistle: For your love we are continually mortified and considered like sheep to be slaughtered. Let us hear the voice of the martyrs in the psalm, and see what good cause this voice defends when it says for your love. For this same reason the Lord also added for the sake of justice when he said: Blessed are those who suffer persecution for justice, so that no one who suffers persecution may gain the glory of the same punishment when the good cause is lacking in the same punishment. Hence, exhorting his people, he says: You will be blessed when men tell you and infer to you these and these things through me. Therefore for this it is said: For your love we are continually mortified. 2 [v.l]. It is a plan of God of great consideration and of immense depth, because after having brought our patriarchs and the entire people of Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand, submerging the enemy pursuers in the sea, and having led them through enemy nations, and having placed them in the promised land defeating the adversaries, and having obtained great victories with a handful of them against a huge multitude of opponents, it pleased him to distance himself from his people so that his saints would suffer the ravages of carnage and death without anyone opposing them, without anyone defending them, without anyone prohibiting them, appearing as if they had turned their attention away from their moans, as if they had forgotten them, as if it were not their God who, with a strong hand and a strong arm, with very evident power, established our fathers as a kingdom; sumpsít versum, quem interponeret ad exhortationem et consolationem patientiae. Hic cnim dictum est, quod ille in Epistle sua posit: Propter te mortificamur tota die, deputati sumus velut oves occisionis (Rom 8,36). Vocem ergo martyrum audiamus in Psaimo: et vox martyrum videte quam bonam causam habeat, cura dicit, Propter te. Nam et Dominus ideo addidit, propter iustitiam, cum diceret: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam (Mt 5,10): ne quisquam persecutionem patiens, ex ipsa poena quaereret gloriam, non bonam habens causam. Et hinc exhortatus suos ait, Beati eritis cum vobis illa et illa fecerint vel dixerint nomines, propter me. Hinc ergo vox, Propter te mortificamur tola die. 2 [v.l].

Est autem magnae considerationis et magnae profunditatis consilium Dei, quid causae fuerit ut cum patres nostros Patriarchas, et totum illum populum Israel eduxerit in manu fortissima de Mgypto, et persequentes inimicos eorum in mari demerserit, duxeritque per contradientes gentes, bellatisque hostibus in terram promissionis posuerit, victoriasque magnas ex pauritate suorum in magna inimicorum multitudine fecerit: postea placuerit ei quasi avertere se a populo suo, ut stragem occisionis et mortis paterentur sancti eius, et nemo resisteret, nemo defendet, nemo prohiberet; quasi averterit fatiem suam a gemitibus eorum,
Lamentation for the state of oppression

that is, to that people who, as I said, freed from Egyptian tyranny, defeated and expelled the Gentiles from their own land, everyone admiring the fact that they were defeated many times by very few. This begins to be told in this psalm with a groan of confession. These things did not happen in vain. They happened so that it would be understood why they were made. Therefore, since it is evident that they were carried out, it must be investigated with elevated views for what reason they were done. It was not only written in the title of the psalm: For the children of Korah, but: For understanding to the children of Korah. These same things are also recorded in the psalm of which the Lord pronounced the first verse from the cross: My God, my God! Look at me; why did you abandon me? Prefiguring us in what He said and in His body, since we are also His body and He our Head, He did not speak from the cross through His mouth, but through ours. For God never abandoned him nor did He ever separate himself from the Father, but he said this for us: My God, my God; why did you abandon me? Well then he adds: The words of my crimes are far from my health. Therefore, manifest in this by whom he said it, for in Him there can be no sin. “I will call upon you,” he also said in the same psalm, “during the day, and you will not hear me; and during the night (it is understood: And you will not hear me); but he adds: but not for my foolishness. That is to say, not hearing me is not for my foolishness, but for my understanding. What does it mean: And you will not hear me so that I understand? You will not listen to me regarding temporal things so that I understand that eternal things must be desired from you. Then quasi oblitus sit eos, quasi ipse non sit Deus, qui in manu valida et brachio excelso evidentissima potentia patres nostros, id est illum populum, sicut dixi, ab Mgypto liberatum, victis pulsisque de terra sua gentibus constituerit in regno, mirantibus ómnibus quod saepe a paucis multi victi essent. Hoc ergo in gemitu confessionis incipit cantori in psaimo isto. Nonfrustra enim ista facta sunt, nisi ut ¡intelligatur quare facta sint. Proinde quia facta sunt, manifestum est: quare sint facta, altius quaerendum est. Ideo titulus non habet tantum, filiis Core; sed, In intellectum filiis Core. Hoc et in illo psaimo est, cuius primum versum ipse Dominus de cruz dixit: Deus meus, Deus meus, réspice in me, quare me dereliquisti?

Transfigurans enim nos in id quod dicebat, et in corpus suum (quia et nos sumus corpus eius, ille caput nostrum), vocem de cruz non dixit suam, sed nostram. Non enim unquam eum dereliquit Deus, nec ipse a Patre unquam recessit; sed propter told us hoc: Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? Nam sequitur ibi: Longe a salute mea verba delictorum meorum. Et ostendit ex quorum persona hoc dixerit; non enim in ipso delictum potuit inveniri. Clamabo ad te, inquit in ipso psaimo, per diem, et non exaudies; et night, subauditur utique, et non exaudies; sed addidit: et non ad insipientiam mibi (Ps 21,2.5), id est, boc ipsum quod non exaudies, non ad insipientiam mihi, sed ad intellectum. Quid est, ad intellectum non exaudies? Id est, me non exaudies ad temporalia, ut intelligam a te desideranda sempiterna. Non ergo relinquit Deus, et cum videtur relinquere, tollit quod male deside-
Ennarrations on the Psalms
Lamentation for the state of oppression

God does not abandon; and, when it seems to give up, take away what you desired badly and teach what you should desire well. If God always favored us in temporal goods, so that we abounded in all of them, and did not endure tribulations in the time of our mortality, we would say that these are the only and supreme goods that God gives to his servants and we would not long for greater ones from Him. That is why he mixes this deceptively sweet life with the bitterness of tribulations, so that the other may be sought, which is healthily sweet, that is, for the understanding of the children of Korah. Let us now hear the psalm and verify this in it. 3 [v.2.3]. With our ears, O God, we have heard; Our fathers told us the work you did in their days and in the days of old. Wondering that in these days God had abandoned those whom He wanted to exercise in work, they recount the past things that they heard from their parents, as if to say: Our parents did not tell us the things that we suffer. This was also said in that 21st psalm: Our fathers trusted in you, and you delivered them; but I am a worm and not a man, a reproach to men and contempt of the people. They trusted, and you delivered them. Didn't I trust too, and you abandoned me? Did I believe in you for no reason and for no reason is my name engraved on you, and yours on me? Our fathers declared these things to us: Your hand destroyed the nations and established our fathers; you destroyed the nations and dissipated them; That is, you drove the nations out of their land to bring in and establish our fathers there and establish their kingdom by your mercy. We have heard this from our parents.

4 £v.4]. But perhaps they were able to carry out this because they were fighters, strong, unbreakable, trained in weapons, warriors. Far from thinking about it. Our parents didn't tell us this; This is not recorded in Scripture. What does it claim? What follows: They did not possess the land by the point of their sword, nor did their own arm save them, but your right hand and your arm and the illumination of your face. Your right hand is your power. Your arm is your Son. Illumination or enhancement of your face, what is it? Present them with such signs that they understood that you were in their presence. When God is present through some miracle, do we see his face with our eyes? However, due to the miracle, he manifests his presence to men. And, if not, what do all those who contemplate this kind of prodigies say? I saw God present. Your right hand and your arm and the light of your face (saved them), because you took pleasure in them. That is, you acted with them in such a way that you manifested your love for them, so that everyone who noticed how they were treated would say: Truly God is with them and guides them. 5 [v.5]. What should we think? Was God one then, and another now? There is no such thing. What's next? You are the same, my king and my God. You are the same; you haven't changed. I see the times changed. The creator of time has not changed: You are the same, my king and my God. You usually lead me, govern me and protect me. You who send health to Jacob. What do you mean you send? Even though by your nature and substance, by which you are what you are, you are completely hidden from the eyes of men, and, therefore, you did not present yourself to our

rasti, et docet quid debenas bene desiderare. Si enim semper Deus in istis prospetitatibus faveret nobis, ut omnia nobis abundarent, nullamque in tempore isto mortalitatis nostrae tribulationem, nullas pressuras anguishesque pateremur; non diceremus nisi ista esse summa bona quae praestat Deus servís suis, et maiora ab illo non desideraremus. Ideo autem huic vitae male dulci miscet amaritudínes tribulationum, ut alia quae salubriter dulcis est, requiratur; hoc est, In intellectum filiis Core. Denique audíamus Psalmum, et ibi potíus hoc vídeamus. 3 [v.2.3.]. Deus, auribus nos tris audimus; paires nostri annuntiaverunt nobis, opus quod operatus es in diebus eoruin, et in diebus antiquis. Adínirantes quare in istis diebus tanquam deseruerit eos quos in passionibus exercere voluerit, recolunt praeterita quae audierunt a patribus, tanquam dicentes: Non ea quae patimur nobis retulerunt patres nostri. Nam et in illo psalmo hoc dixit: In te speraverunt patres nostri, speraverunt, et eruisti eos: ego autem sum vermis, et non homo, opprobrium hominum, et abiectio plebis (Ps 5,7). lili speraverunt, et liberasti eos: egone speravi, et dereliquisti me; et sine causa credidi in te, et sine causa nomen meum scriptum est apud te, et nomen tuum scriptum est in me? Haec ergo nobis indicaverunt patres nostri. Manus tua gentes dispersed, et plantati eos; infirmasti populas, et expulisti eos: id est, populos expulisti de terra sua, ut istos introres atque plantares, eorumque regnum your mercy confirms. Haec audimus a patribus nostris.

4 [v.4]. Be forte ideo illi ist potuerunt, quia fortes erant, quia praeliatores, quia invicti, quia exercitati, quia bellicosi? absit. Non hoc indicaverunt nobis patres nostri, non hoc habet Scriptura; sed quid habet, nisi quod sequitur? Non enim in gladio suo haereditate possederunt terram, et brachium ipsorum non salvos fecit eos; sed dextera tua, et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui. Dextera tua, power tua; brachium tuum, ipse Filius tuus. Ut illuminatio vultus tui: quid est hoc? Quia talibus signis eis affuisti, ut praesens intelligereris. Numquid enim quando nobis Deus aliquo miraculo adest, faciem ipsius oculis nostris videmus? Sed effectu miraculi suam praesentiam insinuate hominibus. Denique omnes qui mirantur ad huiuscemodi facta, quid dicunt? Vidi Deum praesentem. Sed dextera tua, et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui: quoniam complacent in eis: hoc est, sic cum eis egisti, ut bene pleasures in eis, ut quisquis eos attenderet quomodo cum eis ageretur, diceret quia veré Deus est cum lilis, et Deus illos agit. 5 [v.5]. Quid ergo? Alter erat tune, et alter est nunc? absit. Quid enim sequitur? Tu es ipse rex meus et Deus meus. Tu es ipse, non enim mutatus es. Tempora mutata video, creator temporum non mutatur. Tu es ipse rex meus et Deus meus. You soles me ducere, you soles me regere, your mihi soles subvenire. Who are you sending, salute Jacob. What is it, Who are you in charge? Etiamsi tu per tuatn prorsus substantiam atque naturam qua es quidquid es, oceultus es, nec per hoc quod es interfuisti patribus, ut facie ad
Ennarrations on the Psalms

parents so that they could see you face to face, however, through some creature, you send health to Jacob. The complete and perfect vision of God is reserved for the liberated, in the resurrection. Those fathers and also those of the New Testament, although they contemplated the mysteries revealed, although they announced the secrets discovered to them, nevertheless, they affirmed that they saw in a mirror and in an enigma and that they reserve seeing face to face for later, for when what the Apostle himself says comes: Now you are dead and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory. Then for then he reserves the perfect vision, about which Saint John says: Dearest, now we are children of God and what we will be has not yet appeared. We know that, when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is. Therefore if then our fathers did not see you face to face, according to what you are, even though this vision is reserved for the resurrection, yet, despite the fact that the angels appeared (to Abraham), you send health to 'Jacob. Not only for you being present, but for any of your creatures that appear, you order, taking care of the health of your servants, what you do for yourself; and this is also done for the health of your servants, by those whom you command to do it. Then, since you yourself are my king and my God and the one who sends salvation to Jacob, why do we now suffer these things? 6 [v. 6]. Perhaps only the past things were narrated to us and should not something similar be expected from the future? What do I say? Ha faciem te viderent; tamen per quamlibet creaturam tu mandas salutem Iacob. Etenim illa visio facie ad faciem, liberatis in resurrectione servamr. Et illi patres etiam Novi Testamenti quamvis revelationa mysteria tua viderint, quamvis revelationa secreta annuntiaverint; tamen in speculo se videre dixerunt et in aenigmate: servari autem visionem in futurum facie ad faciem (1 Cor 13:12), when venerit quod ipse Apostolus ait: Mortui enim estis, et vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo; cum autem Christus apparuerit, vita vestra, tune et vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria (Coi 3,3.4).

Tune ergo nobis servamr visio iiia facie ad faciem, de qua et Ioannes dicit: Dilectissimi, filii Dei sumus, et nondum apparuit quid erimus; scimus quia cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est (1 lo 3,2). Etsi ergo tune patres nostri non te viderunt facie ad faciem secundum quod tu es, etiamsi ista visio servatur in resurrectione, tamen etsi Angelí affuerunt, tu mandas salutem lacob. Non solum per te ades, sed per quamcumque creaturam mam affueris, tu mandas hoc propter salutem servorum tuorum quod tu ipse per te facis; hoc autem fit pro salute servorum tuorum quod faciunt quibus mandas. Cum ergo tu ipse sis rex meus et Deus meus, et tu commandes salutem Iacob, quare ista nunc patimur? 6 [v.6]. Sed forte praeterita tantum narrata sunt nobis, from the future autem non est aliquid tale sperandum. Imo vero sperandum. In te inimi-
Lamentation for the state of oppression

to be expected. For you we will defeat our enemies. Certainly, our fathers told us what God did in their days and in ancient times; that is, he destroyed the nations and drove the people out of their nations and established them in them. These are things of the past. In the future, what will happen? For you we will defeat our enemies. The time will come when all the enemies of Christians will be fanned like chaff, thrown into the air like dust, driven from the earth. Then if the past things were narrated to us in this way and the future things were also predicted, why do we endure the present things except for the understanding of the sons of Korah? For your sake we will drive away our enemies and in your name we will trample down those who rise up against us. This refers to the future. 7 [v. 7]. I will not trust my bow, as our fathers did not trust theirs. And my sword will not save me. 8 [v. 8]. You saved us from those who afflicted us. This is said figuratively in the past tense, looking ahead to what will happen. It is said as past because it is so true that it must be done as if it had already been done. I understand, therefore, from this why the prophets often speak as if the things they predict that will happen have happened and have not yet come to pass. In this way the prophet predicts the future passion of the Lord, saying: They have pierced my feet and my hands and counted all my bones. He did not say: They will drill and tell. And they themselves looked at me and saw me; He did not say: They will look at me and see me. And they divided my clothes among themselves; He did not say: They will divide. All these things are narrated as past, being still future, because for eos nostros ventilabimus. Ergo patres nostri indicaverunt nobis opus quod operatus is in diebus eorum, et in diebus antiquis: quia manus tua gentes disperdidit, eiecisti populos et plantati eos. Ista praeterita sunt: ​​de futur vero quid erit? In te imicos nostros ventilabimus: veniet tempus quando omnes inimici Christianorum, sicut palea ventilentur, sicut pulvis ventilentur, et de terra proiiciantur. Ergo si et praeterita sic sunt nobis narrata, et future talia praenuntiata; in medio praesentium quare laboramus, nisi in intetectum filiis Core? In te imicos nostros ventilabimus: et in nomine tuo spernemus insurgentes in nos. Future Hoc.

7 [v.7]. Non enim in arcu meo sperabo: quomodo nec patres in gladio suo. Ut gladius meus non salvum faciet me. 8 [v.8]. Except enim fecisti nos ex affligentibus nos. Et hoc figura praeteriti of future dicitur: sed ideo tanquam praeteritum dicitur, quia tam certum est quasi factum sit. Intendite quare pleraque Prophetae ita dicunt tanquam praeterita sint, cum praenuntienturfutura, non facta. Nam et de ipso Domino future passio praenuntiabatur, et tamen, Foderunt, inquit, manus meas et pedes meos, dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea: non dixit, Fodient, et dinumerabunt. Ipsi vero consideraverunt et conspexerunt me: non dixit,considerabunt et conspicient. Diviserunt sibi ropa mea (Ps 21,17.19): non dixit, divident. Ornnia ista tanquam

God, the future is as certain as the past. For us, the things that happened are true; those that are to happen, uncertain. For we know that, when an event happened, it cannot happen that it has not happened. Presents a prophet; The future is as certain to him as the past is to you. As it cannot happen to you that what you remember to have been fulfilled has not been fulfilled, so it cannot happen to the prophet that what he knows will happen is not fulfilled. That is why they confidently narrate those things that are future as past things. Then we trust that you saved us from those who afflicted us (that is, you will save us from those who afflict us) and you confounded those who hated us (that is, you will confound those who hate us). 9 [v. 9]. We will glory in God continually. See how he mixes words of future tense, so that you understand that the words that were written of past tense predict about the future. We will glory in God continually and praise in your name forever. What shall we glory in? Why shall we praise? Because you freed us from all those who afflicted us, because you will give us the eternal kingdom, because what the psalm says will be fulfilled in us: Blessed are those who dwell in your house, Lord; They will praise you forever. 10 [v. 10]. These future things being true to us and also those that we hear from our parents as past, what does it say about the present? But now you have rejected and confused us. You confused us not in our conscience, but in the presence of men. There was a time when Christians were persecuted, when they had to hide in all places, praeterita dkuntur, cum fuga sint; quia Deo etfutura tam certa sunt, tanquam praeterita sint. Nobis enim ea quae praeterierunt, certa sunt; quaefutura, incerta sunt. Novimus enim aliquid accidisse, et non potest fieri ut non acciderit quod accidit. Da prophetam cui tam certum sit futurum quam tibí praeteritum: et quam tibi quod meministi factum, non potest fieri ut non sit factum, tam illi quod novit futurum, non potest fieri ut non fiat. Ideo de securitate dicuntur tanquam praeterita, quae adhucfutura sunt. Hoc ergo speramus. Except enim fecisti nos ex affligentibus nos, et eos qui oderunt nos confudisti. 9 [v.9]. In Deo laudabimur tota die.

Videte quemadmodum miscet etiam verba futuri temporis, ut intelligas et praeterita quae dicta sunt de futur esse praedicta. In Deo laudabimur tota die: et in nomine tuo confitebimur in saecula. Quid, laudabimur? quid, conjitebimur? Quia ex ómnibus affligentibus nos eruisti nos, quia regnum perpetuum dabis nobis, quia complebitur in nobis, Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine, in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). 10 [v.10]. Haec ergofutura cum certa sint nobis, et illa praeterita cum a patribus nostris audierimus, quid manner? Nunc autem repulisti et confudisti nos. Confudisti, non in conscientia nostra, sed in facie hominum. Erat enim tempus quo affligerentur Christiani. cum ubique fugerent, cum ubique diceretur, Christjanus est, tanquam ad insultationem

When wherever it was said: He is a Christian, it was considered a disgrace and ridicule. Then where is our God, our King, who sends health to Jacob? Where is He Who did those things that our parents told us? Where is the one who will do everything that was revealed to us by the Holy Spirit? Has it changed? No. These things were done for the understanding of the sons of Korah. We must understand why he wanted us to suffer all this in the intervening period. What is all this? But now you have rejected and confused us and you do not go out, O God, with our armies. We go out to meet our enemies, and you do not go out with us; We see them, they prevail, and we are invalid soldiers. Where is your strength? Where is your right hand and your power? Where is the dried sea? Where are the Egyptian pursuers buried by the waves? Where is the opponent Amalee, defeated with the sign of the cross? And you don't go out, oh God!, with our armies. 11 [v. l l ]. You put us behind our enemies. They appearing in front and us behind, we being considered as defeated and them as winners. And those who hated us plundered us. What did they loot or who did they kidnap? Us. 12 [v. 12]. You handed us over, like sheep for food, and scattered us among the people. We are eaten by people. In these are represented those who succumbed to sufferings, being converted into a body of Gentiles. The Church mourns these as her devoured members. 13 [v. 13].

et ad opprobrium pertineret. Ubi est ergo ille Deus noster, rex noster, qui mandat salutem Iacob? Ubi est ille qui fecit omnia quae nobis narraverunt paires nostri? Ubi est qui facturus est omnia quae nobis revelavit per Spiritum suum? Numquid mutatus est? Sed in intellectum filiis Core fiunt haec. Aliquid enim intelligere debenmus, quare nos ista omnia medio tempore pati voluit. Quae omnia? Nunc autem repulisti et confudisti nos: et non egredieris Deus in virtutibus nostris. Procedimus ad inimicos us, et tu nobiscum non procedis: videmus eos, praevalent illi, et nos invalidi sumus. Ubi est illa virtus tua? Ubi est dextera et potentia tua? ubi mare siccatum? ubi. Egyptii persequentes fluctibus obruti? (Ex 14,21.27) ubi Amalech resistens, in crucis sign will you overcome? (Ib. 17,11). Et non egredieris Deus in virtutibus nostris. 11 [v. l l ]. Avertisti autem nos retrorsum prae inimicis nostris: ut quasi illi ante sint, nos retro; illi victors, we victi deputemur. Et qui nos oderunt, diripiebant sibi: quid, nisi nos? 12 [v.12]. Dedisti nos tanquam oves escarum, et in nationibus dispersisti nos: a nationibus manducad sumus. Hi signifitur qui sic passi sunt, ut in Corpus gentium verterentur. Plangit enim eos Ecclesia, tanquam membra sua devorata. 13 [v.13]. Vendidisti populum tuum sine pretio. Vidimus enim

seen those whom you gave, but not what you received for them. And there was no great joy in their rejoicings. When Christians fled, persecuted by idolatrous enemies, did they gather together and cry out to God with voices of joy? Perhaps in the Church of God the hymns that are usually sung when at peace were sung, resounding in the ears of God with the sweet song of brotherhood? And there was no great rejoicing in their rejoicings. 14 [v.14.15). You made us a reproach to our neighbors and the ridicule and ridicule of those around us. You placed us in likeness (or imitation) among the people. What does similarity or imitation mean? That, when cursing men offer a likeness or present an imitation of that whom they detest, they say: Thus you die; even if you are punished (like that one). How many similar things were said then! So be crucified! Today there is no shortage of enemies of Christ; Here you have the Jews, who, when we defend Christ, tell us: Die like Him. They would not have inflicted that death if they had not greatly feared dying in that way. But what mystery would be contained in it if they had been able to understand it? When an ointment is applied to a blind man, he does not see the eye drops in the doctor's hand. For thus the same cross was also raised for the benefit of the persecutors. Through her they were later healed and through her they believed in the One they killed. You placed us in similarity among the people, and in movement of heads among the peoples. Well, they shake their heads in order to insult. They grimaced with their lips and shook their heads, says Psalm 21. This they did to the Lord; They also did this to all quos dedisti, non vidimus quid accepisti. Et non fuet multitudo in iubilationibus eorum. Numquid enim quando fugiebant Christiani persequentibus inimicis idololatris, fiebant congregations et iubilationes Deo? Numquid concinebantur hymni de ecclesiis Dei, qui solent in pace concini, dulcique concentu fraternitatis Dei auribus personan? Et non fuet multitudo in iubilationibus eorum. 14 £V.14.15]. Posuisti nos in opprobrium vicinis nostris, subsannationem et derisum bis qui in circuitu nostro sunt. Posuisti us in similarity in nationibus. Quid est, in similarityinem?

When maledicentes homines similarityinem dant de eo quem detestantur: Sic moriaris, sic puniaris. Quanta tune dicta sunt talia? Sic crucifigaris. Hodieque non desunt hostes Christi, illi ipsi Iudaei, contra quos quando defendimus Christum, dicunt nobis: Sic moriaris quomodo ille. Non enim illam mortem intulissent, nisi eo modo morí vehementer exhorruissent; aut quid mysterii haberet, si intelligere potuissent. Caecus quando inunguitur, collyrium in manu medici non videt. Nam crux ipsa et pro ipsis persequentibus facta est. Inde sunt postea sanati, et in eum crediderunt quem ipsi occiderunt. Posuisti nos in similarityinem in nationibus, commotionem capitis in populis: commotionem capitis ad insultandum. Et locuti sunt labiis, et moveunt ctput (Ps 21,8). Hoc Domino, hoc etiam omnibus

saints whom they could persecute, imprison, outrage, deliver, afflict and kill. 15 [v. 16. 17]. I continually see my ignominy, and concussion covers my face because of the voice of him who reproaches and reviles. That is, by the voice of those who insult me ​​and blame me for the crime of worshiping you and confessing you; of those who blame me for the crime of that name by which all my crimes are erased. By the voice of the one who reproaches and reviles, that is, the one who speaks against me. Because of the presence of the enemy and the pursuer. What sense does this have? The things that were narrated as past are not fulfilled in us; those that are expected as future, do not appear yet. The last ones are having brought the people out of Egypt with your great glory, having taken them through the nations, establishing them in a kingdom after expelling the nations. The future ones are to take the people out of this Egypt of the world, having Christ as leader appearing in his glory, condemn the perverse with the devil to eternal fire and receive the eternal kingdom of Christ with his saints. These are future things, those past. And in the middle, what is there? Tribulations. So that? So that the soul that adores God shows how much it adores Him; so that it can be seen if he worships for free the One from whom he receives health for free. If God tells you: What did you give me to create you? For if, certainly done, you deserved something from me, you did not deserve it before I made you. What shall we answer to Him who first created us freely because He was good, not because we had given us something? Furthermore, what are we to say about the second birth, that is, about reparation? Is it perhaps due to sanctis eius, quos persequi, quos tenere, quos illudere, quos tradere, quos affligere, quos occidere potuerunt. 15 [v.16.17]. All verecundia mea contra me est, et confusio vultus mei operuit me: a voce exprobrantis et oblockis: hoc est, a voce insultandum et crime mihi obiicientium, quia coló te, quia confiteor te: et crime mihi obiicientium de illo nomine, unde mea omnia crimina delebuntur. A voce exprobrantis et oblockntis, id est, contra me loquentis. A facie inimici et persequentis. Et quis hic intellectus? Quae praeterita dicta sunt, non in nobis fient: quaefutura sperantur, non apparent.

Praeterita: in magna gloria tua eductus est populus de /Egypto, liberatus a petsequentibus, ductus per gentes, expulsis gentibus collocatus in regno. What future? Educendus populus de ista ¿Egypto saeculi, duce Christo apparente in gloria sua; Pondi sancti ad dexteram, iniqui ad sinistram, damnandi iniqui cum diabolo in aeterna poena; accipiendum regnum to Christ cum sanctis in sempiternum. Haec sunt future, illa praeterita. In the middle quid? Tribuiationes. Quare? Ut appareat animus colens Deum, quantum colat Deum; ut video utrum gratis colat eum a quo salutem gratis accepit. Si enim tibi dicat Deus, Quid dedisti mihi ut facerem te? Certe si factus promeruisti me, non me promerueras antequam facerem te. Quid dicturi sumus ei, qui primo gratis fecit us, quia bonus est, non quia aliquid meruimus? Deinde de ipsa reparatione,

our merits that the Lord would send us that perpetual Health? There is no such thing. If our merits had had any influence, he would have come to condemn us. He did not come to inspect our merits, but to forgive us our sins. You did not exist, and you were made. What did you give to God? You were evil, and you have been delivered. What did you give to God? What have you not received freely from him? It is rightly called grace, because it is freely given. Then you are required to worship Him freely; not because it gives temporal things, but because it offers eternal things. 16. But pay attention to eternal things, lest you think evil of them, and, thinking carnally, do not worship God freely. Well what? If you worship God because he gave you a property, won't you also worship him because he took it from you? Perhaps you say: I adore him because he will give me an eternal fifth. Yet you still worship him with a depraved mind, for you do not worship him with pure love, you still crave reward. You want to have in the future life the things that you will necessarily leave here; you want to change carnal desire, but not destroy it. Fasting is not praised in those who reserve their stomach for an orgy. Sometimes men are invited to a banquet and, wanting to attend it while hungry, they fast. Should this fast be considered a fast of mortification and not of sybaritism? Therefore do not expect that God will give you what he here commands you to despise. These things the Jews hoped for; That's why they were disoriented on this issue. They await the resurrection, but believe that they must be resurrected to enjoy the bodily pleasures they love here. Therefore, de secunda nativitate quid dicturi sumus? Merita nostra fecisse ut nobis illa salus perpetua mitteretur a Domino? absit. Si merita nostra aliquid facerent, ad damnationem nostram vinoet. Non venit ille ad inspectionem meritorum, sed ad remissionem peccatorum. Non fuesti, et factus is: quid Deo dedisti? Malus fuesti, et liberatus is: quid Deo dedisti? Quid non ab eo gratis accepisti? Merit et gratia nominatur, quia gratis datur. Exigitur ergo a te, ut et tu gratis eum queues: non quia dat temporalia, sed quia praestat aeterna. 16. Sed ipsa aeterna vide ne aliter cogites, et cogitando aeterna carnaliter, nihilominus Deum gratis non colas. Quid enim? Si ideo colis Deum, quia dat tibi fundum, non eum culturus es, quia tollit tibí fundum? Be strong you say: Ideo eum colam, quia dabit mihi villam, non tamen temporalem.

Nihilominus adhuc corruptam mentem geris: amore enim casto non colis, adhuc mercedem expetis. Ea enim vis habere in future saeculo, quae hic necesse est derelinquas: mutare vis voluptatem carnalem, non amputare. Non laudatur in iüo ieiunium, qui ad luxuriosam coenam servat ventrem suum. Invitantur enim aliquando homines ad coenam magnam, et eum ad eam volunt avidi vinore, ieiunant: numquid hoc ieiunium continentiae, et non potius luxuriae deputandum est? Noli ergo talia sperare tibi danda a Deo, qualia hic iubet contemnere. Haec enim sperabant Iudaei, ideo turbabantur in illa quaestione. Nam et ipsi resurrectionem sperant, sed ad such voluptates corporis se sperant

When the Sadducees, who did not believe in the resurrection, asked them the question about the woman who had successively married seven brothers, when they were asked which of them she would be the wife of in the resurrection, they gave up and could not answer. On the contrary, when this question was put to the Lord, since we are not promised the resurrection in which pleasures of this kind are sought or claimed, but the resurrection in which eternal joys from God Himself will be provided, He answers and says: You are wrong because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God, because in the resurrection neither women nor men will marry, for they will not begin to die. That is to say, no successor is sought there, because no one will die. So what will happen? They will be equal to the angels of God. Unless you think that angels enjoy themselves with daily banquets and the wine with which you get drunk, or you judge that angels also get married. None of these things occur in angels. What do they enjoy? Of what the Lord says: Do you not know that the angels of God always see the face of my Father? Therefore, if the angels rejoice in the face of the Father, such joy is prepared for you. Will you find another better than contemplating the face of God? Fear for your love if you still suspect that there is something more beautiful than Him for whom everything is beautiful, that captivates your heart, and, therefore, you do not deserve to think about God's. The Lord appeared in the flesh and appeared as a man to men. How did it appear? I already said it: man to men. What extraordinary thing appeared? Meat to meat. What extraordinary thing appeared to Him of whom it was said: We saw Him, and He had no form nor resurrections, quales hic amant. Ideo eum eis proposeretur quaestio illa a Sadducaeis, qui non credunt resurrectionem, de illa midiere quae nupsit septena fratribus sibimet succedentibus, cuius eorum in resurrectione erit uxor, deficiebant, et responderé non poterant. At vero Domino quando est proposita, quia nobis resurrectio talis promittitur, non qua repetantur huiusmodi voluptates, sed qua aeterna de ipso Deo gaudia comparentur, responderit Dominus, et ait: Erratis nescientes Scripturas, ñeque virtutem Dei: in resurrectione enim ñeque cloudnt, ñeque uxores ducent: non enim incipient mori. Id est, non ibi quaeritur successor, ubi non erit decessor. Et quid erit? Be erunt, inquit, aequales Angelis Dei (Mt 22,29-30, et Le 20,35.36).

Nisi strong whores, quod Angelí epulis quotidianis, et vino quo te inebrias, gaudeant, aut hoc forte arbitraris, quod Angelí uxores habeant. Nihil eorum is apud Angelos. Unde gaudent Angelí, nisi unde Dominus ait: Nescitis quia Angelí eorum semper vident faciem Patris? (Mt 18:10). Si ergo ad faciem Patris gaudent Angelí, ad tale gaudium te praepara: aut si invenís melius quam videte faciem Dei? Vae tali amori tuo, si vel suspicaris aliquid pulchrius, quam est ille a quo est omne pulchrum, quod te teneat, ne illum cogitare merearis. Dominus in carne erat, et apparebat homo hominibus. Qualis apparebat? Iam dixi, homo hominibus. Quid magnum apparebat? Expensive meat. Quid magnum apparebat, de quo dictum est: Vidimus eum, et non

loveliness? Who had no form or beauty? The one who is also said: The most beautiful of the sons of men. As a man he had no form or beauty, but he was beautiful and therefore superior to the sons of men. Therefore, showing the eyes of those who saw him that deformed form of flesh, what does he say? Whoever loves me keeps my commandments, and whoever loves me is loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him. He promised that He, whom they saw, would appear. What is this? The same as if he said to them: You see the form of a servant; the form of God is hidden; By this I captive you, by that I save you; For this I nourish you as adults, for that I nourish you as children. Then, in order that our faith, by which we purified ourselves, might be prepared for things invisible, all these things were made for the understanding of the sons of Korah, so that the saints, laying aside the things they had and even of the temporal life itself, would not be interested in the eternal with regard to these same temporal things, but would tolerate for the pure love of the eternal all these things that they had to endure temporally. 17 [v. 18. 19]. Well, since the sons of Korah understood this, what do they say? All this has happened to us, and we have not forgotten you. What does it mean we have not forgotten you? We have not acted wickedly against your commandment nor have our hearts turned back. And you turned our paths away from your path. Here is the meaning: since our hearts have not turned back, since we have not forgotten you, since we have not transgressed iniquitously against your will (therefore), we find ourselves placed in great tribulation.

lations and persecutions on the part of the people. You turned our paths from your path. Our paths were in the prosperity of temporal things, you erased them from your path and showed us how narrow and narrow is the path that leads to life. And you turned our paths away from your path. What does he mean to tell us when he says you turned our paths away from your path? Which is as if he said: You are established in tribulations; you suffer exceedingly; You lost many of the things you loved in this world, but I did not leave you abandoned on the narrow path that I showed you. You look for the wide paths. What will I tell you? The path that I show you leads to eternal life. By whom you intend to walk, you are going to death. How wide and spacious is the path that leads to destruction, and how many there are who walk along it! How strait and narrow is the path that leads to life, and how few there are who walk along it! Who are these few? Those who endure tribulations; those who tolerate temptations; those who do not faint in all these discomforts; Those who do not rejoice only at the time of speaking and when the time of tribulation arrives, as if the sun had appeared, they dry up as if they were without a root, but they have the root of charity, as we have just heard from the reading of the gospel. Have, I will say, the root of charity, so that, when the sun rises, it does not burn you, but nourishes you. All these things have come upon us, and we have not forgotten you, nor have we acted wickedly against your will, nor have our hearts turned back. But as we did all these things in the midst of tribulations walking along the narrow path, you turned our paths away from your path.

habebat speciem ñeque decorem? (Is 53,2). Quis non habebat speciem ñeque decorem? De quo Item dicitur: Speciosus forma prae filiis hominum (Ps 44,3). Ut homo, non habebat speciem ñeque decotem; sed speciosus forma ex eo quod est prae filiis hominum. Ideo formam illam deformem carnis ostendens oculis intuentium, quid ait? Qui diligit me, mandata mea. custodian; et qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo, et ego diligam eum, et ostendam Mi meipsum (lo 14,21). Quem videbant, ostensurum se illis promittebat. Sed quid est hoc? Quasi diceret, Videtis formam servi, occulta est forma Dei: per hanc vobis blandior, illam vobis servo; Make your little ones nourished, make them great pasco. Ergo ut haec fides nostra qua purgamur, ad invisibilia praeparetur, hoc est, quod in intellectum filiis Core facta sunt ista omnia, ut detraherentur sanctis ea quae habebant, detraheretur et ipsa vita temporalis: ut non propter haec ipsa temporalia colerent ipsum aeternum, sed amore illius casto tolerarent haec omnia quae pro tempore paterentur. 17 [v.18.19). Denique quia intellexerunt hoc filii Core, quid dicunt? Haec omnia venerunt super nos, et obliti non sumus te. Quid est, et obliti non sumus te? Et inique non egimus in testament tito: et non recessit retro cor nostrum: et declinasti semitas braces de via tua. Ecce est intellectus, quia non recessit retro cor nostrum, quia obliti non sumus te, quia inique non egimus in testament tuo, positi in magnis tribula-

tionibus et persecutionibus gentium. Declinasti semitas nosPras de via tua. Semitae enim nostrae erant in voluptatibus saeculi; semitae nostrae erant in prosperitatibus temporalium rerum: tulisti semitas nostras de via tua, et ostendisti nobis quam arcta et angusta via est quae ducit ad vitam. Et declinasti semitas nostras de via tua. What is it, declinasti semitas nostras de via tua? Tanquam diceret nobis, In tribulatione positi estis. Semitic cans quaerebatis: quid vobis dico? Hac itur ad vitam sempiternam: qua vultis ambulare, ad mortem pergitis. Quam lata et spatiosa via est quae ducit ad inteñtum, et multi sunt qui ambulant per eam! Quam arcta et angusta via est quae ducit ad vitam, et pauci sunt qui ambulant per illam! (Mt 7,13.14). Who sunt pauci? Qui tolerant tribulationes, qui tolerant temptationes, qui in istis omnibus molestiis non deficiunt; qui non ad horam gaudent ad verbum, et in tempore tribulationis tanquam orto solé arescunt (I 13,20.21.23), sed habent radicem charitatis, sicut audivimus quod moda lectum est in Gospel (Mark 4,16.17.20, et Le 8,13.15). Radicem, inquam, charitatis habe, ut cum sol exortus fuerit, non te urat, sed nutriat. Haec omnia venerunt super nos, et obliti non sumus te; et inique non egimus in testament tuo; et non recessit retro cor nostrum.

18 [v. 20]. You humbled us in the place of weakness. Then you will exalt us in the place of strength. And he covered us with the shadow of death. This mortality (of the body) is the shadow of death. For true death is damnation with the devil. 19 [v. 21]. If we have forgotten the name of our God. This is the understanding of the sons of Korah. And if we have extended (or raised) our hands to a strange god. 20 [v. 22]. Will not God find out these things? He knows the secrets of the heart. Know and find out; If you know the secrets of the heart, what are you doing there? Will not God find out these things? Know yourself, find out by attending to us. In fact, God sometimes investigates, and says that he has known because he made you known. He shows you his work, not his knowledge. Many times we say: The day is happy when it is peaceful. Does the same day make you happy? We say: He is happy, because he makes us happy. Likewise, we say that the sky is sad. Clouds do not experience such sensations; But since men, upon seeing the appearance of heaven in this way, become sad, it is said to be sad because it saddens them. In the same way, it is said that God knows when he makes us known. God says to Abraham: Now I know that you fear God. Didn't you know this before? Yes. But Abraham did not know himself, since in the same temptation he knew himself. Many times man thinks that he can do what he cannot or that he cannot do what he can. of the children, of whom we read in the book of Kings who, insulting the holy prophet Elyseus for his baldness and shouting after him, said to him: Go up bald, go up bald. For these foolishly talkative children, the holy prophet cursing them for their perversity, were devoured by the bears that came out of the jungle. This is written and I have remembered where it was recorded. Those who remember it, keep it in mind; Those who don't remember it, read it, and those who haven't read it, believe it. Therefore, what that event prefigured for the future should not take us by surprise. In those children, foolish men are symbolized, who do not have the sense of reality, of which the Apostle does not want us to be when he says: Do not be children in your mind. But as the Lord had invited us to imitate children when, taking a child, he placed him before him and said: If anyone does not become like this child, he will not enter the kingdom of heaven, there also the cautious Apostle where he discourages the childish mind, also invites us, on the other hand, to imitate children, saying: Do not be children in mind, but be children in malice, so that you may be perfect in feeling. He who takes pleasure in imitating children, does not take pleasure in imitating them in ignorance, but in innocence. Well, the children of whom I previously said that they ignorantly insulted the bald saint of God and shouted behind his back: Bald, bald, prefigured the men who with the same childish, foolishness, mocked the Bald (so called), because he was crucified in the place of the Skull; and as it came to pass that the former were devoured by bears, so these latter were taken as by beasts, that is, by demons; by the terpretari filios Calvi. When I was still ugly. All—says the Apostle—have sinned, and need the glory of God; and also: Christ died for the wicked. She was loved ugly so that she would not remain ugly. However, in reality the ugly woman was not loved, because the ugliness was not loved, since, if she had loved the ugliness, she would keep it. He annulled ugliness and created beauty. Who did it come to, what did it do? He now appears speaking prophetically. Let him come out to our suis, sed non in intellectum. Si enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent (1 Cor 2:8). Ad hunc intellectum oculos alios quaerebat ipse, cum diceret: Qui me videt et Patrem (lo 14,9). Sonet eum iam Psalmus: gaudeamus in nuptiis, et nos erimus cum iis qui fiunt nuptiae qui invitationntur ad nuptias; et ipsi invitationti sponsa est. Etenim sponsa Ecclesia est, sponsus Christus. Solent dici ab scholasticis carmina quaedam uxores ducentibus et Nuntibus, quae vocantur epithalamia; Quidquid ibi cantatur, ad honorem cantatur sponsi et sponsae: an forte et in nuptiis istis, quo invitations sumus, thalamus non est? Et unde dicit alius psalmus: In solé posit tabernaculum suum, et ipse tanquam sponsus proceedens de thalamo suo? (Ps 18,6).

Coniunctio nuptialis, Verbum et caro: huius coniunctionis thalamus, virginis uterus. Etenim caro ipsa Verb est coniuncta: unde etiam dicitur, Iam non duo, sed una caro (Mt 19, 6, et Eph 5,32). Assumpta est Ecclesia ex genere humano, ut caput esset Ecclesiae ipsa caro Verbo coniuncta, et caeteri credentes membra essent illius capitis. Nam vis videre quis venerit ad nuptias? In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum (lo 1,1). Gaudeat sponsa amata a Deo. When does he kill? Dum adhuc foeda, Omnes enim peccaverunt, ait Apostolus, et egent gloria Dei (Rom 3:23). Et iterum: Etenim Christus pro impiis mortuus est (Ib. 5,6). Amata est foeda, ne remaneret foeda. Non enim veré foeda amata est, quia non foeditas
