meeting; Let us love him, and if we find any ugliness in him, let us not love him. He found many ugly things in us, and he loved us. If we find any ugliness in him, let us not love him. For even the very dressing of flesh, for which it was said, We saw him, and he had no form nor beauty, if you consider in it the piety by which he did it, you will also see that it is beautiful. But the prophet spoke in person of the Jews when he said: We saw him, and he had no form or beauty. Because? Because they didn't understand. For those who understood it is sublime beauty: And the Word became flesh. For me, says one of the bridegroom's friends, let it not happen to me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. It would be little not to be ashamed of her if you did not also glorify yourself. Why did it have no form or beauty? Because "Christ crucified is a scandal to the Jews, and foolishness to the Gentiles." Why did he still have beauty on the cross? For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For us believers everywhere the Bridegroom appears beautiful. Beautiful being God, Word in God; beautiful in the womb of the Virgin, where he did not lose divinity and took on humanity; The Word was born a beautiful child, because, even though he was tiny, suckling, being carried in arms, the heavens spoke, the angels praised him, the star directed the Magi, he was adored in the manger and at all times he was food for the meek. Therefore it is beautiful in heaven and it is beautiful on earth; beautiful in the bosom, amata est: nam si hoc amaret, hoc servaret: evertit foeditatem, formavit pulchritudinem. Ad quaiem comer, et quaiem fecit? Veniat iam ipse in verbis propheticis; ecce ipse sponsus procedat nobis: amemus illum; aut si invenerimus in eo aliquid foedi, non amemus. Ecce ipse invenit fines foeda, et amavit nos: si aliquid foedi invenerimus in eo, non amemus. Quia et hoc ipsum quod carnem indutus est, ut de illo etiam diceretur, Vidimus eum, et non habebat speciem ñeque decorem (Is 53,2); If you consider misericordiam qua factus est, et ibi pulcher est. Sed Iudaeorum personam gerebat propheta, cum diceret: Vidimus eum, et non habebat speciem ñeque decorem. Quare? Quia non in intellectum. Intelligentibus autem, et Verbum caro jactum est (lo 1,14), magna pulchritudo est. Mihi autem absit gloriari, dixit unus amicorum sponsi, nisi in cruz Domini nostri lesu Christi (Gal 6,14). Parum est ut non inde erubescas, nisi etiam et glorieris.

Quare ergo non habuit speciem ñeque decorem? Quia Christus crucifixus, Iudaeis quidem scandalum, Gentibus stultitia. Quare autem et in intersection habuit decorem? Quia quod stultum est Dei, sapientius est quam nomines; et quod infirmum est Dei, fortius est quam homines (1 Cor 1,23,25). Nobis ergo iam credentibus, ubique sponsus pulcher occurrat. Pulcher Deus, Verbum apud Deum: pulcher in utero virginis, ubi non amisit divinitatem, et sumpsit humanitatem: pulcher natus infans Verbum; quia et cum esset infans, cum sugeret, cum manibus portaretur, caeli locuti sunt, Angeli laudes dixerunt, Magos stella direxit, adoratus est in praesepi, cibaria mansuetorum (Le 2,8.14, et Mt 2,1). Pulcher ergo in cáelo, pulcher in tetra; pulcher in uteto, pulcher

beautiful in the arms of his parents, beautiful in miracles, beautiful in whippings, beautiful inviting life, beautiful not worrying about death, beautiful giving life, beautiful taking it: beautiful on the cross, beautiful in the tomb and beautiful in heaven. Hear, understanding the song, and the weakness of his flesh, do not turn your eyes away from the splendor of his beauty. The supreme and true beauty is justice. You will not see a beautiful man if you notice that he is unfair. Wherever there is a righteous there is a beautiful. Then come to us to be contemplated with the eyes of the mind the one described by a certain panegyric prophet of yours. See how it starts. 4 [v.2]. My heart broke out a good word. Who is speaking? The Father or the prophet? Some understood that it was the Father, who said: My heart broke out a good word, recommending to us a certain ineffable birth. So that perhaps you would not think that something was used by which God begat the Son, in the same way as man uses something to beget children, namely, copulation, without which man cannot beget offspring; So that you do not think, I repeat, that God needed some union to beget his Son, my heart, he says, broke out a good word. Oh man! Today your heart engenders thought and has no need of a wife. By the thought produced in your heart you build something. Thus, for example, the building, before existing in reality, is found in thought, and there is already what you have to do in that for which you have to do it; What's more, you already praise the non-existent building, the building that is not yet in reality, but in the anticipation in manibus patentum; pulcher in miraculis, pulcher in flagellis, pulcher invitationns ad vitam, pulcher non curans mortem; pulcher deponens animam, pulcher recipiens; pulcher in ligno, pulcher in sepulcro, pulcher in cáelo. In intellectum audite Canticum, ñeque oculos vestros a splendore pulchritudinis illius avertat carnis infirmitas. Summa et vera pulchritudo iustitia est: ibi illum non videbis pulchrum, ubi deprehendís iniustum: si ubique iustus, ubique decotus. Veniat ergo nobis inspiciendus oculis mentis, descriptus a quodam laudatore suo ptopheta: ecce incipit. 4 [v.2J. Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum. Did you say, Pater, a Prophet? Intellexerunt enim quídam Patris personara dicetis, Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum, commendantis nobis nativitatem quamdam ineffabilem.

Ne forte putares aliquid assumptum, unde Filium generat Deus; quemadmodum homo sibi assumit aliquid unde generet filios, coniugium scilicet, sine quo prolem procreare homo non potest: ne igitur putares aliquo coniugio indiguisse Deum, unde Filium generat, Eructavit, inquit, cor meum verbum bonum. Hodie cor tuum, or homo, generat consilium, nec quaerit uxorem: pet consilium natum ex corde tuo aedificas aliquid; et illa fabrica, antequam stet in opete, stat in consilio; et inest iam quod facturus es, in eo per quod facturus es: et laudas fabrican nondum existenm, nondum in specie aedificii, sed in prolatione consilii; nec laudat alius consilium tuum, nisi aut indicaveris, aut víderit quod S.Ag. 20
Ennarrations on the Psalms

of thought; and no one praises your project unless you have first shown it or seen what you did. Therefore, if all things were made by the Word and the Word is from God, contemplate the building made by the Word and through the work understand the thought. What is the Verboo Word by which heaven and earth were made, and all the ornamentation of the sky, the fertility of the earth, the extension of the sea, the diffusion of the air, the brilliance of the stars and the clarity of the moon. All these things are seen; Go beyond these and think of the angels, the principalities, the thrones, the dominions, the powers: all these were made by him. Then how is it that these beings were made good? For a good word was uttered by which they were made, a good word! This same Word or Verb was called good Teacher. To this the same Word or Verb responds: Why do you ask me about what is good? No one is good, but only God. He was called a good Teacher, and he says: Why do you ask me about what is good?; And he also added: No one is good, but only God. Therefore he is good, because he is God. And not only God, but with the Father he is one God. For when he said, "No one is good but God alone," he did not separate himself from God, but joined himself to Him. My heart broke out into a good word. This is what God the Father said about his good Word and our most useful good, for whose good alone we can be good in any way we are. 5. Continue: I declare my works to the king. Does the Father still speak? If the Father still speaks, let us investigate how we are to understand, according to the true and Catholic faith, I declare my works to the king. If the Father manifests his works to his Son, fecisti. Ergo si per Verbum omnia, et Verbum de Deo; inspice fabricata factam per Verbum, et ex isto aedificio mirare consilium. Quale Verbum est per quod factum est caelum et terra, et omnis ornatus caeli, omnis fecunditas terrae, diffusio maris, distentio aeris, fulgor siderum, claritas solis et lunae? Videntur haec: transcende et haec; cogita Angelos, Principatus, Sedes, Dominationes, Potestates: omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Unde ergo is bona facta sunt? Quia eructatum is per quod ieront, Verbum bonum. Ergo Verbum bonum: et ipsi Verbo dictum est, Magister bone.

Et ipsum Verbum respondedit, Why are you asking me questions? Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus (Mt 19,17, et Me 10,18). Dictum est, Magister bone; et dicit, Why are you asking me questions? Addidit etiam, Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus. Quomodo ergo et ipse bonus, nisi quia Deus? Non solum autem Deus, sed cum Patre unus Deus. Non enim saying, Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus, discrevit se, sed univit. Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum. Dixerit hoc Deus Pater de Verbo suo bono atque benéfico bono nostro, per quod solum bonum uteumque boni esse possumus. 5. Sequitur, Dico ego opera mea regi. Adhuc Pater loquitur? Si adhuc Pater loquitur, quaeramus et hoc quomodo secundum fidem veram et catholicam intelligamus, Dico ego opera mea regi. Si enim Pater dicit opera sua Filio suo regi nostro; quae opera Pater dicturus est Filio,

our king, what works must the Father manifest to the Son, since all the works of the Father are done through the Son? Or perhaps, in the words I say my works to the king, the word I say means the generation of the Son? We fear this cannot be understood by the short-witted. However, I will say it. Let him who can follow it, lest it happen that because he is silent about it, he who can understand it ignores it. We read in another psalm: God once spoke. Many times he spoke through the prophets, many times through the apostles, and today he speaks through his saints, and yet he says: God once spoke. How did he speak only once if it were not because he uttered a single word? Since in the phrase my heart broke out a good word we understood that the generation of the Son was declared, it seems to me as if this were repeated in the following verse; so that what he said: My heart broke out a good word, is repeated in what he adds next: I say. What does I say mean? I speak the Word. And where does God utter the word from, if it is not from his heart, from his interior? You, being a man, only say what your heart says; Your word, which sounds and disappears, does not come from anywhere else, and do you wonder that God speaks like this? But God's saying is eternal. You speak something now, before you were silent. Let us grant that you do not yet speak; But, when you begin to utter words, you break, in a certain way, the silence and generate the word that previously did not exist. God does not generate the Word or Verb in this way. His saying has no beginning or end, and yet he says one Word. Say another Word if the one you said has passed. But when He remains by whom it is said, and also what is said and concum omnia opera Patris per Filium facta sint? An forte, Dico ego opera mea regi, ipsum Dico, generationem Filii significat? Vereor ne hoc aliquando a tardioribus non possit intelligi: verumtamen dicam, sequatur qui potest, ne non dicto non sequatur et qui potest. Legimus in alio psalmo dictum: Sernel locutus est Deus (Ps 61,12). Toties locutus est per l'rophetas, toties per Apostólos, hodieque loquitur per sanctos suos, et ait: Semel locutus est Deus. Unde semel locutus est, nisi propter Verbum unum?

Sicut autem Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum, intelleximus ibi generationem Filii; veluti repetitio mihi videtur facta in consequenti sententia, ut illud quod dictum erat, Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum, repeteretur in eo quod ait, Dico. What is enim, Dico? Verbum profero. Et unde profert Deus verbum, nisi ex corde suo, ex intimo suo? Tu non dicis nisi quod ex corde tuo profers; verbum tuum quod sonat et transit itliunde non profertur: et mirais quia ita dicit Deus? Sed dicere Dei ueternum est. You say aliquid moda, quia tacebas paulo ante: vel ecce nunc nondum verbum profers; cum autem proferre coeperis, rumpis silcntium quodammodo, et generas verbum quod antea non etat. Non sic Deus genuit Vetbum: dicere Dei sine initio est, et sine fine; et tamen unum Verbum dicit. Dicat alterum, si quod dixit transierit. Cum vero et a quo dicitur manet, et quod dicitur manet; et semel dicitur et non íuitur; et ipsum semel sine initio dicitur, nec bis dicitur, quia non transit
^.narratives about the Psalms

It is continually said and does not cease to be said, also He Himself is continually said without beginning, and is not said twice, because what is continually being said does not happen. Then it is the same My heart broke out a good word, that I tell my works to the king. Why was it said I say my works? Because in the same Word all the works of God are found. Everything that God had to do in creation was already in the Word; Furthermore, creation would not exist unless it were in the Word; just as, if the project of the building were not in you, the building would not exist either. In the Gospel it is said: What was made had life in Him. Then there was what was made; but it existed in the Word. All the works of God were there although the works did not yet exist; but the Word existed, and this Word was God, and was in God, and was the Son of God, and with the Father was one God. I tell my works to the king. He who understands the Word may hear what He speaks and see, together with the Father, the eternal Word, in whom future things are also found and from Him past things have not departed. These works of God are in the Word as being the Word, as being the Only Begotten, as being the Word of God. 6. What's next? My tongue (is) a writer's pen, a fast writer. In what way is the tongue of God similar to the pen of a scribe? What similarity does the stone have to Christ? How is a lamb like the Savior? What is similar to the lion with the strength of the Only Begotten? And yet all this was said; and, if it had not been said, we would in no way have known the invisible things, since they are made known through these visible things. Therefore, no quod semel dicitur. Hoc est ergo, Eructavit cor meum -verbum bonum, quod est, Dico ego opera mea regi. Quare ergo, Opera mea Meo? Quia in ipso Verbo omnia opera Dei. Quidquid enim facturus erat Deus in creatura, iam in Verb erat; nec esset in rebus, nisi esset in Verb: quomodo et in te non esset in fabrica, nisi esset in consilio. Sicut in Gospel dicitur: Quod factum est in ipso vita erat (lo 1,3.4). Erat ergo quod factum est, sed in Verbo erat: et omnia opera Dei ibi erat, et opera nondum erat: sed Verbum erat, et Verbum hoc Deus erat, et apud Deum erat, et Filius Dei erat, et cum Patre unus Deus erat. Dico ego operates mea regi. Audiat dicentem, qui Verbum intelligit; et videat cum Patre sempiternum Verbum, in quo sunt etiam quaefutura sunt, in quo non abierunt et quae transierunt.

Haec operates Dei in Verbo, tanquam in Verbo, tanquam in Only Begotten, tanquam in Dei Verbo. 6. Quid ergo sequitur? Lingua mea calamus scribae, velociter scribentis. Quid simile, fratres mei, quid habet simile lingua Dei cum calamo scribae? Quid habet simile petra cum Christo? (1 Cor 10:4); quid habet simile agnus cum Salvatore? (lo 1.29); quid habet leo cum Unigeniti fortitudine? (Rev 5,5). Dicta sunt haec tamen: et nisi dicerentur, non aliquo moda per haec visibilia ad invisibilem informaremur. Sic ergo humilem similarityinem calami huius, nec comparemus illi excellentíae,

let us equal the resemblance of this modest pen with that most excellent language, nor let us reject it completely. I ask: Why did he say that his tongue is the pen of a quick writer? No matter how quickly an amanuensis writes, it cannot be compared to the speed of which another psalm says: His word runs with the greatest speed. It seems to me, as far as human intelligence is capable of understanding, that what has been said can be taken: My tongue (is) a writer's pen for the Father. Because what the tongue says, sounds and passes; what is written, remains. When God says the Word or Verb, the Word or Verb that is said does not sound or pass away, but is continually said and remains. For this reason God preferred to compare it to writing rather than sound. What he added: as a quick writer, he drives the mind to understand. But do not remain dumbfounded contemplating the copyists or any fast scribes; If you stop at this, you remain there without knowing. Quickly think the same word quickly and see why it was said quickly. The speed of God is such that there is nothing faster. When writing, you write letter by letter, syllable by syllable, word by word, and you do not move on to the second without having written the first. There is nothing faster than when one speaks with so few words, that in one word they are all contained, and yet nothing is omitted. 7 [v.3]. Behold, that Word or Verb uttered in this way, eternal, coeternal from eternity, comes as a husband. Most beautiful upon the sons of men. And why not also about the angels? What did he mean by saying nec tamen respuamus. Quaero enim quate linguam suam calamum dixit esse scribae velociter setibentis? At veto quantumvis velociter scribat scriba, non comparatur illi velocitati, de qua dicit alius psalmus: Usqae in velocitatem currit verbum eius (Ps 147,15). Sed mihi videtut, quantum audet humano intelligentia, et hoc posse accipi ex petsona Patris dictum, Lingua mea calamus scribae. Quia quod lingua dicitut, sonat et transit; quod scribitur, manet: cum ergo dicat Deus Verbum, et Verbum quod dicitur non sonet et ttanseat, sed et dicatut et maneat; scriptis hoc maluit Deus compare, quam sonis. Quod autem addidit, velociter scribentis, impulit mentem ad intelligentiam: sed non pigta remaneat, respiciendo antique dealers, aut respiciendo qualeslibet veloces notarios; si autem hoc attenderit, temanebit ibi.

Ipsum velociter, cogitet velociter; et videat quare dictum sit, velociter. Velociter Dei tale est, ut velocius nihil sit. In Scripturis enim scribitur littera post litteram, syllaba post syllabam, verbum post verbum; nec ad secundum transitur, nisi primo perscripto. Ibi autem nihil velocius, ubi non tumba sunt verba, nec tamen aliquid praetermissum est, cum in uno sint omnia. 7 {v.3}. Ecce iam. Verbum illud sic prolatum, aeternum, ab aeterno coaeternum, veniet sponsus. Speciosus forma prae filiis hominum. Prae filiis hominum: quare non et ptae Angelis? Quid voluit dicete, Prae filiis hominum, nisi quia homo? Ne hominem Christum quemlibet ho

about the sons of men but was he a man? And so that you would not think that the man Christ was any man, he says: Most beautiful over the sons of men. Man over the sons of men, and also man among the sons of men, over the sons of men; and likewise the name of the sons of men over the sons of men. Grace is poured out on your lips. The law was given by Moses, grace and truth was established by Jesus Christ. Grace is poured out on your lips. No wonder he helped me, because I delight in the law of God, according to the inner man. But there is another law in my members that opposes the law of my mind and holds me captive in the law of sin that exists in my members: "O happy man, who will deliver me from this body of death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord." Then grace is poured out on your lips. He came to us with a word of grace, with a kiss of grace. What is sweeter than this grace? Where is this grace headed? "Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are blotted out." If he had come as a severe judge and had not been accompanied by this grace that is poured out on his lips, who would have even a little confidence in salvation? Who would not fear receiving what is due to the sinner? Coming with grace, He did not demand the debt, but paid what he did not owe. Did the sinner not owe death? Or was the torture not due to you, a sinner? He forgave your debts and paid what he didn't owe. Sublime grace! Why is it grace? Because it is given for free. That is why you are allowed to give thanks, but not to reward, because you cannot. Was He seeking what to repay who said: What will I return to the Lord for all minem putares, ait, Prae filiis hominum speciosus forma. Etiam homo prae filiis hominum; etiam Inter filios hominum, prae filiis hominum; etiam ex filiis hominum, prae filiis hominum. Diffusa est grada in labiis tuis. Lex per Moysen data est; Gratia et verítas per Iesum Christum facta est (lo 1,17). Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis. Merito mihi subventum est, quia condelector legi Dei secundum interiorem hominem.

Sed alia lex in membris meis repugnat legi mentís meae, et captivum me ducit in lege peccati, quae est in membris meis. Miser ego homo, can you free me from corpore mortis huius? Gratia Dei per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum (Rom 7,22,25). Diffusa est ergo gratia in labiis tuis. Venit nobis cum verb gratiae, cum kiss gratiae. Quid is this gratia dulcius? What pertinet gratia ist? Beati quorum remissae sunt iniquitates, et quorum tecta sunt peecata (Ps 31,1). Si severus iudex comeret, nec afferret istam gratiam diffusam in labiis suis, quis de salute aliquid speraret? Quis non sibi hoc timeret quod peccatori debenbatur? Ule veniens cum gratia, non exegit quod debenbatur, solvít quod non debenbat. N u m enim non peccator debenbat mortem? Aut vero tibí peccatori debenbatur, nisi supplicium? Debita tua dimisit, et indebita sua exsolvít. Magna gratia. Quare gratia? Quia free. Propterea tibi gratias agere licet, referre non licet; non enim potes. Quaerebat ille quid retribueret, et dixit: Quid retribuam Domino

the benefits it gave me?; and, as if finding something, he said: I will take the cup of health and call on the name of the Lord. Do you compensate him by taking the cup of health and invoking the name of the Lord? Who gave you the chalice of health? So he was left with thanksgiving because he lacked retribution. Find something that you give to God without having received it from Him, and then you will give it to Him freely. But be careful, lest, while you search for something to give Him that you have not received from Him, you find something: your sin. This, no doubt, you did not receive from Him, but neither should you give it to Him. This is what the Jews gave him, for they returned evils for goods. They received rain from Him, and they did not give Him fruits, but the thorns of suffering. Then all the good that you intend to give to God will only be found in you, but it will be from God. This is the grace of God poured out on your lips. She made you, and freely. There was no one to give before making you. You perished, and he searched for you; found, renewed you. He did not impute the past to you and promise you the future. Truly, grace is poured out on your lips. 8. For this, he says, God blessed you eternally. We still strive so that the following can still be understood as being said by God the Father: For this God blessed you eternally. It seems that this should be taken, more conveniently, as spoken by the prophet. In the holy books of Scripture one finds sudden, completely unforeseen changes in people. If anyone pays attention, they will notice that the divine pages are full of them. For example, in Psalm 119 it says: Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips and deceitful tongues; and then pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi? And invenit quasi aliquid: Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invokebo (Ps 115,12.13). Hoc illi rependis, quia calicem salutaris accipis, et nomen Domini invokes? Quis tibi dedit ipsum calicem salutarem? Remansit in actione gratiarum, nam in relatione defect. Inveni quid Deo des, quod ab illo non acceperis; et retuleris gratiam. Sed cave ne dum quaeris quid illi retribuas, quod ab illo non acceperis, invenías, sed peccatum tuum. Hoc plane ab illo non accepisti, sed nec ei daré deben. Hoc dederunt Iudaei, retribuerunt mala pro bonis; acceperunt ab eo pluviam, et fructum non dederunt, sed spinas dolorum.

Ergo bonum quidquid volueris in te daré Deo, non te invenís accepisse nisi a Deo. Ipsa est gratia Dei diffusa in labiis. Fecit you, free fecit you. Non enim erat cui praestaret antequam faceret. Perieras, quaesivit te; et inventum revocavit te. Praeterita non imputavit, future promisit. I will see diffusa en gratia. in your lips. 8. Propterea, inquit, benedixit te Deus in aeternum. Sedes eius in saecula saeculorum. Quare? Quia headquarters illa prima regni temporalis Fuit. Unde nunc headquarters in saecula saeculorum? Quia Dei. Sedes tua, Deus, in saecula saeculorum. O aeternitatis divinitas! Non enim posset Deus sedem habere temporalem. Your headquarters. Deus, in saecula saeculorum. Virga directionis, virga regni tui. Directionis virga est, quae dirigit homines. Curvi werent, distorted weret: sibi regnare cupiebant, se amarant, facta sua mala diligebant; non voluntatem suam Deo subdebant, sed voluntatem Dei ad suas concupiscentias flectere volebant.

Irascitur enim peccator et iniquus plerumque Deo, quia non pluit; et non vult sibi Deum irasci, quia fluit. Et ad hoc propemodum sedent quotidie homines, ut disputent contra Deum: Hoc faceré debuit hoc non bene fecit. Tu videlicet vides quid facias, ille nescit? Distortus tu es ¡lie rectus est. Does He ignore it? You are crooked, He is straight. When will you couple the crooked with the straight? One cannot be aligned with the other. If you place a crooked piece of wood on a level pavement, it does not fit, it does not adhere, it does not adapt to the pavement. The pavement throughout its entire length is level; but the wood is crooked, it does not fit the level ground. God's will is straight, yours is crooked; That of God seems crooked to you because you cannot adjust to Him. Channel yourself in it and do not try to twist it towards yourself. You will try in vain, because you will not be able to. She is always straight. Do you want to join her? Correct yourself. The rod of equity will be the rod of the one who rules or governs you. Hence the word king is derived from rule, and he who does not correct does not rule. That is why our king is king of those who rule or govern. As the priest is constituted to sanctify us, so the king is constituted to govern us. But what does it say elsewhere? With the saint you will be holy, and with the innocent man, innocent; with the chosen one you will be chosen and with the perverse you will be perverse. But not because God is perverse, but because the perverts consider Him perverse. You like good, God is good; You dislike Him, you consider Him evil. For you God is crooked; Your crookedness makes you see him like this, because his straightness always remains. Hear what is said in another psalm: How good is the God of Israel to the upright in heart! 18 [v.8.}. Scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. You loved justice and hated iniquity. Here is the scepter of righteousness: You loved justice and hated iniquity. Come to this scepter, be your king Christ; rule you with this scepter so that it does not break you. For it is a scepter of inflexible ice. What was said in another psalm? potest. Tanquam si in pavement aequali put lignum curvum; non idiungitur, non cohaeret, non coaptatur pavement: pavimentum ubique aequale est; sed illud curvum est, non coaptatur aequali. Ergo Dei voluntas aequalis est, tua curva est: propterea tibí curva videtut illa, quia tu illi coaptari non potes: direct ad illam te, ne illam velis curvare ad te; quia non potes, frustra conaris: illa semper direct est. Vis illi haerete? C.orrigere. Erit virga ipsius qui te regit, virga directionis. Inde et rex a rcgendo dicitur. Non autem regit qui non corrigit. Ad hoc est rex noster rrctorum rex. Quomodo et sacerdos a sanctificando nos, ita et rex a regendo nos. Sed quid ait alio loco?

You will rule them with a rod of iron and you will pulverize them like a potter's vessel. He rules some, he destroys others; It rules the spiritual, it pulverizes the carnal. Then approach this rod. What do you fear about her? She is an integral rod: You loved justice and hated iniquity. What do you fear? Perhaps you are wicked, and therefore, hearing that your king hates iniquity, you fear. You have a remedy. What do you hate? The iniquity? Does he hate you? Is there iniquity in you? God hates her; Hate her too so that you both hate the same thing. You will be a friend of God if you hate what he hates, and so you will also love what he loves. May your iniquity displease you in yourself and please your creature. You are wicked man. I pronounced two names; Both names are man and wicked. One of these names belongs to nature, the other to guilt; God made one, the other you. Love the one God made, hate the one you made, because He hates him too. See how you already begin to unite with Him when you hate what He hates. Sin must be punished, because the rod of equity is the rod of his kingdom. Well, let it not punish sin. He cannot help but punish him. Sin must be punished. If it were not to be punished, it would not be a sin. Prevent yourself from him. Don't you want him to punish you? You punish him. That is why He now forgives, defers, stays His hand, tightens the bow, that is, threatens. Would you shout so much, saying that you have to hurt, if you wanted to hurt? If He stays His hand in the face of your sins, don't stop it. Begin to punish your sins, because they cannot go unpunished. They must be avenged either by you or by Him. You recognize them so that He forgives you. See the model in that psalm of penance: Turn your face from my sins. (Ps 2,9). Alios regit, alios conterit: regit spirituales, conterit carnals. Ergo agrees ad istam virgam. Quid in ea times? Haec est tota virga: Dilexisti iustitiam, et odisti iniquitatem. What times? Be strong iniquus eras: audis enim regem tuum, quia odit iniquitatem, et times. Est quod facias. What did you hate? Iniquitatem: numquid te? Are you iniquitous? Odit illam Deus, oderis et tu: ut unam rem ambo oderitis. Eris enim Deo amicus, si odisti quod odit. Ita et amabis quod amat. Displiceat in teipso tibi iniquitas tua, et placeat tibi creatura ipsius. Homo enim is iniquus.

Duo dixi nomina; duo nomina, homo et iniquus: in istis duobus nominibus unum est naturae, alterum culpae; unum tibi Deus fecit, alterum tu fecisti: ama quod Deus fecit, oderis quod tu fecisti, quia et ipse hoc odit. Vide quomodo iam illi incipias coniungi, cum odisti quod odit. Peccatum puniturus est, quia virga directionis est virga regni ipsius. Sed non puniat peccatum? Be non-potent. Puniendum est peccatum: si puniendum non esset, nec peccatum esset. Praeveni illum: non vis ut ipse puniat, tu puni. Ideo enim adhuc ipse parcit, differt, tenet manum, arcum intendit, hoc est mines. Clamaret tantum feriturum se, si vellet ferire? Differt ergo manum a peccatis tuis: tu noli differre. Converte ad punienda peccata tua, quia impunita esse peccata non possunt. Puniendum ergo erit, aut a te, aut ab ipso: tu agnosce, ut ille ignoscat. Attend exemplum in illo psalmo poenitentiae: Averte faciem tuam a

Did he say "from me"? In another place it clearly says: Do not turn your face from me. Then turn your face away from my sins. That is, don't focus on my sins. To notice God is to repair or deliberate. That is why it is also said that, when he punishes, the judge repairs or deliberates, that is, he considers carefully, and punishes, because he is a judge. God is also judge. Turn your face from my sins. You don't separate him from them if you want God to separate him. Notice how he promises this to God in another psalm: I acknowledge my crime, and my sin is always before my eyes. He does not want to be before God what he wants to be before himself. The rod of equity is the rod of his kingdom. Let no one flatter himself too much about the mercy of God, for it is the rod of righteousness. But are we saying that God is not merciful? Who is more merciful than He, who truly forgives sinners, who does not concern himself with the past sins of all men who have converted to Him? Love him in such a merciful way that you want him to be truthful at the same time. Mercy cannot be stripped of justice, nor justice of mercy. Meanwhile, while He waits, do not differ, for the rod of righteousness is the rod of His kingdom. 19. You loved justice and hated iniquity; That is why he anointed you, O God, your God. He anointed you so that you would love justice and hate iniquity. Understand how he says: Propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus: Therefore he anointed you, O God, your God. Oh, you are not God! Your God anointed you. God is anointed by God. In Latin it seems that the first word, Deus, will be in peccatis meis (Ps 50,11). Numquid dixit, To me? Alio enim loco aperte dicit: Ne avertas faciem tuam a me (Ps 26,9). Ergo, Averte faciem tuam. a peccatis meis: nolo videos peccata mea. Quia videre Dei, animadvertere est. Ideo et iudex quod punit, animadvertere dicitur, id est, animum illuc advertere; intendere utique ad puniendum, quia iudex est. Sic est et index Deus. Averte faciem tuam a peccatis meis. Tu ab ipsis faciem noli avertere, si vis ut Deus ab ipsis avertat faciem suam. Vide quomodo hoc offert Deo in ipso psalmo: Vacinus meum ego, inquit, agnosco, et peccatum meum ante me est semper (Ps 50,5). Hoc non vult esse ante Deum, quod vult esse ante se. Virga directionis, virga regni tui.

Nemo sibi inultum of mercy Dei blandiatur; virga directionis est. Numquid ilidmus, non esse misericordem Deum? Quid misericordius eo, qui parcit tantum peccatoribus, eo qui in omnibus conversis ad se non curat praeterila? Sic eum dílige misericordem, ut velis esse veracem: non enim misericordia potest illi auferre iustitiam, ñeque iustitia misericordem. Interim quamiliu ille differt, tu noli differre: quoniam virga directionis, virga regni ipsius. 19. Dilexisti iustitiam, et odisti iniquitatem: propterea unxit te, Deus, Deus tuus. Propterea unxit te, ut diligeres iustitiam, et odires iniquitatem. YO! t vide quomodo ait: Propterea unxit te, Deus, Deus tuus. O tu Deus, unxit te Deus tuus. Deus anointed Deo. the same case as the second, Deus tuus; But in Greek the distinction of the case is clear, one is the name of the one who is named and another is the name of the one who names. God anointed you, that is: O you who are God, your God anointed you. This is as if he said: Theungio, because you are God, your God. Take it this way, understand it this way, since this is how it is written very clearly in Greek. Then who is the God-anointed by God? Let the Jews tell us. We have the same Scripture with them. God is anointed by God. You hear that one is anointed, understand that it is Christ. The word Christ is derived from chrism; Therefore, the name Christ means anointing. In no other kingdom in the world were kings and priests anointed except that in which Christ was prophesied and anointed, from which the name Christ came. Never in any other place, in any nation, in any kingdom, did such a custom exist. Then God was anointedby God. With what oil but with spiritual oil? The visible oil is given as a sign; the invisible oil, as a sacrament; the spiritual oil is given internally. God was anointed for us and sent to us. God himself, by the anointing, was man; but he was such a man that he was also God. And God was such that he did not disdain being a man; true man and true God; in nothing lying, in nothing fallacious, because in everything it is truthful, in everything it is the truth. Therefore God is man, and therefore God is anointed because he is manGod, who is Christ. 20. This was prefigured in the fact that Jacob had put a stone as a bolster to sleep on. The patriarch Jacob placed a stone under his head; While asleep, with his head resting on the stone, he saw, with the heavens open, quia unum nomen est quod compellatur, et alterum ab eo qui compellat, Unxit te, Deus. O tu Deas, unxit te Deus tuus: quomodo si diceret, Propterea unxit te, o tu Deus, Deus tuus. Sic accipite, sic intelligite, sic in graeco evidentissimum est. Ergo quis est Deus unctus a Deo? Dicant nobis Iudaei. Scripturae istae communes sunt. Unctus est Deus a Deo: unctum audis, Christum intellige.

Etenim Christus a chrismate: hoc nomen quod appellatur Christus, unctionis est. Nec in aliquo alibi ungebantur reges et priests, nisi in illo regno ubi Christus prophetabatur et ungebatur, et unde venturum erat Christi nomen: nusquam est alibi omnino, in nulla gente, in nullo regno. Unctus est ergo Deus a Deo: quo oleo, nisi spirituali? Oleum enim visible in sign est, oleum invisibile in sacramento est, oleum spirituale intus est. Unctus est nobis Deus, et missus est nobis: et ipse Deus, ut ungeretur, homo erat: sed ita homo erat, ut Deus esset; ita Deus erat, ut homo esse non dedignaretur: verus homo, verus Deus; in nullo fallax, in nullo falsus; quia ubique verax, ubique veritas. Deus ergo homo, et ideo unctus Deus, quia homo Deus, et factus est Christus. 20. Hoc figurabatur in eo quod lacob lapidem sibi ad caput posuerat, et dormierat (Gen 28,11). lacob patriarcha lapidem sibi ad caput posuerat; dormiens autem illo lapide ad caput pósito, vidit apertis caelis scalam

a ladder that reached from heaven to earth on which the angels ascended and descended. When he awoke from the dream, he anointed the stone and left. He understood that Christ was represented on that stone; That's why he anointed her. See since when Christ was announced. What does the anointing of the stone mean, especially before the patriarchs, who worshiped only God? This event was a figurative event and it happened. Well, he anointed the stone, and he did not return there to worship or offer sacrifices. A mystery was represented, not a sacrilege. Look at the stone: The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. And since Christ is the head of the man, the stone was placed at the head. Observe the great mystery: Christ is the stone. The living stone - says Saint Peter - rejected by men is chosen by God. The stone was placed at the head because the head of the man is Christ, and the stone was anointed because the name of Christ is derived from chrism, anointing. And Christ will be seen, making himself known, ladders reaching from heaven to earth or from earth to heaven, on which angels ascend and descend. What does this mean? We will understand it better by remembering the evangelical testimony, uttered by the Lord himself. You know that Jacob is Israel himself. Well, when he fought with the angel and emerged victorious and was blessed by the one who conquered, his name was changed, so that from then on he was called Israel. The people of Israel prevailed against Christ by crucifying him; However, those who believed in Christ were blessed by Him Who conquered. But many did not believe; hence Jacob's lameness. We have, therefore, two things: blessing and lameness. Blessing on those who believed, because later to cáelo in terram, et Angelos ascending et descendants: hoc viso evigilavit, unxit lapidem, et discessit. In illo lapide intellexit Christum, ideo unxit. Videte ex quo praedicatur Christus. Quid sibi vult illa unctio lapidis, praesertim apud Patriarchas, qui unum Deum colebant? Factum est autem in figura, et discessum est. Non enim unxit lapidem, et venit illuc semper adorare, et sacrificia ibi faceré. Expressum est mysterium, non inchoatum sacrilegium. Et videte lapidem: Lapidem quem reprobaverunt aedificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli (Ps 117,22).

Et quia caput viri Christus (1 Cor 11:3), propterea lapis ad caput. Attendite magnum sacramentum: lapis Christus. Lapidem vivum, ait Petrus, ab hominibus reprobatum, a Deo autem electum (1 Petr 2:4). Et lapis ad caput, quia caput viri Christus (1 Cor 6:3). Et unctus lapis quia a chrismate dictus est Christus. Et videntur scalae, revealing Christ, a terra in caelum, vel a cáelo in terram, et ascendants et descendants Angelí (Gen 28,12, et lo 1,51). Quid hoc sit, melius videbimus, cum testimonium evangelicum ab ipso Domino commemoraverimus. Nostis quia lacob ipse est Israel. lili enim cum Angelo luctanti et praevalenti, et benedicto ab eo cui ptaevaluit, nomen mutatum est, ut appellaretur Israel (Gen 32,28): sicut populus Istael praevaluit Christo, ut crucifigeret eum; et lamen in his qui Christo crediderunt, ab ipso cui ptaevaluit, benedictus est. Sed multi non crediderunt, inde claudicatio lacob. Benedictio et claudicatio.

We saw that many of that people believed. Lameness in those who did not believe. And since the majority did not believe and the few did, therefore, to make him lame, he wounded the tendon of his thigh. What does the tendon in your thigh symbolize? The multitude of his lineage. See the scales. When the Lord saw Nathanael, he says in the Gospel: Behold a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. The same is said of Jacob: And Jacob was a simple man, without guile, living in tents. Remembering this the Lord, seeing Nathanael, a man of that nation and that people, without deceit: See here, he says, a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. He called him an Israelite in whom there was no deceit, thinking of Jacob. Nathanael answers: How do you know me? The Lord answers him: When you were under the fig tree I saw you. That is, when you were in that town established under the law, which, like a carnal shadow, covered that people, I saw you. What does it mean I saw you there? There I felt sorry for you. Nathanael, having remembered that he had really been under the fig tree, amazed, because he thought that no one had seen him when he was there, confesses and says: You are the Son of God, you are the king of Israel. Who said this? The one who had heard that he was a true Israelite and that there was no fraud in him. Then the Lord answers him: Because I told you: I saw you under the fig tree, you believed; greater things you will see. Speaking to this one when saying greater things you will see, speak with Israel, with Jacob; that is, with the one who placed the stone under the head. What bigger things (will you see)? Pay attention, since the stone is already placed at the head. He continues: Truly I tell you that you will see heaven open, and the angels of God descend and Benedictio in his qui crediderunt: nam postea novimus ex illo populo multos credidisse. Claudicado autem in his qui non crediderunt. Et quia plures non crediderunt, et pauci crediderunt, ideo ut ieront claudicatio, tetigit latitudinem femoris eius. What is latitudo femoris eius? Many genephis. Videte ergo scalas illas. Dominus quando vidit Nathanaelem in Evangelio ait: Ecce veré Israelita, in quo dolus non est (lo 1,47). Sic enim dicitur de ipso Iacob, Et erat lacob sine dolo habitans in domo (Gen 25,27): hoc recolens Dominus vídens Nathanaelem sine dolo de gente illa et de populo illo, Ecce veré, inquit, Israelita, in quo dolus non est. Appellavit Israelitam, in quo dolus non esset, propter Iacob. Et ille Nathanael, Unde me nosti?

Et Dominus, Cum esses sub arbore fici vidi te: id est, cum esses in illo populo sub Lege constitutus, quae carnali umbra illum populum protegebat, ibi te vidi. What is it, did I see you? Ibi tui misertus sum. Ule autem rememberatus quod fuet etiam sub arbore fici in veritate, admiratus, quia putabat se a nemine visum cum ibi esset, confitetur et dicit: Tu es Filias Dei, tu es rex Israel. Quis hoc dixit? Qui audierat quod verus esset Israelita, et dolus in illo non esset. Et Dominus: Quia dixi tibi, Vidi te sub arbore fici, credidisti; maiora horum videbis. Loquitur cum Israel, cum Iacob, cum illo qui sibi lapidem ad caput posuerat. Maiora h'trum videbis. Quae maiora? Quia iam lapis ille ad caput est. Amen dico vobis, videbitis caelum apertum, et Angelas Dei

ascend upon the Son of man. The angels of God go up and down this ladder. Let this be done in the Church. The angels of God are the preachers of the truth; Go up and hear: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. Come down and observe that the Word became flesh and lived among us. Go up to exalt the great ones, come down to feed the little ones. See Paul, who goes up when he says: If we have been caught up to God... See him going down when he writes: If we have moderated ourselves, it was for you. Look at him going up. We speak wisdom among the perfect. Look at him going down. I gave you milk to drink, not delicacy. This is executed in the Church; The angels of God descend and ascend above the Son of man because above is the Son of man, that is, his head, whom they ascend with their heart; and below is also the Son of man, that is, his body. Its members are here; his head, up. It goes up to the head, it goes down to the limbs. Christ is there, Christ is here. If he is only there and not here, why did he say: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? Who bothered you in heaven? Nobody; neither the Jews, nor Saul, nor the tempting devil. No one bothered him there, but his tongue cries out at the interlocking of the human body when his foot is stepped on. 21. You loved justice and hated iniquity; That is why he anointed you, O God, your God. We have spoken of the anointed God, that is, of Christ. The name of Christ could not have been made more clearly known than by saying: God anointed. Just as you are most beautiful over the sons of men, so you are anointed with the oil of joy over your partners. Who are their co-ascendants and descendants super Filium hominis (lo 1,48.51). Angeli Dei ascendant et descendant per scalas illas, fiat hoc in Ecclesia. Angeli Dei annuntiatores sunr veritatis: ascendant et videant, ln principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Descendant, et videant, quia Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (Ib. 1,14). Ascendant, ut erigant magnos: descendant, ut nutriant parvos. Vide ascendem Paulum: Sive mente excessimus, Deo. Vide descendentem: Sive temperantes sumus, vobis (2 Cor 5:13). Vide ascendem: Sapientiam loquimur interperfects. Vide descendentem: hac vobis potum dedi, non escam (1 Cor 2,6, et 3,2).

Hoc fit in Ecclesia: ascendant et descendunt Angeü Dei super Filium hominis: quia sursum est Filius hominis, ad quem ascendunt corde, id est caput eius; et deorsum Filius hominis, id est corpus eius. Membra eius hic sunt, caput sursum est: ascenditur ad caput, descenditur ad membra. Christus ibi, Christus hic. Nam si ibi tantum, er hic non, unde vox illa: Saule, Saule, why are you after me? (Acts 9,4). Quis enim illi in cáelo molestus Fuit? Nenio, nec Iudaei, nec Saulus, nec diabolus tentator; nemo ibi molestus illi: sed sicut in compage corporis humani pede calcato lingua clamat. 21. Dilexisti iustitiam, et odisti iniquitatem: propterea unxit te, Deus, Deus tuus. Locuti sumus de uncto Deo, hoc est de Christo. Non potuit apertius dici nomen Christi, quam ut diceretur unctus Deus. participants? The sons of men, because the Son of man himself became a participant in his nature to make them a participant in his immortality. 22 [v.9.10]. Myrrh, amber and cinnamon exhale your dresses. Good smells come from your clothes. His clothes are his saints, his chosen ones, his entire Church, which he presents as a garment without spot or wrinkle. Because of stain or sin, he was washed with blood; because of the wrinkles it was spread on the cross. Hence the good smell, which is symbolized in the names of the named aromas. He hears Paul, the youngest, talk about the hem of the garment (of Christ, who are Christians), and that the woman who had the issue of blood touched it and was healed; Hear him say: We are the good odor of Christ in every place, both for those who are saved and for those who are lost. He did not say: We are the good smell for those who are saved, and the bad smell for those who are lost, but, as for us, we are the good smell for both those who are saved and for those who are lost. Saving your man by good smell is natural and credible. But what is the cause of perishing from good smell? She is very powerful; It is a great truth, and if it cannot be understood, yet so it is. So that you would know how difficult it can be to understand, he adds below: And for this, who is suitable? Who can understand that men die for good smell? However, brothers, I will say something so that you can understand. See that Paul himself preached the Gospel; Many loved the preacher of the Gospel, many had ill will towards him; who loved him

They were saved by the good smell, those who envied him perished by the good smell. It was not, therefore, a bad smell for those who perished, but a good one. They envied him all the more angrily the more he stood out with such extraordinary power; no one envies the miserable. He was illustrious in preaching the Gospel and lived by the standard of the rod of equity. He was loved, then, by those who loved Christ in him, who went after the good smell. The husband's friend loved the wife who says in the Song of Songs: We run after the smell of your ointments. The wicked, on the contrary, the more they saw him honored in the preaching of the Gospel, the more they writhed with envy and killed themselves for the good smell. 23. Myrrh, amber and cinnamon ooze your clothes from the ivory palaces from which the daughters of kings delighted you. Choose any ivory houses, great palaces, royal dwellings: from them the daughters of kings delighted Christ. Do you want to understand ivory houses in a spiritual sense? We have heard this psalm sung; We have responded to him by singing; Let us expose the things you know. Perhaps we must also offer you, with the Lord's help and granting it, some attraction by reminding you, so that you ruminate or meditate, the things that you know from other different places. For also ipsa ruminatione, in the same rumination, in which God represents the animal worlds, he wanted to insinuate that every man must so deliver to his heart what he hears, that he is not negligent in reflecting on it afterwards. So that, when he hears, he is like one who eats, and when he brings back to memory the things he has heard and reflects with pleasant meditation, he is like one who ruminates. The same things are said in different ways; and, for the same reason, they make us think with pleasure about the things we know and hear them with pleasure, since, by changing the form of expression, the old matter is renewed by the way of speaking. 2 [v.l]. that, when crucifying Christ in the place of the Skull and lifting Him up on the cross, they themselves said with a childish sense, without understanding what they were saying: Come up, bald man. Well, what does up mean? Crucify, crucify! It is proposed to childhood to imitate humility, and also to escape from fatuity. The Lord proposed childhood as a model to imitate humility when, calling the children to Himself, He said to those who prevented them from approaching Him: Let the children come to me, because theirs is the kingdom of heaven. The Apostle, to guard against fatuity, proposed childhood as a model when he said: Brothers, do not be children in feeling; and he proposed it to be imitated when he wrote: Be children in malice so that you may be perfidious in your minds. The psalm is sung in favor of the children of Korah, then it is sung in favor of the Christians. Let us listen as children of the Bridegroom, whom the foolish youths crucified on Calvary. They deserved to be devoured by beasts; us, to be crowned by angels. We recognize the humility of our Lord and are not ashamed of it. We are not ashamed of Him, he called adomistically bald for having died on Calvary. Because of the same cross on which He was mocked, He does not tolerate our forehead being bald, because He pointed it out with His cross. Finally, so that you know that these things are said to us, pay attention to what follows. 3 [v. 2]. All nations, clap your hands. Did the Jewish people constitute all the nations? The Lord, to the sound of the trumpet. He went up, where? To where we know. Where the Jews did not follow him even with their eyes. Lifted up on the cross, they mocked him; ascending to heaven, they did not see him. God ascended amidst acclamations. What does acclamation mean? Admiration of joy that cannot be explained in words. When the disciples saw the dead man they mourned ascend to heaven, they marveled full of joy; No doubt this joy lacked words, but the joy remained, which no one could explain. Here there was no lack of the sound of the trumpet, the voice of the angels. For it was said: Like a trumpet, lift up your voice. The angels announced the ascension of the Lord; When the Lord ascended, they saw the disciples ecstatic, amazed, astonished, speechless, but inwardly jubilant. Then the disciples heard the sound of the

trumpet, manifested in the clear voice of the angels, who said: Men of Galilee, what are you doing here? This is Jesus. As if they didn't know it was Jesus! Hadn't they seen him in front of them shortly before? Hadn't they heard him talking to them? Then they not only saw his face, but also touched his limbs. So, did they not know that it was Jesus? By the same stupor due to the joy of rejoicing, being as if alienated, the angels say: He is Jesus. This is as if they were saying to them: If you believe in Him; He is the one who, because he was crucified, made your feet waver; He is the one who, because he died and was buried, made you lose hope; see that He is Jesus. He ascends before you, but he will come in the way you see him go to heaven. His body moves away from your eyes, but God does not move away from your hearts. See him rise; believe in Him who is absent, but wait for Him, for He will come; but by a hidden act of piety, perceive him still present. For he who ascended into heaven from your sight promised you, saying: I will be with you until the end of the ages. The Apostle rightly told us: The Lord is near; Don't worry about anything. Christ has his abode in heaven; Heaven is far away, but he who dwells in heaven is near. The Lord, to the sound of the trumpet. 1 [v.l]. The title of the psalm reads: Canticle of praise to the sons of Korah, at the second fair. Whatever the Lord deigns to make known to us about this, receive it as children of the firmament. On the second day of Saturday, which is also called the second fair, that is, on the day following the first day of the week, which we call Sunday, the firmament of heaven was made, that is, the firmament or heaven. For God called the firmament heaven. On the first day God made light, and separated it from darkness; and he called the light day, and the darkness night. As the texture of this psalm demonstrates, God predicted in that work of his something that was to be fulfilled in us; and according to the creation of this creature the centuries slipped by. Not in vain did the Lord say of Moses: He wrote about me. Thus, all things written about the creation of the world can be interpreted as symbolizing something future; By this you can understand that God made light when Christ rose from the dead. Without a doubt, light was separated from darkness when immortality began to be distinguished from mortality. From here, what is deduced? That also took place in the body, which is the Church, what took place in the Head. Finally, there is also a psalm about the first fair or Sunday in the

The learned investigated the meaning of the word "Tarshish," and discovered that it was the name of a city called that. Some believed that Cilicia was called Tarshish, because its metropolis was called Tarsus. The apostle Paul was a native of this city, since he was born in Tarsus of Cilicia. Others thought that it was Carthage, perhaps because it was called that in another time or because of another phrase or word that meant the same thing. Thus we see that the prophet Isaiah writes: Creak, ships of Carthage. The translators of Ezekiel, some write Carthage, others Tarshish. Therefore, taking into account these various interpretations, it can be understood that Tarsus was called what was called Carthage. It is evident that at the origins of the kingdom of Carthage there were an abundance of ships, and such was the profusion that among all nations it stood out in commerce and navigation. For when Dido, fleeing from her brother, arrived in the lands of Africa, where she founded Carthage, the ships she took to escape, with the consent of the primates of her country, were destined for trade in her nation. These ships, when the city of Carthage was founded, were not lacking in the exercise of trade. Every divine word is healthy for those who understand it well, and harmful for those who seek, according to the perversity of their heart, to twist it rather than correct their heart according to its uprightness. This is a custom of men of unparalleled perversity, since, having to live according to the will of God, they want God to live according to theirs. And, not wanting to correct themselves, they intend to make dii gentium daemonia depraved, Dominas autem cáelos fecit (Ps 95,5). Ipse est ergo Deus noster, hic est Deus noster. What? In aeternum et in saeculum saeculi; ipse reget us in saecula. Si Deus noster est, et rex noster est; protect us, quia Deus est, ne moriamur; regit nos, quia rex est, ne cadamus. God, thinking that what God wants is not right, but what they want. We often hear men murmuring against God that the bad live well in this life, while the good suffer; as if He were perverse and did not know what He was doing, or as if He had withdrawn His providence from human things, or as if He did not want to disturb their tranquility by attending to these things, since God would contemplate them with pain or correct them with work. Men who only want to worship God so that it may go well for them in this world, murmur when they see that those who do not worship God excel and enjoy earthly happiness, and those who worship Him find themselves involved in anguish, in needs, in afflictions and in the other setbacks of human mortality. Against this voice, against these blasphemies of the murmurers, the divine voice is always pronounced, healing from the bite of the serpent. This poison is typical of a poisoned heart that exhales the stench of blasphemy against God, and, what is worse, that repels the hand of the healer and does not reject the bite of the snake. I said that the heart of man turns away from itself the severity of the word of God and that it poorly accommodates the flattery of the inciting serpent. Against these the divine word is pronounced and in this psalm it warns us against them. I will direct your attention to this psalm, unless the same psalm directs it to all of us, not only to us, but to the entire globe of the earth. Hear how it begins. 2 [v.2}. Hear this all people. Murmurant ergo homines, qui propterea volunt Deum colere ut hic illis bene sit, quando viderint eos qui Deum non colunt pollere atque florere congratulate yourself terrena; se autem colentes Deum laborare in angustiis, in necessitatibus, in aerumna, caeterisque difficultatibus mortalitatis humanoe. for the apostles, and cried out in as many languages as those to which he sent preachers; and we see that this psalm, which was previously recited in a single nation, in the synagogue of the Jews, is recited throughout the world, by all the churches, and that what was said here was fulfilled: Hear this, all you nations. I have proposed that you attend to this alone, lest your spirit weaken due to physical discomfort fearing the length of this psalm. If I could, I will finish it today; If not, there will be something left for tomorrow; Pay attention at all times. You will only hear, God willing, what does not tire you, but encourages you. Hear this all people. You are also among these. Perceive it, all of you who inhabit the earth. It seems that he repeats the same thing again, as if what he said had been little: Listen. I say that by repeating hear, saying perceive it, it means: Do not hear it lightly. What does perceive it mean? What the Lord said: He who has ears to hear, let him hear. Since all those who were before him undoubtedly had ears, what ears was he looking for when he said: He who has ears to hear, let him hear, except those of the heart? The psalm also pulses or calls to these ears: Listen, all you inhabitants of the earth. Perhaps there is some difference in this. We should not restrict meaning; We do no harm by explaining this sentence. Perhaps there is a difference between saying all the people and saying all of you who inhabit the earth. Perhaps he wanted to give us something more to understand when he said those who inhabit. So that by nations we understand all the wicked, and by "inhabitants" we understand all the righteous of the world. He lives who is not held back; The detained person is forced to be, but does not live. Like what people? Clamavit enim per Apostólos Dominus noster Iesus Christus, clamavit tot linguis quas misit; et videmus hunc psalmum qui ante non recitabatur nisi in una gente, in synagoga ludaeorum, recitari per totum orbem terrarum, per omnes Ecclesias, impletumque esse quod hic dictum est, Audite haec omnes gentes. Ad hoc solum flew attempts faceré spirits vestros, ne propter laborem corporalem non erigatis animum, terrente vos longitudine psalmi huius. Si potuerit, finietur hodie: si non, restabit nobis aliquid in crastinum diem; Also you always tried this. Tantum enim audietis, si Dominus voluerit, quantum vos non gravet, sed relevet. Audite haec, omnes gentes: unde estis et vos. Auribus percipite, omnes qui habitatis orbem.

Hoc iterum videtur repetisse, quasi parum fuerit quod dixit, Audite. Quod dico, inquit, audite, auribus percipite, hoc est, nolite transeunter audire. Quid est, auribus perápite? Quod Dominus dicebat, Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat (Mt 11,25): cum omnes qui in conspectu cius erat, utique haberent aures; quas ille aures quaerebat nisi cordis, cum diceret, Qui habet aunes audiendi, audiat? Has this psalmus aures pulsat. Auribus percipite, omnes qui habitatis orbem. Forte et hic est aliqua distinctio. Non quidem nos coarctare deben, sed nihil malí est etiam istam explicare setitentiam. Forte aliquid distat inter id quod dixit, omnes gentes, et quod dixir, omnes qui habitatis orbem. Significantius enim fortasse voluit nos intelligere quod

He is the owner of his things, he owns everything he has, being a master if he is not entangled in the bonds of greed, thus, he who is held back by greed is a servant, not a possessor. We have in Scripture a certain consecrated word about habitation where it says: I chose to be a SERVANT in the house of the Lord rather than to DWELL in the tents of sinners. But if you are a servant in the house of the Lord, do you not dwell there? He did not want to take the word habitation in its proper sense here, but rather apply it to those who rule, possess, dominate and govern, since those who are held in low regard, like servants, do not properly inhabit, but are subjected. So in this sense he said: I want to be a servant in the house of God, rather than to reign in the tabernacles of sinners. Therefore, there is some distinction between all the people and all the inhabitants of the earth, as there is between hear and perceive, although this seems like repetition; However, it is different and, without a doubt, he wanted to indicate it, because these words were to be heard not only by sinners and impious people, but also by the righteous. Now they all hear intermingled, but when the time comes to render accounts, those who heard without interest will be separated from those who perceived. Then let sinners hear this: Hear these things, all ye nations. Let the righteous, who did not hear lightly and who govern the earth rather than are governed by it, hear this: Let all the inhabitants of the world hear it. 3 [v.3]. It also says: All those born of the earth and the sons of men. In the words born of the earth desigdixit, inhabitatis, ut gentes intelligamus omnes iniquos, habitatores autem orbis omnes, iustos. Ule enim habitat qui non tenetur: nam qui tenetur, habitatur, non habitat. Quomodo ille possidet quaecumque habet, qui dominus est rerum suarum; dominus autem est, qui non est irretitus cupiditate: qui autem cupiditate tenetur, possessus est, non possessor. Habemus enim quoddam verbum habitatione signatum in Scriptura Dei, ubi ait, I chose abiici in domo Domini, magis quam habitare in tabernaculis peccatorum (Ps 83,11). Quid enim, si abiiceris in domo Domini, non ibi habitas? Noluit significare habitationem, nisi in eis qui regunt, et tenent, et dominantur, et gubernant: qui autem contemnuntur, non quasi habitant, sed subiecti sunt. Ita autem dixit: Subditus flew esse in domo Dei, magis quam regnare in tabernaculis peccatorum.

Itaque si est aliqua distinctio inter omnes gentes, et habitatores orbis, sicut est distinctio inter audite, et auribus percipite, hoc quidem videtur repetisse; sed tamen aliud est, quod sane voluit significare; quia ista eloquia audituri werent non solum peccatores et impii, sed et iusti. Permixte modo audiunt omnes: sed cum ventum fuerit ad reddendam rationem, separabuntur qui sine causa audierunt, ab illis qui auribus perceperunt. Audiant ergo et peccatores: Audite haec, omnes gentes. Audiant et iusti, qui non sine causa audierunt, et regunt potius terram, quam reguntur a terra: Auribus percipite, omnes qui habitatis orbem. 3 [v.3]. Et iterum dicit: Quique terrigenae et jilii hominum. Quod ait, terrigenae, ad peccatores retulit; quod ait, filii hominum, ad fideles S.Ag.

No to the sinners, and in the subsection and the sons of men, to the believers and righteous. Then see how this distinction or division is observed. Who are those born from the earth? The children of the earth. Who are the children of the earth? Those who strive for the possessions of the earth. Who are the sons of men? Those who belong to the Son of man. On another occasion I have already presented this distinction to your holiness, and in it we saw that Adam was a man, but not the son of man. Christ was the son of man and was also God. All who belong to Adam are born of the earth and all who belong to Christ are sons of men. However, listen to everyone, I do not withhold my word from anyone. He is a man born of the earth, listen to the judgment; He is the son of man, hear for the kingdom. Let the rich and the poor listen together. Again he repeats, because rich refers to the one born of the earth, and poor, to the children of men. By rich he means the proud; for poor, the humble. The man who possesses much wealth, if he does not boast about it, is poor; He does not have any, but he desires them and is puffed up, God counts him among the rich reprobates. God investigates wealth or poverty in the heart of man, not in his ark or in his house. Are they not poor who receive the command of the Apostle, which he imposes on Timothy: Command the rich of this world not to be arrogant? How did he make those who were rich poor? Teaching them to seek wealth. Everyone who wants to be rich longs for it in order to become arrogant among those with whom he lives and appear superior to them. When he said: Teach them not to be arrogant, he equated them with those who are righteous. Videtis ergo, quia servatur ista distinctio. Qui sunt ergo terrigenae? Filii teirae. Who sunt filii terrae? Qui haereditates terrenas requirunt. Who sunt filii hominum? Qui pertinent ad filium hominis. Aliquando iam ista distinximus Sanctitati Vestrae, et invenimus quia Adam homo erat, filius hominis non erat; Christus autem filius hominis erat, et Deus erat. Quicumque enim pertinent ad Adam, terrigenae: quicumque pertinent ad Christum, filii hominum. Omnes tamm audiant, ego nulli subtraho sermonem meum. Tetrigena est, audiat propter iudicium; filius hominis est, auditat propter regnum. Simul in unttm dives et pauper. Iterum ipsa sunt repetita. Quod ait dives, ad terrigenas pertinet; quod ait, pauper, ad filios hominum. Divites intellige superbos, pauperes humiles.

Habeat fines facultates pecuniarum; si in eis non extollitur, pauper est: non habeat aliquid, et cupiat et infletur; inter divites et reprobos eum deputat Deus. Et divites et pauperes in corde interrogat Deus, non in arca et domo. Nonne pauperes sunt qui accipiunt mandamm Apostoli dicetis Timotheo: Praecipe divitibus huius saeculi non sujerhe sapere? How do those who divites weret fecit paupetes? Tulit illis quare quaeruntur divitiae. Nenio enim vult esse dives, nisi ut infletur Inter eos inter quos vivit, et superior illis videatur. Cum autem dixit, non supebe sapere, aequales eos fecit non habentibus; ut fortassis pauculis inimrnis mendicus plus extollatur, quam ille dives qui audit Apostolum dkeritem: Praecipe diviti-

they have nothing. In this way, perhaps the beggar becomes more proud with a handful of coins than the rich man who puts into practice what the Apostle says: Command the rich of this world not to be arrogant. How will you avoid arrogance? Fulfilling what follows: Do not put your hope in the fickleness of riches, but in the living God, who abundantly gives us all things to enjoy. He didn't say that he gives them, but that he gives us. Did Paul himself not have wealth? I had them. What riches? Those of which Scripture speaks elsewhere: The whole world is riches to a faithful man. He hears the Apostle himself say: Having nothing and possessing everything. Therefore whoever wants to be rich must not take only part, and then he will possess everything. Join Him who created all things. Together the rich and the poor, In another psalm it is said: The poor will eat, and will be satisfied. How did he recommend the poor? The poor will eat and be satisfied. What will they eat? What the faithful know. How will they be satisfied? Imitating the passion of the Lord and receiving its price in reward. The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek him will praise the Lord. And the rich, what will they do? They will also eat. How will they eat? All the kings of the earth ate and worshiped. The psalm did not say: They ate and were satisfied, but: They ate and worshiped. They certainly adore God, but they do not want to show fraternal delicacy. They eat these and worship, they eat those and are satisfied. As you see, everyone eats. What he eats is demanded of him who eats; Do not forbid him to eat the one who distributes, but warn him to fear the one who collects. Let the just and the pecatibus huius saeculi non superbe sapere hear these words. Unde non superbe sapere? Si faciant quod sequitur, Ñeque sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo, qui praestat nobis omnia abundantr ad fruendum (1 Tim 6,17). Non dixit, qui praestat illis; thirst, qui praestat nobis. Numquid ipse Paulus non habebat divitias? Habebat plane. What did you divide? De quibus dicit alio loco Scriptura: Fideli homini mundus totus divitiarum est (Prov 17:6, sec. 70). Audi et ipsum confitentem: Quasi nihil habentes, et omnia possidentes (2 Coi 6,10). Qui vult ergo esse dives, non haereat parti, et totum possidebit: illi inhaereat qui totum creavit. Simul in unum dives et pauper. Dicit in alio psalmo: Edent pauperes, et saturabuntur. How do you commendavit pauperes? Edent pauperes, et saturabuntur. Quid edunt? Quod sciunt fideles. How do I saturabuntut?

Imitando passionem Domini sui, et non sine causa accipiiendo pretium suum. Edent pauperes, et saturabuntur, et laudabunt Dominum, qui requirunt eum. Do you have fun? Etiam ipsi edunt. Sed quomodo edunt? Manducaverunt et adoraverunt omnes divites terrae (Ps 21,27.30). Non dixit, Manducaverunt, et saturad sunt; sed, Manducaverunt, et adoraverunt. Adorant quidem Deum, sed humanitatem nolunt exhíbete ftatetnam. Manducant illi, et adorant; manducant isti, et saturantur: tamen omnes manducant. Exigítur de manducante quod manducat; non prohibeatut manducare a dispensatore, sed moneatur timere exactrem. Audiant ergo ista peccatotes et iusti, gentes

dores, the people and those who inhabit the earth: Those born of the earth and the sons of men; together the rich and the poor join together: without dividing and separating. This will be done at harvest time; the beadletter will do it. Now together united let the rich and the poor hear; Let the goat and the lamb feed together until he comes who will separate some to the right and others to the left. Let it not happen that you hear the judge separately from one another. 4 [yA}. And what are they to hear now? My mouth speaks wisdom, and the thoughts of my heart, knowledge. These words seem more like a repetition so that perhaps you would not understand when my mouth said that the person speaking to you had wisdom only on his lips. Many have it on their lips and not in their hearts. Of these the Scripture says: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. What, then, does He who speaks to you say? That when you say: My mouth speaks wisdom, you understand that what the mouth pronounces emanates from the depths of the heart; and that is why he added: and the thoughts of my heart (speak) knowledge. 5 [v.5J. I will incline my ear to the parable, I will discover my purpose in the psalter. Who is this of whom the thought of the heart speaks science, so that he not only has it on the surface of his lips, but also possesses it within himself? Who is this that hears and speaks in this way? Many speak what they have not heard. Who are these? Those who don't do what they say. To these the Lord says that, like Pharisees, they sit on the seat of Moses. The Lord wanted to speak to you from the seat of Moses for those who

They expose the things they don't do and at the same time wanted to give you security. Do not fear. The things that they say, declares the Lord, obey them; those that do, do not do, for they say and do not do. They don't hear what they say. Those who act in accordance with what they speak, hear what they say, and therefore speak fruitfully, because they hear. He who speaks and does not hear, benefits others, not like this. Then this one who wanted to hear and say and who declares to you before saying: I will discover my purpose in the psaltery, which is to speak through the body, since it uses the soul of the body in such a way as the cytar player uses the psaltery, said: I will incline my ear to the parable. Before, he says, speaking to you through the body, before the psaltery is played, first I will incline my ear to the parable, that is, I will hear what I have to tell you. And why will he incline his ear to the parable? Because now we see through a mirror, in an enigma, as the Apostle says. While we live in the body, we make a pilgrimage towards God. Now we still do not see face to face, as we will see when there are no longer hidden things, enigmas and similarities. Everything we understand now, we see in enigmas. The enigma is a dark parable that is difficult to understand. No matter how much a man purifies his heart and seeks to understand interior things, as long as we see through the corruptible body, we will see only in part. When we receive incorruption in the resurrection of the dead, when the Son of man appears, who will judge the living and the dead, then he will see the Son of man, who was first judged, judging, separating the evil from the good, placing

et qui habitant orbem, terrigenae et filii hominum, simid in unum dives et pauper: non divisi, non separad. Tempus messis hoc faciet, manus ventilatoris hoc poterit (Mt 3:12). Nunc simul in unum audience dives et pauper, simul in unum pascantur haedi et agni, doñee veniat qui segreget alios ad dexteram, alios ad sinistram (Ib. 25,32.33). Simul in unum audiant maestrom, ne segregati ab invicem audiant iudicantem. 4 [v.4]. Et quid est quod never audituri sunt? Os meum loquetur sapientiam, et meditatio cordis mei, intelligentiam. Et haec repetita potius, ne forte cum dixisset, os meum, intelligeres eum tibi loqui, qui in labiis haberet sapientiam. Multi enim habent in labiis et non habent in corde, de quibus dicit Scriptura: Populas iste labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum lon-ge est a me (Is 29,13). Quid ergo ait ille qui tibi loquitur? qui cum dixefit, Os meum loquetur sapientiam; ut ¡intelligas quia illud quod ex ore funditur, de vena cordis emanat, intulit, Et meditatio cordis mei intelligentiam. 5 [v.5]. I inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam, aperiam in psalterio propositionem meam. Quis est hic cuius meditatio cordis loquitur intelligentiam, ut non sit in sola superficial labiorum, sed hominis interiora possideat? Quis est iste qui audit, et sic loquitur? Multi enim loquuntur quod non audiunt? Who sunt qui loquuntur quod non audiunt? Qui non faciunt quae dicunt: quales dicit Dominus Pharisaeos sedere super cathedram Moysi. Voluit tibi loqui in cathedra Moysi, per eos qui ea

loquuntur, et non faciunt; et tibi securitatem Dominus voluit daré. Nolitc timere, Quae dicunt, inquit, facite, quae autem faciunt nolite faceré; dicunt enim, et non faciunt (Mt 23,2.3). Non audiunt quod dicunt. Qui vero faciunt, et sic dicunt, audiunt quod dicunt: et ideo fructuose dicunt, quia audiunt. Qui ergo dictor et non auditor est, alteri prodest, sibi non prodest. Iste ergo qui et auditor volebat esse et dictor, qui tibi loquitur, antequam diceret, Aperiam in psalterio propositionem meam, quod est ¡am loqui per corpus, sic enim utitur anima corpore, quomodo utitur citharista psalterio, dixit, Inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam. Antequam loquar tibi, inquit, per corpus, antequam psalterium sonet, primo ego inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam, id est, audiam quid tibi dicam. Et quare, in parabolam? Quia videmus nunc per speculum in aenigmate (1 Cor 13:12), sicut dicit Apostolus. Quamdiu sumus in hoc corpore, pilgrimage to Domino (2 Cor 5,6). Quia nondum est illa visio nostra facie ad faciem, ubi iam non sint parabolae, ubi iam non sint aenigmata et similaritiesines. Quidquid moda intelligimus, per aenigmata conspicimus. Aenigma est obscura parabola quae difficile intelligitur. Quantumvis excolat homo cor suum, et ad interiora intelligenda refuget, quamdiu per corruptibilitatem carnis huius videmus, ex parte videmus. Assumpta autem incorruptione in resurrectione mortuorum, cum apparuerit Filius hominis iudicaturus vivos et mortuos, tune videbitur Filius hominis, qui primo iudicatus est, iudicans, discernens malo a bonis, pones malo a sinistris,
