I place the good ones on the right and the bad ones on the left. Then the good and the bad will see him; but he will say to the wicked: Go into eternal fire; and to the good: Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom. And the wicked will go to everlasting fire, and the righteous to eternal life; and here the vision will be given face to face, of which the prices are not worthy. Pay attention to what I say. As here, when the Son of Man was yet to be judged, the good and the bad saw him, for the apostles who followed him saw him, and the Jews saw him, who crucified him, so also, when he comes to judge, the good and the bad will also see him; the good ones, to receive the prize, because they followed him; the bad ones, to receive the punishment, because they crucified him. But then only those who crucified him will be condemned? Dare I say: Only them. Therefore we, say the sinners of this time, are safe. If God did not examine the soul, you would be safe. But what did I say? Let your charity understand, so that you do not say in the judgment of God that you did not understand. The Jews, who saw Christ, crucified him, and you, who do not see him, oppose his word. If you resist his word, would you not also crucify his flesh if you saw him? The Jews despised him while hanging on the cross, you despise him while sitting in heaven. Both kinds of men saw him when he was here; The two of them will also see him when he comes. For the Son of man will come to judge, because he came to be judged. Since the Father was not incarnate nor suffered, that is why he judges by the Son of Man, as he stated in the Gospel: The Father judges no one, since he has delivered all judgment into the hands of the Son; and shortly after

He adds: and he gave him power to judge, because he is the Son of man. He, inasmuch as he is the Son of God, is always the Word with the Father; and, as he is always with the Father, he always judges with Him. Inasmuch as he is the Son of man, he was judged and will judge. Just as he was seen by those who believed in him and by those who crucified him when he was judged, so will he be seen, when he begins to be judge, both by those whom he will condemn and those whom he will crown. But the vision of divinity that he promised to his lovers when he said: Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father. And he who loves me observes my commandments, and I will love him and show him myself, the wicked will not see it. This somewhat familiar manifestation is reserved for his own and will not be tasted by the wicked. Of what nature is this vision? Who is Christ? (The Son of God), equal to the Father. Who is Christ? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God." Now we sigh for this vision and groan during our pilgrimage. To this vision we will be presented at last; now we see it in darkness; If we see it in darkness, let us incline our ears to the parable, and thus discover our thoughts in the psalter. Let us hear what we say, let us do as we command. 6 [v.6]. And what did he say? Why will I fear in evil days? The iniquity of my heel will surround me. The dark part begins. Why should I fear, he says, in evil days? The iniquity of my heel will surround me. He must greatly fear if the iniquity of his heel surrounds him. Let man not fear, he says,

bonuses to dextris. Videbunt illum et boni et mali, sed malis dicet, lte in ignem aeternum: bonis autem dicet, Venite benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum. Abibunt mali in ambustionem aeternam, iusti autem in vitam acternam (Mt 25,33,34,41,46); et ibi erit illa visio facie ad faciem, qua illi non sunt digni. Attendite quid dicam. Filium enim hominis sicut hic cum esset adhuc iudicandus, et mali víderiint, et boni; viderunt enim Apostoli qui secuti sunt, viderunt Iudaei qui crucifixerunt; sic cum venerit iudicaturus, et boni illum videbunt et mali: boni, ut percipiant mercedem, quia secuti sunt; mali, ut percipiant poenam, quia crucifixerunt. Soli ergo illi damnabuntur, who crucifixerunt? Audeo dicere, solí. Ergo nos, inquiunt peccatores huius temporis, securi sumus. Si non animum interrogat Deus, securi estis. Quid est quod dixi? Intelligat Charitas Vestra, ne hoc dicant in iudicio Dei, quia non intellexerunt. Iudaei quia viderunt Christum, crucifixerunt; tu quia non vides Christum, verb ipsius resistís. What verb resistis, carnem non ctucifigeres si videres? Contempsit Iudaeus in ligno pendentem, contemnis tu in cáelo sedentem. Ergo viderunt eum both genera, dum hic esset: both genera videbunt, et cum venerit. Filius enim hominis veniet ut iudicet; quia Filius hominis venit ut iudicaretur. Ideo quia Pater non est incarnams, Pater non est passus, et per Filium hominis iudicat, sicut ipse dixit in Gospel, Pater non iudicat quemquam, sed omne iudicium dedit filio: secutus paulo post ait, Et

dedit ei potestatem iudicii jaciendi, quoniam Filius hominis est (lo 5,22. 27). Secundum. enim quod Filius Dei est, Verbum semper cum Patre; et quia semper cum Patre, cum Patre semper iudicat: secundum autem quod Filius hominis est, et iudicatus est, et iudicaturus est. Quomodo autem visus est ab eis qui crediderunt, et ab eis qui crucifixerunt, quando iudicatus est; sic videbitur, cum coeperit esse iudex, et ab eis quos damnabit, et ab eis quos cotonabit. Visionem autem illam divinitatis, quam promisit dilectoribus suis, quando ait, Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo: et qui diligit me, mandata mea custodit, et ego diligam eum, et ostendam meipsum illi (Ib. 14,21), iam impii non videbunt. Ista demonstrado quodammodo familiaris est, suis illam servat, non illam otendit impiis. What is this vision? Qualis Christus? Aequalis Patri. Qualis est Christus? In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum (Ib. 1,1). Huic visioni suspiramus moda, et gemimus quamdiu peregrini sumus; huic visioni in fine reddemur, hanc visionem moda in aenigmate videmus, si ergo in aenigmate videmus, inclinemus in parabolam aurem nostram, et sic apetiamus in psalterio propositionem nostram: audiamus quod dicimus, faciamus quod praecipimus. 6 [v.6]. Et quid dixit? Utquid timebo in die m.ala? Iniauitas calcanei mei circumdabit me. Coepit obscurius, Utquid timebo, inquit, in die mala? Iniquitas calcanei mei circumdabit me. Magis ergo debent timere,

which is not in your power to avoid. For example: he who fears death, what must he do to not die? Let him who was born from Adam tell me how he must use himself to escape from what must come from Adam. Consider that you were born from Adam and that you followed Christ, and, therefore, that it is in your best interest to pay what you owe to Adam and get what Christ promised you. Therefore this one who fears death has nowhere to escape; But he who fears the condemnation that the wicked will hear: Go into eternal fire, has a way to escape. So there is no need to fear? Why should you fear? Shall the iniquity of his heel surround him? If you avoid the iniquity of your heel and walk in the paths of God, you will not fall into evil days; the bad days, the last day will not be bad for him. Therefore, the last day will be bad for some, and good for others. Will it be bad for those to whom it will be said: Come, you blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom? It will be bad for those to whom it will be said: Go into eternal fire. If the iniquity of his heel surrounds him, why should he fear on an evil day? Take the necessary measures now while you live; remove iniquity from your heel; walk on that path of which the Lord said: I am the way, the truth and the life, and you will not fear on the evil day, because he who made himself the way gives you security. Why will I fear on an evil day? The iniquity of my heel will surround me. Then remove iniquity from your heel. Everyone falters and falls through the heel. Take care of your charity. What did God say to the snake? She will spy on your head and you will spy on her heel. The devil spies on your heel when you falter to

knock you down He spies on your heel, you spy on his head... What is his head? The beginning of bad suggestion. When he begins to suggest something bad to you, reject him before delight appears and consent follows, and then you will escape his head and he will not catch your heel. Why did (God) say this to Eve? Because man falls through the flesh. The flesh is our inner Eve. He who loves—he says—his wife, loves himself. What does it mean to itself? He declares it below: No one ever hated his flesh. Therefore, as the devil overthrew man Adam through Eve, so he intends to overthrow us through the flesh. Eve was ordered to spy on the devil's head because the devil spies on her heel. Therefore, if the iniquity of the heel surrounds us, why should we fear on the evil day, seeing that, turning to Christ, we have the power not to commit iniquity, and, therefore, there will be nowhere to surround us, and in this way we will rejoice on the last day and not weep? 7 [v. 7]. Who are those who will be surrounded by the iniquity of the heel? Those who trust in their strength and glory in the abundance of their riches. Then I will avoid these things and the iniquity of my heel will not surround me. How do you avoid these things? Not trusting our strength; not boasting about the abundance of our riches, but glorifying ourselves in Him who promised exaltation to the humble and threatened the conceited with damnation. Thus the iniquity of the heel will not surround us. Those who trust in their strength and glory in the abundance of their riches.

if iniquitas calcanei eius circumdabit eum. Non enim timeat, inquit, homo quod non habet in potestate devitare. Verbi gratia: qui timet mortem, quid facturus est ut non moriatur? Dicat mihi qua evadat quod debent Adam, qui natus est ex Adam. Sed cogitet quia natus est ex Adam, et secutus est Christum, et oportet eum solvere quod debent Adam, et consequi quod promisit Christus. Qui ergo timet mortem, non est qua evadat: qui autem timet damnationem quam audient impii, he in ignem aetemum, est qua evadat. Non ergo timeat? Utquid enim timeat? Iniquitas calcanei ipsius illunl circumdatura est? Si ergo vitet iniquitatem calcanei sui, et ambulet per vias Dei, non perveniet ad diem malam: dies mala, dies novissima, non erit illi mala. Etenim dies novissima mala erit quibusdam, bona erit quibusdam. Numquid mala erit illis quibus dicetur: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum? Sed mala erit illis quibus dicetur: lte in ignem aetemum (Mt 25,34.41). Quod si iniquitas calcanei sui circumdabit eum, utquid ergo timet in die mala? Modo eum vivunt provideant sibi, tollant iniquitatem a calcaneus suo: ambulent illam viam, ambulent per viam de qua ipse dixit, Ego sum vid, et veritas, et vita (lo 14,6): et non timeant in die mala, quia dat illis securitatem, qui factus est via. Utquid timebo in die bad? Iniquitas calcanei mei circumdabit me. Ergo vitent iniquitatem calcanei sui. In calcaneus quisque labitur. Intendat Charitas Vestra. A Deo quid dictum est serpenti? Ipsa tuum observabit caput, et tu eius observabis calcaneum (Gen 3:15). Diabolus

calcaneum tuum observat, quando labaris, ut deiiciat te. lile observat calcaneum tuum, tu observa caput illius. Quod est caput illius? Initium malae suggestionis. When incipit mala suggerere, tune repelle antequam surgat delectatio, et sequatur consensio; et tune vitabis caput eius, and non apprehendet ille calcaneum tuum. Quare autem Evae hoc dixit? Quia per carnem labitur homo. Eva nobis interior caro nostra est. Qui diligit, inquit, uxorem suam, seipsum diligit. What is it, seipsum? Sequitur, et dicit: Nemo enim unquam carnem suam odio habuit (Eph 5,28.29). Quia ergo quomodo illum hominem Adam per Evam supplantavit (Gen 3:6), sic diabolus per carnem vult nos supplantare; praeceptum est Evae ut observat caput diaboli, quia diabolus calcaneum ipsius observat. Si ergo iniquitas calcanei circumdabit nos, utquid timemus in die mala, eum conversi ad Christum habeamus in potestate ut non faciamus iniquitatem; et non erit quod nos circumdet, et gaudebimus in die new, non plangemus? 7 [v.7]. Qui sunt autem quos circumdabit iniquitas calcanei? Qui conjidunt in virtute sua, et in abundantia divitiarum suarum gloriantur. Ergo vitabo ista, et non iniquitas calcanei mei circumdabit me. Quid est vitare ist? Non confidamus in virtute nostra, non gloriemur in abundantia divitiarum nostrarum; sed gloriemur in eo qui nobis promisit humilibus altitudinem, et minatus est elatis damnationem; et non nos iniquitas calcanei circumdabit. Qui conjidunt in virtute sua, et in abundantia divitiarum suarum gloriantur.

8 [v. 8]. There are some who trust their friends, there are others who boast of their power, and others of their wealth. This is the presumption of mankind, not the presumption of those who trust in God. He talked about power, riches, friends. If the brother does not save, will the man save? Do you expect man to save you from the wrath to come? If the brother does not save you, will the man save you? Who is the brother who, if he does not save, no man will be saved? He who said after the resurrection: Go and tell my brothers. He wanted to be our brother, and this is what is declared in us when we say to God "Our Father." He who calls God our Father, calls Christ brother. Therefore, whoever has God as his Father and Christ as his brother, do not fear on an evil day. The iniquity of his heel will not surround him, because he does not trust in his strength, nor does he boast about the abundance of his riches, nor does he boast about his powerful friends. Trust in Him who died for him so that he would not die eternally; who humbled himself for him so that he might be exalted; who sought the wicked so that He might be sought by the already believer. Therefore if He does not redeem, shall man redeem? If Christ does not save, must Adam save? If the brother does not save, will the man save? 9 [v. 9]. He will not give God his atonement or the ransom price for his soul. He who does not give God his atonement, that is, the appeasement by which he inclines God to forgive sins, trusts in his power and glories in the abundance of his riches. Nor does he who boasts of his power, his friends and

his riches the price of the ransom of his soul. Who are those who give the ransom price for their soul? Those to whom the Lord says: Make friends with the wealth of iniquity so that they may receive you into eternal tabernacles. Those who do not tire of giving alms give the price of the ransom of their soul, the Apostle, to those who do not want to become arrogant, he warns through Timothy so that they do not boast in the abundance of their riches. Furthermore, he does not want what they possess to grow old by having it with them, but rather that they gain from it something that is the price of the ransom of their soul. Thus he writes to him: Command the rich of this world not to be arrogant nor to place their hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who gives us all things to enjoy. And as if asking him: So, what should we do with our wealth? Nothing: Be rich in good works, generous, alms-giving, and you will not lose this. How do we know? Hear what follows: Lay up for yourselves a good foundation for the future so that you may attain true life. Thus they will give the price of the ransom of his soul. The Lord commands the same: Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, a treasure that does not perish in heaven, where the thief does not have access nor the moth destroys. God does not want you to lose your wealth; That's why he advises you to change their location. You collected fatigue, because you have placed it in a damp place; In a few days he will be rotten, wouldn't you say to him: Brother, what will I do? He will then tell you: Take him to the upper floor. You hear a friend suggesting that you move the wheat from the bottom to the top, and will you not listen to Christ, who warns you to raise your treasure from earth to heaven, especially taking into account that what you kept will not be returned to you, since you kept earth, and you will receive heaven; You deposited expired things, and will you receive eternal things? You lend to Christ: He receives small things from you on earth, to return great things to you in heaven. Therefore, those who are surrounded by the iniquity of their heel, who trust in their strength, boast of the abundance of their riches and boast of their friends, men, who are of no use to them, do not give to God their atonement nor the price of the ransom of their soul. 10 [v.10]. And what did the psalmist say about such a man? He will tire eternally and live temporarily. His work will have no end, but his life will. Why did he say he will live temporarily? Because these put living in everyday delights. To such an extent that many of our indigent and poor brothers, not very firm in the faith, not understanding what God promises them in reward for these works, when they see the rich in continuous banquets, among the glory and shine of silver and gold, what do they say? Only these live; these truly live. This is said; We admonish that it should no longer be said; and, if it has to be said, it should be said much less than it would be said if we did not admonish. Because we do not presume that I say this in such a way that it is no longer said; but at least it is said by a few, since it must

be said until the end of the world. It is little to say that he alone lives; That is why he adds and says: Only him is heard; he just camps. You think he just lives. May he live; his life will end; Since he does not pay the ransom price for his soul, his life will end and the torment will not end. He will suffer eternally and live temporarily. How will you live temporarily? How lived the one who dressed in purple and linen and ate sumptuously every day; and, proud and swollen, he despised the one who, ulcerous, was lying at his door, licked by dogs and longing for the crumbs that fell from his table. Of what use did those riches benefit him?... Destiny was changed. This, from the rich man's gate, was transported to Abraham's bosom; that one, from the sumptuous banquets, was taken to hell. This one rested, that one burned. This one was satisfied, that one was dying of thirst. He had suffered temporarily, but lived eternally; that one had lived temporarily, but suffered eternally. And what did it profit the rich man, who, being in hell among torments, asked for a drop of water to fall on his tongue from the finger of Lazarus, expressing the reason: Because I am burned here in the midst of flames, and it was not granted? The rich man longed for a drop of water from the finger, as the poor man longed for crumbs from the rich man's table. The suffering of the poor is over, and so is the life of the rich. The suffering of the rich is eternal, the life of the poor is everlasting. Those of us who perhaps suffer on earth do not have life here, because we will not live like this later, since our life will be Christ for all eternity. Those who want to have life here will suffer eternally and live only in time.

Quomodo vivebat ille qui induebatur purpura et bysso, et epulabatur quotidie splendide; et iacentem ulcerosum ante ianuam, cuius ulcera canes lingebant, et desiderantem micas quae de mensa eius cadebant, superbus et tumidus contemnebat. Mutaverunt vices ambo: ille a anua divitis sublatus est in sinum Abrahae; ille ab epulis splendidis, missus est in ignem: ille requiescebat, ille ardebat; satiabatur ille, ille sitiebat: ille laboraverat in finem, vivebat in aeternum; ille vixerát in finem, laborabat in aeternum. 11 [v. l l ]. Because he will not see death when he sees the wise die. He who will suffer eternally and live temporarily will not see death when he sees the wise die. What does this mean? That he will not understand what death is when he sees that the wise die. Therefore he will say to himself: Has not this man who was wise, and who was acquainted with wisdom, and who worshiped God with piety, died? I will treat myself well while I live, because if those who felt differently than me had had any power, they would not have died. He sees them die and doesn't understand what death is. He will not see death when he sees the wise men die, just as the Jews did not see what death was when they saw Christ hanging on the cross, and, for the same reason, they said in mockery of him: If this were the Son of God, he would come down from the cross. If they had understood what death was, if they had understood it, they would have seen that He died temporarily to live eternally and that they lived temporarily to die eternally. But, as they saw him die, "they did not see death", that is, they did not understand what true death was. But what do these also say in the book of Wisdom? Let us condemn him to an ignominious death, for, as He says, someone will look after Him. If He is truly the Son of God, He will deliver him from the hands of his adversaries. That is to say, he will not allow his Son to die if he is certainly His Son. And as if insulting him, they saw him hanging from the cross, not coming down from it, and said: He is only a man. received when he was expelled from his job. He defrauded his master to get friends to welcome him into their homes. Don't be afraid to disappoint; the Lord himself exhorts you to do so. He says to you: Make friends with the riches of iniquity. Perhaps the riches you acquired were acquired through iniquity; or perhaps they are in themselves iniquity, because you have them and so does your neighbor; You swim in abundance, and your neighbor is in misery. From these riches of iniquity, from these possessions that the wicked call riches, get friends, and you will be wise. You buy them; Therefore, you do not disappoint. Now it seems to you that you lose them. Will you lose them by putting them in storage? Brothers, watch the children; I don't know that they buy something, but they find some coins together and put them in the piggy bank, and they don't open it until later. Will they lose it because they don't see what they have collected? Fear not; The children put the money in the piggy bank, and they are safe; You place it in the hands of Christ, and do you fear? Preserve what their parents left them; but it is little to conserve it, they increase it. And for whom do these children keep it? For yours, and so on. But what do they leave for Christ? What do they leave for their souls? Nothing; everything will end up in the hands of the children. Blessed is he who leaves them to his own. I refute this sense, because I incline my ear to the parable, and I hear that the Scripture does not speak in this way. Well, I observe that many perverts die and are succeeded by their perverted children; Therefore, the Scripture could not speak in such a way as to preserve from misery those whose lives it disapproves of. And, for the same reason, what do you think I understand, brothers? That all of these leave their wealth to strangers. How come children are strangers? The children of the wicked are strange, for we find a certain strange man who became a debtor or close friend because he took advantage. If one of yours is of no use to you at all, it is strange. Where do we find the man who became a close stranger? In the Gospel. A man lay on the ground wounded by robbers; The Lord had said to a law expert: You will love your neighbor as yourself. The doctor answered: And who is my neighbor? Then the Lord began to say: A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who wounded him and left him lying on the road half dead; Those close to him passed by; The wounded man descending from Jerusalem to Jericho was a Jew. A priest passed by there and passed by; He pierced a Levite, and left him on the road; A Samaritan passes by, this Samaritan was a stranger, and he approaches him, contemplates his misfortune and with kindness heals his wounds, puts him on his donkey and takes him to the inn; and have them take care of it at your expense. This was said enclosing a mystery that now seems too long to explain; However, considering what I proposed to explain, the Lord says to the legislator: Who

Of these is the mourner of that wounded man? The doctor of the law answered him: I believe that he who showed mercy to him. Well, Jesus said to him: Do the same. The one you feel sorry for is your loved one. Then if the Samaritan, who was a stranger and, by practicing mercy and helping, became a relative or close friend, also anyone who cannot help you in tribulation becomes a stranger to you. Now let us consider the rich who lived badly, who were arrogant and when they died they left their property, not to a stranger, but to their children. But these children follow the lives of their parents; and as those were proud, so are these; and as those were thieves, so are these; and as those were miserly, so are these; therefore, they are strangers to their parents. For this reason you must know that those who inherited his property are strangers to the rich man who was burning in hell, otherwise they would have helped him. But perhaps he had no one to succeed him, and, for the same reason, strangers possessed his property? From the Gospel it is seen that he had them, since it says: I have five brothers. His brothers could not help him who was burning in hell. What does the rich man tell you? I have five brothers; but I did not make friends with a brother who lay before the door. Those brothers who own my wealth cannot help me, they became my strangers. Do you see how all those who live badly leave their wealth to strangers? 15 [v.12]. But do these strangers who call themselves theirs or those close to them really help them? They can't help you at all. And yet, it seems to them that they can be useful in something. And their tombs will be their homes forever. As tombs are built, that is why tombs are houses. When he thinks about making and chiseling a mausoleum, he only thinks as if it were the eternal house where this rich man would live there forever. If I had to live there, I wouldn't burn in hell. The tents are the dwellings in which they will remain temporarily. The houses are the dwellings in which they seem to live eternally, that is, they are the tombs. Then they leave to their own the tents in which they lived when they lived and from here they pass as to eternal houses, that is, to the grave. What do stores benefit from generation to generation? Understand that generation and generation are children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. What do they do? What do your stores benefit from? That? Hear: They will invoke their name in their lands. What does this mean? They will bring bread and wine to the tombs and invoke the names of the dead there. Do you think how the name of that rich man was remembered after his death, when men became drunk remembering him and not a drop of water fell on the tongue of him who burned in hell? This (bringing wine and bread to the tombs of the dead) men do to fill their bellies, but not to profit the souls of the dead.

Aliens? Quia nihil eis prodesse possunt. Et tamen in quo sibi videntur prodesse: Et sepulcro-eorum domus eorum in aetemum. Iam quia ista structa sunt sepulcra, domus sunt sepiliera. About the second part of Psalm 48 1 [v.14]. Having begun yesterday the exposition of the psalm, it was due, as your charity will remember, for its conclusion. In his exposition we reach the verse where the Spirit of God points out to men who pay attention to present, worldly and earthly things, and do not think about what is to come after this life, judging that there is no other happiness than riches, worldly honors and passing power. Therefore, they only expect that after their death they will receive a pompous burial and be buried in magnificently sculpted mausoleums and that their name will be invoked on earth by those close to them. Fools, you do not worry where the spirit will rest after this life, and, for the same reason, you do not tremble at the voice of Christ, who says: Fool, this night you will die, and what you have acquired, for whom will it be? Nor do they notice that after the daily and lavish banquets, the luxurious dresses of purple and linen, the rich man was condemned to the torment of hell, and the poor man, after suffering, ulcers and hunger, rested in the bosom of Abraham. They do not worry, I repeat, about these things, they only pay attention to what they have in mind, and they only look to the fact that, after death, their name, rejected from heaven, is invoked on earth. Describing these, the Holy Spirit says: Their path is their stumbling block.

And then they will bless with their mouth. Almodoque our Lord Jesus Christ said of some, who come to faith to receive the grace of God and be baptized, and, having first been purified by the word of God and exorcisms in the name of Christ, then they return to commit worse evils than those committed previously, what happens to them as Saint Peter says: The ends become worse to them than the beginnings. Which the Lord confirms, saying: And the last days of that man will be worse than the beginnings. Because? Because first he was a patent pagan; Later, under the Christian name, an evil man is hidden under the veil of religion. And it will be worse, because it is hidden, as the psalm says: And then he will bless with his mouth, that is, you will hear the name of God and Christ on his lips, but you will not find them in his heart. Of these it was said: This people praises me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. Up to this point the psalm has already been expounded. 2 [v. 15]. The verses that we must discuss and present today continue: Like sheep placed in hell, for death is their shepherd. Whose? Of those whose path is their stumbling block. Whose? Of those who only attend to present things, without worrying about future things; of those who do not believe in any life other than this earthly one, which must be called death. Therefore, not without reason, they are like sheep placed in hell, having death as their guide or shepherd. What does it mean to have death as a shepherd? Is death some thing or some power? Death is reprobatur in cáelo, invocetur in terra. Describens ergo such Spiritus sanctus ait: Haec via ipsorum scandalum ipsis, et postea in ore sao benedicent. Sicut dixit Dominus Iesus Christus de quibusdam, qui primo accessunt ad fidem mundati verbo Dei et exorcismis in nomine Christi, ut accipiant gratiam Dei, ut baptizentur, et postea redeuntes ad peiora mala quam antea commiserant, Fient Mis, inquit, posteriora deterioration prioribus (2 Petr 2,20): hoc Petrus apostolus: Dominus autem, Et erunt posteriora, inquit, illius hominis peiora quam erant priora (Luke 11:26). Quare? Quia primo vel apertus paganus erat, postea palliatur nomine christiano, sub velamine religionis oceultus malus.

Et erit deterior, quia oceultus est, sicut ait, Et postea in ore suo beneticent: id est, nomen Dei et nomen Christi audis in labiis, in corde non invenís. Quibus? lilis qui praesentia sola attendunt, dumfutura non cogitant; illis qui vitam non putant nisi istam, quae mors diceda est. Non igitur immerito tanquam oves in inferno, mortem habent pastorem. separation of the soul from the body. This separation of the soul is what men fear; but true death, which men do not fear, is the separation of the soul from God. Often, as men fear the death of the body, they fall into the death of the soul. And this is true death. How is death your guide or shepherd? Christ is life, the devil is death. In Scripture we have many passages that declare to us that Christ is the life. The devil is death, not because he is death, but because death comes from him. Through his persuasion, that which Adam incurred was inferred to man. This death by which the soul is separated from the body has as its author the one who first, falling through pride, envied him who was standing, and who cast him down with invisible death so that he would also pay with visible death. Those who belong to the devil have death as their guide or shepherd. We who think about future immortality and not without reason carry the sign of the cross of Christ on our foreheads, have no guide or shepherd but life. The guide or shepherd of the unbelievers is death; that of believers, life. Therefore, if the sheep who are guided by death are in hell, the sheep who are guided by life are in heaven. So what? Are we already in heaven? In heaven according to faith. If we are in heaven, how do we say "hearts up"? If we are not in heaven, how is it that the apostle Saint Paul says: Our conversation is in heaven? With the body we walk on earth, with the heart we live in heaven. We live there if we send something there that keeps us there. No one dwells with the cocorpore: et ea quidem quam timent homines, separatio es animae a corpore: mors autem vera quam non timent homines, separatio es animae a Deo. Et plerumque cum timent homines istam quae separat animam a corpore, incidentunt in illam ubi anima separatur a Deo. Haec est ergo mors. Quomodo autem mors pastor est illis? Si vita Christus est, mors diabolus. Habemus autem multis locis in Scriptura, quia vita est Christus. Mors autem diabolus est; Non quia ipse mors est, sed quia per illum mors.

Sive enim illa in qua lapsus est Adam, ipsius persuasione homini propinata est, sive ista in qua separatur anima a corpore, ipsum habent auctorem qui primo per superbiam cadens invidit stanti, et morte invisibili deiecit stantem, ut etiam mortem visibilem penderet (Gen 3,2). Ad eum pertinent, pastorem mortem habent: we autem qui de future immortalitate cogitamus, et non sine causa in fronte signum crucis Christi portamus, non habemus pastorem nisi vitam. Infidelium pastor mors, fidelium pastor vita. Si ergo in inferno sunt oves quibus pastor mors est, in cáelo sunt oves quibus pastor vita est. Quid igitur? lam in cáelo sumus? In caelo secundum fidem. Si ergo in cáelo, ubi, Sursum cor? Si non in cáelo, unde apostolus Paulus dicit, Nostra enim conversatio in caelis est? (Phil 3:20). Corpore ambulamus in terra, corde habitus in cáelo. reason somewhere if not in that place where he thinks. And in the one in which he thinks he treasures. Did he treasure up on earth? His heart does not leave her. Did he treasure in heaven? That's where your heart is set. The Lord says this clearly: Where your treasure is, there your heart will also be. 3. These for whom death is their shepherd seem to prosper in this life. Quanquam et illud cum evigilaverit non erit: tamen dormienti magis illud erat quod in somnis videbat, quam illud quod non sentiebat. Quid ergo, fratres (dicant sibi homines, Erogetur ad mortem meam; quare dimitro haeredes meos divites? Multa habebunt de meo, habeam et ego aliquid de meo, in corpore meo), quid habebit Corpus mortuum? quid habebit caro putrescens? quid habebit caro non sentiens? Si aliquid habuit dives ille, cuius lingua sicca erat (Luke 16:24), tune habet homo aliquid de suo. Fratres, numquid sic ¡egimus in Gospel, quia dives iile cum holosericis et byssinis tegumentis apparebat in igne? Numquid qualis erat in epulis ad mensam, talis erat et apud inferas? The container that contained the man lies, the house where he lived. Let's call the body a house; Let's call the spirit inhabitant of the house. The spirit is tormented in hell. What profit, then, does it profit him that his body lies wrapped in precious linens and among cinnamon and ointments? This is the same as having banished the owner of the house, and yet you adorn the walls of it. He who is in need in exile perishes from hunger, he barely has a small room in which he sleeps; and you say: He is happy, because his house is decorated. Who won't think you're joking or crazy? You adorn the body and the spirit is tormented. Give something to the spirit and you have given something to the dead. But what should you give him, when, wanting a drop of water, he was denied. This one thought little of sending something before him. Why did he think little of it? Because this path is. stumble for them. He only appreciated the present life, he only thought about how he should be shrouded in beautiful clothes when buried. But his soul was taken from him, as the Lord says: You fool; Tonight you will die, and what you accumulated, who will it be for? And so what this psalm says was fulfilled in him: Do not fear because the man has become rich and because he has increased the glory of his house a hundredfold, since when he dies he will take nothing with him, nor will his glory go down with him to the grave. 8 [v.19]- Because as long as he lives his soul will be blessed. Let him understand your charity while he was alive his soul was blessed. As long as he lived, he did good to himself. Everyone says this, but falsely. The blessing comes from the intention of the one minem, domus quae habebat hominem. Corpus dicamus domum, spiritum dicamus habitatorem domus. Spiritus torquetur apud inferos: quid illi prodest, quia Corpus iacet in cinnamis et aromatibus, involutum pretiosis Unteis? Tanquam si dominus domus mittatur in exsilium, et tu ornes parietes ipsius. Ule in exsilio eget, et fame deficit, vix sibi unam cellam invenit ubi somnum capiat, et tu dicis: Félix est, nam ornata est domus illius. Quis te non aut iocari, aut insanire arbitretur? Ornas Corpus, torquetur spiritus. Give aliquid spiritui, et dedisti aliquid mortuo. Sed quid illi dabis, quando unam guttam desideravit, et non accipit? Hic enim contempsit mittere ante se aliquid. Quare contempsit? Quia haec via eorum scandalum est illis.

Non putavit vitam nisi praesentem, non cogitavit nisi quemadmodum pretiosis vestibus obvolutus sepeliretur. Ablata est ab illo anima eius, sicut Dominus dicit: Stulte, bac nocte auferetur anima tua, et quae praeparasti, cuius erunt? (Ib. 12,20). Et impletum est in illo quod iste psalmus dicit: Ne timueris, cum dives factus fuerit homo, et cum multiplicata fuerit gloria domus eius: quoniam non cum morietur accipiet omnia, ñeque simul descendet cum eo gloria eius. 8 [v.19]- Quoniam anima eius in vita ipsius benedicetur. bless, not in the same words. What do you say? He did well because he ate and drank, because he did what he wanted, because he ate abundantly. I say he did wrong to himself. It is not I who say it, but Christ is the one who says that he did wrong to himself. For when that rich man ate splendidly every day, it was thought that he did good to himself; but when he began to burn in hell, then he saw that what he believed to be good was bad. What he had eaten on earth he digested in hell. I say therefore, brothers, that he ate iniquity. He ate exquisite delicacies with his mouth, but with his heart he swallowed iniquity. What he ate with his heart on earth, he digested between tortures in hell. And, without a doubt, what he had eaten in time, he always digested poorly. But does iniquity eat? Perhaps someone will say: what is he saying? Does iniquity eat away? I'm not saying it; Listen to the Scripture: As bitter grapes harm the teeth, and smoke harms the eyes, so iniquity harms those who eat it. Whoever has eaten iniquity, that is, whoever has willingly given iniquity (into his heart), will not be able to eat righteousness. Justice is bread. And who is bread? I am the living bread that came down from heaven. This is the bread of our heart. Just as someone who eats bitter grapes with his bodily mouth becomes set on edge and his teeth become numb, and, therefore, he is incapable of eating bread, and he has no choice but to praise what he sees, since he cannot eat, so also someone who has eaten iniquity and fed his heart with sin begins to be unable to eat bread. In these circumstances he praises the word of God, but does not put it into practice.

ethics. And why? Because it suffers when trying to act, just as we feel the discomfort of our teeth when we begin to eat bread after having eaten sour grapes. But what do those whose teeth are sore? They abstain for some time from eating sweet grapes, and thus their teeth return to normal, then they give themselves up to eating bread. In the same way, we also praise justice; but, if we want to eat it, we must abstain from iniquity, and in this way not only the delight of praising it, but also the aptitude to eat it will be generated in the heart. Because if the Christian says: God knows that I like him, but I cannot act, his teeth are worn due to the long time during which he ate iniquity. Then justice is also eaten? If it were not eaten, the Lord would not say: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. Then while he lived his soul would be blessed. He will be blessed in life and tormented in death. 9- He will confess to you when you do him good. est, ideo secum fecit bene? Didic ego: Fecit secum male. Non ego dico, sed Christus: Fecit secum male. Etenim di ves ille quando quotidíe epulabatur splendide, bene secum faceré putabatur: cum autem coepit arderé apud inferos, tune inventum est male quod putabatur bene. Quod enim manducaverat apud superos, hoc digerebat apud inferos. Iniquitatem dico, fratres, quam epulabatur. Manducabat pretiosas epulas ore carnis, ore cordis manducabat iniquitatem. Quod apud superos ore cordis manducabat, hoc apud inferos in illis suppliciis digerebat. Et quidem temporaliter manducaverat, in aeternum male digestebat. Manducatur ergo iniquitas? forte aliquis dicit: Quid est quod loquitur? Manducatur iniquitas? Non ego dico, audi Scripturam: Sicut uva acerba dentibus vexatio est, et fumars oculis, sic iniquitas utentibus ea (Prov 10:26). Qui manducaverit enim iniquitatem, id est, qui libenter habuerit iniquitatem, non poterit manducare iustitiam. Pañis enirn iustitia est. Quis est pais? Ego sum pañis vivus qui de cáelo descendí (lo 6,41). Ipse est pañis cordis nostri. Quomodo qui manducat ore corporis grapes acerbas, obrigescunt et obstupescunt dentes eius, et minus idoneus fit ad manducandum panem, et remanet illi laudare quod videt, et manducare non posse: sic et qui iniquitate usus est, et pastus peccatis in corde, incipit non posse manducare panem, laudat verbum Dei, et non facit. Unde non facit? Quia cum coeperit faceré, laborat; quomodo sentimus laborare dentes post

bitter grapes, cum coeperimus panem manducare. Sed quid faciunt illi quibus obstupuerunt dentes? Temperant se aliquantum ab uvis acerbis, et redeunt dentes ad stabilitatem suam, et incumbunt pañi. Sic et nos laudamus iustitiam: sed si volumus manducare iustitiam, temperemus nos ab iniquitatibus; et was born in corde non solum delectatio laudandi iustitiam, sed etiam facilitates manducandi. Nam si dicit Christianus, Deus novit quia delectat me, sed non possum faceré: quassatos dentes habet, diu manducavit iniquitatem. Ergo et iustitia manducatur? Si non manducaretur, non diceret Dominus: Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt iustitiam (Mt 5,6). Ergo quoniam anima illius in vita ipsius benedicetur: in vita benedicetur, in morte totquebitur. 9. Confitebitur tibi, cum bene feceris ei. Attendite et pascimini, haereat in cordibus vestris; mandúcate, videte tales, et nolite esse tales: cávete talia verba. Confitebitur tibi, cum bene feceris ei. of God, who corrects you. By being corrected, you are taught. He corrects you a lot because you have to receive a lot. If you compare the correction with what you are to receive, you will see that the correction is insignificant. The apostle Saint Paul says this like this: As far as the lightness of present and temporal tribulation is concerned, it works for us in an incredible way an eternal weight of glory. But when? When we do not set our sights on the things that are seen, but on those that are not seen; not in the temporal ones, but in the eternal ones. For the things that are seen are temporary, those that are not seen are eternal. Also in the Epistle to the Romans it says this: The sufferings of this time are not proportionate to the future glory that will be manifested in us. What, then, is it that you suffer? But — you say — I am continually suffering. I grant it. From the moment you were born, during all the periods of your life until old age, until you die, think that you will suffer what the holy Job suffered. What he suffered for a few days, perhaps someone has suffered since childhood; but what you suffer passes, it ends. There is no end to what you have to receive. Do not compare the penalty with the reward; Equate, if you can, time with eternity. 10. He will confess to you when you do him good. Do not be like that, brothers; see that for this we have said these things, for this we have sung, for this we have expounded, for this we have striven; don't act like that. Your businesses test you; sometimes in them you hear the truth, and you blapheme; you blaspheme against the Church. Because? Because you are Christians. If so - you say -, I'll join Donato's party, I want to be a pagan. Because? Because you have bitten Deo qui te emendat. Erudiris enim, cum emendaris. Sed multum emendat, quia magnum est quod habes accipere. Nam si appendas quod emendaris cum eo quod accepturus es, invenies quia nihil est quod emendaris. Apostolus Paulus hoc dicit: Etenim quod ad praesens est temporale leve tribulationis nostrae, iuxta incredibilem modum aeternum gloríae pondus operatur nobis. Thirst when? Non respicientibus, inquit, quae videntur, sed quae non videntur; non quae temporalia, sed quae aeterna. Quae enim videntur, temporalia sunt; quae autem non videntur, aeterna (2 Cor 4:17, 18). Et iterum: Non sunt condignae passiones huius temporis, adfuturam gloriam quae revelabitur in nobis (Rom 8:18). Quid est ergo quod pateris? Be semper pateris.

Adam begot two; in teeth. Quando videbas ipsum panem, laudabas; coepisti manducare, et dolent dentes: id est, quando audiebas sermonem Dei, collaudabas, cum tibi dicitur, Fac hoc, blasphemas. Introibit usque in progenies patrum suorum: id est, imitabitur patres suos. Quia iniqui qui moda sunt, habent fratres, habent patres. Antiqui iniqui, patres sunt praesentium; et moda qui iniqui sunt, patres sunt posterorum iniquorum: quomodo patres iustorum antiqui iusti, patres sunt iustorum qui moda sunt; et qui modo sunt, patres sunt eorum qui futuri erunt. the one iniquity existed; in the other, justice: iniquity in Cain, justice in Abel. It seems that iniquity prevailed over justice, because the wicked Cain killed the righteous Abel in the night, that is, alone in the field. Did he kill him in the morning, that is, in front of someone? The righteous will dominate them in the morning. The morning will come, and it will be seen where Abely is and where Cain is. And so it will be to all those who lived according to Cain and to all those who lived according to Abel until the end of the age. He will enter until he is of the lineage of his fathers; will never see the light. Because, when he lived in this world he was in darkness, enjoying false goods and not loving true goods, and that is why from here he will go to hell. The darkness of torment will receive him who comes from the darkness of dreams. Then it will never see the light. And why this? For what was written in the middle of the psalm is also written at the end of it: The man, when he found himself surrounded by honors, did not understand, and was compared to the donkeys, lacking reason, and became like them. You, brothers, consider that you have been made men in the image and likeness of God. The image of God is found within, not in the body; It is not in these ears that you see; It is not in the eyes, nor in the nose, nor in the palate, nor in the feet, nor in the hands; however, it has been done. Where the understanding is found, where the mind is found, where the reason is found to investigate the truth, where faith, your hope, your charity is found, there God has his image printed. There you understand, there you see that these things happen, as said in another psalm: Although a man walks in an image, yet he is troubled in vain. He treasures, and does not know for whom one iniquitas, in uno iustitia: iniquitas in Cain, iustitia in Abel. Praevaluisse videtur iniquitas super iustitiam, quia occidit Cain iniustus Abel instum in nocte (Gen 4,8). Numquid mane? Be dominabuntur eis recti mane. Veniet mane, et videbitur ubi sit Abel, et ubi Cain. Sic omnes qui secundum Cain, et sic omnes qui secundum Abel usque in finem saeculi. Introibit usque in progenies patrum suorum: usque in aeternum non videbit lumen.

Quia et hic cum esset, in tenebris erat, gaudens falsis bonis, et non amans bona vera; et ideo hinc ad tartarum ibit: a tenebris somniorum excipient eum tenebrae tormentorum. Ergo usque in aeternum non videbit lumen. Sed quare hoc? Quod posit in medio Psalmo, hoc et in fine: Homo cum in honore esset, non intellexit; comparatus est iumentis insensatis, et simitis factus est Mis. 1 [v. l]. Let each one weigh in himself how much the word of God is worth to correct our lives, to wait for the reward and fear the penalties. Likewise, let each one present his conscience without deception before his eyes and do not flatter himself in such danger, for you see that the Lord himself and our God flatters no one. And if he consoles us by promising us his goods and strengthening our faith, however, he does not forgive those who live badly and despise his word in any way. Let each one also ask himself when there is time and see where he is and if he perseveres in good and distances himself from evil. For, as it is said in this psalm, not just any man or any angel spoke, but the Lord, God of gods (was the one who) spoke. What did he do when he spoke? He called to the land from the east to the sunset. The one who called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting was our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, Word made flesh to dwell among us38,7). Non turbemini, quia qualiacumque sunt ista, transitoria sunt, si homines estis in honore positi, et intelligitis. Nam si homines in honore positi non intelligitis, comparamini iumentis insensatis, et similes efficimini illis.

1 [v.l]- Quantum nobis valeat sermo Dei ad correctionem vitae nostrae, et ad speranda praemia eius poenasque metuendas, unusquisque in se metiatur; et conscientiam suam ante oculos eius sine dolo ponat, nec sibi blandiatur in tanta periculo; quoniam et ipse Dominus Deus noster videtis quia nulli blanditur: et si consolatur nos ptomittendo bona sua, et confitmando spem nostram; male vivirentibus tamen, et contemnentibus verbum suum omnino non parcit. Interroget se unusquisque cum tempus est, et videat ubi sit, et aut perseveret in bono, aut mutetur a malo. Sicut enim dicit in hoc psalmo, non quicumque homo, aut quicumque angelus, sed Deus deorum Dominus locutus est. Loquendo autem quid egit? Vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum. Who vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, Dominus nostet et Salvatot est Iesus Chtistus, Verbum caro factum, ut inhabitaret in nobis.

others. Therefore our Lord Jesus Christ is God of gods, because through him all things were made and without him nothing was made. If it is God, the Word of God, without a doubt, is God of the gods. Let it be God, the Gospel says: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. And if all things were made by Him, as He says next, then the gods also, if some were made, were made by Him. One alone is the unmade God and truly He alone is God. This one God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit is unique. 2. Then the gods of which God is the true God, what are they or where are they? Another psalm says: God stands in the congregation of the gods and judges the gods in the midst. We are still unaware that there are some gods gathered in heaven; and in their meeting, that is, in their congregation, God is standing judging them. Observe what is said about them in this same Psalm 81: I said: You are all gods and sons of the Most High; However, you, as men, will die and, like one of the princes, you will fall. Therefore it is evident that he called men gods, whom he elevated to such high dignity by means of his grace, but not by proceeding from his substance. Only He who is righteous justifies by Himself, not by another; and deifies Him who is God by Himself, not through the participation of another. He who justifies deifies, because by justifying he makes children of God. Well, he gave them the power to become children of God. If we are made children of God, we are made gods, but this is due to the grace of the adopter, not to the nature of the one who begets. There is only one Son of God, God, and with the Father, one God, the Lord and Savior

ours, Jesus Christ, who in the beginning was the Word, the Word in God, and the Word was God. The rest who were made gods have been so by his grace, not because they were born of his substance so that they could be what he is, but so that by his mercy they could come to him and be co-heirs of Christ. Tangrande was the charity of the Heir, who wanted to have co-heirs. What greedy man would have wanted to have co-heirs? However, if someone is found who wants it, he divides his inheritance with them, and by dividing it, he is left with less than if he alone owned it. But the inheritance in which we are joint heirs with Christ does not decrease with the number of possessors nor does it become scarcer with the multitude of heirs, for it is the same for many as for few, and the same for each as for all. (All for all and all for each one.) See, says the Apostle, what charity God has given us, since we call ourselves children of God, and we are; and in another place: Dearest friends, we are children of God and it has not yet been shown what we will be. Therefore we are in hope, not in reality: We know, he says, that when he appears, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is. He is the only one similar by birth; we, similar by vision. For we are not like Him, who is the same as Him by whom He was begotten. We are similar, but not equal; He, because he is equal, is similar. We have known who are the gods made by justification who are called sons of God, and the gods who are not gods, for whom that God is terrible. Et si omnia per ipsum facta sunt, sicut consequenter dicit, et dii si qui facti sunt, per ipsum facti sunt. Unus enim Deus non factus, et veré Deus ipse solus. Ipse autem solus Deus, Pater et Filius et Spiritus sanctus, unus Deus. 2. Dii ergo quorum Deus est verus Deus, qui sunt, aut ubi sunt? Dicit alius psalmus: Deus stetit in synagoga deorum; in medio autem déos discernit. Adhuc nescimus ne forte dii aliqui in cáelo congregad sint, et in eorum congregatione, hoc est enim in synagoga, stetit Deus discernere illos. Videte in eodem psalmo quibus dicat: Ego dixi, Dii estis, et filii Excelsi omnes: vos autem ut homines monemini, et sicut unus ex principibus cadetis (Ps 81,1.6.7). Manifestum est ergo, quia homines dixit déos, ex gratia sua deificatos, non de substantia sua natos. lile enim iustificat, qui per semetipsum non ex alio iustus est; et ille deificat, qui per seipsum non alterius participatione Deus est. Qui autem iustificat, ipse deificat, quia iustificando, filios Dei facit. Dedit enim eis potestatem filios Dei fieri (lo 1,12). Si filii Dei facti sumus, et dii facti sumus: sed hoc gratiae est adoptantis, non natnrae generatis.

Unicus enim Dei Filius Deus et cum Patre unus Deus, Dominus et Salvator noster Iesus Christus, in principle Verbum et Verbum apud Deum, Verbum Deus. Caeteri qui fiunt dii, gratia ipsius fiunt, non de substantia eius nascuntut ut hoc sint quod ille, sed ut per beneficium perveniant ad eum, et sint cohaeredes Christi. So many enim charitas est in illo haerede, ut voluerit habere cohaeredes. Quis hoc avarus homo velit, habere cohaeredes? Sed et qui invenitur velle, dividet cum eis haereditatem, minus habens ipse dividens quam si solus possideret: haereditas autem in qua cohaeredes Christi sumus, non minuiturcopia possessorum, nec fit angustior numerositate cohaeredum; thirst as many est multis as paucis, as many singulis as omnibus. Videte, inquit apostolus, qualem dilectionem nobis dedit Deus, ut filii Dei vocemur et simus. Et in alio loco: Dilectissimi, filii Dei sumus, et nondum apparuit quid erimus. Ergo sumus in spe, nondum in re. Scimus autem, inquit, quoniam cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est (1 lo 3,1.2). Unicus similis nascendo, nos similes videndo. Non enim ita similes ut ille, qui hoc est quod ille a quo geni tus est: nos enim similes, non aequales: ille quia aequalis, ideo similis. Audivimus qui sint dii facti iustificati, quia filii Dei dicuntur; et dii qui non sunt dii, quibus ille Deus deorum terribilis est. Dicit enim alius psalmus: Terribilis est super omnes déos. Et quasi quaereres, Quos déos?

Gods of the Gentiles are demons or simulacra. It is terrible for the gods of the people, for the demons; kind to the gods made by him, to the children. In short, I see that both confess the majesty of God, because the demons confess Christ, and likewise the faithful confess Christ. You are Christ, the son of the living God, said Peter. We know who you are; You are the Son of God, said the demons. I hear the same confession, but I find different love. What do I say? There love speaks, here fear. Therefore those to whom it is kind are children, those to whom it is terrible are not. He made gods of those to whom he is kind, he showed that those to whom he is terrible were not gods. The former have been made gods, the latter consider themselves gods. Truth made the first gods, the second are gods by error. 3. Then the Lord, God of gods, spoke. He spoke in many ways: he spoke through the angels, through the prophets, through his own mouth, through his apostles, he speaks through the faithful, through my humble person, because when I expose some truth, He is the one who speaks. See how speaking frequently in many ways, through many instruments, through many organs, yet He is the one who lets His voice be heard everywhere, exciting, reforming, inspiring. See what he did. He spoke, and called to the earth. What land? Perhaps to Africa? Taking into account those who say: Donato's party is the Church of Christ? He did not call only Africa, although he did not exclude it. Who called the whole earth from the rising of the sun to its setting, not deQuoniam omnes dii gentium daemonia (Ps 95,4.5). Diis gentium, daemoniis terribilis; diis a se factis, filiis amabilis. Proinde confitentes maiestatem Dei utrosque invenio, et daemonia confessa sunt Christum, et fideles confessi sunt Christum. You are Christus Filius Dei viví, Petrus said (Mt 16,16). Scimus qui sis: you are Filius Dei, dixerunt daemones (Mt 5,7). Parem audio confessionem, sed non parem invenio dilectionem; imo vero hic dilectionem, ibi timorem. Quibus ergo amabilis, filii sunt; Quibus terribilis, filii non sunt: ​​quibus amabilis, déos illos fecit; quibus terribilis, non esse déos convincit. Hi enim dii fiunt, illi dii putantur: hos déos facit veritas, illos error existimat. 3. Deas ergo deorum Dominus locutus est.

Locutus est multis modis. Per Angelos ipse locutus est, per Prophetas ipse locutus est, per os proprium ipse locutus est, per Apostólos suos ipse locutus est, per fideles suos ipse loquituf, per humilitatem nostram, cum aliquid verum dicimus, ipse loquitur. Videte itaque, loquendo multipliciter, multis modis, per tumba vasa, per plana organa, ipse tamen sonat ubique, tangendo, modifying, inspiring: videte quid egerit. Locutus est enim, et vocavit terram. Quam terram? An forte Africam? propter eos qui dicunt, Ecclesia Christi pars Donati est, Solam quidem Africam non vocavit, sed et Africam non separavit. Who enim vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, nullas relinquens partes quas non vocarit, in sua vocatione

Going nowhere without knocking, Africa was also found in his calling. Rejoice in unity and do not be proud of division. We say well that the voice of the God of gods reached Africa, but not that it was limited to it. For he called the earth from the rising of the sun until its setting. There is no place where the snares of heretics can hide, there is no shadow of lies in which they can hide, because there is no one who hides from their heat. He who called the earth, called the whole earth. He who called the earth, called as much as he created. Why do false Christians and pseudo-prophets rise up against me? Why do they strive to seize me with deceitful words, saying: Go, here is Christ; Hey, is he there? I don't listen to those who show me parts. The God of gods shows me the entire world. He who called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting, redeemed the whole earth and condemned the parties that slander. 4 [v. 2]. If we have heard that from the rising of the sun until its setting the earth has been called, from where did he who called it begin to call it? Hear it: From Zion, image of its beauty. Without a doubt, the psalm agrees with the Gospel, which says: For all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. Listen: For all nations it is the same thing that called the earth from the rising of the sun until its setting. He also hears that it is the same starting from Jerusalem as it is from Zion, the image of its beauty. Then he called the earth from the rising of the sun until its setting agrees with what the Lord says: It is fitting that Christ suffer and rise on the third day from the dead, and that penance and the remission of Africam invenit be preached in his name. Gaudeat ergo in unitate, non superbiat in divisione. Bene dicimus quia vox Dei deorum et in Africam venit, non in África remansit. Vocavit enim terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum. Non est ubi lateant insidiae haereticorum, non habent in qua se umbra falsitatis abscondant: nec enim est qui se abscondat a calore eius (Ps 18,7). Qui terram vocavit, et totam terram vocavit: qui terram vocavit, tantam vocavit quantam fabticavit. Quid mihi exsutgunt pseudochristi et pseudoprophetae? quid est quod me verbis captiosis illaqueare moliuntur, dicentes, Ecce hic est Christus, ecce illic est? (Mt 24,23).

Non audio ostendentes parts: Deus deorum totum mihi ostendit: qui vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, totum redemit; autem slanderous parts condemnavit. 4 [v.2}. Sed audierimus, a solis ortu usque ad occasum vocatam terram: unde coepit vocare qui vocavit? Et hoc audite: Ex Sion species decoris eius. Certe concordat Psalmus Gospel diceti: ​​Per omnes gentes, incipientibus ab lerusalem. Audi, Per omnes gentes: Vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum. Audi, Incipientibus ab lerusalem: Ex Sion species decoris eius. Ergo, Vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, concordat verbis Domini dicetis: Oportebat Christum pati et resurgere a mortuis tertia díe, et praedicari in nomine eius poeniten-

sins for all nations, for all nations are from the rising of the sun until its setting. Also what was written: From Sian, image of his beauty, since from there the splendor of his Gospel began, since from there the most beautiful of the sons of men began to be announced, also agrees with the words of the Lord, who says: Beginning from Jerusalem. New things sing harmoniously with old things, and old things with new things. Together the two seraphim say: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, God of hosts. The two Testaments sing in unison. There is only one voice. Let the voice of the Testaments be heard, which sing, but not that of the disinherited, who slander. The God of gods did these things: He called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting, its beauty beginning from Zion. There were the disciples who received, fifty days after his resurrection, the Holy Spirit, sent from heaven. From there the Gospel began. From there the preaching began, from there the entire world began to fill with faithful by virtue of faith. 5. When the Lord came to earth, as he came to suffer, he came in secret; and, being strong in himself, he appeared weak in flesh. It was advisable that it appear in such a way that it would not be known; It was appropriate that he be despised so that he could be killed. The beauty of his glory was found in divinity, but it was hidden in the flesh. If they had known the King of glory, they would never have crucified him. Thus he walked hidden among the Jews, among the enemies, doing good, suffering evil, until he was suspended from the tree. When the Jews saw him suspended from the cross, tiam et remissionem peccatorum per omnes gentes (Luke 24,46,47). Omnes enim gentes sunt a solis ortu usque ad occasum. Quod vero Ex Sion species decoris eius, quod inde coepit decus Evangelii eius, quod inde annuntiari coepit speciosus forma prae filiis hominum (Ps 44,3), concordat verbis Domini dicetis, Incipientibus ab Ierusalem. Concinunt nova veteribus, vetera novis: dicunt ad invicem seraphim duo, Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dominus Deus Sabaoth (Is 6,3)- Et consonant duo Testamenta, et unam vocem habent duo Testamenta: auditur vox concinentium Testamentum, non calumniantium exhaeredatorum. Fecit ergo ista Deus deorum, Vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, ex Sion proceeding specie sua.

Ibi enim erant discipuli, qui acceperunt Spiritum sanctum quinquagesimo post resurrectionem eius die missum de cáelo (Act 2,4). Inde Evangelium, inde praedicatio, inde impletus orbis terrarum, et hoc in gratia fidei. 5. Nam cum ipse Dominus venisset, quia passurus venit, oceultus venit: et cum esset fortis in se, infirmus in carne apparuit. Oportebat enim eum videri, ut non intelligeretur; contemni, ut occideretur. Erat gloriae species in divinitate; sed haec latebat in carne. Si enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent (1 Cor 2:8). Sic ergo inter Iudaeos, Inter inimicos ambulavit oceultus, mira faciens, mala

They viciously despised him, and, shaking their heads before the cross, said: If he is the Son of God, let him come down from the cross. The God of gods was hidden and he shouted rather for our mercy than to manifest his majesty. Where did that voice come from: My God, my God! Why did you abandon me? If not from having taken it from us? For when did the Father abandon the Son, or the Son the Father? Are not the Father and the Son one God? Is it not most certain: The Father and I are one? Then why did he say: My God, my God! Why did you abandon me? If it were not because the voice of the sinner was manifested in the flesh of weakness? He who took the likeness of the flesh of sin, why should he not take the likeness of the voice of sin? Then hidden was the God of gods when he walked among men; when he was hungry and thirsty; when, tired, he sat down; when, his body exhausted, he fell asleep; when he was arrested, whipped and brought before the judge; when he answered the conceited man: You would not have power over me if it had not been given to you from above; when, led to the sacrifice, he did not open his mouth before the shearer; when he was crucified and buried. In all the circumstances of life, the God of gods was always hidden. How was he after his resurrection? The apostles were amazed and did not believe until after they had touched and handled him. He resurrected the flesh because it had died in it, but the divinity, which cannot die, was still hidden in the flesh of the resurrected one. His bodily figure could be seen, his limbs could be touched and his scars could be felt, but to the Word, by whom all things were made, who patiens, doñeesuspenretur in ligno; videntesque pendentem Iudaei magis magisque contemnerent, et ante cruzem caput agitantes, dicerent: Si Eilius Dei est, descendat de cruz (Mt 27,38.39). Oceultus ergo erat Deus deorum, et voices edebat magis ex compassione nostra, quam ex maiestate sua. Unde enim illae voices, nisi ex nobis assumptae, Deus, Deus meus, utquid me dereüquisti? (Ps 21,2, et Mt 27,46). Quando autem Pater Filium dereliquit, aut Filius Patrem? Nonne unus Deus, Filius et Pater? nonne vetissimum, Ego et Pater unum sumus? (10.30). Unde ergo, Deus, Deus meus, utquid me dereüquisti, nisi quia in carne infirmitatis agnoscebatur vox peccatoris?

Who enim suscepit similarityinem carnis peccati (Rom 8:3), cur non susciperet similarityinem vocis peccati? Oceultus ergo Deus deorum et cum inter homines ambulavit, et cum esurivit et sitivit, et cum fatiguetus sedit, et cum lassato corpore dormivit, et cum apprehensus, et cum flagellatus, et cum ante iudicem positus, et cum superbienti responder, Non haberes in me potestatem, nisi data Fuisset desuper (lo 19,11): et quod ductus ad victimam, coram tondente se non aperuit os suum (Is 53:7), et quod crucifixus, et quod sepultus, semper oceultus Deus deorum. Quid post quam resurrectexit? Mirati discipuli, et primo non crediderunt, doñee tangerent atque palparent (Le 24). Sed caro resurrexerat, quia caro mortua erat: divinitas quae mori non poterat, adhuc etiam in catne tesurgentis latebat. Vi-

Did you see him? Who understood him? Who touched him? And yet, the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Thomas, who had the man before him, understood God as he could; So, having touched his scars, he exclaimed: /My Lord and my God! The Lord, however, manifested the bodily figure and flesh that they had seen on the cross, which had been placed in the tomb. He dealt with them for forty days. He did not reveal himself to the wicked Jews, but only to those who had believed in him before he was crucified, so that those whom he had left wavering when he was crucified he might transform into strength by resurrecting. Then, on the fortieth day, recommending his Church, that is, called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting so that those who want to perish in schism may not have an excuse, he ascended to heaven, telling them: You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, from where the beauty of her beauty begins, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. Having said these words, a cloud hid him from his eyes. They gazed ecstatically at who they knew. However, they saw him in the humility of the flesh, not in the majesty of divinity; and, as he was heading towards heaven away from them, they were warned by the angelic voice, which said to them: Men of Galilee: what are you doing in ecstasy looking at heaven? This Jesus whom you have seen ascend to heaven will come as you saw him go to heaven. Then he ascended to heaven. But they returned rejoicing to the city, where they remained, according to the command, until they received the Holy Spirit. What was said to Thomas when he felt it? Because you saw me you believed; blessed are those who do not see and believe. Then we went deri forma potuit, teneri membra, palpari scars: Verbum per quod facta sunt omnia, quis videt? do you have? do you palpat? Et tamen Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,14). Et qui tenebat hominem Thomas, intelligebat ut poterat Deum. Palpatis enim cicatricibus, exclamavit: Dominas meus et Deus metis (lo 20,28). Ostendebat tamen Dominus eam formam, eamque carnem quam in intersection viderant, quae in sepultura posita fuet. Fecit cum eis quadraginta dies. Impiis Iudaeis non se demonstravit: illis demonstravit se, qui in eum crediderant antequam crucífigeretur; ut quos crucifixus dimiserat titubantes, resurgens faceret fortes.

Deinde quadragesimo die commendans Ecclesiam suam, id est vocatam terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, ne haberent excusationem qui volunt in schismate deperire, ascendit in caelum, dices eis, Eritis mihi testes in lerusalem (unde species decoris eius), et in totam ludaeam et Samariam, et usque in totam terram. His enim dictis, clouds suscept eum. Intuebantur illi quem noverant: noverant tamen in humilitate, nondum in claritate. Et cum ab eis iret in caelum, admoniti sunt voce angélica dicente: Quid statis, viri GalilaeiP Hic lesus quem videtis iré, sic veniet quemadmoium vidistis eum eantem in caelum. Ascendit ergo: regressi illi laetantes, manserunt in civitate, secundum eius praeceptum, doñee implerentur Spiritu sancto (Acts 1,3-12). Quid autem dictum erat Thomae palpaati? Quia vidisti, credidisti; beati qui non lident, et credunt (lo 20,29). Praedicti sumus.

predicted. That land called from the rising of the sun to the setting did not see, but believed. Therefore the God of gods is hidden from those with whom he conversed, from those for whom he was crucified, from those before whose eyes he rose again, and from us, who did not see him walk on earth and who believe he is seated in heaven. And if we did see him, would we not see what the Jews saw, and yet they crucified him? It is more meritorious not to see Christ and believe that he is God than to see him only as a man, as the Jews had him. In short, they, judging wrongly, caused their deaths; We, believing well, give ourselves our lives. 6 [v. 3]. So what shall we say, brothers? That God of gods who was hidden then and now also, will he always be hidden? No way. Hear what follows: God will manifestly come. He who came hidden will come manifest. He came hidden to be judged, he came manifest to judge; He came hidden to be before the judge, he will come manifest to judge the judges. He will come clearly, and will not be silent. So what, shut up now? So, who does what we say come from? Whose precepts, these warnings, this trumpet of tetror? Don't keep silent and keep quiet. He does not stop warning, but refrains from punishing; He does not stop commanding, he refrains from judging. He daily endures sinners who do evil, who do not care about God, nor about having Him in their conscience, nor about seeing Him in heaven or on earth. These things are not hidden from God; He generally warns everyone, and when he punishes, it is a warning, not a condemnation. Then he refrains from judging. It is hidden in the sky; still intercedes for Terra illa vocata a solis ortu usque ad occasum non videt, et credit. Occultus ergo Deus deorum, et eis intet quos ambulavit, et eis a quibus crucifixus est, et eis ad quorum oculos resurtexit, et nobis qui credimus in cáelo sedentem, quem non vidimus in terra ambulantem. Sed etsi videremus, nonne hoc videremus quod Iudaei viderunt et crucifixerunt? Plus est quod non videntes Chtistum credimus Deum, quam quod illi videntes nonnisi hominem putavetunt. Illi denique male putando mortificaverunt, nos bene credendo vivificamur. 6 [v.3]. Quid ergo, frattes? Ule Deus deotum, et tune occultus, et moda occultus, numquid semper occultus?

Non plañe: audi sequentia: Deus manifestus veniet. Qui venit occultus, veniet manifestus: venit occultus iudicandus, veniet manifestus iudicaturus; venit occultus ut ante iudicem staret, veniet manifestus ut etiam de iudicibus iudicet: Veniet manifestus et non silebit. Quid enim? silent mode? Et unde sunt quae dicimus? Where is this accepted? where is it monita? Where is this terror? Non silet, et silet: non silet a monendo, silet a vindicando; non silet a praecepto, silet a iudicio. Patitur enim peccatores quotidie mala facientes, Deum non curantes, non in conscientia sua, non in cáelo, non in terra: non eum latent haec omnia, et universaliter omnes admonet, et quando aliquos flagellat in terra, admonitio est, nondum damnatio. Silet ergo a iudicio, occultus in cáelo est, adhuc interpellat pro nobis: patiens est
