us; He shows himself to be patient with sinners by not getting angry, waiting for repentance. In another place it says: I was silent; But will I always be silent? When there is no silence, God will manifestly come. What God? "OurGod." That is, that God who is our God, since the one who is not our God is not God. The gods of the Gentiles are demons; The God of Christians is the true God. This one will come, but not to be mocked, slapped, whipped; it will manifestly come; but not to be struck on the head with the reed, to be crucified, killed and buried, because God, being hidden, wanted to suffer all these things. He will come clearly, and will not be silent. 1. The following words show that He will come to judge: "Fire advances before Him." Do we fear? Let us change, and we will not fear. Fear the straw in the fire. What does fire do to gold? Now it is in your power what you have to do so that you do not experience, because it is not corrected, what will happen to you without wanting it. Even if, brothers, we could prevent the day of judgment from taking place, I think that this is not how we should live badly. If the fire did not come on the day of judgment and sinners were only threatened with the punishment of not seeing God, in whatever abundance of pleasures sinners found themselves, without seeing Him by whom they were created, that is, just by the mere fact of being separated from that ineffable sweetness of His face, even if they enjoyed any eternity and impunity from sin, they would have to cry. But what do I say? Or who am I talking to? This is a punishment for those who love, not for those who despise. Those who somehow began to perceive super peccatores, non exercens iram, sed exspectans poenitentiam. Dicit alio loco: Tacui, numquid semper tacebo? (Is 42,14). Quando ergo non tacebit, Deus manifestus veniet. Quis Deus? Deus noster. Et ipse Deus, qui Deus noster: non enim Deus est, qui non est noster Deus. Dii enim Gentium daemonia: Deus Christianorum, verus Deus. Ipse veniet, sed manifestus, non adhuc illudendus, non adhuc exalapandus et flagellandus; veniet, sed manifestus, non adhuc calamus in capite percutiendus, non adhuc crucifigendus, occidendus, sepeliendus: quia haec omnia occultus Deus pati voluit. Veniet manifestus, et non silebit. 7. Quia vero ad iudicium veniet, sequentia docent. Ignis ante eum praeibit (Ps 96.3). Timemus?

Mutemur, et non timebimus. Ignem palea timeat: auro quid facit? Est autem nunc in potestate quid facias, ne illud quod et te nolente venturum est, non correctus experiaris. Si enim possemus faceré, fratres, ut dies iudicii non vinoet, puto quia nec sic erat male vivirdum. Si non vendeet ignis die iudicii, et sola peccatoribus immineret separé a facie Dei, in qualibet essent affluentia deliciarum, non videntes a quo creati sunt, et separati ab illa dulcedine ineffabilis vultus eius, in qualibet aeternitate et impunitate peccati, plangere se debenent. Sed quid loquar, aut quibus loquar? Haec amantibus poena est, non contemnentibus. Qui dulcedinem sapientiae et veritatis utcumque will feel coeperunt, noverunt quod dico, quanta poena sit
The acceptable worship of God

the sweetness of wisdom and truth, you will know what I say, that is, how much pain it is to be separated only from the sight of God. Those who did not taste that sweetness, if they still do not wish to see God, at least fear the fire. Let torture be frightening to those who are not encouraged by rewards. What God promises you seems vile to you; tremble before what he threatens you with. You contemplate the sweetness of God, and you don't change, you don't get excited, you don't yearn for it, you don't desire it, you give yourself over to your sins and the flattery of the flesh? You pile firewood; the fire will come. The fire will burn in his presence. This fire will not be like that of your stove, in which, however, if they force you to put your hand, you will rather do whatever the person who threatens you with this wants. If anyone tells you, speak against your father's origin, speak against your children, because if you don't, I will put your hand in your oven, you do it so that your hand does not burn, so that your member does not temporarily burn, which will not feel eternal pain. Your enemy threatens you with the slightest evil, and you carry out the evil; God threatens you with eternal evil, and you do not do good! Threats should not drag you to do evil or deter you from doing good. The threats of God, the threats of eternal fire, prohibit evil and invite you to good. Why are you sad? Because you don't believe. Let each one examine his heart and see what faith there is in it. Brothers, if we believe in the future judgment, let us live well. Now is the time of mercy, then it will be the time of judgment. No one will say: Make me go back to the first years. However, he will regret it then, but in vain. Repent now, when there is room for penance. Now se tantummodo a facie Dei separai: qui autem iliam dulcedinem non gustaverunt, si nondum desiderant Dei faciem, timeant vel ignem; supplicia terreant quem praemia non inviting. Vile tibi est quod Deus pollicetur, contremisce quod minatur. Veniet dulcedo praesentiae; non mutaris, non excitaris, non sighs, non desideras: amplexaris peccata tua et delicias carnis tuae, stipulam ad te congetis, veniet ignis. Ignis in conspectu eius ardebit. Non erit iste ignis sicut focus mus; quo tamen si manum mittere cogaris, facies quidquid voluerit qui hoc minatur.

Si ribi dicat, Scribe contra caput patris tui, scribe contra capita filiorum tuotum; nam si non feceris, manum tuam mitto in focum tuum: facies ne ardeat manus tua, ne atdeat ad tempus membrum tuum, non semper in dolore fututum. By not mentioning either the right or the left, it is understood that good and bad fish are mixed. On this occasion, as the truth of the Gospel attests, so many fish were caught that the nets broke. This first capture indicated the current time; the breaking of the networks, the ripping and tearing of the heretics and schismatics. Nets that were thrown to the right represent the good ones already separated from the bad ones. However, will there be only one hundred and fifty-three of the righteous who are on the right? A certain individual had become numb and cold from the loss of the fervor of prayer and said: I was surrounded by tribulation and pain, and I called on the name of the Lord. He found tribulation a useful thing; habebat nescio quis pauper hospes in dolio suo; alius nec in heritage, nec in saccello, nec in dolió aliquid habebat, totum habebat in animo suo: salus domui Zacchaei (Luke 19:8); et plus misit haec vidua quam di vi tes illi (Mark 12:42); iste calicem aquae frigidae porrigens (Mt 10:42), non perdet mercedem suam; sed et pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntiitis (Luke 2:14). Immola Deo sacrificium laudis. O sacrificium gratuíum, gratia datum! Non quidem hoc emi quod offerrem, sed tu donasti: nam nec hoc haberem. Immola Deo sacrificium laudis.

Et haec immolatio sacrificii laudis, gratias agere illi a quo habes quidquid boni habes, et cuius misericordia tibi dimittitur quidquid tuum mali habes. Immola Deo sacrificium laudis: et redde Altissimo preces tuas. Hoc odore Dominus delectatur. Redde Altissimo prays yours. 22 [v.15]. Et invokes me in die tribulationis tuae: et eximam lo, et glorificahis me. Non enim praesumere must de viribus tuis, omnia auxilia tua mendacia sunt. He calls upon me in die tribulationis: eruam te, et glorificahis me. Ad hoc enim permisi diem tribulationis tibi fieri: quia forte si non tribulareris, non invoking me; cum tribularis autem, you invoke me; cum you invoke me, excuse me; cum eximam te, glorificahis me, ut iam non discedes a me. Obtorpuerat quídam et friguerat a fervore prayeris, et dixit: Tribulationem et dolorem inveni, et nomen Domini

do in a state of putrefaction due to the pus of their sins; He was already senseless, and then tribulation came upon him as a caustic surgical remedy. I found, he says, tribulation and pain, and I called on the name of the Lord. Do not doubt, brothers, that the tribulations are known to everyone. See that the human race is full of them: one laments, affected by the damage, another cries, hurt by orphanhood; who is sad in exile and wishes to return to the homeland, considering exile intolerable; Another had his vineyard stoned, looks at his efforts, and considers all his work wasted uselessly. When can man not be sad? Endure the enemy for the sake of the friend. Can there be greater misfortune in the human race? They all deplore these things, they grieve and are surrounded by these tribulations, and in all of them they call upon the Lord, and do good. Invoke God, for he is powerful either to teach to tolerate them or to remedy those who endure them. He does not allow us to be tempted more than we can bear. Let us invoke God in these tribulations, for they crowd upon us as it is written in another psalm: God is our help in the tribulations that surround us too much. There is a tribulation that we must examine. These tribulations surround us, but there is one that we must go out to meet and discover. Which is it? The happiness you find in this world and the riches of temporal goods? No, these are not tribulations properly; They are relief from our tribulation. Of what tribulation? Of our pilgrimage. This same thing about not yet being with God, this

Even finding ourselves surrounded by temptations and worries, for which we cannot be without fear, is a tribulation, since it is not the security that has been promised to us. He who has not recognized the tribulation of his pilgrimage does not think about returning to his homeland. This, brothers, is the real tribulation. Certainly now we do good works when we give bread to the hungry, lodging to the pilgrim, etc.; but this is also a tribulation. Certainly we find poor people with whom we practice mercy; Their misery makes us compassionate. But how much better off would we be if we did not find hungry people to feed, pilgrims to host, naked people to clothe, sick people to visit, litigants to appease? There all things are perfect, true, holy, eternal. There our bread is justice; our drink, wisdom; our dress, immortality. Our house in heaven is eternal; our stability, immortality. Does illness penetrate there, does fatigue lead to sleep there? There is no death there, there are no strife; everything is peace, stillness, joy, justice. The enemy has no place there, and the friend does not disappear. How quiet it is there! If we reconsider and see where we are and where the one who cannot lie promises to be, through the same promise we will realize what tribulation we are in. Only he who investigates this tribulation knows. You are healthy, see if you are unhappy; It is easy for the patient to feel unhappy. When you are healthy, pay attention to see if you are unhappy, because you are not yet with God. I encountered tribulation and pain, and called on the name of the Lord. Immolate a sacrifice of praise to God. Praise him who promises,

invokevi (Ps 114,3.4). Invenit tribulationem tanquam aliquid utile; putruerat tabe peccatorum suorum, iam sine sensu remanserat, invenit tribulationem tanquam ustionem et sectionem. Inveni, inquit, tribulationem et dolorem, et nomen Domini invokevi. Et quidem, fratres, sunt tribulationes omnibus Notae. Ecce istae quae abundant in genere humano: alius damno affectus plangit, alius orbitate percussus luget; alius patria exsulatus moeret, et rediré cupit, intolerabilem peregrinationem deputans; alteri vinea grandinata est, attendit ad labores suos, et consumptam omnem operam incassum. When homo potest non contristari? Inimicum patitur ex amico. Quae maior misery in human genere? Plangunt haec omnes, et dolent, et tribulationes sunt istae: et in his omnibus invokent Dominum, et recte faciunt. Invocent Deum, potens est vel docere tolerandum, vel sanare toleratum. Novit ille non sinere tentari nos supra quam possumus ferré (1 Cor 10:13). Invocemus Deum etiam in istis tribulationibus: sed hae tribulationes inveniunt nos, sicut in alio psalmo scriptum est, Adiutor in tribulationibus quae invenerunt nos nimis (Ps 45,2): est quaedam quam nos debenmus invenire. Inveniant nos istae tribulationes: est quaedam tribulatio quam nos debenmus quaerere, et invenire. What is this? Ea ipsa in hoc mundo congratulations, affluentia rerum temporalium: non quidem ipsa tribulatio est; solada sunt nostrae tribulationis. Cuius tribulationis? Nostrae peregrinationis. Hoc enim ipsum quod cum Deo nondum sumus, hoc ipsum quod inter

temptationes molestasque versamur, quod sine timore esse non possumus, tribulatio est: non enim est illa securitas quae nobis promissa est. Hanc tribulationem peregrinationis suae qui non invenerit, ad patriam rediré non cogitat. Tribulatio illa est, fratres. Certe moda facimus bona opera, quando porrigimus panem esurienti, domum peregrino, et caetera: tribulatio est et haec. Invenimus enim miseros super quos misericordiam facimus; et miserorum miseria facit nos compatientes. Quanto melius ibi iam esses, ubi non invenís esurientem quem pascas, ubi non invenís peregrinum quem suscipias, non nudum quem vestias, non aegrum quera visitas, non litigantem quem concordes? Omnia enim ibi summa sunt, vera sunt, sancta sunt, aeterna sunt. Pañis noster ibi iustitia est, potus noster ibi sapientia est, vestís nostra ibi immortalitas est, domus nostra aeterna in caelis, firmitas nostra immortalitas. Numquid aegritudo subrepit? numquid lassitudo ad somnum trahit? Nulla mors, nulla lis: ibi pax, quies, gaudium, iustitia. Nullus intrat inimicus, nullus labitur amicus. Quae ibi quies! Si cogitemus, et attendamus ubi simus, et ubi nos Futures esse promisit qui lyingi nescit, ex ipsa eius promissione invenimus in qua sumus tribulatione. Hanc tribulationem nemo invenit, nisi qui quaesierit. Sanus es, vide si miser es: nam facile est ut qui aegrotat, sentiat se miserum: quando sanus es, vide si miser es; quia cum Deo nondum is. To him who calls, to him who exhorts, to him who helps, and understands what tribulation you are in. Invoke, you will be delivered, you will glorify, you will remain. 23 [v. 16]. Heed what follows, my brothers. Perhaps someone, since the Lord has told him: Immolate a sacrifice of praise to God, and this was imposed as a tribute, will think within himself and say: I will get up every day, I will go to church, I will sing one hymn in the morning, another in the afternoon; the third and the fourth, in my house; Every day I offer a sacrifice of praise and sacrifice to God. Very good works if you execute this. But pay attention, don't think you're sure why you're doing this; Perhaps your tongue will bless God, and your life will curse Him. O my people, says the Lord, God of gods, who spoke calling the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting, even if you still find yourself living among tares, sacrifice to your God a sacrifice of praise and fulfill your promises. But pay attention, lest you live badly and sing well. Why am I telling you this? For God says to the sinner: Why do you announce my righteousness and take my testament in your mouth? You see, brothers, with what fear we say these things. We take the testament of God in our mouths and preach to you the doctrine and justice of the Lord. But what does God say to the sinner? Why you? Does he then prohibit sinners from being preachers? So, where does that come from: Do what they say, don't do what they do; and this: Should Christ be announced either with a true spirit or with a feigned spirit? These things are said so that those who hear may not fear, even if they hear anyone,

but not so that those who speak well and do evil may be safe. Therefore now you, brothers, are safe. If you heard good things, you heard God from whomever you heard him. May God not leave those who speak without correction, so that it may not happen that just because of what they say they become lethargic in their evil life and say within themselves: The God who wanted so many good things to be announced to his people through our mouths will not lose us. On the contrary, listen to what he says, whoever says it: You who want to be heard, listen first and say what the psalmist says in another psalm: I will hear what the Lord God speaks in me, for he will speak peace to his people. Who am I, that I do not hear what is spoken within me and I want others to hear what is said by me? I will hear first; I will hear, and, above all, I will hear what the Lord God speaks within me, because he will speak peace to his people. I will hear, "And I will punish my body and bring it into bondage, lest by preaching to others I become a reproach." Why do you announce my justices? Why, O sinner, do you announce them for yourself, when it does not benefit you? In this he admonishes him to listen; Don't stop preaching, but follow the advice. Well, why do you take my will in your mouth? 24 fv.17]. You hated teaching. You hated the doctrine. When I forgive, you sing and praise; When I punish, you murmur. As if I were only your God when I forgive and not when I correct and punish. I correct and punish those I love. You hated teaching and put my words behind your back. The things you say

mini invokevi. Immola ergo Deo sacrificium laudis. Lauda promittentem, lauda vocantem, lauda exhortantem, lauda adiuvantem: et intellige in qua tribulatione positus es. Invoke, erueris, glorificabis, permanebis. 23 [v.16]. Videte autem quod sequitur, fratres mei. Iam enim nescio quis, quia dixerat illi Deus Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, et hoc quodammodo vectigal indixerat, meditabatur sibi, et dicebat: Surgam quotidie, pergam ad Ecclesiam, dicam unum hymnum matutinum, alium vespertinum, tertium aut quartum in domo mea; quotidie sacrifico sacrificium laudis, et immolo Deo meo. Bene facis quidem, si hoc facis: sed vide ne iam securus sis, quia iam hoc facis, et forte lingua tua Deum benedicat, et vita tua Deo maledicat. O popule meus, dicit tibi Deus deorum Dominus qui locutus est, vocans terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum, quamvis adhuc inter zizania constitutus sis, immola sacrificium laudis Deo tuo, et redde illi preces tuas: sed vide ne vivas male, et cantes bene. Quare hoc? Peccatori enim dicit Deus: Utquid tu enarras iustitias meas, et assumis T'estamentum meum per os tuum? Videtis, fratres, cum quo tremóte ista dicamus. Assumimus Testamentum Dei per os nostrum, et praedicamus vobis eruditionem et iustitias Dei. Et quid dicit peccatori Deus? Utquid you? Prohibet ergo praedicatotes peccatores? Et ubi est illud: Quae dicunt facite, quae autem faciunt, faceré nolite? (Mt 23,3). Ubi est illud: Sive vertíate sive occasione Christus annunúetur? (Phil 1,

18). Sed haec dicta sunt, ne timeant qui audiunt a quniumque audiant: non ut securi sint qui dicunt bona, et faciunt mala. Ergo mode, fratres, vos securi estís: si bona auditis, Deum auditis, per qucmlibet auditatis. Sed noluit Deus sine correptione dimittere illos qui dicunt; Ne hoc solo quod dicunt, securi sibi obdormiscant in mala vita, et dicant sibi: Ñeque enim perdet nos Deus, per quorum os voluit tanta bona dici populo suo. Imo vero audi quod dicis, quicumque dicis; et qui vis te audiri, prior te audi; et dic quod dicit in alio psalmo quidam: Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus, quoniam loquetnr pacem populo suo (Ps 84,9). Qualis ergo ego, qui non audio quod in me loquitur, et voló ut alii audiant quod per me loquitur? Audiam prior, audiam, maximeque audiam quod loquitur in me Dominus Deus, quoniam loquetur pacem populo suo. Audiam, et castigem Corpus meum, et servituti subiiciam, ne forte alus praedicans, ipse reprobus inveniar (1 Cor 9,27). Utquid you enarras iustitias meas? Utquid tibi quod tibi non prodest? Admonet illum ut audit: non ut deponat praedicationem, sed ut assumat obedientiam. Tu vero utquid assumis Testamentum meum per os tuum? 24 [v.17]. Tu vero odisti eruditionem. Odisti disciplinam. When I spare, you sing and praise; When I punish, you murmur: quasi when I kick, sim Deus tuus; et quando punishment, non sim Deus tuus. Ego quos amo, arguo et punishment (Rev 3:19). Tu vero odisti eruditionem: et
Ennarrations on the Psalms

you put them on your back. And you threw my words behind your back. Wherever you don't see them, but they weigh on you. And you put my words behind your back. 25 fv.18]. When you saw the thief you ate with him, and you participated with the adulterers. Speak in this way so that perhaps you will not say: I did not steal, I did not commit adultery. If you applaud the one who committed it, did you not take part in this same assent, did you not participate in praising him with the one who committed it? This is contributing to the thief and participating with the adulterer. Because, if you do not execute, but praise what was executed, you become a pimp and guarantor of the deed, since the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul and he who executes iniquitous works is blessed. You do not do evil, but you praise him who acts in this way. Is it a small evil to participate with adulterers? 26 [v. 19]. Your mouth abounded in malice and your tongue gave in to the pull. Call, brothers, evil and lies from certain men who out of flattery, although they know that what they hear are bad things, nevertheless, in order not to displease those from whom they hear them, they not only consent by not correcting them, but also by remaining silent. It is little not to say: You did wrong; but they say what is much worse: You did good, knowing that it was bad. Therefore his mouth abounds in evil and his tongue gives itself over to fallacy. The fallacy consists of a certain deception in words, declaring one thing and feeling another. The psalmist does not say: Your tongue gave way or perpetrated the fallacy, but, to show you that you feel a certain delight in it, he said: It gave itself or embraced. Little by little, more post-tea sermons were reproied. Quae dicuntur per te, proiicis post te. Et proiecisti sermones meos post te: ubi non videantur a te, sed onerent te. Et proiecisti sermons meos post te. 25 [v.18]. If you videbas jurera, concurrebas ei, et cum adulteris portionem tuam dondebas. Ne forte diceres: Non feci furtum, non feci adulterium. Quid, si placuit tibí qui fecit? Nonne ipso plácito concurristi? nonne portionem tuam cum illo qui fecit, laudando posuisti? Hoc est enim, fratres, concutrere cum fure, et seguiré cum adultero portionem tuam: quia etsi non facis, et laudas quod fit, astipulator es facti; quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animae suae, et qui iniqua gerit, benedicitur (Ps 9,3). Non facis mala, laudas mala facientes. Hoc enim parvum malum est? Cum adulteris portionem tuam ponebas. 26 [v.19].

Os tuum abundavit malitia, et lingua tua amplexa est dolositatem. Malevolentiam et dolositatem, fratres, quorumdam hominum dicit, qui per adulationem, quamvis sciant mala esse quae audiunt, ne offendant eos a quibus audiunt, non solum non reprehendendo, sed tacendo consentiunt. Parum est, quia non dicunt, Male fecisti; sed dicunt, Et bene fecisti: et norunt malum esse; sed abundat os eorum malitia, et lingua eorum amplexatur dolositatem. Dolositas is fraus quaedam in verbis, aliud promendi, aliud sentiendi. Non ait, Lingua tua admisit dolositatem, aut, perpetravit dolositatem; sed ut ostenderet tibí quamdam delectationem in ipso malo facto, amplexa est, dixit. Parum est quia
The acceptable worship of God

duce what you do; you rejoice; You praise the moment and laugh within yourself. You lose the man who carelessly manifests his vices without knowing he is such a thing. You who know that they are iniquities do not say: Where are you rushing? If you saw him walking recklessly in the dark where you know there is a well and you remained silent, what would you be like? Would you not be considered the cause of his death, even though, by falling into the pit, he was not to die as regards his soul, but only as regards his body? He sinks into vice, he declares his evil deeds to you; you know that they are bad, and yet you praise and laugh within yourself. Oh, if at some time the one whom you mock, and whom you did not want to help, would turn to God and say to you: "Let those who say to me be confused: Take heart, take heart." And your tongue perpetrated the pull. 27 [v. 20]. Sitting down, you talked about your brother. Sitting is the same as what was said above: perpetrated or embraced. He who works while standing or walking does not work with joy; On the contrary, he who sits down to act, what peace and delight does he not seek in acting! Sitting down, you spoke ill of your brother. With all care you spoke badly; sitting down, you executed it; You tried to occupy yourself with this, you gave yourself over completely to evil, you cherished your fallacy. Sitting, you spoke evil of your brother, and you placed stumbling blocks against your mother's son. Who is your mother's son? Isn't he your brother? With this he wanted to repeat what he previously said: your brother. Or perhaps he suggests to us some distinction that we must perceive. I firmly believe, brothers, that there is such a distinction. Thus, then, a hermafacis; et delectaris: laudas in promptu, irrides apud te. Praecipitas hominem impudent vitia sua proferentem, et an sint vitia nescientem: tu qui seis vitium esse, non dicis, Quo irruis? Si illum videres ambulare seized in tenebris ubi tu puteum esse scires, et taceres, qualis esses? nonne inimicus deputareris animae eius? Et tamen si in puteum cadete, non anima, sed corpore moreretur. Praecipitat se in vitia sua, praedicat apud te mala facta sua; tu nosti mala esse, et laudas, et irrides apud te. Or if convertatur aliquando ad Deum ille quem irrides, et quem corripere noluisti, et dicat: Confundantur qui dicunt mihi, Euge, euge (Ps 39,16).

Et lingua tua amplexa est dolositatem. 27 [v.20]. Sedens adversus fratrem tuum detrahebas. Et ipsum sedens ad hoc pertinet quod superius dixit, amplexa est. Qui enim stans aut transiens facit, non cum voluptate facit: qui vero ad hoc seder, quantum otium quaerit ut faciat! Sedens adversus fratrem tuum detrahebas: ipsam detractionem malam diligenter faciebas, sedando faciebas; volebas ibi oceupari, amplexabaris malum tuum, osculabaris dolum tuum. Sedens adversus fratrem tuum detrahebas: et adversus lilium matris tuae ponebas scandalum. Quis est filius matris? nonne frater? Hoc ergo repetere voluit, quod superius dixerat, fratrem tuum. An aliquam distinctionem nobis intelligendam insinuavit? Plane, fratres, puto essedistinguindum. Frater adversus fratrem detrahit, verbi gratia, ut puta quasi firmus et
Ennarrations on the Psalms

He does not speak evil against another brother. Well, when someone who is considered authoritative, educated and of some prestige defames his brother who is perhaps well educated and walking on the right path, by doing so in front of someone who is weaker, it scandalizes him. Indeed, when the good are spoken ill of by those who enjoy some prestige and are learned, the weak, who are not yet capable of judging, are scandalized. Therefore, this weakling is called the mother's child, not the father's, since he still needs milk and clings to the mother's breasts. He is still carried in the arms of mother Church; He cannot yet approach solid food from his father's table, but draws sustenance from his mother's breast, ignoring the way of judging, because he is still animal and carnal. The spiritual man, says the Apostle, discerns all things, but the animal man does not perceive the things that belong to the Spirit of God, because to him they are foolishness. To these the same Apostle says: I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal people; As to infants in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not food, because you could not eat it yet, nor can you now. I became a mother for you; This is what it says in another place: I became little in your midst, like a mother caressing her children. She was not a nurse who fed others, but a mother who caressed her children. There are many mothers who, after giving birth, give their children to wet nurses; These mothers do not raise their children, since they give them to others to feed them. Those who raise them do not raise their own, but those of others. This apostle begot, raised, and did not give to any nurse those he gave birth to, for he also said in another place: To you, to whom I again give alicuius iam momenti doctor et doctus, detrahit fratri suo, forte bene docenti et bene ambulantí: est autem alius infirmus; adversus illum ponit scandalum huic detrahendo. Etenim cum detrahitur bonis ab his qui videntur alicuius momenti esse et docti esse, in scandalum cadunt infirmi qui adhuc nesciunt iudicare. Ideo infirmus ille filius matris dictus est, nondum patris, adhuc lacte indigens et uberibus adhaerens. Portatur adhuc sinu matris Ecclesiae, non valet accesoré ad solidum cibum mensae patris sui, sed de ubere matris victum trahit, ignarus iudicandi, quoniam adhuc animalis atque carnalis est.

Spiritualis enim omnia diiudicat; animalis autem homo non percipit ea quae sunt Spiritus Dei, quoniam stultitia est Mi (1 Cor 2,15.14). Talíbus dicit Apostólus: Non potui loqui vobis quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnaubas: tanquam parvulis in Christo lac vobis potum dedi, non escam; ñeque enim poteratis, sed nec adhuc quidem potestis (Ib. 3,1.2). Mater vobis fue: quomodo dicitur alio loco, Vactus sum parvulus in medio vestrum, tanquam nutrix fovens filios suos (1 Thess 2,7). Non nutrix nutriens filios alienes, sed nuttix fovens filios suos. Sunt enim matres quae cum pepererint, dant nutricibus: illae quae pepererunt, non fovent filios suos, quia nuttienes dederunt; illae autem quae fovent, non suos fovent, sed alíenos: iste veto ipse pepererat, ipse fovebat, nulli nutrici quem pepe-
The acceptable worship of God

to light until Christ is formed in you. Then he raised and breastfed. There were some who, claiming to be learned and spiritual, spoke ill of Saint Paul, saying: His epistles are certainly weighty and vigorous, but the figure of his body is weak, and his word despicable. Paul himself says in his epistle that some of his detractors propagated this. They sat and spoke evil against their brother, and scandalized that son of their mother who should be breastfed. No wonder they made her give birth to them again for their mother. And they scandalized their mother's children. 28 [v. 21]. You did this and I was silent. That is why the Lord our God will come and will not be silent. Now you did this and callé, what does callé mean? I withheld the punishment, I deferred my rigor, I prolonged my patience and waited a long time for your repentance. You did this and I was silent. I waited for you to repent, but you—according to the Apostle says—according to the hardness of your heart and its impenitence, you store up for yourself wrath for the day of wrath and the manifestation of the just judgment of God. You wickedly thought that I must be like you. It seems little to you that you like your bad deeds, and you think that they please me too. Since you cannot tolerate the avenging God, you want to have him as a cooperator and make him, like a judge who sells himself, a partner in the loot. You suspected because of your iniquity that I am like you because you did not want to be like me. Be perfect, as your Father is in heaven, who makes his sun rise on the evil and the good. You did not want to imitate him who gives good also to rerat committebat; dixerat enim, Quos iterum parturio, doñee Christus formetur in vobis (Gal 4,19). Fovebat etgo, et lactabat. Erant autem quidam quasi docti et spirituales qui Paulo detraherent. Epistolae quidem, aiunt, graves et fortes sunt, praesentia autem corporis infirma, et sermo contemptibiüs (2 Cor 10,10): dicit ipse in Epístola sua quosdam detractores suos ista dixisse. Sedebant, et adversus fratrem suum detrahebant, et adversus lactandum illum filium matris suae ponebant scandalum. Merit fecetunt ipsi matri ut iterum parturiret. Et adversus filium matris tuae ponebas scandalum. 28 [v.21], Haec fecisti, et tacui. Ideo veniet Dominus Deus noster, et non silebit. Modo, Haec fecisti, et tacui. What is it, tacui?

A vindicta supersedi, severitatem meam distuli, patientiam tibi prolongavi, poenitentiam tuam diu spectavi. Haec fecisti, et tacui. Ego autem cum ad hoc exspectarem ut te poeniteret, secundum Apostolum dicentem, Tu autem secundum duritiam cordis tui, et cor impoenitens, thesaurizas tibi iram in die irae et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei (Rom 2:5). Carnal delight, which is directed especially toward illicit and foreign things, must be restrained, not left free; dominated with empire, not giving him command. Consider carefully if you don't have something that you are moved by. You answer: I am firm. Are you stronger than David? 4. By this example we are admonished that no one should be conceited in prosperity. Many fear adverse things, but do not fear prosperous things. A prosperous thing is more dangerous for the mind than an adverse thing for the body. Prosperity first weakens, so that adversity finds ready what it must break. My brothers, in the face of happiness it must be watched with more caution. For the same reason, see how the word of God nullifies our security in our happiness. Serve, he says, the Lord with fear and praise him with trembling. In joy, so that we give thanks, and in fear, so that we do not fall. David did not commit this sin when he endured his persecutor Saul. When the holy David tolerated his enemy Saul, when he was tormented by his persecutions, when he fled through different places to avoid falling into his hands, he did not desire another man's wife, he did not kill the man after committing adultery with his wife. In the hardship of his tribulation he gave himself all the more intensely to God the more miserable he found himself. Tribulation is undoubtedly of some use; The doctor's scalpel is useful, as is the devil's temptation. Having defeated his enemies, he believed himself secure; He was freed from oppression and vanity grew. Then this example serves to show us

iniquior, quae cura propterea fecerit quia David fecit, ideo peius quam David fecit. Dicam hoc ipsum, si potero, planius. David nullum sibi ita ad exemplum proposuerat, ut tu: cecidcrat lapsu cupiditatis, non patronage sanctitatis: tu tibi tanquam sanctum proponis ut pecces; non imitaris eius sanctitatem, sed imitaris ruinam. Hoc amas in David, quod in se odit David: praeparas te ad peccandum, disponis peccare: librum Dei ut pecces inspicis; Scripturas Dei ad hoc audis, ut facías quod displicet Deo: hoc non fecit David; correptus est per prophetam, non lapsus est in propheta. Alli vero audientes salubriter, in casu fortis metiuntur infirmitatem suam; et quod damnat Deus devitare cupientes, ab aspectu securo abstinent oculos: non eos defigunt in pulchritudine carnis alienae, nec seipsos faciunt de perversa simplicitate securos, non dicunt: Bono animo attendi, benigne attendi, de charitate diu aspexi. Proponunt enim sibi casum David, et ad hoc illum magnum vident cecidisse, ut parvi nolint videre unde possint cadere. Reprimunt enim oculos a petulantia, non se facile adiungunt, non miscent se mulieribus alienis, non raise easy oculos ad aliena maeniana, ad aliena solaría. sit; sed, non regnet. Inest peccatum, cum delectaris; regnat, if you consent. prosperity. Tribulation and pain surrounded me, and I called on the name of the Lord. 5. The fact was this. I said these things to those who did not commit them so that they would be vigilant while maintaining their integrity; and, when they see that the strong has fallen, let the weak fear. If anyone who has fallen hears these things and his conscience reproaches him for some crime, heed the words of this psalm, heed, without a doubt, the magnitude of his wound, but do not despair of the power of the doctor. To despair of the forgiveness of sin is certain death. Let no one say: If I committed a crime, I must be condemned, for God does not forgive these sins, and therefore why do I not add sins to sins? I will enjoy in this world pleasure, lasciviousness, nefarious desires, because, having already lost the hope of reparation, let me at least have what I see, since I cannot be what I believe. Just as this psalm warns those who did not fall, in the same way it does not want those who fell to despair. Whoever sinned, do not hesitate to do penance for your sin, despairing of your health. “Hey,” David moans. The prophet Nathan is not sent to you, but the prophet David is. Hear him cry and cry with him, hear him groan and groan with him, hear him cry and join your tears to his, hear him repent and rejoice with him. If sin could not block your path (to commit it), it does not intercept the hope of forgiveness. Nathan was sent to this man; see the humility of the king. He did not reject the words of the corrector, he did not say: "Do you dare to speak to the king?" The illustrious king heard the prophet; his humble people hear Christ.

6 [v. 3]. Then hear these things and say with him: O God, have mercy on me according to your great mercy. He who begs for great mercy confesses great misery. Let those who sinned through ignorance ask for your little mercy. Have mercy on me, he says, according to your great mercy. Come to the aid of the serious wound with your great medicine. What I suffer is a serious thing, but I take refuge in the Almighty. I would despair of my mortal wound if I did not find such an excellent doctor. O God, have mercy on me according to your great mercy and, according to the immensity of your mercy, blot out my iniquity. What he now says: Erase my iniquity, is the same as, O God, have mercy on me; and what he writes: according to the immensity of your pities or commiserations, is the same as according to your great mercy. Because mercy is great, there are many mercies; and from your great mercy come your many commiserations. You look for the despisers to correct them, for the ignorant to teach them, for those who confess to forgive them. Did he do this by ignoring him? A certain individual who did some bad things, what am I saying?, many bad things, says: I got mercy, because, being ignorant, I did it in disbelief. David couldn't say: I did it by ignoring him. Well, he was not ignorant of the great evil that was the union with another's wife and the murder of the ignorant husband, who, because he was ignorant of it, neither opposed nor became angry. He begs for mercy, but heeds justice. Mercy consists of forgiving sins; justice, in punishing them. So what happens? If you seek mercy, will sin go unpunished? Answer David, let the fallen answer; Answer with David in order to obtain mercy and say: No, Lord, my sins will not go unpunished. I knew the justice of the One from whom I receive my mercy. They will not go unpunished; but I don't want you to punish me, since I punish them; Therefore, I ask my forgiveness, because I recognize and detest them. 8 [v. 5]. For I recognize my wickedness, and my crime is always before me. I did not put what I committed behind my back, I did not look at others, forgetting about myself; I don't try to remove the speck from my brother's eye, when I have a beam in my eye; My sin is before me, not my back. He was behind me when the prophet was sent to me and told me the parable of the poor man's sheep. For this is what NathanaDavid the prophet says: There was a certain

rich man who had many sheep and a poor neighbor had a single lamb, which he raised in his lap and fed with his bread; When a guest arrived at the rich man's house, he took nothing from his flock; He longed for the poor neighbor's lamb and killed it for his guest. What do you think he is worthy of? David, angry, sentenced. The king then being completely unaware of what he had been reproached for, said that the rich man was worthy of death and that he should pay four times as much for the sheep. He judged very severely and fairly. His sin was not yet before him, he carried his action behind his back, he did not yet know his iniquity, and that is why he did not forgive others. To this end the prophet was sent; He removed the sin from his back and placed it before his eyes so that David could see that sentence, so rigorous and so just, that he decreed against himself. From his tongue he formed the scalpel to cut and heal the wound in his heart. The Lord did the same with the Jews when he presented the adulterous woman to him, proposing a snare of temptation, and they themselves fell into what they proposed. This woman - they say - has been caught in adultery; Moses ordered those to be stoned. You, what do you think of this one? By tempting, they try to catch the wisdom of God in a dead end; so that, if he ordered her to be killed, he would lose the reputation he had for meekness, and, if he ordered her released, he would incur imposture as a reformer of the law. What did he answer? He did not say: Kill her; He did not say: Let her go, but: He who among you knows that he is without sin, let him first throw the stone. Just is the law that commands the adulteress to kill, but this law requires innocent ministers to put it into practice. See what you present; see who you are.

When they heard this, they separated one after another. The Lord and the adulteress were left alone. The wound and the doctor remained, who gave great misery and Sublime Mercy. Those who presented it, ashamed, did not ask for forgiveness; the one presented became confused and healed. Well the Lord said to her: Woman, has no one condemned you? She answered: No one, Lord. Jesus told him; Nor will I condemn you; Go and from now on sin no more. Did Christ act against the law? The Father had not given the law without his Son. If heaven and earth and all the things they contain were made by Him, was the law written without the Word of God? God did not act against the law, since not even the emperor acts in opposition to his laws when he grants pardons to the repentant. Moses was the executor of the law; Christ, the promulgator of it. Moses stones as a judge, Christ forgives as a king. God took pity on David according to his great mercy, as he urges here, as he asks, as he exclaims and grieves here. Those who brought the adulteress before Jesus did not want to do this; They found out about their wounds when the doctor showed them to them and they did not obtain the medicine from the doctor. This is how many behave who are not ashamed of sinning, but their penitence fills them with shame. Oh miserable madness! You are not ashamed of the wound itself and the bandage of its healing causes you to blush. Is she not perhaps more shameful and pestiferous when she is naked? Go to the doctor; do penance and say: I acknowledge my iniquity, and my crime is always before me. 9 [v.6].

What does it mean Against you alone I sinned and did evil in your sight; so that you can be justified in your words and win when you are judged? The psalmist contemplates the future judge, who is to be judged, who is to be judged by the righteous for sinners, and sees him as the victor, because he had nothing in him to be judged of. To this one who had no sin, the prophet David says in this circumstance: Against you alone I have sinned and done evil in your sight; so that you can be justified in your words and win when you are judged. For you surpass all men, all judges; and he who judges himself righteous before you is unjust. You, who have the power to give your life and take it again, are the only one who judges fairly and are judged unjustly. Then you win by being judged. You surpass all men, because you are greater than all men, for through you men were made. 10 [v. 7]. Against you alone I have sinned and done evil in your sight; so that you can justify yourself in your words and win when you are judged. Behold, I was conceived in iniquity. This is as if it were said that all those who did what you did will be defeated, O David! For it is not a small evil, a slight sin, adultery and murder. But it remains to know what you think of those who, since they came out of their mother's womb, have not done such a thing. You also impute some sins to these, so that he will conquer them all when he begins to be judged. David personified the human race in himself, he kept in mind the origin of all, he considered the root of death, he noticed the origin of iniquity and said: See, I was conceived in iniquity. Was David born of adultery? Was he not born of Jesse, a righteous man, and his lawful wife? Why do you say it was con-

filled with sin, if it is not because it emanates from Adam's iniquity? The very bond of death grew one with iniquity. No one is born unless it is in sin and carrying with it the merit of punishment. Well, another prophet also says in another place: No one is clean in your presence, not even the child who has been alive for one day on the earth. We also know that through Christian baptism sins are erased and that this baptism of Christ has the power to remit sins. If children are completely innocent, why do mothers run with them to church? What is forgiven for that baptism, what for that remission? I rather see the child crying than getting angry. What does baptism wash away? What destroys that grace? Destroy the germ of sin. If the child could speak to you, he would tell you, and, if he already had the knowledge that David had, he would answer you: Why do you consider me a child? Surely you do not see my crimes, but I was conceived in iniquity and my mother nourished me in sins in her womb. Without this bond of carnal lust, Christ was born: without a man, of the Virgin, who conceived by virtue of the Holy Spirit. It cannot be said of Christ that he was conceived in iniquity, it cannot be said that his mother fed him in her womb in sins, since it was said to her: The Holy Spirit will descend upon you and the virtue of the Most High will overshadow you. But men are not conceived in iniquity, nor are they nourished in sins in the wombs of mothers because the union of spouses is a sin, but because what is done is done of flesh, subject to punishment. Death is the punishment of the flesh, and mortality itself is inherent in it. from here

You threaten him; And when you threaten him, what evil do you want to impose on him? Abandon himself. No matter how hard you try, the most you have to do is hand him over to the beasts. But he is worse for himself than the beasts. The beasts can tear his body to pieces, but he cannot help but tear his heart. He punishes himself internally, and you demand external punishments for him? On the contrary, he prays to God for him so that he may be free from himself. Yet, my brothers, this psalm is not a petition for or against the wicked, but a prophecy of what is to come to the wicked. For do not think that he speaks any psalm wishing evil, but threatening with a spirit that prophesies 9. What next? All your power, and your thinking of continuous iniquity, and the relentless exercise of the malignancy of your permanendum; quae autem faciunt ad destructionem faciant propter disciplinam proficientium, non propter oppressionem innocentium. Huic ergo potentiae comparatum corpus illud terrenum, quare non auditat ex his verbis, Quid gloriatur in malitia qui potens est? 8 [v.4]. In iniquitate tota die iniustitiam cogitavit lingua tua. In iniquitate tota die, id est toto tempote, sine lassitude, sine intervallo, sine pausetione. Et quando non facis, cogitas; ut quando aliquid mali abest a manibus, a corde non absit: aut facis malum, aut dum non potes faceré, dicis malum, hoc est, maledicis: aut quando nec hoc potes, vis et cogitas malum. Tota die ergo, id est sine intermissione.

Exspectamus huic homini poenam. Parva sibi poena est? Minaris ei: tu cum ei minaris, quo eum vis mittere in malum? Dimitte illum in se. Ut multum saevias, subiectutus es bestiis: in seipsum peiot est bestiis. Bestia enim lacerare corpus eius potest: ipse cot suum sanum telinquere non potest. Interius in se ipse saevit, et tu exterius pests inquirís? Imo ora Deum pro illo, ut liberetur a se. Vetumtamen in hoc psalmo, ftatres mei, non oratio est pro malis, aut contra malo, sed prophetia quid sit eventurum malis. Non ¡taque putetis ex malevolentia Psalmum aliquid dicere: dicitur enim in spiritu prophetiae. 9. Quid ergo sequitur? Tota potentia tua, et tota cogitatio iniquitatis tota die, et meditado malignitatis in lingua tua sine intetmissione,

You choose what you have to eat, you also choose what you have to talk. You put injustice before justice, and malignancy before kindness. You loved every word that causes sinking, (you loved) the deceitful tongue. The deceitful tongue precedes the sinking word. What job does the deceitful tongue perform? For this, God will destroy you forever, although now it appears that you live like grass in the field before the heat of the sun appears. Then God will destroy your jin, uproot you and make you emigrate from your tent. Now this Doeg, an Idumean, is in the tent, but the servant does not dwell eternally in the house. Now this Doeg performs some good, if not through his own actions, at least through the words of God, so that, in seeking his own good in the Church, he speaks what belongs to the glory of Christ. It will take you out of your tent. Truly I tell you that these have already received their reward. And he will uproot you from the land of the living. Then we must be rooted in the land of those who live. Our roots are there. The root is hidden. You can see the fruits, but not the root. Our root is charity; our fruits, good works. It is necessary that your works come from charity; then your root will be established in the land of the living. From there this Doeg will be uprooted, for there is no way he can remain there, because he did not put down deep roots there. Just as that seed that fell on a stone, although it took root, dried up the moment the sun rose because it lacked moisture, so will this Doeg dry up. On the contrary, those who put down deep roots, what do they hear from the Apostle? I fall on my knees for you before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ so that you may take root and be established in charity. And, since they already have roots, he adds: So that you can understand

der the height, width, length and depth; and also know the most eminent science of the charity of Christ so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God. Worthy of such fruits is this great root, so pure, so vigorous, so deeply rooted in the germ. On the contrary, the root of Doeg will be uprooted from the land of the living. 13 [v.8}. And the righteous will see it, and will fear and laugh at it. When will they fear? When will they laugh? Let us understand and usefully distinguish these two times of fear and laughter. While we are in this world it is not the time to laugh, lest we cry later. We read what is reserved for the end of this Doeg. We read it and, because we understand it and believe it, we see it, but we fear it. This was said: The righteous will see and fear. Why do we fear seeing what will ultimately happen to the evil ones? For the Apostle said: With fear and trembling do the work of your salvation, for it has been said in a psalm: Serve the Lord with fear and praise him with trembling. Why with fear? Because he who thinks he stands firm, must see that he does not fall. Why with tremor? For it is said in another place: Brethren, if a man has been caught in any crime, you spiritual ones correct him in a spirit of meekness, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted. Then those who are righteous now, those who live by faith, so contemplate what is to happen to this Doeg, that they also fear for themselves, since they know what they are, but they do not know what they will be tomorrow. Then now the righteous will see and fear. But when

Et videbunt iusti, et timebunt, et super eum ridebunt. When timebunt? when ridebunt? Intelligamus ergo et discernamus duo ista tempora satis utiliter timendi et tidendi. Quamdiu enim sumus in hoc saeculo, nondum est ridendum, ne postea ploremus. Legimus quid servetur in finem huic Doech; legimus, et quia intelligimus et credimus, videmus, sed timemus. Hoc ergo dictum est, Videbunt iusti et timebunt. Quamdiu videmus quid eventurum sit in finem malis, quare timemus? When iniquity disappears, when the time of uncertainty has passed, as it has largely passed, when the darkness of this age has been dispelled, in which we now walk in the light of Scripture, and therefore we fear as if we walked in the night. Now we walk in the light of prophecy, of which the apostle Saint Peter says: We have the prophetic word more secure, to which you do well to pay attention as to a lamp that shines in a dark place until the day shines and the morning star dawns in your hearts. When our day has come, that is, the manifestation of Christ, of which the Apostle says: When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you also will appear with Him in glory, then the righteous will laugh at this Doeg. Then there will be no help, because it will not happen as now, when, seeing a man who lives iniquitously, you intend to make efforts to correct him, since he who is unjust can, once converted, be just, just as the just, if he deviates from the good path, can be unjust. Therefore, do not boast about yourself or despair of him; If you are benign, if you do not love iniquity more than kindness, devote yourself fully, as far as you can, to correcting the man who is on the wrong path so that he may enter the right path. judge; repair the fault and you will be happy before the judge. Today he exhorts you not to judge yourself. He who will be your judge tomorrow is your lawyer today. And they will laugh at him and say: here lies the man who did not establish God for his help. See the mass or the earthly guild. "You are worth as much as you have." This is the proverb of the greedy, of thieves, of those who oppress the innocent, of those who take possession of other people's things, of those who deny those that were given to them in custody. What — do you say — is this proverb? "You are worth as much as you have", that is, the more power you will have the more money you have, the more wealth you acquire. Here is the man who did not take God for his help, but trusted in the abundance of his riches. Don't let the poor guy say: I don't belong to this union. The poor bad guy, upon hearing the prophet say: He hoped in the abundance of his riches, immediately takes care of his rags, perhaps sees next to him the elegantly dressed rich man in the people of God, and mutters within himself: The prophet is referring to this one, not to me. Quamdiu ergo ad Iucernam ambulamus, necesse est ut cum timore vivamus. Cum autem venerit dies noster, id est manifestatio Christi, de qua Idem dicit Apostolus, Cum Christus apparuerit vita vestra, tune et vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria (Col 3,4); tune iusti ridebunt istum Doech. Non est enim iam subveniendi locus: non quomodo nunc, quando vides hominem iniuste vivostem, vis cum illo laborare ut corrigas; quia qui iniustus est, conversus poterit iustus esse, quomodo et iustus aversus potest iniustus esse. Itaque nec de te praesumas, nec de illo desperes; et da operam quantum potes, si benignus es, si non diligis malitiam super benignitatem, ut ambulantem hominem in via mala et errantem corrigas ad viam bonam. Tune vero cum venerit iudicii tempus, correctionis locus non erit, sed tantum damnationis: et erit ibi poenitentia, sed infructuosa, quia sera. Vis ut sit fruitful? Non sit sera: hodie corrects you.

Reus es, ille iudex est: corrects reatum, et gaudebis ad iudicem. Hodie enim hortatur te, ne iudicet te; et qui iudex tuus futurus est, ipse est hodie advocatus tuus. Tune ergo, fratres, restat ridendi tempus. Nam ipsam irrisionem iniquorum quaefutura est iustis, significavit liber ille Sapientiae. In suis enim, in quorum animas transferí, se sapientia, invoice est quod dixit: Increpabam, et non exaudiebatis; loquebar, et meis sermonibus non intendebatis; et ego vestrae perditioni superridebo (Ptov 1,24-26). Hoc fiet tune a iustis in istum Doech. Modo autem videamus et timeamus, ne hoc simus quod in eum dicimus: et si hoc eramus, hoc esse desinamus, ut moda timentes, postea rideamus. 14 [v.9]- Quid autem tune digant qui ridebunt? Et super eum ridebunt, et dicet: Ecce homo qui non posit Deum adiutorem suum. Videte corpus terrenum. Quantum habebis, tantus eris. Proverbium avarorum, rapacium, innocentes opprimentium, res alienas invadentium commendata negantium. Quale hoc proverbium? These are such that they say in their hearts: There is no God. To such I present. How do I make it clear to them? These believe they please God with their works. The psalmist did not say: Some say, but: The fool said in his heart: There is no God. Those I have been speaking of believe to such an extent that there is God, that they think what they do pleases God. However, if you wisely understand what was recorded: The fool said in his heart: There is no God, if you pay attention, if you understand, if you discover the subtlety, you will see that whoever thinks that God is pleased with evil works, does not consider Him to be God. Well, if it is God, it is just; If he is just, he dislikes injustice and iniquity. Therefore, when you think that he delights in iniquity, you deny that he is God. If God is the one to whom iniquity displeases, it will not seem to you that it is God to whom iniquity displeases. Since God alone is the one who displeases iniquity, when you say in your heart: God protects my iniquities, you say: There is no God.

What sacrifice must I take here, brothers; What worthy thing should I offer to the Lord in reward of his mercy? Will I search the flock for sheep victims, will I choose a goat, will I set my eyes on some bull in the herd, will I offer incense brought from the land of the Sabeans? What will I do? What will I offer if it is not what another psalm says: A sacrifice of praise will honor me? So why is it said voluntarily? Because I freely love what I praise. I praise God and rejoice in the same praise. I rejoice in the praise of him with whom I am praised and not put to shame. I do not praise him in the way that the charioteer, the hunter or any comedian is praised by fans of the frivolities of spectacles, nor in the way in which others are invited and exhorted by their panegyrists to praise on a par with them; despite the fact that many times when everyone has shouted, when their patronage was defeated,

swimming, everyone is ashamed. This does not happen with God our Lord. He is praised willingly and loved with tenderness; He is freely loved and praised. What does gratuitously mean? For Him, not for anything else. If you praise God to give you something, you no longer love Him for free. You would be ashamed if your wife loved you for money, and even more so if perhaps when poverty came upon you, she thought about adultery. Whether we are in tribulation or anguish, in joy or rejoicing, let us praise him who also teaches in tribulation and comforts in joy. What does intelligence mean to David? David was, as we know, a holy prophet, king of Israel and son of Jesse; But since our Lord Jesus Christ came into the world for our salvation, proceeding from his lineage in the flesh, Christ is frequently prefigured under this name, and is written David

for Christ taking into account the origin of his flesh. According to one thing he is the son of David and according to another he is Lord of him. He is the son of David, according to the flesh, and he is Lord of David, attending to the divinity. If by Him all things were made, by Him David was also made, from whose flesh Christ proceeded, with which He presented Himself to men. Therefore, when the Lord asked the Jews whose son Christ was and they answered: Of David, seeing that they remained in the flesh, ignoring divinity, he corrected them with the following proposition: How David in spirit calls him Lord, saying: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool. If, then, David calls him Lord in spirit, what is his son like? He proposed this question; He said he was his son. You heard the word Lord when Christ said: Tell me: what is he like as a son? You heard the word son when he added: Say: what is it like, Lord? This question is resolved by the Catholic faith. What is it like Lord? In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. What is he like son? The Word became flesh and lived among us. David prefigures Christ; but Christ, as I have said many times to your charity, is Head and Body; and, therefore, we should not consider ourselves strangers to Christ, since we are members of his body, and, therefore, we should not consider ourselves different from him, because they will be two in one flesh. ma their exercise by suffering or enduring these men. Do not think that evil people are found at random in this world and that God does not bring any good from them. The bad person either lives to correct himself, or he lives so that the good can be exercised through him. May those who exercise now convert and be exercised with us! However, while they are such that they exercise, let us not hate them, because we do not know which of them will persevere to the end in their wickedness. And many times, when it seems to you that you hated the enemy, you are wrong, and you hate your brother. Only the devil and his angels do we know from the Holy Scriptures that they are destined for eternal fire. Of them alone we should distrust the correctness at all. Against them we maintain a hidden struggle, to which the Apostle encourages us when he says: We do not fight against flesh and blood—that is, against the men you see—but against the princes, the powers and leaders of this world of darkness. So that you would not understand when he said of this world that the demons are the rulers of heaven and earth, he added of this world of darkness. He called the lovers of the world the world, he called the wicked and perverse the world; He called the world the one of whom the Gospel says: And the world did not know him. If the world did not know the light, because the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not know it; and the darkness, which did not know the present light, is called the world; they are the directors of this darkness. Regarding these directors we have an exhaustive sentence in Holy Scripture telling us that we should not expect the conhominum exercitationem suam dixit. Ne putetis gratis esse malo in hoc mundo, et nihil boni de illis agere Deum. Omnis malus aut ideo vivit ut corrigatur, aut ideo vivit ut per illum bonus exerceatur. Utinam ergo qui nos modo exercent, convertantur, et nobiscum exerceantur: tamen quamdiu ita sunt ut exerceant, non eos oderimus; quia in eo quod malus est quis eorum, utrum usque in fínem perseveraturus sit, ignoramus; et plerumque cum tibí videris odisse inimicum, fratrem odisti, et nescis. Christus secundum quod caput Salvator corporis, ille natus ex virgine crucifixus, qui iam nobis exemplum resurrectionis nostrae in resurrectione suae carnis ostendit, qui sedet ad dexteram Patris, et pro nobis interpellat, est et hic, sed in corpore suo quod est Ecclesia.

Corpus coniunctum est capiti suo, caput pro corpore clamat: Saule, Saule, why are you after me? (Acts 9,4). Et nos ibi seedmus, et ipse hic laborat: nos ibi seedmus secundum spem, et ille hic nobiscum est secundum charitatem. Haec compago tanquam unius hominis facit duos in carne una, sponsum et sponsam. Unde et ipse Dominus dicit: Igitur iam non duo, sed una caro (Mt 19,6). Quomodo ergo hic tenetur in Geth? Tenetur in torculari corpus eius, id est Ecclesia eius (Eph 1,22.23). Quid est, in torculari? In pressuris. Sed in torculari fructuosa pressura est. Uva in vite pressuram non sentit, integra videtur, sed nihil inde manat: mittitur in torcular, calcatur, premitur; iniuria videtur fieri uvae, sed ista iniuria sterilis non est; imo if nulla iniuria accesoet, sterilis remaneret.

They direct all their evil advice against me. 9 [v. 7]. They stop by and hide. Incolere means to dwell in passing or to pilgrimage. Upstart inhabitants, those who live in a foreign country, are called incolae. Every man is a pilgrim in this life. In it you contemplate that we are clothed in the flesh, because of which we cannot see the heart. That is why the Apostle says: Let us not judge anything before its time until the Lord comes, who will illuminate the hidden things of darkness and reveal the thoughts of the heart, and then praise will be given to each one by God. Before this happens, each one takes his heart on this pilgrimage of carnal life and every heart is hidden from every heart. Therefore, these who plot evil against him dwell in passing and hide. As they are on this pilgrimage and carry the flesh, they cover the deception in their hearts and hide the evil they think. Because? Because this life is still fleeting. Keep hiding; What they hid will appear, but they will not hide. The word "hide" has another meaning that may be more pleasing. Thus, it is understood that certain false brothers have distanced themselves from the saints and that, meddling in the Church, they cause worse tribulations to the body of Christ, since, by not considering them for

complete strangers, they are not completely distrusted. Commemorating the very serious dangers caused by these, after enumerating their multiple sufferings and saying: Dangers from rivers, dangers from thieves, dangers from my lineage, dangers from the people, dangers in the city, dangers in the desert, dangers in the sea, he adds: Dangers among the false brothers. These are too dangerous, and it is said of them in another psalm: They came in to see me or spy on me. They came in to spy, and no one told them: Don't go in to spy. Omnis homo in hac vita peregrinus est: in qua vita videtis quia carne circumtegimur, per quam carnem cor videri non potesr. Ideo Apostolus dicit: Nolite ante tempus quidquam indicare, quoadusque veniat Dominus, et illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit cogitationes cordis, et tune laus erit unicuique a Deo (1 Cor 4,5). Antequam hoc fiat, in hac peregrinatione carnalis vitae quisque cor suum portat, et omne cor omni cordi clausum est. Proinde isti quorum consilia adversus hunc in malum, incolent, et abscondent; Quia in this peregrinatione sunt et carnem portant, dolum tegunt in corde, quidquid mali cogitant abscondunt. Quare? Quia adhuc peregrina est vita ista. Abscondant; apparebit quod abscondunt, et ipsi non abscondentur. Est et in hoc abscondito alius intellectus, qui fortasse magis placebit. Etenim ex iis qui longe facti sunt a sanctis, subintrant quídam ficti, et peiores tribulationes faciunt corpori Christi, quia non tanquam penitus alieni devitantur. Ab ipsis pericula graviora comme-

morans Apostolus, cum enumeraret fines passiones suas, et diceret, Periculis fluminum, periculis latronum, periculis ex genere, periculis ex gentibus, periculis in civitate, periculis in deserto, periculis in mari: Periculis, inquit, in falsis fratribus (2 Cor 11:26). Hi nimis periculosi sunt, de quibus dicitur in alio psalmo: Et ingrediebantur ut viderent (Ps 40,7). Ingrediebantur ut viderent, et nemo dicit: Non intres ut videos. Intrat etenim tanquam tuus, non cavetur ut alienus. Isti ergo incolent, et abscondent. Certainly morany hide in such a way that they glimpse where man falls. They are attentive to the heel; They observe the slip to prepare the foot for the fall or to subject him to the stumble in order to find something to accuse him of. And who walks in such a way that he never slips? Without a doubt, this frequently happens especially with the language. For it was written: If anyone does not stumble with his tongue, he is a perfect man. And who will dare to say or think that he is a perfect man? Therefore it cannot but happen that man does not sometimes stumble over his tongue. Those who dwell in passing and hide lie in wait for every word, try to lay snares everywhere and raise cunning accusations, with which they entangle themselves before entangling those who try. So they themselves are caught and perish before they catch and lose the others. Indeed, the (good) man enters his heart and here he welcomes God and knows how to say: In God I will exalt my words. Everything good, everything true that I spoke, I said from God and proceeding from God. Everything that I perhaps said that I should not have said, I said as a man, but under the permission of God. He who gives strength to the lieentur, dixerunt: Cum dormeremus, venerunt discipuli eius, et abstulerunt eum (Mt 28:13). Such autem caeci weret Iudaei, ut crederent dicto omnino incredibili: crediderunt testibus dormientibus! Aut falsum erat quod dormierunt, et mendacibus credere non debuerunt: aut verum erat quod dormierunt, et quod factum est nescierunt. Incolent, et abscondent. Incolant, et abscondant: quid facturi? Ergo necesse est ut aliquis labatur in lingua. lili autem qui incolent et abscondent, aucupantur verba omnia, quaetentes alicubi laqueos et nodosas faceré slanders, quibus prius ipsi implicantur quam quos implicare contendunt; ut prius ipsi capiantur et pereant, quam alios capiant ut perdant. You will save them in such a way that it will not cost you anything, that is, it will not involve any work for you. It is a desperate case for men, but you cure them with words. You will not work healing even when we marvel at it. This verse you will save them for nothing has another meaning. Heleah: you will not save them by any previous merit of theirs, for the Apostle says: I was first a blasphemer, a persecutor, a harmer. He received letters or documents from the priests so that wherever he found Christians he would arrest them and take them to Jerusalem. Certainly to capture and drive he lived before passing and hid. Therefore no good merit on his part had preceded him; On the contrary, they had preceded such that they deserved condemnation. He presented no good, and yet he was saved. You will save them for nothing. They do not offer you goats, rams, bulls; nor do they bring offerings and incense to the temple nor do they pour out the liquor of a good conscience; Everything about them is acrid, infected, abominable, and when they do not present you with anything by which you can save them, you will save them for nothing, that is, your grace is given freely. What had the thief carried the cross? See him go from the crossroads to the court, from the court to the cross, from the cross to paradise. He believed, so he spoke. As you gave me life, that is why I declare my life to you. But does God ignore what he gives? What do you declare to God? Do you intend to teach God? In no way. Then why does he say I manifested to you? Perhaps because it is advantageous to God to manifest my life to Him? But what does it profit God? Man takes advantage of the riches of God. I manifested my life to God because God gave me life. How the apostle Saint Paul manifested his life, saying: First I was a blasphemer, a persecutor, a harmer! Manifest your life and say: I obtained mercy. He did not manifest his life to himself, but to God; because it was manifested to him in such a way that he believed; then he did it not seeking his own interest, but that of God. Well, what does it add? Christ died and rose again so that whoever lives no longer lives for himself, but for Him who died for all. Therefore, if you live and do not live for yourself, since He gave you life, manifest -

celebrate your life, not to yourself, but to Him, without seeking your own interests, without living for yourself, but for Him who died for all. Well, what does the Apostle say about certain reproaches? Everyone seeks their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ. If you manifest your life so that it benefits you and not others, you manifest yourself, not God. On the contrary, if you manifest your life in such a way as to induce others to receive the life that you received, you manifest your life to Him from whom you received it, and you will have a great reward, because you were not ungrateful for having received it. Oh God, I will manifest my life to you. You placed my tears in your presence. You heard me pleading. According to your promise. Because just as you promised you kept it. You said that you should listen to him who cries. I believed, I cried: I was heard; I found you merciful in promising, true in giving, according to your promise. 15 [v. 10]. Let my enemies turn back. This benefits them; I do not wish them harm. Indeed, they want to go ahead, that's why they don't want to correct themselves. You admonish your enemy to live well, to correct himself; He despises you, rejects your word. Look who admonishes me, look from whom I have to hear the instructions by which I live! He wants to precede you (your enemy), and by preceding you he does not correct himself. Don't pay attention to the fact that your words are not yours; It does not pay attention to the fact that you manifest your life to God and not to yourself. Preceding you do not want to correct yourself. It would be a good thing for him to stand behind and follow the one he wanted to precede. Deus, vitam meam enuntiavi tibi. Posuisti lacrymas meas in conspectu tuo. Exaudisti me deptecantem te. Sicut et in repromissione tua. Quia sic promiseras, hoc egisti. Praecedere te vult, et praecendo non corrigitur. Non attendet quia verba tua non sunt tua; non attendit quia vitam tuam Deo enuntias, non tibi. such a thing. He who a short time before had said: You are Christ, the Son of the living God, confessing him for God, feared that he would die as a man. The Lord, who had come to suffer, since we could in no way be saved if we were not redeemed with his blood, a little earlier praised Peter's confession and said to him: It was not flesh and blood that revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. Therefore, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not overcome it; and I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven. See how he rewarded the true, pious, and faith-filled confession: You are Christ, the Son of the living God. On the contrary, shortly afterwards, when the Lord began to speak of his passion, Peter, fearing that he would perish by dying, whereas we would have perished if he had not died, says: Do not think such a thing, O Lord; this will not happen. But the Lord answered him who had said shortly before: Blessed are you (Peter); and: On this rock I will build my Church; Go back, satan; You are my stumbling block. Then why does he now call Satan the one who shortly before called him blessed and a stone? Because you don't feel my things, but those of man. Shortly before he felt the things of God (for it was said to him): For flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. When he praised the word in God, it was not Satan, but Peter coming from stone. But when, carried away by human weakness, he praised himself with the carnal love of man, being an obstacle to his health and that of others, he was called Satan. Because? Because he wanted to precede the Lord and give worldly advice to the Head of heaven: Do not think such a thing, he says, oh Lord! this will not happen. You say: Do not think such a thing, and you add: Tu es Christus Filias Dei vivi, confessus Deum, timuit eum mori quasi hominem. Dominus autem qui sic venerat ut pateretur, ñeque enim aliter salvi esse possemus, nisi eius sanguine redimeremur, paulo ante confessionem Petri laudaverat, et dixerat: Quia non tibi caro et sanguis revelavit hoc, sed Pater meus qui in caelis est. Propterea tu es Petrus, et super istam petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam; et tibi dabo keys regni caelorum.

Videte quemadmodum prosecutus est confessionem veram, piam, plenam fiduciae, quia dixit, Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi. Continuo autem ubi coepit loqui Dominus de passione sua, timuit ille ne periret moriendo, cum ipsi nos periremus nisi ille moreretur; et ait, Absit, Domine, non fiet istud. Et Dominus illi, cui paulo ante dixerat, Beatus es, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, Redi, inquit, retro satanás, scandalum mihi est. Quare ergo satan, qui paulo ante beatus et petra? Non enim sapis quae mei sunt, ait, sed quae sunt hominis (Mt 16:16-23). Paulo ante quae Dei: quia non revelavit tibi caro et sanguis, sed Pater meus qui in caelis est. Quando in Deo laudabat sermonem, non satanás, sed Petrus a petra: quando autem a se, et ex humano infirmitate, amore hominis carnali, quod impedimento esset saluti ipsius et caeterorum, satanás dictus est. Quare? Quia praecedere Dominum volebat, et Duci caelesti terrenum

Let my enemies turn back, but do not stay behind. They turn back in such a way that they do not precede; turn back, but continue, not parking. Let my enemies turn back. 16. On any day that I called upon you, behold, I knew that you are my God. Excellent knowledge! It does not say: I knew that you are God, but: that you are my God. It is yours when it helps you; It is yours when you are not a stranger to Him. Hence it is said: Blessed are the people who have God as their Lord. Why do you say you have it? Who doesn't have it? No wonder it does not please foreign children, who are far from the saints, because they lack the light of the living, by which they can see what pleases God. The light of the living is the light of the immortals, the light of the saints. He who does not live in darkness delights in the light of the living. Man and the things that are in him are measured, and no one knows him; only God sees what it is like. Sometimes it is also hidden from the devil, and, unless

tempts him, he will not know him, as happened with him whom I commemorated little. God knew him and bore witness to him. The devil did not know him, and that is why he said: Does Job praise God gratuitously? See where the enemy tempts, where there is perfection. Observe how the enemy objects. He saw that man served God, that he obeyed him in all things, that he worked well in everything; And since his household was rich and happy, he argues that he worships God because he had given him all these goods. And he says: Does Job praise God freely? This was the true light, the light of the living; praise God freely. God saw his free worship in the heart of his servant. That heart pleased in the presence of the Lord in the light of the living; but he hid himself from the devil, because he was in darkness. God allowed the tempter to enter, not so that He could know what He already knew, but so that we could know Him and offer us an example of imitation. Perhaps, if the tempter had not been allowed to tempt, would we have known in Job what we should do and want to imitate? The tempter was allowed entry; He took away all his possessions, he was left alone, devoid of everything, without family, without children, without God. However, he reserved the wife for him. Do you think that the devil was merciful because he kept the wife for him? He knew that Adam was deceived by her. She left him her helper (from the devil), not her husband's comforter. He was full of God and had within him the vows that he should offer in praise of God to demonstrate that he worshiped Him freely and not because he had received such immense riches from Him. Now, brothers, we have heard in the gospel how much we love our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, God with the Father and man with us, who is absent from us and will now be seated at the right hand of the Father.
