Hear how the Father resurrected him: according to the Apostle, he became obedient to death, even death on a cross; Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him a name that is above every name. You heard how the Father resurrects and exalts the Son. Hear how He Himself resurrects His flesh, for He says transeat iniquitas: id est, you protect me, et ut ab aestu iniquitatis non arescam, tu umbraculum praebebis mihi. 7 [v.3]. Clamabo ad Deum altissimum. If altissimus is here, how can we audit you? Nata est experiment fiducia: Deum, inquit, qui benefecit mihi. Si antequam eum quaererem benefecit mihi, clamantem me non exaudiet? Bene enim nobis fecit Dominus Deus mittendo nobis Salvatorem nostrum Iesum Christum, ut moreretur propter delicta nostra, et resurgeret propter iustificationem nostram (Rom 4:25). Pro qualibus mori voluit Filium suum? Pro impiis. Impii autem non quaerebant Deum, et quaesiti sunt a Deo. Sic est ergo ille altissimus, ut non sit ab illo longe miseria nostra et gemitus nostet; quia prope est Dominus his qui obtriverunt cor (Ps 33,19). Clamabo ad Deum altissimum, Deum qui benefecit mihi. 8 [v.4.5]. Misit de cáelo, et salvum fecit me.

Iam homo ipse, iam caro ipsa, iam Filius Dei, secundum nostram participationem manifestum est, quia salvatus est, et misit de cáelo Patet, et salvavit eum; misit de cáelo et resuscitavit eum: sed ut noveritis quia et ipse Dominus se resuscitavit; utrumque positum est in Scriptura, quia et Pater illum resuscitavit, et quia ipse se resuscitavit. Audite quia Pater illum resuscitavit: Apostolus dicit, Factus est, inquit, obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis: propter quod et Deus eum exaltavit, et donavit ei nomen quod est super omne nomen (Phil 2,8.9). Audistis Patrem resuscitantem et exaltantem Filium; audite quia et ipse carnem suam resuscitavit:

to the Jews under the symbolism of the temple: Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. The evangelist explained the meaning of these words by adding: And he said this about the temple of his body. Then now he says in person of the one who supplicates, in person of man, representing the flesh: He sent from heaven and saved me. 9. He covered those who trampled me with shame. He covered with shame those who despised him, those who reviled him when he was dead, those who crucified him as a man, because they did not know him as God. See if it has been fulfilled. We no longer believe it as coming, but as fulfilled. The Jews became angry in Christ, they became arrogant against Christ. Where? In the city of Jerusalem. Where they reigned, there they became arrogant, there they became arrogant. After the passion of the Lord they were thrown out of there and lost the kingdom in which they did not want to recognize Christ as king. In what way were they covered with shame? See it: he dispersed them throughout all the nations, without being stable and lacking a fixed residence. Therefore, it is the Jews who, to their confusion, carry our books around. When we want to demonstrate to the pagans that Christ was prophesied, we present these writings to them. And so that, as opposed to the faith, they do not say that Christians composed these prophetic writings, so that with the Gospel that we preach we have devised the prophecies by which what we preach is predicted, we show them that all these writings in which Christ was prophesied are found in the books of the Jews and all these writings are preserved by the Jews. We present the codices of the enemies in figura templi dicit ad Iudaeos, Solvite templum hoc, et in triduo suscitabo illud. Evangelista autem exposuit nobis quid dicetet: Hoc autem, inquit, dicebat de temple corporis sui (lo 2,19.21). Modo ergo ex persona precantis, ex persona hominis, ex petsona carnis dicit, Misit de cáelo, et salvum fecit me. 9. Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me. Qui illum conculcaverunt, qui mortuo insultaverunt, qui tanquam hominem crucifixetunt, quia Deum non intellexetunt, dedit eos in opprobrium. Videte si non est factum: non futurum credimus, sed completum agnoscimus. Saevietunt Iudaei in Christum, superbierunt in Christum: ubi? In civitate Ierusalem. Ubi enim regnabant, ibi tumebant, ibi cervices erexerunt. Post passionem Domini eradicati inde sunt; et perdiderunt regnum, in quo tegem Chtistum agnoscere noluerunt.

Quemadmodum dad sunt in opptobfium, videte: dispersi sunt per omnes gentes, nusquam habentes stabilitatem, nusquam certam sedem. Proptetea autem adhuc Iudaei sunt, ut Libros nostros portent ad confusionem suam. Quando enim volumus ostendere prophetatum Christum, proferimus Paganis istas Litteras. Et ne forte dicant duri ad fidem quia nos illas Christiani composuimus, ut eum Gospel quod praedicamus finxerimus Prophetas, per quos praedictum videretur quod praedicamus; hinc eos convincimus quia omnes ipsae Litterae quibus Christus prophetatus est, apud Iudaeos sunt, omnes ipsas

to confuse other enemies. What disgrace are the Jews covered with? The Jew treasures the codex by which the Christian believes. They are our booksellers; They become like the servants who usually carry the codices after their masters, so that they get tired carrying them and the masters take advantage of them by reading them. The Jews were covered with such disgrace. Thus what was prophesied so long before was fulfilled. He covered those who trampled me with shame. What more disgrace, brothers, than to read this little verse and, blind, look in your mirror? The Jews behave with the holy Scriptures that they guard like the face of the blind man behaves in the mirror: it is seen by others, they do not see it. He covered those who trampled me with shame. 10. Perhaps you were asking when he said: He sent from heaven and saved me: What did he send from heaven? Who did he send from heaven? Did he send an angel to save Christ, and thus through a servant did he cause the Lord to be saved? All angels are creatures that serve Christ. The angels could have been sent to entertain, to serve, but not to help. For it is written: And the angels served him; not as merciful to a needy person, but as servants submitted to the Almighty. So, what does it mean that He sent from heaven and saved me? We recently heard in the next verse of the same psalm what he sent from heaven: He sent from heaven his mercy and his truth. And for what? To get my soul out of the midst of the lion cubs. He sent—he says—his mercy and his truth from heaven. Christ himself says: I am the

true. He sent his truth to take my soul from here, from among the lions' cubs; then his mercy was sent. Christ is mercy and truth: mercy sympathizing, truth repaying. This is the same thing I said a little earlier, namely, that he rose from the dead. If the truth raised Christ and the truth delivered the soul of Christ from the midst of the lions' cubs, then he was merciful in dying for us and truthful in rising to justify us. He had said that he would rise again, and the truth could not lie; and since it is true and truthful, that is why it manifested true scars, because it endured true wounds. The disciples saw them, they touched them; These scars were shown to them, and that is why the one who put his fingers into the wounded heart exclaimed: My Lord and my God! Out of mercy he died for him; and, likewise, it was truly resurrected for him. He sent his mercy and his truth from heaven and delivered my soul from the midst of the lions' cubs. Who are the lion cubs? The lowly people, badly deceived and seduced by the princes of the Jews. These were the lions, and those were the cubs. They all roared, they all killed him. We must also hear their death here now in the following verses. 11. And he brought out or delivered my soul from the midst of the lions' cubs. Why do you say: And he delivered your soul? What would you have to suffer to free your soul? Disturbed, I fell asleep. With this Christ manifested his death. We read of David that he fled to the cave, but not that he fell asleep in it. A David is the one who

Litteras habent Iudaei. Proferimus Codices ab inimicis, ut confundamus alios inimicos. In quali ergo opprobrio sunt Iudaei? Codicem portat Iudaeus, unde credat Christianus. Librarii nostri facti sunt, quomodo solent serví post dominos codices ferré, ut illi portando deficiant, illi legendo proficiant. In tale opprobrium dati sunt Iudaei; et impletum est quod both ante praedictum est: Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me. Quale autem opprobrium est, fratres, ut hunc versum legant, et ipsi caeci attendant ad speculum suum? Sic enim apparent Iudaei de Scriptura sancta quam portant, quomodo apparet facies caeci de speculo: ab alus videtur, ab ipso non videtur. Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me. 10. Quaerebas forte cum diceret, Misit de cáelo, et salvum me fecit: Quid misit de cáelo? quem misit de cáelo? Angelum misit, ut salvum faceret Christum, et per servum salvus fit Dominus? Omnes enim Angelí creatura serviens Christo est. Ad obsequium mitti potuerunt Angelí, ad servitium mitti potuerunt, non ad adiutorium: sicut scriptum est, quod Angelí ministrabant ei (Mt 4,11), non tanquam misericordes indigenti, sed tanquam subiectí omnipotenti. Quid ergo misit de cáelo, et salvum fecit me? Modo audimus in allio versu quid de cáelo miserit: Misit de cáelo misericordiam suam et veritatem suam. Ad quam rem? Et eruit animam meam de medio catulorum leonum. Misit, inquit, de cáelo misericordiam suam et veritatem suam: et ipse Christus ait, Ego sum

veritas (lo 14,6). Missa est ergo veritas, ut erueret animam meam hinc de medio catulorum leonum; missa est mercy. Ipsum Christum invenimus et misericordiam et veritatem; Misericordiam nobis compatientem, et veritatem nobis retribuentem. Hoc est ergo quod paulo ante dixi, quia et ipse se resuscitavit. Si enim veritas resuscitavit Christum, et si veritas animam Christi eruit de medio catulorum leonum; ut misericors Fuit mori pro nobis, ita verax Fuit resurgere ad iustificandos nos. Dixerat enim se resurrecturum, et veritas lyingi non potuit; et quia veritas et verax, propterea scars veras ostendit, quia vera vulnera pertulit. You have scars tenuerunt discipuli, palpaverunt, manifestaverunt sibi; exclamavit qui misit digits in compunctum latus, et ait, Dominus meus et Deus meus (Ib. 20,28). Misericordia pro illo mortuus erat, et veritate ad illum resurrexerat. Misit de cáelo misericordiam suam et veritatem suam: et eruit animam meam de medio catulorum leonumQui sunt catuli leonum? Populus ille minutus, male deceptus, male seductus a principibus Iudaeorum: ut illi leones, illi catuli leonum. Omnes fremuerunt, omnes occiderunt. Audituri enim sumus hic et caedem ípsorum, moda in consequentibus versibus psalmi huius. 11. Et eruit, inquit, animam meam de medio catulorum leonum. Quare dicis, Et eruit animam meam? Quid enim passus eras, ut erueretur anima tua? Dormivi conturbatus. Expressit Christus mortem suam. Certe de illo David legimus quod fugerit in speluncam, non tamen quia

is in the cave and another one who says: Troubled, I fell asleep. We know your disturbance. It was not he who was troubled, but they. But he said that he was disturbed by the feelings of those who bellowed, but not by the opinion of the wounded man. They thought they had disturbed him, they thought they had defeated him; but he fell asleep troubled. This disturbed man was so calm that, when he wanted to, he fell asleep. No one sleeps when disturbed. All those who are disturbed, or awake, or cannot fall asleep. But he, troubled, fell asleep. Great abjection is that of the disturbed, great power is that of the one who sleeps (in such circumstances). From what power did sleep come? Of the power he made known: I have power to lay down my life and power to take it again. Nobody takes it away from me; I hand it over and take it again. They were disturbed and he fell asleep. Adam was a figure of him when God gave him sleep to form his wife from his side. Could he not form the wife for the first man from the side of the awakened man? Or did he want him to be asleep so that he wouldn't feel pain when his rib was pulled out? Well, who sleeps so deeply that when a bone is pulled out, he doesn't wake up? He who could painlessly extract the rib from the sleeping person, could extract it from the awake person. But why did he want to do it while he was asleep? Because, Christ sleeping on the cross, the bride was formed at his side. When the side of Christ hanging from the cross was wounded with the spear, the sacraments of the Church emerged. “I fell asleep,” he says, “disturbed.” In another psalm he declares this same thing when he says: I fell asleep and took sleep. In this ma-

He does not celebrate his power. He could have said there: I slept, as he said in the psalm we discussed. But what does it mean: I fell asleep but I slept because I wanted to? They did not force me to go to sleep without my wanting it, but by my will I fell asleep, according to that: I have the power to give my life and to take it again. Therefore, that psalm continues and says: I fell asleep and took sleep, and I rose up, because the Lord sustained me. 12. I fell asleep disturbed. How disturbed? Disturbed by who? Let's see how the bad conscience betrays the Jews, who wanted to excuse themselves from the death of the Lord. According to the Gospel, they handed him over to the judge so as not to appear criminals. But when the judge Pilate said to them: Take him and judge him according to your law, they answered: We are not permitted to kill anyone. Is it not allowed to kill, and is it allowed to kill? Who then killed him? Who, hearing the shouting, bowed down, or who, shouting for him to be killed, achieved it by force? The Lord himself testifies by whom he was killed, whether by the Jews or by Pilate, that he did not want to kill him, and that is why he scourged him, clothed him in ignominy and, scourged, presented him before the Jews so that, at least satisfied with the scourging, they would not force him to kill him; but, seeing that they persevered in their attempt, as we read, he washed his hands and said: I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; Therefore you will understand that, if the one who gave in to the shouting was not innocent, much less

dorrnivit in spelunca. Alius David est in spelunca, alius David est qui dicit, Dormivi conturbatus. Videmus perturbationem ipsius; non illo turbato, sed lilis turbantibus. Turbatum se enim dixit, secundum opinionem frementium, non secundum cedentis conscientiam. Putaverunt se illi turbasse, putaverunt vicisse: ille autem dormivit conturbatus. Tam plaquetus erat iste turbatus, ut when vellet, sleepet. Nemo dormit turbatus: omnes qui perturbantur, aut a somno excitantur, aut in somnum vergi non permittuntur. lile autem turbatus est, et dormivit. Magna humilitas perturban, magna potestas doimientis. De que potestate veniebat quod dormivit? De qua ipse dicit: Potestatem drooling Pondi animam meam, et potestatem drooling sumendi eam: nemo tollit eam a me; sed ego eam pono, et iterum samo eam (lo 10,18). Turbaverunt illi, et dormivit ipse. Cuius typum gerebat Adam, quando immisit ei Deus soporem, ut de latere illi coniugem faceret (Gen 2:21). Num enim non poterat uxorem faceré primo homini etiam de latere vigilantis? aut propterea voluit eum I'll sleep, don't feel with sibi costa detraheretur? Postremo, quis ita dormit, ut osse sibi convulso non expergiscatur? Qui potuit sine dolore auferre costam dormienti, potuit et vigilante. Sed quare voluit dormienti facete? Quia dormienti Christo in intersection facta est coniux de latere. Percussum is enim latus pendentis de lancea (lo 19,34), et profiuxerunt Ecclesiae Sacramenta. I slept, restless, conturbatus. Et in alio psalmo manifestat hoc, ubi ait: Ego dormivi, et

somnum cepi. Ibi expressit potestatem suam. Poterat et illic dicere, Dormivi, sicut dixit hic. Quid est autem, Ego dormivi? Id est, quia volui, dormivi. Non illi me in somnum nolentem compulerunt; sed mea volúntate ego dormivi, secundum illud: Potestatem drool ponendi animam meam, et potestatem drool iterum sumendi eam. Propterea ibi sequitur et dicit: Ego dormivi, et somnum cepi; et exsurrexi, quoniam Dominus suscipiet me (Ps 3,6). 12. Dormivi conturbatus. Unde turbatus? quibus turbantibus? Videamus quomodo inurat malam conscientiam Iudaeis, volentibus excusare se ab intetfectione Domíni. Nam propterea eum, sicut loquitur Evangelium, iudici tradiderunt, ne ipsi eum occidisse viderentur. Cum enim dixisset eis iudex tune Pilatus, Acápite eum vos, et secundum legem vestram iudicate eum; responderunt, Nobis non licet interficere quemquam (lo 18,31). Interficere non licet, tradere interficiendum licet? Quis autem occidit? Qui audio clamore cessit, an qui clamando ut occideretur extorsit? Ipse Dominus dicat testimonium a quibus occisus est, utrum ab illo Pilato qui nolens eum occidit: unde etiam eum flagellavit, et veste ignominiosa induit, et flagellatum ad eotum oculos produxit, ut saltem poena flagellorum eius satiati, eum occidi non extorquerent. Propterea etiam cum videtet eos perseverare, sicut legimus, lavit manus suas, et dixit: Innocens ego sum a sanguine iusti huius (Mt 27,24). Videris utrum ille innocens, qui vel cessit clamantibus: multo magis tamen illi nocentes, qui clamando eum occidere voluerunt. Sed us interrogemus et audiamus

They were the ones who shouted and wanted to kill him. Let us ask and listen to the Lord to whom he attributed his death, for he said: Troubled, I fell asleep. Let us ask him and say: How did you fall asleep troubled? Who chased you? Who killed you? Was it Pilate, who handed you over to the soldiers to suspend you from the tree, to impale you with nails? Hear who: The sons of men. He says that these were the persecutors he endured. But how did those who didn't carry weapons kill him? How did those who did not draw the sword, those who did not fall on Him to kill Him, kill Him? His teeth are weapons and arrows, and his tongue is a sharp sword. Don't look at the helpless hands, but at the armed mouth; From here came the sword that burned Christ, just as from the mouth of Christ came the sword that killed the Jews. Well, He also has a two-stranded sword. When he resurrected, he wounded them and separated them from those whom he made his faithful. They had the bad sword, He the good one. They the bad arrows, He the good ones. Well, He also has good arrows; Good words are those that attack the faithful heart so that it loves Him. Therefore there are some of their arrows and another of their swords. The sons of men (are the persecutors), and their teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword. The tongue of the sons of men is a sharp sword, and their teeth are weapons and arrows. When were you injured? When they shouted: Crucify, crucify him! 13 [v. 6]. And to you, what did they do to you, oh Lord? Now the prophet is already rejoicing. Previously, the Lord spoke all the verses. That is, the prophet spoke, but in person of the SeDominum, quibus tribuat mortem suam, quia dixit, Dormivi turbatus. Interrogemus eum, et dicamus: Quoniam dormisti turbatus, qui te persecuti sunt? who occiderunt you? Numquid forte Pilatus, who militibus dedit in ligno suspendendum, clavis transfigendum? Audite qui: Filii hominum. Illos utique dicit, quos persecutors passus est. Sed quomodo ipsi occiderunt, qui ferrum non ferebant? Qui gladium non strinxerunt, qui impetum in eum non fecerunt ad occidendum, unde occiderunt? Dentes eorum arma et sagittae, et lingua eorum gladius acutus. Noli attendere inermes manus, sed os armatum: inde gladius processit quo Christus occideretur; quomodo et de ore Christi, unde et Iudaei occiderentur.

Habet enim ille gladium bis acutum (Rev 1,16): et resurgens percussit eos, et divisit ab eis quos faceret fideles suos. lili malum gladium, ille bonum: illi saginas malas, ille bonas. Nam habet et ipse sagittas bonas, verba bona, unde sagittat cor fidele, ut ametur. Ergo aliae istorum sagittae, et alius istorum gladius. Filii hominum dentes eorum arma et sagittae, et lingua eorum machaera acuta. Lingua filiorum hominum machaera acuta, et dentes eorum arma et sagittae. Quando ergo percusserunt, nisi quando clamaverunt: Crucifige, crucifige? (Mt 27,4, et lo 19,6). 13 [v.6}. Et quid tibi fecerunt, o Domine? Exsultet hic Propheta. Superius enim omnes illos versus Dominus locobatur: Propheta quidem, sed ex persona Domini, quia in Propheta Dominus. Et when loquitur

Lord, because the Lord was prefigured in the prophet. Also, when the prophet speaks in his own person, the Lord himself speaks through the prophet and suggests to him the truth that he proclaims. Now therefore, my brothers, hear the prophet speak in his own person. This prophet saw in spirit the Lord humiliated, beaten, whipped, punched, slapped, spit upon, crowned with thorns, suspended on the cross; He also saw the Jews being cruel, Him tolerating; to them jumping for joy, to Him defeated. But after all that humiliation and the fury of the Jews he saw him resurrected, and he saw how all those things that the Jews perpetrated were in vain. For this reason, rejoicing as if he saw it already accomplished, he says: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens. Man on the cross and God above the heavens. Let the angry people stay on earth, you be in heaven judging. Where are those who were angry? Where are their teeth, which were weapons and arrows? Weren't the wounds they caused like those of children's arrows? In another psalm he says this same thing, wanting to show them that they were vainly angry and futilely angry, because they could not do anything to the man crucified in an instant, who was later resurrected and sat in heaven, since his wounds were like those caused by the children's arrows. What do children make their arrows? Of reeds. And what arrows are they? What strength do they have? What bow? What aim? And what injuries do they cause? May you be exalted, O God, above the heavens, and your glory (spread) throughout the earth. Why are you exalted, O God, above the heavens? We do not see, brothers, God exalted above the heavens, but we believe it. May your glory be found ex persona sua Propheta, ipse Dominus loquitur per rum, qui ei dictat veritatem quam loquatur. Modo ergo ex persona Proplictae audite, fratres mei. Vidit Dominum in Spititu iste propheta humiliatum, caesum, flagellatum, colaphis peteussum, expalmatum manibns, sputis illitum, spinis coronatum, ligno suspensum; illos saevientes, illum tolerantem; illos exsultantes, illum quasi victum vidit in Spititu: et post illam iam omnem humiliationem, et illorum furorem resurrexisse eum, et illa omnia quae fecerant Iudaei saevientes facta esse inania; et elatus gaudio, tanquam videret fieri, Exaltare, inquit, super cáelos, Deus.

Homo in ctuce, et supet cáelos Deus. Remaneant in terra saevientes, tu in cáelo esto judicans. Ubi sunt qui furebant? ubi sunt dentvs eorum arma et sagittae? Nonne sagittae infantium factae sunt pestae vorum? Alio enim loco psalmus hoc dicit, volens eos ostendere inaniter.incvisse, et inaniter in furias praecipitatos esse: quoniam nihil potuerunt faceré Christo ad horam crucifixo, et postea resurgenti, atque in cáelo sedenti, sagittae infantium factae sunt plaguee eorum (Ps 63,8). Quomodo infantes faciunt sibi sagittas? From cannis. Sagittae autem quae? aut quae vires? aut qui arcus? aut qui stroke? aut quod vulnus? I will exalt super caelos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua. Utquid exaltaris super caelos Deus? Frattes, exaltatum Deum super cáelos, non videmus, sed ctedimus: super omnem autem tetram gloriam eius non tantum ctedimus, sed

spread throughout the earth, we not only believe it, but we see it. I beg you to observe the madness that invades heretics. They, separated from the union of the Church of Christ, retaining a part and losing the whole, do not want to communicate with the world, in which the glory of Christ is spread. We Catholics are throughout the earth, because we communicate with the entire earth, in which the glory of Christ is spread. We see, then, that what was announced then is now fulfilled. Our God was exalted above the heavens and his glory (is spread) over all the earth. Oh heretical madness! What you don't see, you believe with me, and what you see, you deny. You believe that Christ was exalted above the heavens, which we do not see. And you deny what we see, that his glory is spread throughout the earth. May you be exalted, O God, above the heavens, and over all the earth (let your glory spread). 14 [v. 7]. Now the psalmist takes the word again into the mouth of the Lord, and the Lord himself begins to narrate to us as if consoling us after the prophet had rejoiced and said: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens, and your glory (spread) over all the earth. The Lord himself gives us courage, as if telling us: See. What could those who persecuted me do with me? Why does it comfort us? Because they do it to us too. But those who also persecute us do nothing. See in your charity how the Lord speaks to us and exhorts us with his example. They set a trap for my feet and brought down my soul. They wanted to dethrone her from heaven and bring her down to earth: They humbled my soul. They dug a grave in front

from me and they fell into it. Did they harm me or harm themselves? God was exalted above the heavens, and his glory is spread throughout the earth. We see the kingdom of Christ. Where is that of the Jews? Because they did what they should not do, what they should suffer came upon them. They dug the pit, and fell into it. It did not harm Christ to have been persecuted by them, but rather them. And do not think, brothers, that this happened only to them; Anyone who prepares a hole for his brother necessarily falls into it. Pay attention, brothers, and look with Christian eyes so that you are not amazed by visible things. Perhaps because I said this it now occurs to some of you who wanted to defraud his brother, who wanted to prepare plots for him, who prepared them and carried them out, that the brother fell into them and was stripped of his property, or oppressed either by torture, now by false testimony, or surrounded by an infamous accusation, and that, therefore, when it appears that this one was subjugated and the other subjugated, that this one was defeated and the other conquered, you judge what I said to be false, that Anyone who prepares a pit for his brother falls into it himself. I invite you to consider this as Christians so that you take the example of the things we know. The pagans persecuted the martyrs, and they were captured, bound, imprisoned, and thrown to the beasts; some wounded with the sword, others burned by fire. Did the persecutors win and were the martyrs defeated? There is no such thing. Why is the glory of the martyrs exalted before God, why is the pit of the pagans dug in the conscience detested? And I say in the conscience because the hole where it falls

etiam videmus. Qualem verum vesaniam patiantur haeretici, quaeso ut attendatis. lili praecisi a compagine Ecclesiae Christi, et partem tenentes, totum amittentes, nolunt communicare orbi terrarum, qua diffusa est gloria Christi. Nos autem Catholici in omni terra sumus, quia omni terrae communicamus quacumque gloria Christi diffusa est. Videmus enim quod tune cantatum est, moda completum. Exaltatus est super cáelos Deus noster, et super omnem terram gloria ipsius. O haeretica insanity! Quod non vides credis mecum, quod vides negas: credis mecum exaltatum Christum super caelos, quod non videmus; et negas gloriam eius super omnem terram, quod videmus. I will exalt super caelos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua. 14 [v.7]. Redit ad verba Domini: et ipse Dominus narrare nobis incipit, tanquam alloquens nos, exsultante etiam Propheta et dicente, Exaltare super cáelos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua. Confirmat nos et ipse, so they say nobis: Quid mihi faceré potuerunt illi qui me persecuti sunt? Quare autem nos alloquitur? Quia faciunt et nobis. Sed nihil faciunt qui nos similiter fuerint persecuti. Videat enim Charitas Vestra alloquentem nos Dominum, et exhortantem nos exemplo suo. Muscipulam paraverunt pedibus meis, et incurvaverunt animam meam. Voluerunt illam quasi de cáelo deponere, et ad inferiora deprimere: Curvaverunt animam meam. foderunt ante jaciem meam foveam,

et ipsi incidenterunt in eam. Mihi nocuerunt, an sibi? Ecce ille exaltatus est super cáelos Deus, et ecce super omnem terram gloria ipsius: regnum Christi videmus, ubi est regnum Iudaeorum? Quoniam ergo fecerunt quod faceré non debuerunt, factum est in illos quod pati debuerunt: ipsi foderunt foveam, et ipsi incidenterunt in eam. Quod enim persecuti sunt Christum, Christo non obfuit, sed ipsis obfuit. Et nolite putare, fratres, ipsis solis hoc accidisse. Omnis qui parat foveam fratri suo, necesse est ut ipse incidat in eam. Intendite, fratres mei, christianos oculos habete, nolite decipi visibilibus. Forte enim alicui vestrum, quia hoc dixi, subvenitmo aliquis qui voluit fratri suo fraudm faceré, et voluit ei aliquas insidias machinan, et machinatus est, et implevit, et cecidit frater in insidias eius, et spoliatus est, aut pressus est, sive carcere, sive false testimony, sive aliqua nefaria criminatione circumventus: videtur autem iste oppressus, ille oppressisse; iste victus, ille vicisse; et falsum putatur quod diximus, quoniam quicumque foveam paraverit fratri suo, ipse cadit in eam. Interrogo vos tanquam christianos, utsumatis exemplum de his quae iam novimus. Pagani persecuti sunt martyres, et martyres capti sunt, ligati sunt, in carcerem missi sunt, bestiis subrecti sunt, alii ferro percussi, alii ignibus concremati: vicerunt persequentes, et victi sunt mattyres? absit. the wicked is the bad conscience. Do you think that he who lost the light of Christ and became blind did not fall into the ditch? He would not have fallen into the pit if he had seen it before his eyes. He doesn't know where he's going. It happens to him like someone who, walking along the path, falls into the ditch and loses his way. You see how all the evildoers who got involved in crime lost their way. But perhaps you have already fallen into the hands of the thief, or into the hands of some wicked person or some judge bought by him; and you are in trouble and he rejoices and exults. I already said that you should not look with pagan eyes, but with Christian eyes. You see that he rejoices. This joy is their grave. Better is the sadness of him who endures wicked things than the joy of him who commits them. The joy of him who works wickedly is a pit; When someone falls there, they lose their eyes. You complain because you lost your dress, and don't you grieve for him who lost his faith? Which of the two suffered the most harm? See that he kills, you are killed. He lives, did you die? There is no such thing. Where is the faith of Christians? Where is he who dies temporarily? Hear your Lord: He who believes in me, even though he has died, lives. Therefore he who does not believe, even if he lives, is dead. They dug up the pit before me, and they fell into it. This necessarily happens to all bad people. 15 [v. 8]. The patience of the good gladly accepts the will of God and glories in tribulations, saying as follows: My heart is prepared, O God! my heart is prepared; I will sing and chant. What did he do to me? He prepared the grave for me; my heart is prepared. He prepared the pit for me

deceive me, and I will not prepare my heart to suffer? He prepared the pit for me to bring me down, and shall I not prepare my heart to tolerate him? Therefore he rushed into it; I will sing and salmear. Hear how the Apostle, who imitated his Lord, had his heart prepared: We glory, he says, in tribulations, because tribulation cultivates patience; patience, trial; Probation is hope, and hope does not confuse, because the charity of God has been spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. He was in the midst of afflictions, of chains, of prisons, of schemes, of hunger, of thirst, of cold, of nakedness, of all kinds of labor and pain, and he said: We glory in tribulations. Because? Because his heart was prepared. And, for the same reason, he sang and chanted: My heart is prepared, O God!; my heart is prepared; I will sing and chant. 16 [v. 9]. Arise, my glory. He who had fled from the presence of Saul taking refuge in the cave (says): Arise, my glory, that is, let Jesus be glorified after the passion. Arise, psaltery and zither. What invites you to get up? I see that it mentions two instruments, but the body of Christ is only one. One flesh was resurrected, and yet two organs were resurrected: the psaltery and the zither. All musical instruments are called organs. Organ is not only called the large instrument that is inflated with bellows, but also any instrument that adapts to the song and is corporeal, and which the singer uses. These instruments that we are talking about now are different from each other. I want, as soon as God gives me to understand, tell you how they are distinguished

quo cadit impius, in conscientia mala. Putas eum in foveam non cecidisse, qui luzem Christi perdidit et caecitate percussus est? Si non cadete in foveam, videret ante se: nescit qua eat; quomodo qui ambulat in via cum ceciderit in foveam, lost viam. Videtis ergo omnes malefactores perdidisse viam, implicatos facinore. Sed iam te tradidit in manus forte latronis, aut in manus alicuius iniusti vel circumventi a se iudicis: et tu in pressura es, ille laetatur, ille exsultat. Noli, iam dixi, noli habere oculos Paganorum: christianos oculos habe. Vides illum qui exsultat: ipsa exsultatio est fovea ipsius. Melior est enim tristitia iniqua patientis, quam laetitia iniqua facientis. Ipsa laetitia iniqua facientis, ipsa est fovea: illuc quisque cum ceciderit, oculos perdit. You hurt, quia perdidisti vestem; et illum non doles, quia perdidit fidem? Quis vestrum graviore damno percussus est? Ecce ille occidit, tu occideris: vivit ille, tu mortuus es? absit. Ubi est fides Christianorum? ubi est ille qui moritur ad tempus? Audiat Dominum suum: Qui credit in me, licet moriatur, vivit (lo 11.25). Ergo qui non credit, licet vivat, mortuus est. Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam, et ipsi incidenterunt in eam. Omnibus malis necesse est ut hoc contingat. 15 [v.8]. Bonorum autem patientia praeparatione cordis excipit voluntatem Dei, et gloriatur in tribulationibus, dices quod sequitur: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum; cantabo et psallam. Quid fecit mihi? Paravit foveam, cor meum paratum est. Ille paravit foveam

ad decipiendum, ego cor non parabo ad perpetiendum? Ule paravit foveam ad opprimendum, ego cor non parabo ad tolerandum? Propterea ille incidet in eam, ego autem cantabo et psallam. Audi cor paratum in Apostólo, quia imitatus est Dominum suum: Gloriamur, inquit, in tribulationibus; quia tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia probationem, probatio spem, spes vero non confundit: quia charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum qui datus est nobis (Rom 5,3-5). Erat in pressuris, in catenis, in carceribus, in plagis, in fame et siti, in frigore et nuditate, in omni vastatione laborum et dolorum (2 Cor 11:27), et dicebat: Gloriamur in tribulationibus. Unde, nisi quia paratum est cor eius? Ideo cantabat et psallebat: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum; cantabo et psallam. 16 [v.9]. Exsurge, gloria mea. Ule qui fugerat a facie Saül in speluncam, Exsurge, gloria mea, glorificetur Iesus post passionem. Exsurge, psalterium et cithara. Quid vocat, ut surgat? Duo organa video, Corpus autem Christi unum video: una caro resurrexit, et duo organa surrexerunt. Alterum ergo organum psalterium, alterum cithara. Organa dicuntur omnia instrumenta musicorum. Non solum illud organum dicitur, quod grande est, et inflatur follibus; sed quidquid aptatur ad cantilenam, et corporeum est, quo instrument utitur qui cantat, organum dicitur. Distincta sunt autem Inter se ista organa; et flew, quantum Dominus dat, indicare vobis, et quomodo distincta sunt, et quare distincta, et

and why; and also why it is said to both: Get up. We have already said that the flesh of the Lord was resurrected, and yet it is now said: Arise, psaltery and zither. The psaltery is an organ or musical instrument that has taut strings and is supported by the hands of the player; but the part where the strings acquire sound, that is, the concavity or wooden resonance box with which the psaltery is equipped and which resonates to the touch, because it collects the air, is located in the psaltery at the top. The zither, on the other hand, has its resonant wooden box at the bottom. Thus, in the psaltery the strings acquire the sound due to the upper part, and in the zither, to the lower part. In this, then, the psaltery and the zither differ. What do these two instruments symbolize to us? Jesus Christ, our Lord and God, plays his psaltery and his zither, and says: I will rise in the morning. I think you notice that it is about the resurrection of the Lord here. Let's read the Gospel; note the hour of the resurrection. Very early in the morning they were looking for Christ. He appeared; was recognized; He rose very early in the morning. But where is the psalter? Where is the zither? The Lord performed, through his flesh, two kinds of works; He performed miracles and endured suffering. Miracles came from above; the sufferings, below. The miracles he performed are divine works, but he performed them through the body, he performed them through the flesh. Therefore, the flesh working divine things is a psalter. The flesh suffering human things, it is a zither. When the psaltery is played, the blind see, the deaf hear, the paralyzed move, the lame walk, the sick are healed, the dead are raised; this is the sound of

psaltery. When the zither plays, Jesus is hungry, thirsty, sleeps; He is captured, whipped, abused, crucified and buried. When you hear that at one time something from above and from below sounded in the flesh, then observe that one flesh was resurrected, and in it let us recognize the psaltery and the zither. These two kinds of facts filled the Gospel and are preached to the people, since the miracles and sufferings of the Lord are announced to the world. 17 [ 10. 12 }. Then he resurrected the psaltery and the zither early in the morning and praised the Lord. And what does it say? I will praise you, O Lord, among the people and praise you among the nations, because your mercy has been magnified to the heavens, and your truth to the clouds. The heavens are above the clouds, and the clouds are under the heavens; and yet the clouds belong to this near sky. But sometimes the clouds rest on the mountains, in such a way that they gather over this air close to us. Heaven is above, and is the abode of angels, thrones, dominions, principalities and powers. It seems that perhaps it should have been said: Your truth was magnified to the heavens, and your mercy to the clouds. For, indeed, the angels praise God in heaven, contemplating the very beauty of the truth without a shadow of vision, without any admixture of falsehood: they see, they love, they praise without fatigue. There is the truth; here, in our misery, mercy. Mercy must be offered to the unfortunate, since in heaven, where there is no unfortunate person, mercy is not necessary. I said this because it seems that it could have been said more congruently: Your truth has been magnified to the heavens.

quare utrique dicatur, Exsurge. Iam diximus, an expensive Domini resurrected; et dícítur. Exsurge, psalterium et cithara. Psalterium est organum, quod quidem manibus fertur percutientis, et chordas disientas habet; sed illum locum unde sonum accipiunt chordae, illud concavum lignum quod pendet et tactum resonat, quia concipit aerem, psalterium in superiore parte habet. Cithara autem hoc genus ligni concavum et resonans in infetiore parte habet. Itaque in psalterio chordae sonum desuper accipiunt; in cithara autem chordae sonum ex inferiore parte accipiunt: hoc interest inter psalterium et citharam. Quid ergo duo haec organa nobis figurant? Excitat enim Christus Dominus Deus noster psalterium suum et citharam suam, et dicit, Exsurgam diluculo. Puto quia hic iam agnoscitis Dominum resurgentem. Legimus in Gospel: videte horam resurrectionis. Quamdiu per umbras quaerebatur Christus? Luxit, agnoscatur; I dilute resurrection (Mark 16,2). Sed quid est psalterium? what is cithara? Per carnem suam Dominum duo genera factotum operatus est, miracula et passiones: miracula de super fuerunt, passiones de inferiore fuerunt. Illa enim quae fecit miracula, divina weret; thirst per Corpus fecit, per carnem fecit. Caro ergo divina operans, psalterium est: caro humano patiens, cithara est. Sonet psalterium; illuminentur caeci, audiant surdi, stringantur paralytici, ambulent claudi, surgant aegroti, resurgant mortui: iste est sonus psalterii. Sonet et cithata; esutiat, sitiat, dormiat, teneatur,

flagelletur, irrideatur, crucifigatur, sepeliatuf. Cum ergo vines in illa carne quaedam sonuisse desuper, quaedam de inferiore parte, una caro resurrexit, et in una carne agnoscimus et psalterium et citharam. This duo generates factotum impleverunt Evangelium, et praedicatur in gentibus; nam et mitacula et passiones Domini praedicantur. 17 [v.10.12]. Ergo surrexit psalterium et cithata diluculo, et confitetur Domino: et quid ait? Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine, et psallam tibi in gentibus: quia magnificata est usque ad cáelos mercy yours, et usque ad clouds your sales. Caeli supra clouds, et clouds infra caelos: et tamen ad hoc caelum proximum pertinent clouds. Sed aliquando clouds recumbunt in montibus, usque adeo in cerca aere conglomerantur. Caelum autem sursum est, habitats Angelorum, Sedium, Dominatíonum, Principatuum, Potestatum. Illud ergo forte videatut fuesse digandum, Magnificata est usque ad cáelos veritas tua, et usque ad clouds mercy yours. Etenim in cáelo Angelí laudant Deum, videntes ipsam speciem vetitatis, sine ulla calígine visionis, sine interpolatione aliqua falsitatis: vident, diligunt, laudant, non fatiguentur. Ibi veritas: hic autem in nostra miseria utique misericordia. Misero enim praebenda est misericotdia. Non enim opus est misericordia sursum, ubi nullus est miser. Hoc propterea dixi, quia videtur congruentius dici potuisse, Magnificata est usque ad cáelos veritas tua, et usque ad clouds

and your mercy, to the clouds. By the clouds we understand the preachers of the truth, men who carry this earthly flesh, where God makes the miracle shine and his precepts thunder. They are the clouds, of which Isaiah speaks, in the person of the Lord, rebuking a certain bad, barren vineyard full of thorns: I will command my clouds not to pour water on it; That is, I will command my apostles to abandon the Jews and not evangelize them, but rather evangelize in the good land of the Gentiles, where not thorns but grapes germinate. We know that the clouds are the preachers of the truth: the prophets, the apostles, all those who rightly proclaim the word of truth and who have hidden light within them, as the clouds do, which is why they flash. Therefore men are the clouds. Lord, what does it mean: Because your mercy has been magnified to the heavens, and your truth to the clouds? The truth culminates in the angels, but you also gave it to men and led it to the clouds. The angels, being in heaven, do not seem to need mercy; But since you have compassion on miserable men and by giving it to them by participating in the resurrection you make them angels, that is why your mercy reaches to heaven. Glory to our Lord, to his mercy and to his truth, because his mercy did not fail to make us blessed through his grace nor did he deprive us of the truth. First, the truth came to us hidden by the flesh, and so, through its flesh, it healed the inner eye of our heart so that later we could behold it face to face. Give thanks, let's say with the last verse of the psalm that your mercy is now yours. Clouds enim intelligimus praedicatores veritatis, homines portantes istam carnem caliginosam quodammodo, unde Deus et coruscat miraculis, et tonat praeceptis: et ipsi sunt illae clouds of quibus dicit Isaiah ex persona Domini, increpans quamdam vineam malam, sterilem, spinosam, Mandabo nubibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem (Is 5,6): id est, mandabo Apostolis meis, ut deserant ludaeos, et non illis evangelizent, sed evangelizent in terra bona Gentium, unde non spinae, sed uvae procedant.

Novimus ergo clouds Dei esse praedicatores veritatis, Prophetas, Apostólos, omnes recte proferentes verbum veritatis et habentes in se lumen occultum, sicut habent clouds unde coruscant: homines ergo clouds. Quid sibi itaque vult, Domine, Quia magnijicata est usque ad caelos your mercy, et usque ad clouds your sales? Veritas praepollet in Angelis: sed dedisti illam et hominibus, et deduxisti illam usque ad clouds. Sursum mercy videntur Angeli non indigere; sed quia homines miseros tu miseraris, et praebendo illis misericordiam communicatione resurrectionis Angelos facis, usque ad cáelos est misericordia tua. Gloria Domino nostro, et misericordiae ipsius, et veritati ipsius, quia nec deseruit nos misericordia faceré beatos per gratiam suam, nec fraudavit nos veritate: quia primo veritas carne operta venit ad nos, et sanavit per carnem suam oculum interiorem cordis nostri, ut eam postea facie ad faciem videre possemus (1 Cor 13:12). 1 [1.2]. What we have sung should rather be heard than cried out. The truth addresses everyone as if preaching to the audience of the human race, saying: If you truly speak justice, judge righteously, sons of men. Is it not easy for a pervert to speak justice? Or who, having been asked about justice, not being in judgment, will not easily answer what is just, since the truth was carved in our hearts by the hand of our Creator: What you do not want done to you, do not do to another? Before the law was given, no one was allowed to ignore what we say so that they would have a way of judging those to whom the law had not been given. But so that men would not try to obtain something they lacked, what they did not read in their hearts was written on tablets. They had the law written, but they did not want to read it. It was contrary to his camus cum ipso Psalm lasts versus, quos iamdudum etiam dixit: Exaltare super cáelos Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua. eyes what they were forced to see in their conscience; Therefore, when man heard the voice of God externally, he was impelled to penetrate within himself, as the Scripture says: He will question the thoughts of the wicked. Where there is interrogation there is law. But as men, desiring external things, turned away from themselves, the written law was given; not because it was not already written in hearts, but because, having fled from your heart, you had to be welcomed by Him who is everywhere and returned to the interior of yourself. Therefore, what does the law written on tables cry out to those who have abandoned the law written in their hearts? Return, prevaricators, to the heart. Well, who taught you not to want someone to get close to your wife? Who taught you not to want anyone to steal from you? Who taught you not to want to suffer injuries and everything that in particular and even in general can be said about this? Well, there are many things about which men, when asked about each one in particular, answer without hesitation that they do not want to suffer. It is very good that you do not want to suffer these things; but are you the only man? Don't you live in the society of the human race? He who was made with you is your companion, and we were all made in the image of God, that is, we are all children of God if we do not fulfill through earthly desires what He formed; Therefore, what you do not want done to you, do not do to another. By the mere fact of not wanting to suffer it, you judge that it is bad, and this forces you to recognize the intimate law that is written in your own heart. You worked, and he (the oppressed) cried out between your hands. How can you not be forced to return to your heart when

Do you suffer this in the hands of others? I ask: Is theft good? No. Is adultery good? Everyone shouts: No. Is homicide good? Everyone cries out that he must be detested. Is it good to desire the goods of one's neighbor? They all say no. If you still don't confess, pay attention: someone is approaching who wants your property. You like it and answer what you want. Then everyone who is questioned about these things answers that they are not good. Let's talk about the benefits, not only those that do not cause detriment, but also those for which one helps, and by helping, one gets rid of something. Everyone who is hungry is asked: Are you hungry? Well, one has bread and there is even plenty left over; knows that you need it; He doesn't give it to you. You dislike the hungry; You also dislike the fed up when you know that the other is hungry. A pilgrim is coming to your homeland. You need hospitality; He is not received at home. Then he shouts that that city is inhuman and that he could easily have found lodging among the barbarians. He notices iniquity because he suffers it. Maybe you don't perceive it; It is necessary that you feel like a pilgrim and see how you would dislike someone who did not lend you what you in your homeland do not want to offer to the pilgrim. I ask everyone: Are these things true? And they say: They are true. Are they fair? And they answer: they are.

fruit for the righteous. Then there is God, who judges the wicked on earth. 23. If I was a bit long, forgive me. I urge you, in the name of Christ, to consider the things you heard for your benefit. For it is of no use to preach the truth if the heart disagrees with the tongue, and it is of no use to hear the truth if a man does not build on rock. He who builds on stone is he who hears and acts; He who hears and does not act builds on sand; He who neither hears nor acts, builds nothing. Just as he who builds on sand builds ruin for himself, in the same way, he who does not build on stone, when the flood comes, is swept away and is left without a house. Then all that remains is to build, and build on stone, that is, hear and act. Let no one say: Why am I going to church? See that those who go to church every day do not do what they hear. They do something: listen and so it may happen that they hear and act; but you are so much further from acting as you avoid hearing. But I—you say—do not build on sand. The barrage hasn't hit you yet. Isn't that why it should drag you along? Will the rain not drown? Will the wind not cut down? Then you must say: I will come and hear; but, once you have heard, work. Qui aedificat super petram, ipse est qui audit et facit: qui autem audit et non facit, aedificat super arenam (Mt 7,24.26): qui nec audit nec facit, nihil aedificat. Nam si audieris, et non feceris, aedificasti quidem, sed super arenam. What does it mean to show me in my enemies? If God, wanting to manifest his wrath and make his power known, endured with great patience the vessels of wrath made for perdition, and for this reason "made his riches known in the vessels of mercy," if God, I repeat, endured the vessels of wrath and made his riches known in the vessels of mercy, it was most rightly said: His mercy went before me. My God showed me in my enemies; That is to say, God showed me the great mercy he had for me on those with whom he did not have it. If the debtor is not kept in suspense, he will give less thanks to the one who forgives the debt. My God showed me in my enemies. 21. What does he say about these enemies? Do not kill them, lest they forget your law. Pray for your enemies, fulfill the precept. What does it mean, have no mercy on anyone who commits iniquity; and also: Do ​​not kill them, so that they do not forget your law? How does he say that he does not pity any of those who commit iniquity, and, on the other hand, that he does not kill them, so that they do not forget his law? Certainly he spoke here of his enemies. And? Do your enemies do justice? If His enemies work equity, then He works iniquity. But since He works equity, therefore, he who works equity undoubtedly endures iniquity from his enemies. Therefore, there is no choice but to say that those who are enemies of the righteous work iniquity. How is it that a little while ago he said that he will not have mercy on any of those who commit iniquity, and now he says of his enemies: Do not kill them, lest they forget your law? Therefore this means: Will you not take pity on luck that you eches in inimicis meis? Si enim Deus volens ostendere iram, et demonstrare potentiam suam, attulít in tumba patientia vasa irae, quae perfection sunt in perditionem, et propter quid hoc? Ut notes faceret divitias suas in vasa misericordiae (Rom 9:21-23): si ergo vasa irae attulit, in quibus notes faceret divitias suas in vasa misericordiae, rectissime dictum est, Misericordia eius praeveniet me. Deus meus demonstravit mihi in inimicis meis: id est, quantam circa me habuit misericordiam, in illis mihi demonstravit circa quos non habuit. Nisi enim debitor suspendatur, minus agit gratias cui debitum relaxatur. Deus meus demonstravit mihi in inimicis meis. 21. De ípsis auteru inimicis quid? Therefore, when we recognize our voice, we cannot help but recognize it without becoming emotional; and the more we delight ourselves the more we realize that we belong to it. King David was a single man, but he did not always represent a single man, for he sometimes prefigured the Church, which consists of many members and extends to the ends of the earth. When he prefigured a man alone, he personified the one who is Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. In this psalm, or, rather, in this title of the psalm, some of David's victories are narrated, which he carried out by forcefully defeating some enemies and making them his tributaries when, after the death of Saul, his persecutor, he clearly took the reins of the kingdom of Israel, since he was also king before being persecuted,

but only known by God. After having clearly, evidently, and solemnly taken possession of the kingdom, he defeated those commemorated in this title. The title of the psalm reads: For the end, for those who will be changed in the inscription of the title for David, in teaching; when he burned the Mesopotamia of Syria and Zobah and when Joab returned, and defeated Edon in the valley of the Salt Mines, defeating twelve thousand. In the second book of Kings we read these battles and also that all the places and names recorded in the title were devastated by David, namely, Mesopotamia of Syria, Zobah, Edon and Joab. This happened, and as it happened it was written, and so it is read. Read it whoever wants. However, the prophetic spirit is accustomed to deviate somewhat in the titles of the psalms from the description of the facts and record something that is not found in history, and, therefore, to warn us that the titles were not written to know the things carried out in this way, but to prefigure future events. For example, it was said of David that he disfigured his face before Abimelec, and abandoned him and walked away, whereas the book of Kings says that he did this not before Abimelec, but before King Achish. Thus, also in this title we find something by which we are warned to understand something else. In that narrative of the battles and extraordinary acts of King David in which we are told that all those we have commemorated were defeated, we do not read that he burned anything. But here in a special way what is not written there was inserted, which burned the Mesopotamia of Syria and the Syria of Soba. Let us now begin to explain these events.

The word was sent to these four parts so that they would all be called in the Trinity. The number twelve is formed from four added three times. Then twelve thousand earthly men were rightly wounded, since in them the whole world was wounded and the Church was chosen from all the world, dead to earthly life. But why in the Salinas Valley? The valley prefigures humility; the salt flats, the flavor. Many humiliate themselves, but vainly and fatuously; They humble themselves in vain old age. When someone endures anguish for money, for temporal honor, for the discomforts of life, he will undoubtedly suffer tribulation and be humiliated. Why don't you suffer for God? Why not for Christ? Why not the taste of salt? Do you not know that it was said to you: You are the salt of the earth. And if the salt loses its strength, will it be of no use except to be thrown out? Let your charity know that every faithful person who keeps the word of God in his heart; who lives plausibly so that the name of his Lord may not be reviled by him; who fears the future judgment of his Lord with dread, yet he also asks for many things according to the taste of this world, and is not heard; But when he asks for eternal life, he is always heard. Who is there who does not ask for health when he is sick? And yet, perhaps the illness still suits him. It may be said that he is not heard in this. You are not heard by attending to your will to be heard by attending to your health. However, let us offer some testimony by which we see how justification is directed to health. Here is one from the Gospel. Who do you call healthy, who sick? He continues and says: I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to penitence. Then he called the righteous healthy, not because the Pharisees were healthy, but because they believed themselves to be healthy; and for this reason they became arrogant, and, finding themselves sick, they rejected the doctor, and, therefore, becoming more seriously ill, they killed the doctor. Pascet te qui solem suum oriri facit super bonds et malas, et pluit super iustos et iniustos (Mt 5,45). Si pascit damnandos, non pascet liberandos? Ergo in rapinam noli concupiscere. Dictum est hoc pauperi, fortassis aliquid de necessitate rapturo. Dives proceedat: Non habeo ego, inquit, necessitatem rapiendi: nihil mihi deest; abundant omnia. Et tu audi: Divitiae si fluant, ne apponatis cor. lile non habet; iste habet: ille non quaerat rapere quod non habet; This is not apponat cor in eo quod habet. Divitiae si fluant, id est, si exundent, tanquam de fonte currant, Ne apponatis cor: noli de te ptaesumere, noli ibi te figere: certe vel hoc time, Divitiae J fluant. tol to Timothy: Command the rich of this world not to be arrogant. And what does it mean don't put your heart in them? Don't put hope in the uncertainty of riches. Therefore, if riches abound, do not set your heart on them, do not trust in riches, do not boast about them, lest it be said to you: Here is the man who did not count on God for his help, but trusted in the abundance of riches and was emboldened in his vanity. Therefore, vain and lying sons of men, do not steal nor set your heart on riches if they abound; Do not love vanity anymore nor go after lies. "Blessed is the man who puts his hope in the Lord his God and does not pursue vanities and deceitful follies." Do you want to deceive, do you want to defraud? What do you use for this? Of crazy scales. Liars are—says the psalmist—the sons of men in the balance, presenting mad Roman women to deceive. With false faith you deceive those who look. Do you not know that one is the one who weighs and another is the one who judges the weight? The one for whom you weigh does not see, but the One who weighs you and your neighbor sees. Then do not defraud, nor steal, nor trust in the things you possess, says, admonishes and commands this Iditho. 17 [v.12-13]. What's next? Once God spoke, and I heard these two things: that power is from God and that in you, Lord, there is mercy, because you will give to each one according to his works. Iditho spoke, (something) sounded high above where he passed. There he heard something and announced it to us. But I shudder a little, brothers, at what he announced to us: and until I communicate my disturbance to you and vent, I want you to pay attention. The exposition of the psalm, ayucipe ditivibus huius mundi non superbe supere. Et quid est, Ne apponatis cor? Ñeque sperare in incerto divitiarum (1 Tim 6,17). Ergo, Divitiae si fluant, ne apponatis cor, ne in divitiis confidatis, non praesumatis, non speretis; ne dicatur: Ecce homo qui non posit T)eam adiutorem suum; sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, et praevaluit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, and praevaluit in vanitate sua (Ps 51,9). Ergo, vani filii hominum, mendaces filii hominum, ñeque rapiatis, ñeque si fluant divitiae, cor apponatis; non iam vanitatem diligatis, et mendacium quaetatis. Beatus enim cuius est Dominus Deus spes eius, et non respexit in vanitates et insanias mendaces (Ps 39,5). Decipere vultis, fraudm vultis faceré; quid affertis ut decipiatis? Intentional acts.

Mendaces enim, ínquit, filii bominum in stateris, ut decipiant proferendo stateras dolosas. False examine fallitis intuentes: nescitis alium esse qui appendit, alium qui de pondere iudicat? Non videt cui tu appendis; sed videt qui te et ipsum appendit. Ergo non fraudm, non rapinam concupiscatis; non in his quae habetis spem ponatis: monui, praedixi, ait iste Idithun. 17 fv.12.13]. Quid sequitur? Semel locutus est Deus, duo haec audivi; quoniam potestas Dei est, et tibi, Domine, mercy: quia tu reddes unicuique secundum opera sua. Dixit Idithun, sonuit de alto, quo transilivit; audivit ibi quiddam, et dixit nobis: sed aliquantum in hoc quod nobis dixit penurbor, fratres; et doñee vobiscum participate!, vel

God giving me, it is already coming to an end. After what we have to say, there is nothing else to explain. So, strive with me to see that you can understand this. But if I cannot understand it and one of you understands it, I will rather be glad than envy him. It is very difficult to investigate how it was first written: God spoke once, and how, speaking only once, he then said: I heard two things. If he had said: God spoke once, and I heard only this, it would seem that he settled the question in part, so that we would only investigate what God spoke once means. But now we must ask what it means that God spoke once, and that I heard two things, since He spoke only once. 18. God spoke only once. What do you say, Iditho? How is it that you who passed through them say: God once spoke? I consult another scriptural passage, and it tells me: God spoke in another time, in many circumstances and in many ways, to the fathers through the projects. What does God speak once mean? Is He not the God who spoke to Adam at the origins of the human race? Did He not Himself speak to Cain, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, all the prophets and Moses? There was only one Moses, and how many times did God not speak to him? See that he did not speak to one just once, but many times. Later he is said to have spoken to his Son, saying: You are my Son, the beloved. God spoke to the apostles, he spoke to all the saints; If not through the echo of the cloud, He spoke to them in their hearts, where He is the perturbationem, vel aliquam respirationem meam, attempts you flew. Etenim Psalmum ad terminum duximus adiuvante Domino: post haec quae dictuii sumus, non restat aliquid quod de hoc ulterius exponamus. Itaque adnitimini mecum, utrum possimus intelligere hoc: et si non potuero, et intelligit aliquis vestrum quod ego non possum; gaudebo potius quam invidebo. Omnino investigare difficile est quemadmodum positum sit ptius, Semel locutus est Deus: deinde cum ille semel locutus est, ego duo audivi. Si enim diceret, Semel locutus est Deus, unum hoc audivi; videbatur partem quaestionis huius amputavisse, ut tantummodo quareremus quid sit, Semel locutus est Deus. Nunc vero quaesituri sumus, et quid sit, Semel locutus est Deus; et quid sit, duo haec audivi, cum semel ille locutus sit. 18. Semel locutus est Deus. What do you say, Idithun? Si tu loqueris qui transilivisti eos: Semel locutus est?

Ego Scripturam aliam consulo, et dicit mihi: Multis partibus, et multis modis olim Deus locutus est patribus in Prophetis (Hebr 1,1). Quid est, Semel locutus est Deus? Nonne ille est Deus, qui in primordio generis humani locutus est ad Adam? Nonne idem ipse locutus est ad Cain, ad Noe, ad Abraham, ad Isaac, ad Iacob, ad Ptophetas omnes, et ad Moysen? Unus etat Moyses; et quoties ad eum locutus est Deus? Ecce etiam uni non semel, sed saepius locutus est Deus. Deinde locutus est ad Filium hic positum: T« is Filius meus dilectus (Mt 3,17). Locutus est Deus Apostolis, locutus est omnibus sanctis, etiamsi non voce sonante per cloudm, in corde tamen ubi ipse magister est. Unde ille dicit: Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus

Only in God do we have to wait

Teacher. Hence the psalmist says: I will hear what the Lord God speaks in me, for he will speak peace to his people. So what does it mean that God spoke once? He had gone through a lot to get to where God spoke only once. Note that I told you briefly. Here among men and to men God spoke many times in various ways and forms through various creatures; In itself God only spoke once, because He generated a single Word. Then this Iditho, passing through them, had crossed with the discerning, powerful and confident gaze of the mind the earth and what is found in it; the air, all the clouds, from which God spoke many things frequently and to many; had pierced all the angels with the penetration of faith. This wanderer was not content with earthly things, but, flying like an eagle, he passed through all the fog that covers the earth. For Wisdom says: And I covered the whole earth like a cloud. Traversing all creation, he came to a pure region, and, seeking God and pouring out his soul within himself, he came to the Beginning, to the Word of God, God in God, and found the one Word of the one Father, and saw that God spoke only once; He saw the Word, by whom all things were made and in whom they are all at the same time, not divided, nor separated, nor unequal. For God knew everything he did through the Word; and, if he knew what he did, what he did was in Him before he did it. Well, if what He did was not in Him before He did it, where did He know what He did? You cannot say that God created without knowing things. God knew what he did. And where did he know it before it was made, if it cannot be known before it is made? Certainly things cannot be known

before they are made, but only by those who are made; namely, by you, by man, made and placed below. But before all things were made, they were known by Him who made them and who made what He knew. Therefore in that Word through which God made all things they were all before they were made. And, once they are done, they are all there; in one way there and in another here; in one way in the very nature in which they were made and in another in the art by which they were made. Who will explain this to us? We can try it. Walk with Iditho and observe. 19. I have already told as best I could how God spoke only once; Let us see how he heard two things, for he says: I heard these two things. Perhaps it does not follow that he heard only these two things; but he says: I heard these two things. It is in our best interest for you to tell us the two things you heard. Perhaps you heard many others, but we do not need you to explain them to us. For thus says the Lord: I have many things to tell you, but you are not able to understand them now. What does it mean: I heard these two things? These two things that I have to tell you, I do not tell you as if they were mine, but I tell you as I heard them. God spoke only once, that is, God has only one begotten Word. In this Word are all things, since by the Word all things were made. It has only one Word, where all the treasures of wisdom and science are hidden. It has only one Word: God spoke only once. I heard the two things I will tell you there. I don't speak, I don't say anything of my own making; This is what you are referring to I heard. The Bridegroom's friend is present and hears (the husband) speaking truth. He listens to him so that it does not happen that,

Deas, quoniam loquetur pacem populo suo (Ps 84,9). Quid est ergo. Semel locutus est Deus? Multum transiliverat iste, ut perveniret illuc, ubi semel locutus est Deus. Ecce breviter dixi Charitati Vestrae. Hic inter homines, hominibus saepe, multis modis, multis partibus, per multiformem creaturam locutus est Deus: apud se semel Deus locutus est, quia unum Verbum genuit Deus. Iste ergo Idithun transiliens eos, transiliverat acie mentís forti, et valida, er praefídenri, transiliverat terram, et quidquid in terra esr; aerem, clouds omnes ex quibus locutus est Deus Fine, et saepe, et multis: transiliverat etiam omnes Angelos acie fidei. Erat enim iste transiliens non contentus terrenis, sed velut aquila volans praetervectus omnem nebulam qua tegitur omnis terra. Dicit enim Sapientia: Et sicut nebula texi omnem terram (Eccli 24,6). Pervenit ad aliquid liquidum, universal transiliens creaturam, et quaerens Deum, et effundens super se animam suam; pervenit ad principium, et Verbum Deum apud Deum; et invenit unius Patris unum Verbum; et vidit quia semel locutus est Deus; vidit Verbum per quod facta sunt omnia (lo 1,3). et in quo simul sunt omnia, non diverse, non separata, non inaequalia. Non enim Deus quod per Vetbum faciebat, ipse non noverat; si autem quod faciebat noverat, in illo etat antequam ieront quod fiebat. Si enim non in illo erat quod fiebat antequam fiebat, ubi noverat quod faciebat?

Non enim potes Deum dicere ignorata fecisse. Scivit itaque Deus quod fecit. Et ubi scivit antequam faceret, si sciri nisi facta non possunt? Sed a factis sciri nisi ante facta non possunt; a te scilicet, ab homine in imo facto, et in imo pósito: antequam autem ieront haec omnia, sciebantur ab illo a quo facta sunt, et quod scivit fecit. Ergo in Verbo illo per quod fecit omnia, antequam ieront etant omnia; et cum facta sunt, ibi sunt omnia: sed aliter hic, aliter ibi; aliter in propria natura in qua facta sunt, aliter in arte per quam facta sunt. Quis hoc explain? Conari possumus: ite cum Idithun, et videte. 19. Iam ergo, ut potuimus, diximus quomodo semel locutus est Deus: videamus quomodo duo haec audivit, Duo haec audivi. Forte non est consequens, ut sola duo haec audierit: sed, duo haec, inquit, audivi; quaedam duo quae nobis opus est ut dicantur, audivit. Audivit forte alia fine; sed non opus est ea dici nobis. Ait enim et Dominus: Fine drooling vobis dicere; sed non potestis illa portare moda (Ib. 16,12). Quid est ergo, Duo haec audivi? Haec duo quae vobis dicturus sum, non a me vobis dico, sed quae audivi dico. Semel locutus est Deus: unum Verbum habet unigenitum Deum. In illo Verbo sunt omnia, quia per Verbum facta sunt omnia. Unum Verbum habet, ubi omnes thesauri sapientiae et scientiae absconditi (Col 2,3). Unum Verbum habet; semel locutus est Deus. Duo haec, quae vobis dicturus sum, ibi audivi; non ex

speaking of his own harvest, speak lies; and therefore lest you should say, You who speak these things to me, who are you? Where does this thing you tell me come from? I heard these two things, and I speak to you because I heard them, I who also knew that God spoke only once. Do not despise the listener who tells you two things necessary for you; Do not despise him who, transcending every creature, came to the only begotten Word of God, where he knew that God spoke only once. 20. Tell us these two things now. We are extremely interested in these two things: that power belongs to God and in you, O Lord, there is mercy. Are these, perchance, the two things: power and mercy? They are indeed. Understand the power of God, understand his mercy. Almost all of Scripture is contained in these two. Because of them the prophets, the patriarchs, the law, our Lord Jesus Christ, the apostles, all the preaching and estimation of the word of God in the Church appeared. All this is contained in these two things, in the power of God and in his mercy. Fear his power, love his mercy. Do not presume so much on his mercy that you despise his power; nor fear his power so much that you distrust his mercy. In Him is power, in Him is mercy. He humiliates this one, he exalts that one; He humiliates this one with his power, he exalts that one with his mercy. Thus says Saint Paul: God, wanting to manifest wrath and make his power known, endured with immense kindness the vessels of wrath prepared for perdition. Here you have its power. Investigate his mercy, and hear me loquor, non ex medico: ad hoc pertinet audivi. Amicus autem sponsi stat et audit eum (lo 3.29), ut verum loquatur. Audit enim eum, ne loquendo mendacium de suo loquatur (Ib. 8,44): ne díceres, Quis es tu qui mihi hoc dicis? where mihi hoc do you say? Audivi haec duo, et ille tibí loquor quia audivi haec duo, qui etiam cognovi quia semel locutus est Deus. Noli contemnere auditorem dicentem tibi quaedam duo tibi necessaria, eum qui transiliendo universam creaturam pervenit ad Verbum unigenitum Dei, ubi sciret quia semel locutus est Deus. 20. Dicat ergo iam quaedam duo. Multum enim ad nos pertinent haec duo. Quoniam potestas Dei est, et tibi, Domine, mercy. Ista sunt duo; potestas, et mercy? This plan: intelligite potestatem Dei; intelligite misericordiam Dei. His duobus continentur prope omnes Scripturae.

Propter haec duo, Prophetae; propter haec duo, Patriarchae; propter haec, Lex; propter haec, ipse Dominus noster Iesus Christus; propter haec, Apostoli; propter haec, annuntiatio omnis, et celebratio verbi Dei in Ecclesia: propter haec duo; propter potestatem Dei et misericordiam. Potestatem eius timete; Misericordiam eius amate. Nec sic of mercy eius praesumatis, ut potestatem contemnatis: nec sic potestatem rimeatis, ut of mercy desperetis. Apud illum potestas; apud illum mercy. Hunc humiliat; et hunc exaltat (Ps 74,8): hunc humiliat potestate; illum exaltat mercy. Si enim Deus volens ostendere iram, et demonstrare potentiam suam, attulit in fine patientia vasa irte, quae perfection

you laugh below: In order to make known his riches in the vessels of mercy. Then it is his power to condemn the wicked. And who will say to him: Why have you made me? You, man, who are you to reply to God? You fear and tremble before his power, but trust in his mercy. The devil has a certain power; However, many times he wants to harm and cannot, because his power is subject to another power. If the devil could harm as much as he wants, there would not be a righteous person or a believer left on earth. He pushes through his minions like a tilted wall; but he only pushes as much as he is allowed. But the Lord sustains so that the wall does not fall, since he who gives power to the tempter offers his mercy to the tempted. The devil is allowed to tempt with measure, for it is said: You will give us tears to drink with measure. Do not fear the tempter, who was allowed to tempt in something, for you have the most merciful Savior at your hand. He is only allowed to tempt you as much as he benefits you so that you may be exercised and tested, so that you, who did not know yourself, may know yourself. Where or why should we be safe if not by the power and mercy of God, according to the sentence of the Apostle: God is faithful, and will not allow you to be tempted beyond your ability? 21. Power belongs to God. Because there is no power that does not come from God. Don't say: Why does he give him so much power? Don't let it give you power. He who gives power possesses justice. You may murmur wickedly; He cannot lose justice. Perhaps sunt in perditionem. Audisti potestatem: quaere misericordion. Ut Notas, Inquit, Faceret Divitias Suas In Vasa Misericordiae. Pertinet ergo ad eius potestatem damnare iniquos. Et quis illi dicat: Quid fecisti? Your enim, or homo, who is it, who will you answer Deo? (Rom 9,22.23-20). Time ergo et treme eius potestatem; sed spera eius misericordiam. Diabolus potestas quaedam est; plerumque tamen vult nocere, et non potest, quia potestas ista sub potestate est. Nam si tantum posset nocere diabolus quantum vult, non aliquis iustorum remaneret, aut aliquis fidelium esset in terra. Ipse per vasa sua impellit, quasi parietem inclinatum; sed tantum impellit quantum accipit potestatem. Ut autem non cadat paries, Dominus suscipiet; quoniam qui dat potestatem tentatori, ipse tentato praebet misericordion. Ad mensuram enim permittitur tentare diabolus: Et potabis nos, inquit, in lacrymis in mensura (Ps 79,6).

Noli ergo timere permissum aliquid faceré tentatorem; habes enim misericordissimum Salvatorem. Tantum permittitur ille tentare quantum tibi prodest, ut exercearis, ut proberis; ut qui te nesciebas, a te ipso inveniaris. Nam ubi, vel unde, nisi de hac Dei potestate, et misericordia securi esse debenmus, secundum illam apostolicam sententiam: Fidelis Deus, qui non permittit vos tentari super id quod potestis? (1 Cor 10:13). 21. Ergo, Potestas Dei est: Non est enim potestas nisi a Deo (Rom 13,1). Noli dicere, Et quid ei dat tantam potestatem? Et non det potestatem. Quid dat potestatem, habet aequitatem? Your inique I will murmur
