is there iniquity in God? There is no such thing. Record this in your heart. Do not erase this inscription from your thoughts. God can do something without knowing why he does it; However, He in whom there is no iniquity cannot act iniquitously. I talk to you; Pay attention a little, see that you censure God for iniquity. You would not censure iniquity if you did not see justice. He who does not recognize justice cannot reproach iniquity; distinguished, when comparing it with iniquity, censures the latter. How do you know that something is unfair? Because you know what is fair. What if what you call unfair is fair? There is no such thing, you reply; It's unfair. And you shout as if seeing it with your eyes and you revile it as an architect who discerns the just from the unjust by contemplating that this is unjust due to a certain standard of justice, with which you confront what you see to be perverse and that you appreciate does not adapt to the rectitude of your standard. Now I ask you: How do you see that this is fair? Where, I will tell you, do you see this just, so that, having seen it, you censure what is unjust? Where does that come from with which your soul is illuminated, which, on the other hand, is placed in darkness? I mean, where does this I don't know what shines in your mind come from? Where does this just come from? Doesn't it have its own origin? Does what is right for you come from you? Can you give yourself justice? No one gives to himself what he does not possess. Therefore, being unjust as you are, you cannot be just except by addressing yourself to a certain immanent justice, from which, if you depart, you are unjust, and, if you approach, you are just. When you move away, it does not decline, and when you draw closer, it does not grow. Where is this justice? Do you look for it in the potes, ille aequitatem I will lose non potest. Numquid iniquites apud Deum? Absit (Ib. 9,14). Hoc fige in corde; hoc de cogitatione tua non excutiat ¡nimicus. Faceré potest aliquid Deus, ut tu nescias quare faciat: inique tamen faceré non potest, apud quem non est iniquitas. Nam ecce reprehendis Deum quasi de iniquitate (ago tecum aliquid, attende paululum): non reprehenderes iniquitatem, nisi videndo iustitiam. Reprehensor iniquitatis esse non potest qui non cernit iustitiam, cui comparatam reprehendat iniquitatem. Unde enim six quia hoc iniustum est, nisi scias quid sit iustum?

What if enim iustum est et hoc, what do you say iniustum? Absit, inquis, iniustum est: et clamas quasi videntibus oculis, videns hoc iniustum esse utique ex aliqua regula iustitiae, cui comparans hoc quod vides pravum, et cernens non convenire rectitudini regulae tuae, reprehendis; tanquam artifex discernens iustum ab iniusto. Ergo quaero a te: Iustum hoc esse unde vides? Ubi, inquam, vides hoc iustum, quo viso, reprehendis iniustum? Unde illud nescio quid, quo aspergitur anima tua, ex multis partibus in caligíne constituta, nescio quid hoc quod coruscat mentí tuae? unde hoc iustum? Itane non habet fontem suum? A te tibí est quod iustum est, et tu tibi potes daré iustitiam? Nemo sibi dat quod non habet. Ergo cum sis iniustus, esse non potes iustus, nisi convertendo te ad quamdam iustitiam manentem; a qua si recedes, it is iniustus; ad quam if you agree, iustus is. Recedent non-deficit; you access not
Only in God do we have to wait

land? You look for her in vain; You do not look for gold or precious stones when seeking justice. Look for it in the sea, in the clouds, in the stars; look for her in los angeles; in them you will find it; but they also drink from the fountain. The justice of angels is found in all, but is contained in one. Then look, go through, go to where God spoke once, and you will find the fountain of justice where the fountain of life is, because in you is the fountain of life. If you by a faint dew try to discern what is just and unjust, will there be iniquity in God, from where justice flows for you as from a fountain so that you know what is just, since, on the other hand, you have iniquitously lost good sense? God has within himself the source of justice. Do not look for iniquity in Him, for in Him everything is light without shadows. Perhaps the reason may be hidden from you. If the reason is hidden from you, examine your ignorance, see what you are. Hear these two things: Power belongs to God, and in you, Lord, there is mercy; and: Do not seek things stronger than yourself and do not search for things higher than you, but those that the Lord commanded you; always think about them. These two belong to these that God commanded you: Power belongs to God; and: In you, Lord, there is mercy. Notice the enemy; He can only execute what is granted to him. Fear him who has supreme power; He fears him who does whatever he wants and who does nothing unjustly and everything he does is just. We thought something was unfair; Because God has made it, he believes it is just. 22. If someone kills an innocent man, does he act justly or wickedly? Without a doubt, he works wickedly. So why did it grow? Ubi est ergo ista iustitia? Quaeres in terra? absit. Non enim aurum aut lapides pretiosos quaeris, iustitiam quaerens. Quaere in mari, quaere in nubibus, quaere in stellis: quaere in Angelis; invenís in illis, sed et ipsi de fonte bibunt. Iustitia enim Angelorum in ómnibus est, sed ab uno capitur. Réspice ergo, transcende, vade illuc ubi semel locutus est Deus; et ibi invenies fontem iustitiae, ubi est fons vitae: Quoniam apud te est fons vitae (Ps 35,10).

Si enim tu de rore exiguo iudicare vis quod iustum est, et quod iniustum est; numquid iniquitas apud Deum, unde ad te manat tanquam de fonte iustitia, in quantum iustum sapis, cum ex multis partibus inique desipias? Habet ergo fontem iustitiae Deus. Noli ibi quaerere iniquitatem, ubi lux sine umbra est. Sed plane latere te potest causa. Si latet causa te, réspice ignorantiam tuam, vide qui sis; attende haec duo: Quoniam potestas Dei est, et tibi, Domine, misericordia. Fortiora te ne quaesieris, et altiora te ne scrutatus fueris; sed quae praecepit tibi Dominus, illa cogita semper (Eccli 3,22). Quia ad haec quae tibi praecepit Deus pertinent ista duo: Quoniam potestas Dei est, et tibi, Domine, misericordia. Noli timere inimicum: tantum facit quantum acceperit potestatem. Eum time qui habet summam potestatem; eum time qui quantum vult, tantum facit, et qui iniuste nihil facit, et quidquid fecerit, iustum est. This psalm speaks in person of Christ our Lord, that is, of the head and the members. For the only one who was born of Mary, and suffered, and was buried, and ascended into heaven, and now sits at the right hand of the Father and intercedes for us, is our head. If He is our head, we are his members. His entire Church, which is spread throughout the entire world, is his body, of which He is the head. All the faithful, not only those present, but also those who existed before us and those who after us will exist until the end of the world, belong to his body, of which he is the head, which is in heaven. As we already know the head and the body, scriptum est ante immensa volumina annorum per istos quos moda legimus, quando iam ista impleri videmus. Sed quoniam scripta sunt et illa quae nondum venerunt, id est, quia Dominus noster lesus Christus venturus est ut iudicet, qui primo venit ut iudicaretur; come enim primo humilis, postea venturus est excelsus; venit ut ostenderet exemplum patientiae, postea venturus est ut pro meritis iudicet omnes, sive bonds, sive malo: quia ergo nondum venit hoc quod speramus, venturum Christum iudicem vivorum et mortuorum, debenmus illud credere. Psalmus ergo iste dicitur ex persona Domini nostri Iesu Chrisri, et capitis et membrorum. Ule enim unus qui natus est de Maria, et passus est, et sepultus est, et resurrexit, et ascendit in caelum, et moda ad dexteram Patris sedet et interpellat pro nobis, caput nostrum est. Si ille caput est, nos membra sumus: tota Ecclesia eius quae ubique diffusa est, corpus ipsius est, cuius est ipse caput. Non solum autem fideles qui moda sunt sed et qui fuerunt ante nos, et qui post nos futuri, sunt usque in finem saeculi, omnes ad corpus eius pertinent; cuius corporis ipse caput est, qui ascendit in caelum (Col 1:18). He the head and we the body, when we hear His voice, we must understand it as coming from the head and the body, because whatever He suffered, we also suffered in Him, and, likewise, what we suffer, He suffers in us. If in man the head suffers something, can we say that the hands do not suffer? Or if the hands suffer something, can it be said that the head does not suffer? Or if the feet suffer something, can it be said that the head does not suffer? When one of our members suffers from something, all the remaining members rush to help the suffering member. Therefore, if, when He suffered, we suffered in Him, and He has already ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father, everything that His Church suffers in the tribulations of this world, in the temptations, in the needs, in the anguish, since it is fitting that she be trained so that, like gold, she may be purified by fire, He also suffers. We prove that we suffer in Him with these words of the Apostle: If you died with Christ, why do you let yourselves be guided by the teachings of the world, as if you lived from it?; and also: Our old man was crucified one with Christ so that the body of sin might be annulled. Therefore, if we have died in Him, in Him we have been resurrected. For the same Apostle says: If you have risen with Christ, taste the things above, seek the things from above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. If we have died in Him and in Him we have risen, He also dies in us and rises in us, for He is the union of the head and the body. Then Corpus, ille est caput, nos corpus. The title of this psalm is the following: Of David, being in the desert of Idumea. By Idumea this world is understood. Idumea was a nation made up of nomadic men in which idols were worshiped. Therefore the word "Idumea" is not recorded here in a good sense. If it is not taken here in a good sense, it must be understood that under the name of Idumea this life is meant, in which we endure so much work, and are subjected to immense needs. Here is the desert where great thirst is felt and where now you must hear the voice of the one who thirsts in the desert. If we recognize ourselves as thirsty, let us also recognize ourselves as drinkers. For whoever thirsts in this world will be satisfied in the future, as the Lord testifies when he says: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied. Therefore in this world we should not desire satiety. Here the need must be felt; there we will be satisfied. But now, so as not to faint in the desert, the dew of the word of God sustains us and does not allow us to dry up completely so that we do not have a new aspiration for what is ours, but rather feel such a thirst that we drink. But to drink, we are now sprinkled by some grace of his; However, we feel thirsty. And what does our soul say to God? 4 [v.2]. God, my God, I watch over you from the dawn. What does it mean to watch? Not sleeping. What is sleep? Rest in dreams. There is a dream proper to the soul and another proper to the body. immerito vox ipsius etiam nostra est, et vox nostra etiam ipsius est. Audiamus ergo Psalmum, et in eo Christum loquentem intelligamus. 3 [v.l]. Titulum habet iste psalmus, Ipsi David, cum esset in deserto Idumaeae. Per Idumaeae nomen intelligitur saeculum istud. Idumaea enim gens erat quaedam errantium hominum, ubi idola colebantur. Non in bono ponitur Idumaea ista. Si non in bono ponitur, intelligendum est istam vitam, ubi patimur so many labors et ubi tantis necessitatibus subditi sumus, Idumaeae nomine mean. Et hic est desertum ubi multum sititur, et audituri estis vocem moda sitientis in deserto. Si autem cognoscamus nos sitientes, cognoscemus nos et bibentes. Quia qui sitit in isto saeculo, in future saeculo satiabitur, dicente Domino: Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt iustitiam, quia ipsi saturabuntur (Mt 5,6). Ergo in hoc saeculo non debenmus quasi amare saginam.

Hic sitiendum est; alibi saginabimur. We all need the sleep of the body, because, if we lack it, the man faints and the body perishes. Our weak body cannot support for long a soul that is attentive and dedicated to exercise. If the soul remained for a long time fully devoted to its activity, the body, weak and earthly, would not tolerate it, would not sustain it working perpetually, and, therefore, would faint. For this reason God granted sleep to the body, so that, its members being repaired by him, they could sustain the awake soul for times. But we must prevent our soul from sleeping, since the sleep of the soul is a bad thing. The body's sleep, with which its health is repaired, is a good thing. The dream of the soul consists of forgetting God. The soul that forgets its God sleeps. That is why the Apostle reproaches certain individuals who forgot God and, as if given over to sleep, surrendered to the delirium of worshiping idols. Those who worship idols are like those who see fantastic things in dreams. The awakened soul understands by whom it has been made and does not worship what it has forged. To those who are asleep in soul the Apostle says: Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you. Did the Apostle wake up the sleeping body? It awakened the sleeping soul when it excited it to be illuminated by Christ. Then, attending to this vigil, the psalmist says: God, my God, I watch over you from the dawn. You would not be awake if the light did not appear to wake you from sleep. Christ illuminates souls and makes them stay awake; If he turns away his light, they surrender to sleep. That is why it is said in another psalm: Enlighten my eyes so that I never fall asleep in death. For the con-

On the other hand, it may also happen that, when the light is present to the souls, as they sleep when they move away from the light, they cannot see, because they sleep. For just as he who sleeps bodily during the day, although the sun has already risen and the day is already warm, nevertheless he is as in the night, because he is not awake to see the day already born, so also some, when Christ is already present and the truth preached, are in the sleep of the soul. Then, if you watch, you must daily say to these: You who sleep, wake up and arise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you. Your life and your customs must be awake in Christ so that others, the sleeping pagans, may perceive them, and thus, at the noise of your vigil, they may become excited and awaken their sleep and begin to say with you in Christ: God, my God, I watch for you from the dawn. 5. My soul thirsted for you. Behold the desert of Idumea. See how He feels thirsty here, but notice how good it is here to thirst for Him. There are some who thirst, but not for God. Everyone who wants to get something for themselves is in the ardor of desire. This desire is the thirst of the soul. See how many desires are contained in the heart of man; one desires gold, another silver, another property, another estates; this one abundant money, that one big house, another woman, that honors, this one children. See how these desires are found in the heart of man. All men burn with desire and hardly anyone can be found who says: My soul thirsted for you. Men feel thirst for the world, and they do not understand that they are in the desert of Idumea, where the soul must feel thirst for God. Let us say: He thirsted for you

Sitivit tibi anima mea. Ecce illud desertum Idumaeae. Videte quomodo hic sitit: sed videte quid hic bonum est, Sitivit tibi. Sunt enim qui sitiunt, sed non Deo. Videtis desideria ista, quomodo sunt in cordibus hominum. Ardent omnes homines desiderio; et vix invenitur qui dicat: Sitivit tibi anima mea. Sitiunt enim homines saeculo; et non se intelligunt

my soul Let us all say it, because in union with Christ we are all one soul. Let the soul feel thirsty in Idumea. 6. My soul, he says, thirsted for you, and my flesh also in many ways. It was little that my soul felt thirst; My flesh also feels it. Therefore, if the soul thirsts for God, how does the flesh also thirst for God? When the flesh is thirsty, it thirsts for water, and when the soul feels thirst, it thirsts for the source of wisdom. With the water of this fountain our souls will be intoxicated; Another psalm says: They will be drunk with the abundance of your house and you will give them to drink from the stream of your delights. Then you must feel a thirst for wisdom, you must feel a thirst for justice. But we will only be satisfied and fed up with it when this life ends and we arrive at the promise of God. God promised us equality with the angels. The angels do not now feel hunger and thirst like we do; However, they are satisfied with truth, with light, with incorruptible wisdom. For this they are blessed; and they are so blessed that from that city, the heavenly Jerusalem, towards which we are heading, pilgrims contemplate us and feel compassion for us and help us, by command of the Lord, so that we may eventually reach our common homeland and there be saturated with them with truth and holiness at the fountain of the Lord. Then now our soul feels thirsty. But how does our flesh feel it in very different ways? My flesh—he says—thirsts for you in many ways. This happens because the resurrection is promised to our flesh. As blessedness is promised to the soul, so resurrection is promised to the soul.

For a long time we are eating and drinking, although we eat and drink to restore our strength, the same prolonged refection is a fainting; If we stand for a long time, we get tired, and that is why we sit down; and, if we sit for a long time, we also get tired, and that is why we get up. See also that our flesh never remains in a constant state, because from infancy it passes to puerce; You look for his childhood, and you no longer find it, because instead of childhood, childishness presents itself. This also migrates towards adolescence; You ask about childishness, and you no longer find it: the adolescent has become young; you look for adolescence, and it no longer exists: the young man has become old; You look for the young man, and he has disappeared; and the old man dies; You look for the old man, and he no longer exists. Therefore our age does not remain in an unalterable state. At all times he finds fatigue; everywhere, fainting; everywhere, corruption. Given the hope of the resurrection that God promises us in all these multiple decays, we thirst for that incorruption, and thus our flesh thirsts for God in many ways. In this Idumea, in this desert, he thirsts in as many ways as he suffers; He thirsts for that indefatigable incorruption in as many ways as he is tired of. 7 [v.3]. If the flesh, my brothers, of the good Christian and believer thirsts for God in this world, since the flesh needs bread, water, wine, money and support, it must be asked of God, not of demons or idols or some other powers of this century. There are some who, when they are physically hungry, turn away from God and pray to Mercury or ask Jupiter to

remedy, or the goddess they call Celeste, or other similar demons. The flesh of these does not thirst for God. Those who thirst for God must feel it completely, with their soul and with their flesh, because God gives the soul its bread, and also gives the flesh the things it needs, since God made the soul and the flesh. Do you ask the demons for what the flesh needs? Did God make the soul, and demons the flesh? He who created the soul also created the flesh; He who created both things feeds them. Let both thirst for God and be satisfied with simplicity through multiple work. 8. When our soul feels thirsty, and also, in various ways, our flesh, but not for anyone, but for ri, O Lord! That is, for our God, where do we feel it? In the desert land, without road and without water. We said that this world is Idumea, namely, the desert of Idumea, because of which this psalm received its title. In a desert land; It is little to be deserted, that is, to be found without men to inhabit; That is why it is added and without road and without water. I wish that at least the desert had a road! I wish that the man who ventures there knew where to get out of that place! She finds no man for her comfort, she finds no way to leave the desert aside. Then he stays there. I wish there was water at least, with which to cool down those who cannot get out of there! Painful desert, horrible and worthy of fear! However, God took pity on us and gave us a way in the desert: to our Lord Jesus Christ; and he gave us comfort, sending us preachers of his word; and he also gave us water in the desert,

quamvis propter refectionem manducemus et bibamus, ipsa diuturna refectio defectio est: si diu stemus, fatiguemur: ideo sedemus: et si diu sedeamus, et ibi fatiguemur, et ideo surgimus. Non stat ergo aetas nostra: ubique fatiguetio est, ubique Iassitudo, ubique corruptio. Attendentes qualem nobis spem resurrectionis promittat Deus, in istis omnibus multiplicibus defectionibus nostris sitimus illam incorruptionem; et sic caro nostra multiplicitei sitit Deo. In this Idumaea, in isto deserto, quam multipliciter laborat, tam multipliciter sitit; quam multipliciter fatiguetut, tam multipliciter sitit illam infatigabilem incorruptionem. 7 [v.3]. Quanquam, fratres mei, boni christiani et fidelis etiam in hoc saeculo caro Deo sitit: quia si opus est carni pane, si opus est aqua, si opus est vino, si opus est nummo, si opus est jumento carni huic, a Deo petere debent, non a daemoniis, et idolis, et a nescio quibus potestatibus huius saeculi. Sunt enim qui, quando famem patiuntur in

isto saeculo, dimittunt Deum, et rogant Mercurium, aut rogant Iovem ut det illis, aut quam dicunt Caelestem, aut aliqua daemonia similia: non Deo sitit caro ipsorum. Qui autem Deo sitiunt, undique debent sitire, et anima, et carne: quia et animae Deus dat panem suum, id est verbum veritatis; et carni Deus dat quae necessaria sunt, quia Deus fecit et animam et carnem. Propter carnem tuam rogas daemonia: numquid animam Deus fecit, et carnem tuam daemonia fecerunt? Qui fecit animam, ipse fecit et carnem: qui fecit both res, ipse pascit both res. Utrumque nostrum Deo sitiat, et ex labore multiplici simpliciter satietur. 8. Ubi autem sitit anima nostra, et multipliciter caro nostra, non cuicumque, sed tibi, Domine, id est Deo nostro; ubi sitit? In terra deserta, et sine via, et sine aqua. Saeculum istud diximus; ipsa est Idumaea, hoc est desertum Idumaeae, unde titulum Psalmus accepit. In terra deserta. Parum est, deserta, ubi nullus hominum habitat; insuper, et sine via, et sine aqua. Utinam vel viam haberet ipsum desertum! utinam illuc homo incurrens, vel nosset qua inde exiret! Non videt hominem ad solatium, non videt viam qua careat deserto. Ergo ibi divertit. Utinam esset vel aqua, unde reficeretur, qui inde non potest exire! Malum desertum, horribile et timendum! et tamen Deus misertus est nostri, et fecit nobis viam in deserto, ipsum Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum (lo 14,6); et fecit nobis consolationem in deserto, mittendo ad nos praedi-

giving the Holy Spirit to his preachers so that the fountain of water that flows to eternal life would be formed in them. See that we have all this here, but it does not come from the desert. Then the psalm reminded us, above all, of the peculiarity of the desert so that, when you know what misfortune you find yourself in, if by chance you could have some consolations from companions on the road or water, you would not attribute them to the desert, but to Him who deigned to visit you in the desert. 9. So I came to you in the sanctuary to see your power and your glory. First my soul and my flesh thirsted for you in many ways in the desert, and in the land, without path and without water, and so I presented myself to you in the sanctuary to see your glory and your power. If someone does not first feel thirsty in the desert, that is, in the evil in which he finds himself, he will never reach the good that is God. And I presented myself to you, he says, in the sanctuary. It is already a great comfort to be in the sanctuary. What does it mean I introduced myself to you? I appeared so that you could see me, and for this reason you saw me so that I could see you. I showed up to you to see. He did not say: I appeared to you that you might see, but: I appeared to you to see your power and your glory. Hence the Apostle also says: But now, having known God, or rather, having been known by God. First you presented yourselves to God so that God could present himself to you. To see your power and your glory. Indeed, if man in this desert, that is, in this solitude or wasteland, removes from the wilderness what is convenient for his health, he will never see the power and glory of the Lord, but will remain dead of thirst and will not find the way or consolation,

nor water, without which he will not be able to survive in the desert. But, if he turns to God, saying from the depths of his heart: My soul and my flesh thirsted for you in many ways, so that perhaps I may not ask for the necessary things of the flesh from others and not from God, and not desire from others the resurrection of the flesh that God promises us, you will obtain many small consolations. 10. See, brothers, that just as our flesh, even when it has not yet received perfect health, with which it will not suffer hardship or any need, while it is mortal and fragile before the resurrection, is endowed with certain aids with which we live: bread, water, fruits, wine, oil, and, if we lacked all these aids and aids, we could not survive; Likewise, our soul, while it is in this flesh in the midst of the temptations and dangers of this world, is still weak and is also endowed with the help of the word, of prayer, of controversy. These things are to our soul what those were to our flesh. As when our flesh is resurrected it will have its own disposition and state of incorruption whereby it will no longer need these things, so also the soul will then possess its own food: the same Word of God, by which all things were made. However, let us give thanks to God, who did not abandon us now in this desert, since he gave us what the flesh and the soul need. But when He teaches us to endure needs, He wants us to love Him even more, lest perhaps we become perverted with food and forget Him. Sometimes He takes away from us the things that are necessary to us and hurts us so that we may know what He is.

quam duret in eremo. Cum autem erexerit se ad Deum, ut dicat illi ex medullis ómnibus, Sitivit tibi anima mea: quam multipliciter tibi et caro mea; ne forte vel necessaria carnis ab alus petat et non a Deo, aut non desidetet illam resurrectionem carnis quam nobis promittit Deus: cum ergo se erexerit, habebit non parvas consolationes. 10. Ecce, fratres, quomodo caro nostra quamdiu mortalis est, quamdiu fragilis est, ante illam resurrectionem habet solatia ista quibus vivimus, panem, aquam, fructus, vinum, oleum (ista omnia solatia et subsidia si nos deserant, utique durare non possumus) quamvis nondum receperit caro ista sanitatem illam petfectam, ubi nullam patietur anguishan!, nullam indigentiam: sic et anima nostra cum hic est in ista carne, inter temptationes et pericula saeculi huius, adhuc est infirma; habet etiam ipsa solatia verbi, solatia orationis, solatia disputationis: sic sunt ista animae nosttae, quomodo illa carnis nostrae. Cum autem resurrexerit caro nostra, ut iam istis non indigeamus, habebit locum quemdam et statum incorruptionis suae: sic et anima nostra habebit cibum suum, ipsum Vetbum Dei, per quod facta sunt omnia (lo 1,3). Also thank you Deo, how we did it did not desert us; sive dar nobis quod necessarium est catni, sive dar nobis quod animae necessatium est: et quando nos aliquibus necessitatibus erudit, vult ut amplius illum diligamus; ne forte per saginam corrumpamur, et obliviscamur eum, Subtrahit S.Ag. 20

Father and Lord, who not only caresses, but also punishes. In this way he prepares us for a certain great and incorruptible inheritance. If you, thinking about leaving your son a barrel, or a cellar, or something else that you have at home, and so that he does not lose anything of yours, which he must also leave here the same as you, instruct him, call him to order and punish him, would you not want our Father, who is to give us such an inheritance, to instruct us with the lashes of necessity and tribulation, which will not be able to disappear? God is to give us an inheritance of Himself so that we may possess Him and be eternally possessed by Him. 11. Then we present ourselves to God in the sanctuary so that He may present Himself to us, let us present ourselves to Him with the holy desire that He may present Himself to us with the power and glory of the Son of God. Many do not show up. Meet in the sanctuary so that it may be presented to you. Not a few think that He was only a man, since He was born of man, that He was crucified and died, that He walked on the earth, that He ate and drank and that He performed other human operations, and for this they judge that He was like other men. You have recently heard when reading the Gospel how His Majesty remembered, saying: I and the Father are one. See how great was the greatness and equality of the Father, who came down to the flesh because of our weakness! See how much we are loved before we loved God! If before loving God we were loved by Him in such a way that He made His Son a man, equal to Him, for love of men, what will He not reserve for those who love Him? Many think that it is nobis aliquando quae necessaria sunt, et atterit nos; ut sciamus quia Pater et Dominus est, non solum blandiens, sed et flagellans. Praeparat enim care for us haereditati incorruptibili et magnae. Si unam cuppam, aut unam cellam tuam, aut si quid habes in domo tua, cogitas dimittere filio tuo, et nc perdat illud, erudis eum, et flagellis eum ad disciplinam corrigis, ne peidat nihil tuum, quod et ipse hic dimissurus est, sicut et tu: non vis ut nos erudiat Pater noster in flagellis etiam necessitatum aut tribulationum, qui nobis talem haereditatem datums est, quae transite non possit? Haereditatem enim nobis dabit seipsum Deus, ut ipsum possideamus, et ab ipso possideamur in aeternum. 11.

Ergo in sancto appareamus Deo, ut appareat nobis; appareamus illi in sancto desiderio, ut appareat nobis in potentia et gloria Filii Dei. Multis enim non apparuit; sint in sancto, ut appareat et illis. Nam multi putant illum tantummodo hominem Fuisse, quia praedicatur natus ex homine, crucifixus et mortuus, ambulasse in terra, manducasse et bibisse, et caetera egisse, quae sunt humano; et putant illum talem Fuisse, quales sunt caeteri nomines. Audistis autem moda eum Evangelium legeretur, quomodo commendavit maiestatem suam: Ego et Pater unum sumus (Ib. 10,30). Ecce quanta maiestas, et quanta aequalitas Patris descendit ad carnem propter infirmitatem nostram! Ecce quantum dilecti sumus, antequam Deum diligeremus! Si antequam Deum diligeremus, tantum ab ¡lio dilecti sumus, ut aequalem sibi Filium suum hominem faceret propter nos; quid nobis servat iam diligentibus se? Ergo multi nessio
Prayer of fugitive David in the desert

It is a small thing for the Son of God to have appeared on earth. Since they are not in the sanctuary, neither its power nor its glory is manifested to them; That is to say, since they have not yet sanctified their hearts so that they can understand the excellence of his power, and therefore give thanks to God, because, being immense, he was born and suffered for men, they cannot see his glory and his power. 12 [v. 4]. Because your mercy is better than lives. There are many kinds of human lives. But God promised only one life, and he does not give it to us as if it were due to our merits, but out of his mercy. Well, what good did we do to deserve it? What good works did we do so that God would give us his grace? Did he perhaps find justice to reward and only crimes to forgive? If he had wanted to punish the crimes he forgave, it certainly would not have been unjust. Well, what is more just than punishing the sinner? Since it is just to punish the sinner, not punishing him, but justifying him, and converting a sinner into a just one, and from an impious one into an innocent one, is a matter of God's mercy. Therefore his mercy is better than lives. What lives? Those that men chose for themselves. One chooses the commercial life, the other the agricultural life, the other the banking life, the other the military life; some one and some another. There are different lives, but your mercy is better than lives. Better is what you give to the correct than what the wicked choose. You give a life that must be preferred to all of ours, whatever we could have chosen in the world. Because your mercy is better than lives; my lips will praise you. No quid minimum putant apparuisse in terra Filium Dei; quia non sunt in sancto, non eis apparet potentia ipsius, et gloria ipsius: id est, quia nondum sanctificatum habent cor, unde intelligant eminentiam virtutis illius, et gratias agant Deo quia propter ipsos tantus quo venit, ad quam nativitatem, ad quam passionem; non possunt videre gloriam ipsius et potentiam ipsius. 12 [v.4]. Quoniam melior est mercy tua super vitas. Multae sunt vitae humanoe; sed Deus unam vitam promittit; et non illam dat nobis quasi propter merita nostra, sed propter misericordiam suam.

Quid enim boni egimus, ut illud mereremur? aut quae bona facta nostra praecesserunt, ut Deus nobis gratiam suam daret? Numquid invenit iustitias quas coronaret, et non delicta quae donaret? Utique delicta quae donavit si puniré vellet, non esset iniustum. Quid enim tam iustum, quam ut puniatur peccator? Cum iustum sit ut puniatur peccator, pertinuit ad misericordiam ipsius non puniré peccatorem, sed iustificare, et de peccatore faceré iustum, et de impio faceré pium. Ergo mercy ipsius melior super vitas. What do you live? Quas sibi nomines elegerunt. Alius elegit sibi vitam negotiandi, alius vitam rusticandi, alius vitam fenerandi, alius vitam militandi; alius illam, alius illam. Diversae sunt vitae, sed melior est misericordia tua super vitas nostras. Melius is quod das correctis, quam quod eligunt perversi. Unam vitam donas, quae praeponatur omnibus nostris, quascumque in mundo willelect potuerimus. Quo-

My lips would praise you unless your mercy had preceded you. For your gift I praise you; Because of your mercy I praise you. For I would not have been able to praise God if He had not given me something to praise Him. Because your mercy is better than lives, my lips will praise you. 13 [v. 5]. Thus I will bless you in my life, and in your name I will raise my arms. This is how I will bless you in my life: in the life you gave me, not the one I chose, with others, according to the world, among the many lives that are in it; in which you gave me because of your mercy so that I would praise you. This is how I will bless you in my life. What does that mean? That I will attribute my life in which I praise you to your mercy, not to my merits. And in your name I will raise my hands. Raise your hands in prayer. Our Lord Jesus Christ lifted and extended his hands on the cross for us. He extended his hands on the cross so that we could extend ours in good works. His cross offered us mercy, since, when He raised His hands and offered Himself for us as a sacrifice to God, through that sacrifice all our sins were erased. Let us also raise our hands to God in prayer, for our hands raised to God will not go wrong if they are exercised in good works. What is he doing who raises his hands? Where are we commanded to pray to God with our hands up? The Apostle says: I want therefore that men should pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and without dispute. When you raise your hands to God, remember your works, for when these hands are raised to ask for what

If you want, you must think about exercising the same hands in good works so that they will not be ashamed of being lifted up to God. In your name I will raise my hands. These hands are our prayers in this Idumea, in this desert, in this land without water and without a path, where Christ is our way, but not the way of this land. In your name I will raise my hands. 14 [v. 6]. And what will I say when I raise my hands in your name? What will I ask for? Hey, brothers, when you raise your hands, consider carefully what you have to ask for, because you ask the Almighty. Ask Him for something great, not what those who do not believe in Him ask of Him. You know what things are also given to the wicked. Should you ask your God for money? Does He not also give it to the wicked, who do not believe in Him? Then if he also gives it to the wicked, then what great thing do you ask of him? It pleases you that the things he gives to the wicked are of such little importance that they are worthy of giving to them as well, so that it does not seem to you that what can be given to the wicked is a great thing. Certainly all earthly things belong to God; But keep in mind that the goods that he also gives to the evil ones are not to be considered great. Another good is what he reserves for us. Let us reconsider what he gives to the bad, and therefore let us understand what he reserves for the good. See what it gives to the bad: this light, but observe that the good and the bad see it; the rain that falls on the earth, and from which so many good things are derived, but which is given to good and bad, as it is said in the Gospel: God makes the sun rise on the bad and the good and rains on the righteous and sinners. The goods that come from rain or sun,

niam melior est mercy tua super vitas, labia mea laudabunt te. Non te laudarent labia mea, nisi me praecederet mercy tua. Dono tuo te laudo, per misericordiam tuam te laudo. Non enim ego possem laudare Deum, nisi mihi donaret laudare se posse. Quoniam melior est mercy tua super vitas, labia mea laudabunt te. 13 [v.5]. Sic benedicam te in vita mea, et in nomine tuo levabo manus meas. Sic benedicam te in vita mea: iam in vita mea quam mihi donasti; non in illa quam ego elegi secundum mundum cum caeteris, Inter fines vitas, sed quam dedisti mihi per misericordiam mam ut te laudarem. Sic benedicam te in vita mea. What is it, sic? Ut Misericordiae tuae tribuam vitam meam in qua te laudo; non meritis meis. Et in nomine tuo levabo manus meas. Leva ergo manus in oratione. Levavit pro nobis Dominus noster manus in intersection, et extensoe sunt manus eius pro nobis. Ideo extensoe sunt manus eius in intersection, ut manus nostrae extendantur in bona opera; quia crux ipsius misericordion nobis praebuit. Ecce levavit ille manus, et obtulit pro nobis sacrificium Deo seipsum, et per illud sacrificium deleta sunt omnia peccata nostra. Levemus et nos manus nostras ad Deum in prece; et non confundentur manus nostrae levatae ad Deum, si exerceantur in bonis operibus. Quid enim facit qui levat manus? Unde praeceptum est ut levatis manibus oremus ad Deum? Apostolus enim dicit: Levantespuras manus, sine ira et disceptatione

(I Tim 2,8). Ut cum levas manus ad Deum, veniant tibi inmentem opera tua. Quia enim manus istae levantur ut impetres quod vis, ipsas manus cogitas in bonis operibus exercere, ne erubescant levari ad Deum. In nomine tuo levabo manus meas. Istae preces nostrae sunt in hac Idumaea, in hoc deserto, in terra sine aqua, et sine via, ubi nobis Christus est via (lo 14,6); sed non via de hac terra. In nomine tuo levabo manus meas. 14 [v.6]. Et quid dicam, cum levabo manus meas in nomine tuo? quid petam? Eia, fratres, quando levatis manus, quaerite quid petatis; ab Omnipotent enim petitis. Aliquid magnum petite; non qualia petunt qui nondum crediderunt. Videtis qualia dentur et impiis. Petiturus is a Deo tuo pecuniam? Numquid non donat eam et sceleratis qui in illum non credunt? Quid ergo magnum petiturus is quod donat et malis? Sed non tibi displiceat, quia quae donat et malis tam frivola sunt, ut et malis donari dignified sint: ne tibi quasi magna videantur quae possunt donari et malis. Dei quidem sunt et omnia dona terrena; sed videte quia quae donat et malis non pro magno habenda sunt. Est aliud quod nobis servat. Cogitemus autem quae donat et malis, et hinc íntelligamus quid servet bonis. Quae donat malis videte: donat illis luzem istam; videte quia vident illam boni et mali: pluviam quae descendit super terram; et hinc quanta bona nascuntur! Et malis inde praestatur, et bonis, dicente Gospel: Qui solem suum oriri facit super bonds et malo; et pluit

without a doubt we must ask God for them when we need them; but not only these, since they are given to good and bad people. What should we ask for when we raise our hands? The psalm said it as best it could. What does what I said mean: how could he? As the human word could communicate it to human ears. Since these things were said through human speech, and also using certain similarities so that all the weak and all children could understand it. What did he say? What did you ask for? In your name, he says, I will raise my hands. What must you receive? My soul will be filled with substance and fatness. Do you think, my brothers, that this soul desired any fatness of flesh? She did not wish as a great thing that lambs and fattened pigs had been killed for her, nor did she wish that she had reached some inn where she would find sumptuous food to fill her fill. If we believed this, we would be worthy of hearing these things. Then we must understand something spiritual. Our soul has a certain fatness. The saturation of wisdom. Souls that lack this wisdom fail and become so weak that they soon lack strength for any good work. Why do they quickly lose the strength for every good work? Because they do not have the fat of their satiety. Listen to the Apostle, who speaks about the fatness of the soul, commanding that each one do good. And what does it say? God loves a cheerful giver. Where does the soul come from to be full of life if not from being saturated by God? And yet, no matter how much fat it has here, what must it not have in the other world, where God himself will feed us?

While we are in this exile, it cannot be said which one we will have then. Perhaps, when we raise our hands, we desire here this satiety of heaven, with which we will be so saturated that all indigence will disappear completely and we will no longer desire it, because with it everything we desire here, everything we consider great, everything will instantly be within our reach. Our parents died, but God lives. Here we cannot always have parents; There we will always have a Father alive living in our homeland. We cannot remain in the earthly homeland forever; It is necessary that others be born, and precisely the children of its citizens are born to drive their parents away from there. The child is born saying to the eldest: What are you doing here? It is necessary that those who are born and succeed others cast out those who preceded them. But there we will all live together; there will be no successor, because there will be no decessor. What will that country be? Do you love riches here? God himself will be your wealth. Do you delight in a pure fountain? What is purer than wisdom? What is more transparent? Everything you can love here will be replaced for you by the one who made all things. My soul will be filled with substance and fatness; and the lips of joy will praise your name. In this desert I will lift up my hands in your name, and my soul will be filled with substance and fatness, and my lips will exalt your name with joy. Now, while you are thirsty, you pray; When thirst passes, prayer passes and praise follows, and the lips of rejoicing will praise your name.

super iustos et iniustos (Mt 5,45). Dona ergo ista quae nascuntur, vel de pluvia, vel de solé, a Domino quidem nostro petere debenmus, cum sint necessaria; sed non ista sola, quia ista dantur et bonis et malis. Quid ergo debenmus petere, quando levamus manus? Quia quomodo potuit dixit illud Psalmus. Quid est quod dixi, quomodo potuit? Quomodo potuit os humanum auribus humanis. Quia per ora humano is dicta sunt, et per quasdam similaritiesines dicta sunt, quomodo capere possent omnes infirmi, omnes parvuli. Quid dixit? quid petivit? In nomine, inquit, tuo levabo manus meas. Quid accepturus? Tanquam adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea. Putatis aliquam pinguedinem carnis desiderasse animam istam, fratres mei? Non enim hoc pro magno desideravit, ut pingues arietes, ut pingues porci illi mactarentur; aut vendeet ad aliquam popinam, ubi inveniret obsonia pinguia, unde saturaretur. Si hoc crediderimus, digni sumus qui ista audiamus. Ergo aliquid spirituale debenmus intelligere. Habet quamdam pinguedinem anima nostra. Est quaedam saturitas pinguis sapientiae. Sapientia enim ista animae quae carent, marcescunt; et omnino ita exiles fiunt, ut in omnibus bonis operibus cyto deficiant. Quare cyto deficiunt in omnibus bonis operibus? Quia non habent pinguedinem saturitatis suae. Audi Apostolum dicentem de pingui anima, praecipientem ut quisque bene operetur. Quid ait? Hilarem datorem diligit Deus (2 Cor 9:7). Pinguis anima unde esset pinguis, nisi a Domino saturaretur? Et tamen quantumlibet hic sit pinguis, quid erit in

illo future saeculo, what did God pass us by? Interim in hac peregrinatione, quid erimus tune nec dici potest. Et fortasse ipsam saturitatem optamus hic, quando levamus manus nostras, ubi pinguedine sic saturabimur, ut omnino omnis indigentia nostra intereat, et nihil desideremus: quia totum praesto nobis erit quidquid hic desideramus, quidquid hic pro magno amamus. Iam patres nostri mortui sunt; Deus autem vivit: non hic potuimus semper habere patres; ibi autem semper habebimus vivum unum Patrem, habentes patriam nostram: quaecumque terrena est, semper ibi esse non possumus; et necesse est ut alii nascantur, et ad hoc nascantur filii civium illorum ut excludant inde parentes suos. Ad hoc enim nascitur puer, ut dicat maiori: Quid hic agis? Necesse est ut qui succedunt, et qui nascuntur, excludant eos qui se praecesserunt. Ibi omnes pariter vivemus; non ibi erit successor quia nullus decessor. Qualis illa patria? Be divine, did you love? Ipse Deus tibi erit divitiae tuae. Do you love fontem bonum? Quid praeclarius illa sapientia? quid lucidius? Quidquid hic potest amari, pro omnibus tibi erit qui fecit omnia. Tanquam adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea; et labia exsultationis laudabunt nomen tuum. In hac eremo, in nomine tuo levabo manus meas: impleatur anima mea tanquam adipe et pinguedine; et labia exsultationis laudabunt nomen tuum. Mode enim oratio, quamdiu sitis; cum sitis transitierit, transit oratio, et succedit laudatio: Et labia exsultationis laudabunt nomen tuum.

15 [v.7-8]. If I remember you in my bed, in the early mornings I will meditate on you, because you became my helper. He calls his rest a bed. When anyone rests, let him remember God; When anyone is at rest, let him not dissipate and forget God. If you remember God when you are at rest, you will meditate on God in your activities. He called his actions early morning because every man begins to do something early. What did he say when he said: If I remember you in my bed, I will meditate on you in the morning? If I do not remember in my bed, I will not remember you in the morning. He who does not think about God when he is at rest, in his activities, will not be able to think about Him. But whoever remembers Him when he is at rest, meditates on Him when he works so as not to falter in action. So what does it add? And in the early mornings I will meditate on you, because you became my helper. Indeed, if God does not help us in our good works, we cannot execute them. And yet, we must do good things, that is, we must act as in the light when we work by teaching ourselves Christ. Anyone who acts perversely acts at night and not at dawn, as the Apostle tells us: Those who get drunk get drunk at night, and those who sleep sleep at night; We, who belong to the day, are sober. We are exhorted, then, to walk honestly as in the day: As in the day, he says, let us walk honestly. And also: You are children of light and children of the day, not of the night or darkness. Who are the children of the night and darkness? Who execute all kinds of evils. In such a way they are children of the night, that they fear being seen what they do; and, when they execute pu-

Physically bad works, they do them in the sight of everyone, because there are many who do them; but, when there are few who do them, they do them secretly. Those who perform such works publicly do them in full sunlight, but in the darkness of the heart. Therefore no one works early in the morning unless he works in Christ. Whoever, being idle, remembers Christ, meditates on Him in all his activities, and Christ helps him in doing good so that he does not faint due to weakness. If I remember you in my bed, in the early mornings I will meditate on you, because you became my helper. 16. And in the covering of your wings I will rejoice. I rejoice in good works because above me is the veil of your wings. If you do not protect me, since I am a chick, the kite will snatch me away. In a certain place our Lord Himself says to Jerusalem, the city in which He was crucified: Jerusalem, Jerusalem! How many times I wanted to gather your children together like a hen her chicks, and you did not want to! We are little children, God shelters us under the shadow of his wings. What will happen to us when we grow up? It will be a good thing for us if He also shelters us so that under that Greater One we will always be chicks, since He will always be greater no matter how much we grow. Let no one say: Cover me while I am a child; as if in some time it could reach such greatness that it would be enough for itself. You are nothing without God's protection. We want to always be protected by Him, because we can always be great.

15 [v.7-8]. Si memoratus sum tui super stratum meum, in dilucuüs meditabar in te; quia factus is adiutor meus. Stratum suum quietem suam dicit. Quando alíquis quietus est, memor sit Dei; quando aliquis quietus est, non per quietem dissolvatur et obliviscatur Deum; si memor est Dei quando quietus est, in actionibus suis in Deum meditatur. Diluculum enim dixit actiones, quia omnis homo diluculo incipit aliquid agere. Quid ergo dixit? Si memor fue tui in strato meo, et in iiluculis meditabar in te. Si ergo non fue memor in strato meo, et in diluculo non meditabar in te. What when otiosus est non cogitat Deum, in actionibus suis cogitare potest Deum? Qui autem memor eius est quaado quietus est, in ipso meditatur cum agit, ne in actione deficiat. Ideo quid adiecit? Et in diluculis meditabar in te; quia jactus is adiutor meus. Etenim nisi Deus adiuvet bona opera nostra, impleri a nobis non possunt. Et dignified debenmus operari; id est tanquam in luz, quando Christo demonstrante operamur. Quicumque operatur mala, in nocte operatur, non in diluculo, Apostle saying: Qui inebriantur, nocte inebria-ntur; et qui dormiunt, nocte dormiunt: nos qui diei sumus, sobrii simus. Hortatur nos ut secundum diem ambulemus honeste: Sicut in d-ie, inquit, honeste ambulemus (Rom 13,13). Et iterum: Vos, inquit, filii lucís estis, et filii diei; non sumus noctis ñeque tenebrarum (1 Thess 5,5.8). Qui sunt filii noctis,

et filii tenebrarum? Qui omnia mala operantur. Usque adeo filii noctis sunt, ut timeant videri quae operantur: et quae publice operantur mala, ideo publice operantur, quia multi illa operantur; quae pauci operantur, in abscondito operantur. Qui autem talia publice operantur, sunt quidem in luz solis, sed in tenebris cordis. Nemo ergo in diluculo operatur, nisi qui in Christo operatur. Sed qui otiosus memor est Christi, in ipso meditatur in omnibus actionibus suis; et est illi adiutor in bono opere, ne per infirmitatem suam deficiat. Si memoratus sum tui super stratum meum, in dilucuüs meditabar in te; quia factus is adiutor meus. 16. Et in velamento pennarum tuarum exsultabo. Hilaresco in bonis operibus, quia super me est velamen pennarum tuarum. If you don't protect me quia pullus sum, milvus rapiet me. Dicit enim quodam loco ipse Dominus noster ad Ierusalem, quamdam civitatem illam, ubi crucifixus est: Ierusalem, inquit, Ierusalem, quoties volui filios tuos congregare, tanquam gallina pullos suos, et noluisti! (Mt 23,37). Parvuli sumus: ergo protegat nos Deus sub umbraculo alarum suarum. Quid cum maiores facti fuerimus? Bonum est nobis ut et tune protegat nos, ut sub illo maiore semper nos pulli simus. Semper enim ille maior est, quantumeumque creverimus. Nemo dicat, Protegat me, cum parvulus sum: quasi aliquando ad tantam magnitudeinem possit pervenire, quae sibi sufficiat. Sine protectione Dei nihil es. Semper ab illo protégé velimus: tune semper in

Give in Him if we always remain little children under Him. And in the covering of your wings - I will rejoice. 17 [v.9]. My soul adhered to you. See the anxious one, see the thirsty one, see how he clings to God. Let this affection be born in you. If it has already been born, let it be watered and grow, and reach such robustness that you also say from your heart: My soul clung to you. What is this binder? This gluten is charity. Have charity; With that binder your soul adheres to God. Not with God, but after God, so that He may go before you and you may follow. When the Lord, who had come to redeem us and give his blood as a price for us, began to announce his passion, Peter was horrified as if he saw the Lord already dead, whom he wanted to have always with him, living here, the way he saw him, because, given over to the eyes of the flesh, he felt a carnal affection in relation to the Lord, and that is why he says to Jesus: Lord, take this idea away from you; God will be kind to you. 1. Celebrating today the triumph of the holy martyrs, let us rejoice remembering them, thinking about what they suffered and understanding what they attempted. They would never have endured so many tribulations in the flesh if they had not had great peace in their mind. Let us discuss this reason, attending to the festivity. Yesterday your charity heard many things. Today we must deny this festival our tribute. In this psalm the passion of the Lord is especially recommended; But since the martyrs could not have been strong unless they contemplated the one who suffered first, nor could they endure in his passion the torments that he endured unless he expected in the resurrection such joys as he demonstrated in himself, let us recognize here not only the voice of the Lord, but also our own, and that all those who are united to him are members of his head. You have here, then, a very well-known voice that speaks not only in the name of the head, but also in the name of the body; and some words that not only point out and announce our Lord Jesus Christ, who ascended to heaven, but also his members, who must follow their own head. Others, on the contrary, fearing, consented, and remained alive; However, they were devoured by enemies. The slain were spared, and the living were devoured. Hence that voice of congratulation: Maybe they would have swallowed us alive. Many were devoured, and they were alive; but many were devoured dead. Let the Jews not say: We

We did not kill Crisro, because they handed him over to Judge Pilate to pretend that they were innocent of his death. When Pilate said to them, "You kill him," they replied, "It is not permitted for us to kill anyone." Therefore, they wanted to put the evil of their crime on the male judge. But were they deceiving the judge God? Without a doubt, Pilate participated somewhat in his evil in what he did; but, compared to them, he was much less perverse, because he insisted as much as he could to free him from their hands. That is why he presented him scourged before them. He did not scourge the Lord out of malice, but rather he wanted to appease the Jewish fury so that, moved by this, they would desist from wanting to mar him when they saw him already scourged. Certainly he did this. But, as they persevered in their attempt, you know that he washed his hands, saying that he did not do it and that he was innocent of the death of Jesus. However, he killed him. But, if it is criminal because he did it, even if forced, will those who forced him to do it be innocent? By no means. He decreed a sentence and ordered him to be crucified, and it appeared that he had branded him, but you killed him, O Jews! How did you kill him? With the sword of the tongue, for you sharpened your tongues. When did you hurt him? When you shouted: Crucify, crucify him!

Pertulit omnes infirmos eorum, curavit omnes languidos eorum, praedicavit regnum caelorum, non tacuit vitia eorum, ut ipsa potius eis dispücerent, non medicus a quo sanabantur: his ómnibus curationibus eius ingrati, tanquammulta febri phrenetici, insanientes in medicum qui venerat curare eos, excogitaverunt consilium perdendi eum; tanquam ibi volentes will prove utrum veré homo sit qui mori possit, an aliquid super homines sit, et morí se non permittat. Verbum ipsorum agnoscimus in Sapientia Salomone: Morte turpissima, inquiunt, condemnemus eum. Interrogemus eum; erit enim respectus in sermonibus illius: if enim I will see Filius Dei est, liberet eum (Wis 2,18-20). Videoamus ergo quid factum sit. 4 [v.4.5]. Quia exacuerunt tanquam gladium linguas suas. Filii hominum, dentes eorum arma et sagittae, et ling-ua eorum gladius acutus (Ps 56,5), quod dicit et alius psalmus: sic et hic, Exacuerunt tanquam ¿Udium linguas suas. Non dicant Iudaei: Non occidimus Christum. Ete-

nim propterea eum dederunt iudici Pilate, ut quasi ipsi a morte eius viderentur immunes. Nam eum dixisset eis Pilatus, Vos eum occidite, responderunt: Nobis non licet occidere quemquam (lo 18,31)- Iniquitatem facinoris sui in iudicem hominem refundere volebant: sed numquid Deum iudicem fallebant? Quod fecit Pilatus, in eo ipso quod fecit, aliquantum particeps Fuit; sed in comparatione illorum multo ipse innocentior. Institit enim quantum potuit, ut illum ex eorum manibus liberaet. Nam propterea flagellatum ptoduxit ad eos. Non persequendo Dominum flagellavit, sed eorum furori satisfácete volens, ut vel sic iam mitescerent, et desinerent velle occidere, eum flagellatum viderent (Ib. 19,1-5): fecit et hoc. At ubi perseveraverunt, nostis illum lavisse manus, et dixisse quod ipse non fecisset, mundum se esse a morte illius (Mt 2?, 24): fecit tamen. Sed si reus cuia fecit vel invitus; illi innocentes qui coegerunt ut faceret? No way. Sed ille dixit in eum sententiam, et iussit eum crucifigi, et quasi ipse occidit; et vos, or Iudaei, occidistis. Unde occidistis? Gladio linguae: acuistis enim linguas vestras. Et quando percussistis, nisi quando clamastis, Crucifige, crucijige? (Luke 33:21). 5. Propterea enim non est praetermittendum, quia venit inmentem, ne forte aliquem perturbet lectio divinorum Librorum: quidam evangelista dicit hora sexta crucifixum Dominum (lo 19,14), et quidam hora tettia (Mark 15,25): nisi intelligamus, perturbamur. 5. So that no one is disturbed by the reading of the holy books, I will not overlook what has now come to my mind: that one evangelist says that the Lord was crucified at the sixth hour, and another at the third hour, because, if we do not understand it, we will be disturbed. It is said that Pilate sentenced Jesus to death at the beginning

the sixth hour, and indeed it was the sixth hour when the Lord was lifted up on the tree. But another evangelist, contemplating the mood of the Jews, since they wanted to appear innocent in the death of the Lord, in his narration demonstrated that they were guilty of the crime by saying that the Lord was crucified at the third hour. Considering all the circumstances of the narrative and the things that could have taken place when the Lord was accused before Pilate in order to be crucified, we see that it could have been the third hour when they shouted: Crucify, crucify him! Then they really killed him when they shouted. The ministers of power crucified him at the sixth hour, the transgressors of the law cried out at the third hour. What the former did with their hands at the sixth hour, these did with their tongues at the third hour. Those who shouted and raged were more guilty of the action than those who obeyed and carried it out. All this is Jewish cunning; This is what they tried to hide as something sublime: let us kill and not kill. Let us kill in such a way that it is not thought that we have killed. They sharpened their tongues like swords. 6. They drew the bow, a bitter thing. Call the insidious arch. He who fights hand to hand with the sword, fights clearly; He who throws the arrow deceives in order to wound, because the arrow strikes before the blow is anticipated. But from whom are the snares of the human heart hidden? Perhaps also our Lord Jesus Christ, who does not need anyone to testify to him about man, since he knows what is in man, as the Gospel attests? However, let us hear them and contemplate them Dominus in ligno, sixth hour erat. Be alius evangelista intuens animum Iudaeorum, quia volebant se immunes víderi a morte Domini, narrando eos ostendit reos, dices Dominum hora tertia crucifixum. Considerants autem omnem circumstantiam lectionis, quanta agi potuerint, cum apud Pilatum Dominus accusaretur, ut crucifígeretur; invenimus horam tertiam esse potuisse, quando illi clamaverunt, Crmifige, crucifige. Ergo verius illi tune occiderunt, quando clamaverunt. Apparitores potestatis sixth hour crucifixerunt; praevaricatores Legis hora tertia clamaverunt: quod illi manibus hora sexta, hoc illi lingua hora tenia. Rei magis isti qui clamando saeviebant, quam illi qui obtemperando administrabant.

Ipstim est totum acumen Iudaeorum; hoc est quod pro magno quaesierunt: Occidamus, et non occidamus; sic occidamus, ut non ipsí occidisse iudicemur. Exacuerunt tanquam gladium ünguas suas. 6. Intenderunt arcum, rem amaram. Arcum dicit insidias. Qui enim gladio cominus pugnat, aperte pugnat: qui sagittam mittit, fallit ut fair. Prius enim sagitta percusir, quam vinore ad vulnus praevideatur. Sed quem laterent insidiae cordis humani? numquid et Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, who non opus habebat ut ei testimonium quisquam perhiberet de homine? Ipse enim sciebat quid esset in bomine, sicut evangelista testatur (lo 2,25). Tamen audiamus eos, et intueamur eos quasi nesciente Domino faceré quod moliuntur. Intenderunt arcum, rem

as if the Lord were unaware of what they were trying to plot. They drew the bow, a bitter thing, to shoot the innocent from the hidden. They stretched the bow in the same way as in the hidden, that is, as if deceiving with tricks. You know how they did this; how they corrupted the disciple who was united to Him with money so that he would surrender to them; What tricks and deceptions they used to attack the innocent from covertly. Great iniquity is this! See that from the hidden comes the arrow that wounded the innocent, who did not even have an iota of iniquity that could be wounded with the point of the arrow. He was a spotless lamb; absolutely immaculate and always immaculate, not because his iniquities had been erased, but because he did not contract them. On the contrary, He made many immaculate by forgiving sins, but He was so by not having sins. To attack the innocent from the hidden. 7 [v.6]. Suddenly they will shoot him, and they will not fear. Oh inveterate heart! Try to kill the man who resurrects the dead. Suddenly, suddenly; that is, insidiously, unexpectedly, at random. The Lord was likened to the ignorant among those who did not know what he knew and what he did not know; What's more, they were unaware that he knew nothing and knew everything and that he came to them to execute what they thought they were doing by their own power. Suddenly they will shoot him and they will not fear. 8. They clung to the perverse purpose. They clung; Despite having performed so many miracles, they were not moved and persisted in their evil advice. Christ was handed over to the judge; The judge trembles and those who hand him over do not tremble. The amaram trembles, ut sagittarent in abscondito immaculatum. Quod dixit, Intenderunt arcum; hoc est, in abscondito; quasi fallantes insidiis. Nostis enim quibus dolis id egerint; quemadmodum discipulum ei cohaerentem pecunia corrupterint, ut sibi traderetur (Mt 26,14.15); quomodo false tests procuraverint; Quibus insidiis et dolis egerint, ut sagittarent in abscondito immaculatum. Great iniquities! Ecce de abscondito venit sagitta quae immaculatum ferit, qui nec tantum habebat maculae, quantum potest pungí a sagitta. Agnus quippe immaculatus, totus immaculatus, semper immaculatus; non cui maculae ablatae sint, sed qui maculas nullas contraxerit. Nam fecit immaculate fines by donating peccata; ipse immaculatus non habendo peccata. Ut sagittent in abscondito immaculatum. 7 [v.6]. Repente sagittabunt eum, et non timebunt.

O cor durum, occidere velle hominem qui mortuos suscitabat! Suddenly, id est insidiose, quasi inopinate, quasi non praevise. Similis enim nescienti erat Inter ípsos Dominus ignorantes quid nesciret, et quid sciret; imo ignorant eum nihil nescire, et omnia scire, et ad hoc venisse ut illi facerent quod se potestate faceré arbitrabantur. Repente sagittabunt eum, et non timebunt. 8. Obiirmaverunt sibi sermonem malignum. Obfirmaverunt: facta sunt tanta miracula; non sunt moti, perstiterunt in consilio sermonis maligni. Traditus est ille judici: trepidat iudex, et non trepidant qui

power, and cruelty remains undaunted; The judge washes his hands, and they stain their tongues. Why this? Because they clung to their perverse purpose. How many things Pilate did not do! How many did he do to prevent him from carrying out his attempt! How much he didn't say! How much he didn't try! But they clung to their perverse purpose. Crucify, crucify him!, they responded. This repetition is confirmation of his evil intent. Let's see how they clung to their perverse purpose. Will I crucify your king? We have no king—they said—except Caesar. They clung to their perverse purpose. Pilate offered them the Son of God as king, they claimed the man. Those who were chosen to have him as king did not want to have him as such. He still hears how they clung to their perverse purpose: I do not find, says the judge, in this man anything worthy of death. They clung to their perverse purpose and said: His blood be on us and on our children. They clung to their evil opinion. They clung to the perverse purpose; but harmful not to the Lord, but to them. How could it not be for them, since they said: Let their blood be on us and on our children? Their attempt fell on them, for it is also said in another place: They dug the pit for me, and they fell into it. Death did not kill the Lord, but He put death to death. But iniquity killed those who did not want to kill it. 9. It is absolutely true, brothers, that you either kill iniquity or iniquity kills you. But do not try to kill iniquity as something outside of you. Look at yourself and see that it fights with you inside and avoids being defeated iudici tradiderunt; contremiscit potestas, et non contremiscit immanitas; vult ille lavare manus, et illi inquinant linguas. Sed quare hoc? Firmaverunt sibi sermonem malignum. How much did Pilatus egit? How much restraint do you have? quae dixit? quid egit? Sed firmaverunt sibi sermonem malignum: Crucifige, crucifige! Repeated, confirmed this sermonis maligni. Videamus quomodo firmaverunt sibi sermonem malignum. Regem vestrum crucifigam? Dixerunt: Non habemus regem nisi solum Caesarem (lo 19,15). Obfirmaverunt sermonem malignum. Offerebat ille regem Filium Dei; illi ad hominem recurrebant: dign quí illum haberent, et illum non haberent.

Adhuc audi quomodo firmaverunt sermonem malignum. Non invenía aliquid in isto homine, ait iudex, quo dignus sit morte (Luke 23,14,22). Et illi qui firmaverunt sermonem malignum dixerunt: Sanguis eius super nos, et super filios nostros! (Mt 27,25). Firmaverunt sibi sermonem malignum. Firmaverunt sermonem malignum, non Domino, sed sibi. Quomodo enim non sibi, cum dicunt: Super nos, et super filios nostros? Quod ergo firmaverunt, sibi firmaverunt: quia ipsa vox est alibi, Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam, et incidenterunt in eam. Dominum mors non occidit, sed ipse mortem: illos autem iniquitas occidit, quia noluerunt occidere iniquitatem. 9. Prorsus, fratres, certum est; aut occidis iniquitatem, aut occideris ab iniquitate. Noli autem quaerere occidere iniquitatem tanquam
The counsels of the wicked, thwarted by God

for iniquity, which is your enemy if you have not put it to death in you. It comes from you, and your soul, nothing else, wars against you. On the one hand you are united to God; on the other hand, chained to the world. That by which you are chained to the world fights against the mind that God joins. Join, unite, do not faint, do not depart from Him; has great help. If you persevere in the fight, you will defeat what wars in it. Sin is in your body; noimpe re. The Apostle says: Let not sin reign in your mortal body obeying its own appetites. If you do not listen to him, even though he persuades and incites evil with his flattery, you cause, by not obeying him, that what is in you does not prevail, and so it will come to pass later that what was in you will not exist. When will this happen? When death is subsumed in victory, when this corruptible puts on incorruption; then there will be nothing to fight against you, there will be nothing to delight you apart from God. The Jews envied the Lord; They liked the principality. It seemed to them that the Lord was going to take away the principality from them, and, due to their own delight, they fought against Him who, if they had fought against His evil intention, would have overcome envy so as not to be defeated by it, and then the Lord, who had come to heal them, would have been their savior. But in such circumstances they preferred the fever and rejected the doctor, doing whatever the fever suggested and refusing everything the doctor ordered against it. Therefore rather they were killed and not the Lord, for in the Lord death was killed and iniquity lived in them, and while they lived, they died. extra liquid tea. Ad teipsum réspice, vide quid tecum pugnet in te; et cave ne expugnet te iniquitas tua, inimica tua, si interfecta non erit: ex te enim est, et anima tua adversus te rebellat, non aliud aliquid. Ex quadam part cohaeres Deo; ex quadam parte delectaris saeculo: illud quo delectaris saeculo, pugnat adversus mentem quae cohaeret Deo. Cohaereat, cohaereat, non deficiat, non se dimittat, magnum adiutorium habet. Vincit quod in illa sibi rebellat, si persevert in fighting. Est peccatum in corpore tuo, sed non regnet. Non ergo regnet, inquit, peccatum in vestro mortali corpore, ad obaudiendum desideriis eius (Rom 6:12).

Si vero non obaudieris; etsi est quod suadeat, quod delectet ad malum; non obtemperando facis ut non regnet quod est, et ita fiet postea ut non sit quod erat. When? Cum absorbebitur mors in victoriam, cum corruptibile hoc induerit incorruptionem (1 Cor 15:54): ibi non erit quod tibi repugnet, non erit quod te aliud delectet nisi Deus. Ergo et isti Iudaei inviderunt Domino; delectabat eos principatus. Quidam videbant sibi ab eo auferri principatum, et ex delectatione sua rebellaverunt adversus Dominum: qui si rebellassent adversus delectationem suam malam, ipsam invidentiam vincerent, nec vincerentur ab ea, et esset illis Dominus salvator, qui venerat ut sanaret. Nunc autem faverunt febri, repugnaverunt medico: quidquid suggerebat febris, faciebant; quidquid iubebat against mediais, negligebant. Ergo illi magis occisi sunt, non Dominus: nam in Domino mors occisa est, in illis iniquitas vixit; vívente autem in se iniquitate, illi mortui sunt.

10. They spoke of setting snares secretly, and said, Who will see them? They thought they would be hidden from Whom they were, from God. See here what they thought: they judged that Christ was a man, like other men, and that he was unaware of what was plotted against him. But does God also ignore it? Oh human heart, why did you say to yourself: Who sees me, when he who made you sees you? They said: Who will see it? God saw them; Christ saw them, because Christ is God. But why did it seem to you that he didn't see them? Hear what's next. 11. [v.7J. They searched for iniquity; the tellers fainted in their scrutiny; that is, in the cruel and subtle advice. They said, Let him not be delivered up for us, but for his disciple; Let us not kill him, but the judge; Let us do everything, but let us pretend that we do nothing. But where is the cry of the tongue: Crucify, crucify him!? Just as you are blind, you are also deaf. Simulated innocence is not innocence; Simulated equity is not equity, but doubled iniquity, because it is simulation and iniquity. Then here the tellers failed in the investigations. The more subtly it seemed to them that they were forging their nefarious plans, the more they were deprived of advice, because, far from the light of truth and all justice, they plunged into the abyss of their perverse thoughts. Justice has its light; inundae illuminates the soul that adheres to it. On the contrary, the soul that turns away from the light of justice, the more it strives to find what is against justice, the more it is repelled by the light and plunged into dark darkness. So with reason these inda10. Narraverunt ut absconderent muscipulas; dixerunt: Quis videbit eas? Latere putabant eum quem occidebant, latere Deum. Ecce puta, homo erat Christus, sicut caeteri nomines; nesciebat quid de illo cogitaretur: numquid et Deus nescít? O cor humanum, quare tibi dixisti, Quis videt me, cum ille videat qui te fecit? Dixerunt: Quis videbit eas? Videbat Deus, videbat et Christus; quia et Christus Deus. Sed quare videbatur eis non videre? Audi sequence. 11 [v.7]. Perscrutati sunt iniquitatem; defecerunt serlitantes scrutationes: id est acerba et acuta consilia.

Non tradatur per nos, sed per discipulum suum: non occidatur a nobís, sed a iudice: totum nos faciamus, et nihil fecisse videamur. Et ubi est clamor linguae: Crucifige, crucifige? Sic caeci estis, ut et surdí sitis. Simulara innocentia non est innocentia: simulara aequitas non est aequitas, sed duplex iniquitas; quia et iniquitas est, et simulated. Ibi ergo isti defecerunt scrutantes scrutationes. Quanto acutus sibi excogitare videbantur, mucho magis deficiebant; quia a lumine verítatis et aequitatis indeep consiliorum malignarum demergebantur. Habet iustitia quamdam luzem suam; perfuse, et illustrat animam inhaerentem sibi: anima vero avertens se a luz iustitiae, quanto magis quaerit quod inveniat contra iustitiam, mucho plus a luz repellirur, et in tenebrosa demergitur. Merit ergo et isti perscrutantes quod contra iustum moliebantur, a iustitia recedebant;
counsels of the wicked, thwarted by God

The investigators, by scheming against the just, departed from justice, and the further they departed from it, the more lacking in judgment were the scrutineers in the scrutiny. What a great resolution of innocence they carried out! When Judas himself repents of having handed over Christ and throws them the money they gave him for the handing over of Christ, they did not want to deposit it in the gasfield, because they said: It is blood money; let's not deposit it in the gasfield. What was gasfilacio? The ark of God where the alms that were offered to help the needs of God's servants were collected. O man, let your heart rather be the ark of God where the riches of God are deposited, where your mind, which has the image of your emperor, is the coin of God. These things being so, what was the pretense of his innocence? Do not put blood money into the ark and put the blood into your conscience. 12. But what happened to them? The tellers vanished in their scrutiny. As? Because the psalm says: Who will see them?, meaning that no one saw them. They said this, they thought within themselves that no one saw them. Observe what happens to the perverse soul when it departs from the light of truth, because it does not see God, it thinks that God does not see it. Thus it happened to these, for turning away from the light, they fell into darkness and did not see God, and therefore they said: Who will see us? He whom they crucified saw them; but they, fainting, saw neither the Son nor the Father. But if He saw, why did He tolerate being captured and killed by them? Why did He want His advice to prevail against Him if He saw it? Because? Because he was a man for man's sake, et quanto a iustitia recedebant, tanta plus deficiebant, scrutantes scrutationes. Magnum consilium innocentiae: quando ipsum ludam poenituit quod tradidisset Christum, et proiecit illis pecuniam quam dederant, illi noluerunt eam mittere in gazophylacium, et dixerunt: Pecunia sanguinis est; non Mam mittamus in gazophylacium (Mt 27,6). What is gazophylacium? Arca Dei, ubi colligebantur ea quae ad indigentiam servorum Dei mittebantur. O homo, cor tuum sit potius arca Dei, ubi habitent divitiae Dei, ubi sit nummus Dei, mens tua habens imaginem Imperatoris tui!

Cum ergo haec ita sint, qualis illa innocentiae simulatio Fuit, pecuniam sanguinis non mittere in arcam, et ipsum sanguinem mittere in conscientiam? 12. Sed quid eis contigit? Defecerunt scrutantes scrutationes. Where? Quia dicit, Quis videbit eos? id est, quia eos nemo videbat. Hoc dicebant, hoc apud se opinabantur quod nemo eos videret. Vide quid contingat animae malae; recedit a luz veritatis, et quia ipsa non videt Deum, putat se non videri a Deo. Sic et isti receding ierunt in tenebras, ut ipsi non viderent Deum; et dixerunt; Can you see us? Videbat et ille quem crucifigebant; illi deficiendo, nec illum Filium, nec Patrem videbant. Si ergo et ille videbat, quare se patiebatur teneri ab eis, occidi ab eis? Quare si videbat, voluit consilia eorum praevalere in se? Quare?
