and God hidden in man, who had come to give the ignorant an example of strength. That is why He, knowing everything, endured all the humiliations. 13 [v. 8]. What's next? The man and the sublime heart will draw near, and God will be exalted. They said: Who will see us? The tellers failed in their investigations, in their bad attempts. The man presented himself to these deliberations and endured being considered a man. For he was not to be had, nor seen, nor wounded, nor crucified, nor killed, but as a man. Then man gave himself over to all those sufferings that would have had no value in Him if He had not been a man. The man and the sublime heart approached; that is, the secret heart; exposing man to human gaze and reserving God within; hiding the form of God, by which he is equal to the Father, and offering the form of a servant, by which he is less than the Father. He himself said both things, but one because he was God, and the other because he was a man. As for it being God, he said: I and the Father are one; and since he was a man: The Father is greater than me. Why does he say, considering that he was God: I and the Father are one? Because, subsisting in the form of God, he did not consider it a shame to be equal to God. Why does he say, considering that he was a servant: The Father is greater than I? Because he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. Then the man and the sublime heart approached, and God was exalted. Man is killed, and God is exalted. Being killed is due to human weakness; having risen and ascended to heaven, to the Quia homo erat propter hominem, et Deus latens in homine, qui venerat nescientibus exemplum fortitudinis daré; ideo ipse sciens omnia sustinebat. 13 [v.8]. Quid enim sequitur? Access homo, et cor altum; et exaltabitur Deus. lili dixerunt: Can you see us? Defecerunt scrutantes scrutationes, consilia mala. Accessit homo ad ipsa consilia, passus est se teneri ut homo. Non enim teneretur, nisi homo; aut videretur, nisi homo; aut caederetur, nisi homo; aut crucifigeretur aut moreretur nisi homo. Accessit ergo homo ad illas omnes passiones, quae in illo nihil valerent, nisi esset homo. Sed si ille non esset homo, non liberaretur homo.

Accessit homo, et cor altum, id est cor secretum: obiiciens aspectibus humanis hominem, servans intus Deum; celans formam Dei, in qua aequalis est Patri, et offerens formam servi, qua minor est Patre. Ipse enim dixit utrumque: sed aliud est ex forma Dei, aliud ex forma servi. Dixit ex forma Dei: Ego et Pater unum sumus (lo 10,30). Dixit ex forma servi, Quoniam Pater maior me est (Ib. 14,28). Unde ex forma Dei, Ego et Pater unum sumus? Quia cum in forma Dei esset constitutus, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. Unde former forma I served, Quoniam Pater maior me? Quia semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens (Phil 2,6.7). Accessit ergo homo, et cor altum; et exaltatus est Deus. Occiditur homo, et exaltatur Deus. Quod enim occisus est, ex infirmitate humano Fuit: quod resurrexit et ascendit, ex

divine virtue. The man and the sublime heart will approach, that is, the secret heart, the hidden heart; that is, not manifesting what he knew, not showing what he was. Thinking that it was only what appeared, they kill man in the hidden heart, and God is exalted in the divine heart. Due to the virtue of his majesty he was exalted. Where was he exalted? To the place from which he did not depart when he humbled himself. 14. The man and the sublime heart will draw near, and God will exalt him. Therefore, pay attention now, my brothers, to the secret heart of man. What man? Mother Zion calls herself a man; and man was made in it, and the Most High founded it. In the same city he was made man, and the Most High, who was made man in it, founded it. Then the man and the sublime heart approached. See the man deep in the heart. See as much as you can, and if you can, also see God in the depths of your heart. The man approached, and since he was God, and since he had to suffer willingly and give an example to the weak, and since those who were cruel were not going to do anything to him, God suffering, but in man, that is, in the flesh, what is added? Children's arrows are their blows. Where is that cruelty? Where is that lion's roar of the people that roared, saying: Crucify, crucify!? Where are the insidiousness of the arch tensioners? Didn't his blows turn into children's arrows? You know that children make their arrows from reeds. And what do they hurt or how do they hurt? Who are the upright in heart? Hey, my brothers, I am continually saying it, and it is good that you know it. Who are the upright in heart? Those who do not attribute to chance the things they endure in life for their own medicine, but to God's purpose; nor do they presume on their own justice, thinking that they suffer unjustly what they suffer; nor do they believe that God is unjust because those who sin more suffer less. See, brothers, I have told you these things many times. You suffer something in your body, in the economy of the house, in the deprivation of some of your loved ones; Do not consider those you know to be worse than you, because perhaps you do not dare to say that you are just, but you know that they are worse than you and that they are champions and are not

punished, and, therefore, may you dislike the ruling of God and say: Certainly I am a sinner, and for that reason I am punished; But why is he who I know of such enormous crimes not punished? Your feet slipped because you envied sinners seeing their peace. Let yourself heal. He, who knows the wound, knows what he is doing. That another is not cut, so what if he despairs of him? 1 [v.l]. By the title of this psalm the voice of prophecy must be recognized. It is titled For the end, a psalm of David, a song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel (Jews), of the people of the transmigration as they begin to leave. How the events that took place in our fathers at the time of the Babylonian transmigration are not known to everyone, but only to those who carefully consider the holy Scriptures when hearing or reading them. The people of Israel were taken prisoner and led into slavery from the city of Jerusalem to Babylon. But holy Jeremiah prophesied that, after seventy years, the people would return from captivity and that the city of Jerusalem itself, which was crying, devastated by enemies, would be restored. At that time there were prophets of the captive people established in Babylon; Among them is Ezekiel. The people waited for the seventy years predicted by Jeremiah to be fulfilled. After seventy years, the temple, which had been devastated, was rebuilt, and most of that people returned from captivity. But as the Apostle says that these things happened to them in figure, but that they were written for our knowledge, upon whom the end of the ages came, first of all we must also know

From there the Jebusites were expelled when the people of God, delivered from Egypt, were introduced into the promised land. Babylon was founded in the interior of the region of Persia, which for a long time was the capital of the other nations. Then these two cities were built at certain times to prefigure the other two cities that began to be built at another time, and which were to remain until the end of the world, in which they were to separate. How can we make them known now, if they are mixed? The Lord will make them known by placing some on the right and others on the left. Jerusalem will be on the right; Babylon, left. Jerusalem must hear: Come, you blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world. votes in Jerusalem. We will be there with our entire being, that is, whole, in the resurrection of the just; There we will fulfill the total vow, not only that of our soul, but also that of the now incorruptible flesh, because it will no longer be in Babylon, but will already be the flesh changed into a celestial body. What change is promised to us? We will all—says the Apostle—be resurrected, but we will not all be changed. He also said who will be exchanged: In a flash of sight, at the sound of the last trumpet, for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorrupt, that is, whole, and we will be exchanged. What must that change be? He tells us next: It is fitting that this corruptible be clothed with incorruptibility, and this mortal with immortality; When this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then what was said will be fulfilled: Death was given over to victory. Where is your sting, O death? Now, as the first desires of the mind begin in us by which we long for the heavenly Jerusalem, many other desires of the corruptible flesh fight against us, which will not fight when death has been subsumed in victory. Peace will win and the war will end. When peace has won, that city that is called the vision of peace will have won. And then there will be no more struggle with death. Well now, how many struggles we have with death! From it come the carnal delights that suggest so many illicit things to us, in which we do not consent, but with which, not consenting, we fight. Firstly, the lust of the flesh nos inmus, Vovete, et reddite Domino Deo vestro (Ps 75,12). Et tibi reddetur votum in lerusalem. Ibi enim erimus toti, id est integri in resurrectione iustorum: ibi reddetur votum totum nostrum; non sola anima, sed ipsa etiam caro iam non corruptibilis, quia iam non in Babylonia, sed iam Corpus caeleste immutatum. Qualis mutatio promittitur? Omnes enim resurgemus, ait Apostolus, sed non omnes immutabimur. Qui autem immutabuntur ipse dixit: ln ictu oculi, in new tuba: canet enim tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti, id est integri, et nos immutabimur.

Qualis autem erit illa immutatio, sequitur et dicit: "Oportet enim corruptibile hoc induere incorruptionem et mortale hoc induere immortalitatem: cum autem corruptibile hoc induerit incorruptionem, et mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, tune fiet sermo qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoriam. Ubi est, mors, aculeus "You?" (1 Cor 15, 51-55). Modo enim inchoatis in nobis primitiis mentis, unde desideramus lerusalem, fines ex carne corruptibili contendunt adversum nos, quae non contendent, cum fuerit mors absorpta in victoriam. Vincet pax, er finietur bellum. Quando autem vincet pax, vincet illa civitas quae dicitur Visio pacis. Nulla ergo erit a niorte contentio. Cum morte mode quanta contendimus! Inde sunt delectationes carnales, quae nobis etiam ilücite fine suggerunt: quibus non consentimus, sed tainen non consentiendo contendimus. Primo ergo concupiscentia carnis sequentes duxit nos, postea renitentes traxit nos; deinde accepta gratia ccepit us

it leads us to follow it; then, opposing us, it drags us along; but, having received grace, it no longer induces or attracts us, but it still continues to fight against us. After the fight, victory will come. If he attacks you now, don't let him knock you down; Later, when death has been submerged in victory, it will cease its combat. Well, what was said? Death will be destroyed as the last enemy. I will fulfill my vow. What vote? The holocaust. The one in which the entire offering is consumed by fire is called a holocaustic sacrifice. The holocaustic sacrifice is given when everything is consumed. The word holocaust is formed from olon, which means everything, and kausis, burning. The holocaust burns everything. Let the fire burn us, the divine fire of Jerusalem, and let us begin to burn with the fire of charity until everything mortal is consumed and what opposes us we offer as a sacrifice to the Lord. Hence in another psalm it is said: Be kind, O Lord, in your kindness to Zion so that the walls of Jerusalem may be built. Then you will accept the sacrifice of righteousness, the offerings and the burnt offerings. To you, O Lord, the hymn is due in Zion and to you the vows will be fulfilled in Jerusalem. We ask here if perhaps the king of this city, our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, is recommended to us; but let us sing until we come to show him. I could already say that He is the one to whom it is said: To you, O Lord, the hymn is due in Zion and to you the vows will be fulfilled in Jerusalem. But if I said it, I would be believed rather than the Scripture, and therefore, lest I be believed, let us hear what follows. 5 [v.3]. Hear—he says—my prayer; All flesh will come to you. The Lord also tells us that he has been given power over nec ducere, nec trahere, sed adhuc contendere nobiscum: post contentionem erit et victoria. Modo te etsi oppugnat, non expugnet: postea cum absorpta fuerit mors in victoriam, et pugnare cessabit. Quid dictum is this? Novissima inimica destruetur mors (Ib. 26). Reddam votum meum. Quod votum? Quasi holocaustum. Holocaustum enim tune dicitur, quando totum ignis absumit: holocaustum sacrificium est ubi totum consumitur; 5Aov enim totum dicitur, Kaüas, incensio. Holocaustum totum incensum. Arripiat ergo nos ignis, ignis divinus in lerusalem: incipiamus arderé charitate, doñee totum mortale consumatur, et quod contra nos fuerit, eat in sacrificium Domino.

Unde alibi dicitur: "Benigne fac, Domine, in bona volúntate tua Sion, ut aedificentur muri lerusalem: tune acceptabis sacrificium iustitiae, oblationes et holocausta (Ps 50, 20.21). Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion; et tibi reddetur votum in lerusalem." Quaerimus hic, ne forte Rex nobis ipsius civitatis commendetur, Dominus et Salvator noster lesus Christus: cantemus ergo doñee ad evidentiora perveniamus. Possem enim iam dicere ipsum esse cui dicitur: Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion; et tibi reddetur votum in lerusalem. Sed si dicerem, mihi potius quam Scripturae crederetur; et ideo forte non mihi crederetur. Audiamus sequence. 5 [v.3]. Exaudií, inquit, orationem meam: ad te omnis caro veniet.

all flesh, not all man. Then the King begins to appear when it is sung: All flesh will come to you. “To you,” he says, “all flesh will come.” Why will all flesh go to Him? Because he took the meat. How will all meat fare? He took the first fruits from the virgin womb. Once these are taken, the rest follow to complete the holocaust. Then do I eat all meat? Every man. And like every man? Were all those who would believe found prefigured in Christ? Perhaps also the infinite number of wicked people who will be condemned? Do not many who do not believe die in their infidelity? Then how will we understand that all flesh will come to you? He said all flesh for all kinds of flesh. All kinds of meat will come to you. What does all kinds of meat mean? Did the poor come and the rich not come? Did the humble come and the illustrious not come? Did the men come and the women not come? Did the ignorant come and the learned not come? Did the lords come and the servants not come? Did the old people come and the young people not come? Or did the young people come and the teenagers not come? Did the teenagers come and the toddlers not come? Did the toddlers come and the children didn't show up? In short, did the Jews come, since the apostles were Jews, and many thousands of those who were first traitors and then believers, and the Greeks did not come? Or did the Greeks come and the Romans not? Or did the Romans come and the barbarians not come? Who will count all the nations that came to Him to whom it was said: Et habemus Dominum dicentem, datam sibi potestatem omnis carnis (lo 17,2). Coepit ergo apparere iam Rex ille, cura diceretur, ad te omnis caro veniet. Ad te, inquit, omnis caro veniet. Quare ad illum omnis caro veniet? Quia carnem assumpsit. Quo veniet omnis caro? Tulit inde primitias ex uterus virginali: assumptis primitiis caetera consequentur, ut holocaustum compleatur. Unde ergo, omnis expensive? Omnis homo. Et unde, omnis homo? Numquid omnes credituri praenuntiati sunt in Christum? Nonne multi impii qui etiam damnabuntur? Nonne quotidie multi non credentes, in sua infidelitate moriuntur? Secundum quid ergo intelligimus, ad te omnis caro veniet? Omnis caro dixit, omnis generis caro: ex omni genere carnis venietur ad te. Quid est, ex omni genere carnis?

All flesh will come to you? Hear my prayer: All flesh will come to you. 6 [v.4]. The words of the wicked prevailed over us, and you will forgive our iniquities. What does it mean: The words of the wicked prevailed over us and you will forgive our iniquities? That those of us who were born in this world have found those we have heard to be wicked. Help me the attention of your charity so that I can explain what I feel. Every man, wherever he is born, learns the language of his nation, or city, or region and becomes imbued with its life and customs. How could a child born among pagans not worship stones, when his parents initiated him into that cult? There he heard the first words; He sucked the error with milk. Since those who spoke to him were older and the child who learned to speak was an infant, he could not help but follow the authority of the elders and take for himself what they praised as good. But, the Gentiles later converted to Christ, remembering the impieties of their ancestors and saying what the prophet Jeremiah himself said: Our fathers truly worshiped lies; vanity, which did not profit them, they already repudiate the opinions and sacrileges of their perverse parents. But since such rulings and sacrileges were recorded in them by allowing themselves to be carried away by the insinuations of those who, the longer they had preceded them with the more authority they thought they should precede them, already wanting to return from Babylon to Jerusalem, they confess and say: The words of the wicked prevailed over nosema cui dictum est: Ad te omnis caro veniet? Exaudi orationem meam: ad te omnis caro veniet. 6 [v.4]. Sermones iniquorum praevaluerunt super nos; et impietates nostras tu propitiaberis. Quid est, Sermones iniquorum praevaluerunt super nos; et impietates nostras tu propitiaberis? Quod nati sumus in hac terra, iniquos invenimus quos loquentes audivimus. If I can explain what I felt, adiuvet me attempted Charitatis Vestrae. Omnis homo ubicumque nascítur, ipsius terrae, vel regionis, vel civitatis linguam discit; illius imbuitur moribus et vita. Quid faceret puer natus inter Paganos, ut non coleret lapidem, quando illum cultum insinuaverunt patents? Inde prima verba audivit; illum errorem cum Jacte suxit: et quia illi qui loquebantur maiores werent, et puer qui loqui discebat infans erat, unde poterat parvulus nisi maiorum auctoritatem sequi, et id sibi bonum ducere quod illi laudarent?

Ergo gentes conversae ad Christum postea, et reminders impietates parentum suorum, et dicentes iam quod dixit propheta ipse Ieremias, Veré mendacium coluerunt paires nostri; vanitatem quae eis non profuit (Ier 16,19): cum ergo iam hoc dicunt, renuntantiant opinionibus et sacrilegiis parentum suorum iniquorum. The words of the wicked prevailed over us: yet they did not destroy us. Because? For you will forgive our iniquities. Take care of your charity. You will forgive our iniquities. Only a certain priest is said to offer something for which impiety is forgiven and atoned for. It is said that impiety is forgiven when God takes pity on it. What does it mean for God to feel sorry for impiety? Be lenient with her and forgive her. But to implore God's forgiveness, propitiation is made by some sacrifice. Then there was a certain priest of ours sent by the Lord God, who took from us what he was to offer to the Lord, the holy firstfruits. The holy firstfruits of the flesh, as we said, taken from the womb of the Virgin Mary. This was the burnt offering that he offered to God by stretching out his hands on the cross and saying: Let my prayer rise to you like incense; be the lifting of my hands the evening sacrifice. As you know, the Lord hung on the cross in the afternoon. And our impieties were forgiven. Otherwise they would have devoured us. The words of the wicked had prevailed over us: the preachers of Jupiter, Saturn and Mercury had carried us away. The words of the wicked prevailed over us. But what will you do? You will forgive our impieties. You who are the priest, you are the victim; You who are the offerer, you are the offering. He is the priest who now penetrated inside the veil, in

where he is the only one of those who carry the flesh who calls for us. Prefiguring this, in that first town and first temple a single priest entered the sancta sanctorum, leaving the people outside; and he who only entered inside the tabernacle offered the sacrifice for the people who remained outside. If this is well understood, the spirit vivifies; if wrong, kill the letter. Now, as you read the Apostle, you heard: The letter kills, the spirit gives life. The Jews did not know, and still do not know, what was done in their town. It was said about them: When they read Moses, a veil was placed over their hearts. There the veil is an allegory; The allegory disappears, and the truth is manifested in them. But when will the veil disappear? Hear the Apostle: When you have passed to the Lord, the veil will disappear. Then, as long as they do not convert to the Lord, they will have the veil over their hearts when they read Moses. Moses' face shone when he spoke to the people, prefiguring this mystery, and he shone in such a way that the children of Israel could not look at his face; you have heard it when it was now read. And a veil was placed between the face of Moses, who spoke, and the people, who listened to his words. They heard through the veil and did not see his face. What does the Apostle say? How intense was the radiance of the face, that the children of Israel could not look at the face of Moses. And they will not look at him—he adds—until the end. What does until the end mean? Until they understand Christ, since the same Apostle also says: The end of the law is Christ, in order to justice, for every believer. There is certainly a radiance in the face of Moses, as in a carnal and mortal face; But can it remain for a long time or forever? Disappear-

Impietates braces your propitiaberis. Intendat Charitas Vestra. Propitiaberis impietates us: non dicitur nisi curam sacerdoti offerenti aliquid, unde impietas expietur et propitietur. Hoc holocaustum obtulit Deo: extendit manus in cruze, ut diceret, Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo; elevated manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum (Ps 140.2). Sicut nosti, quia Dominus circa vesperam pependit in intersection (Mt 27,46): et impietates nostrae propitiatae sunt; alioqui absorbuerant nos: sermones iniquorum praevaluerant super nos; duxerant nos praedicatores Iovis, et Saturni, et Mercurii: Sermones iniquorum praevaluerunt super nos. Sed quid facies? Impietates nostras, tu propitiaberis. Your priests, your victim; your oblater, your oblate. Ipse sacerdos est, qui nunc ingressus interiora veli, solus ibi ex his qui carnem gestaverunt, interpellat pro nobis (Hebr 6,19 et 20). in

cuius rei figura in illo primo populo, et in illo primo temple, unus sacerdos intrabat in Sancta sanctorum; populus omnis fotis stabat: et ille qui solus ingrediebatur in interiora veli, offerebat sacrificium pro populo foris stante (Ib. 9,7). Si intelligatur bene, spiritus vivificat: si non intelligatur, littera occidit. Modo cum legeretur Apostolus, audistis: hittera occidit; spiritus autem vivificat. Quid enim ageretur in illo populo, Iudaei nescierunt; sed nec sciunt mode. De illis quippe dictum est: Quamdiu legitur Moyses, velamen super cor eorum positum est. Ibi velamen figura est: sed tolletur figura, et apparebit veritas in eis ipsis. Sed when tolletur sailmen? Audi Apostolum: Cum autem. transieris ad Dominum, auferetur velamen. Dum ergo non transeunt ad Dominum, quamdiu legunt Moysen, velamen habent super cor. Ad hoc sacramentum fulgebat tune facies Moysi, ita ut non possent intendere filii Israel in faciem eius (audistis moda cum legeretur); et velamen erat inter faciem Moysi loquentis, et populum audientem verba. Per velum verba audiebant; faciem non videbant. Et quid ait Apostolus? Ita ut non possent intendere filii Israel in faciem Moysi. Non intendebant, inquit, usque in finem (2 Cor 3:6-16). Quid est, usque in finem? Usque quo intelligerent Christum. Dicit quippe Apostolus: Finís enim Legis Cbristus, ad iustitiam omni credenti (Rom 10,4). wax, without a doubt, with death. On the contrary, the radiance of glory of our Lord Jesus Christ is eternal. That glow was a temporal prefiguration; this of Christ, what that figure meant: the truth. They read and do not understand Christ. They do not extend their attention to the end because the intervening veil prevents them from seeing the inner radiance. See there, under the veil, Christ. For our Lord Jesus Christ says: If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me. Our sins and impieties forgiven by that evening sacrifice, we pass to the Lord and the veil is drawn. That is also why, when Jesus Christ was crucified, the veil of the temple was torn. Hear my prayer; All flesh will come to you. The words of the wicked prevailed over us, and you will forgive our iniquities. 7 [v.5-6]. Blessed is he whom you chose and took. Who was chosen and taken by Him? Was any chosen and taken by our savior Jesus Christ? Or is He, insofar as He is man, the one chosen and taken according to the flesh, so that, considering that He is the Word of God, it is said that He existed in the beginning, as the evangelist says: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God, since He Himself is the Son of God, Word of God, of whom it is also said: All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made; and, considering that he is a man, let it be said to the Son of God after having taken the flesh, since He is our priest: Blessed is he whom you chose and took; that is, blessed is that man with whom you clothed yourself, who began

in time and was born of a woman, and became, in a certain way, a temple of Him who is always eternal and remains eternally? Or is it rather that Christ himself took a certain blessed person, and does not indicate in the plural number, but in the singular, who he took? He took one because he took the unit. He did not take the schisms, he did not take the heresies; They by themselves constitute the multitude and only one is taken. Those who remain in the union of Christ and are its members constitute, in a certain way, one man, of whom the Apostle says: Until we all come to the unity of the knowledge of the Son of God, to be a perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ. Thus, then, a man is taken for whom the head is Christ, because the head of the man is Christ. He is that blessed man who is not found in the council of the wicked nor in the rest that is said in the first psalm. He is the one taken and is not outside of us, since we are in his members; We are governed under one head, we all live with the same spirit, we all long for one homeland. Then let us see if what is said to Christ refers to us and is also said of us. Let us ask our consciences, let us examine love; and, if it is still small and was born now, because perhaps it germinated now in someone, diligently remove the thorns that sprout next to it, that is, worldly cares, lest by growing they stifle the holy germ. Blessed is he whom you chose and took. In Him we are and are taken, in Him we are and will be chosen. 8. And what will it give us? He will dwell, he says, in your courts. In the

diuturnus aut aeternus esse posset? Morte enim succedente, profect auferretur. Splendor autem gloriae beati Domini nostri Iesu Christi, sempiternus est. Sed illud figura erat temporalis, hoc autem quod illa figura significatur, veritas. Legunt itaque, et non intelligunt Christum: non perducunt intentionem usque in finem, quia velum oppositum negat eis aspectum splendoris interioris. Et vide ibi sub veil Christum. Ait ipse Dominus noster Iesus Christus: Si crederetis Moysi, crederetis et mihi; from me enim Ule scripsit (lo 5.46). Propitiatis autem peccatis nostris et impietatibus per illud sacrificium vespertínum, transimus ad Dominum, et aufertur velamen: propterea et Domino crucifixo, velum templi scissum est (Mt 27,51). I exaudited orationem meam: ad te omnis caro veniet. Sermones iniquorum praevaluerunt super nos; et impietates nostras tu propitiaberis. 7 [v.5.6]. Beatus quem elegisti, et assumptusti, Quis est electus ab eo, et assumptus? Aliquis electus to Salvatore nostto Iesu Christo? An ipse secundum carnem, quod homo est, electus et assumptus est? ut tanquam Verbo Dei dicatur quod erat in principle, sicut dicit evangelista, In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum; quia et ipse est Filius Dei, Verbum Dei, de quo etiam dicit, Omnia per ipsum jacta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil (lo 11-3): ut illi dicatur Filio Dei, quia ipse est sacerdos noster, postea carne assumpta, Beatus quem elegisti, et assumpsisti: id est, ille homo quo

indutus es, qui coepit ex tempore, natus ex femina templum quodammodo illius qui semper in aeternum est, et in aeternum Fuit. An potius ipse Christus assumpsit quemdam beatum, et non dicitur ipse quem assumpsit quasi in plurali numero, sed in singulari? Unum enim assumit, quia unitatem assumit. Schismata non assumit, haereses non assumit: multitudinem de se fecerunt; non est unus qui assumatur. Qui autem manent in compage Christi, et membra eius sunt, faciunt quodammodo unum virum, de quo dicit Apostolus: Doñee oceurramus omnes in agnitionem Filii Dei, in virum perfectum, in mensuram aetatis plenitudinis Christi (Eph 4,13). Itaque unus vir assumitur, cui caput est Christus; quia caput viri Christus est (1 Cor 11:3). Ipse est ille beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum, et caetera quae ibi dicuntur (Ps 1,1): ipse est qui assumitur. It is not strange to us; in ipsius membris sumus, sub uno capite regimur, uno spiritu omnes vivimus, unam patriam omnes desideramus. Videamus ergo quod ad Christum dicitur, utrum ad nos pertineat, et de nobis dicatur: interrogemus conscientías nostras, amorem íllum perscrutemur; et si adhuc parvus est, et moda natus amor iste (forte enim moda in aliquo germinavit), diligenter exstirpet iuxta germinantes spinas, id est curas saeculares, ne crescendo sanctum germen offocent. Beatus quem elegisti et assumpsisti. In illo simus, et assumemur; in illo simus, et electi erimus. 8. Et quid nobis dabit? Inhabitabit, inquit, in atriis tuis. Ierusa-

of that Jemsalem of which those who begin to leave Babylon sing. He will dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the goods of your house. What are the assets of the house of God? Let us represent ourselves, brothers, some rich house. How many goods it is not supplied with, how much abundance there is in it, how much gold and silverware there is there, how numerous servants it does not have, how many donkeys and animals; In short, how attractive it is not to us because of the paintings, the marbles, the coffered ceilings, the columns, the halls and the ceilings!; such things are desired because of the confusion of Babylon. Cut off all these desires, oh citizen of Jerusalem! cut them off. If you want to return to Jerusalem, do not delight in captivity. You've already started dating. Don't look back, don't stop along the way. There will still be no shortage of enemies who advise you captivity and exile; May the words of the wicked no longer prevail over you. Long for the house of God; He desires the goods of his house, but not those that you usually desire either in your house, or in that of your neighbor, or in that of your protector. Others are, certainly, the assets of that house. There is no need for us to point out the good of that house. Let him be told by the one who sings when leaving Babylon: We will be filled with the goods of your house. What goods are these? Perhaps we had turned our hearts towards gold, towards silver, towards other precious things; let us not seek such things; These depress, not elevate. Then let us think here about those goods of Jerusalem, of the house of God, of the temple of the Lord, because the house of God is the very temple of the Lord. We will be filled with the goods of your house. Holy is your temple, admirable in justice. These are the goods

nes of that house. He did not say: Your holy temple is admirable in columns, in marble, in golden roofs, but in justice. To see marble and gold you have external eyes, to contemplate the beauty of justice you have internal ones. Within is the eye with which you see the beauty of justice. Inside, I will repeat, is the eye to see the beauty of justice. If there is no such beauty, why do we love the righteous old man? What does it present on the body that delights the eyes? Its limbs are bent; his forehead, wrinkled; his head, gray; his weakness, completely overwhelmed with suffering and pain. But if this decrepit old man doesn't delight your eyes, perhaps he may delight your ears. With what voice? What do I sing with? Perhaps, as a young man, he sang admirably; but all things disappeared with age. Or is it that your ears are delighted by the sound of the words that he barely pronounces when he is toothless? However, if he is just, if he does not desire what belongs to others, if he gives what is his to the poor, if he advises well and does what is right, if he believes with integrity, if he is willing to give up, for the truth of faith, his broken limbs, since many martyrs were also old, how is it that we love him? What goods do we see in him with carnal eyes? None. Then there is a certain beauty of justice, which we see with the eyes of the heart, and we love it and are enraged. How much men were not loved in their martyrdoms when beasts tore their limbs! Didn't the eyes have something to be horrified about, when all things were stained with blood, when the viscera were thrown from the teeth of wild beasts? What was there in the midst of that cruelty of torn limbs worthy of

lem illa est, cui cantant qui incipiunt exire de Babylonia: Inhabitabit in atriis tuis. Replebimur in bonis domus tuae. Quae sunt bona domus Dei? Fratres, constituamus nobis aliquam domum divitem; quantis bonis referred to sit, quam copiosa sit, vasa quam tumba ibi áurea, sed et argentea; quantum familiae, quantum iumentorum et animalium; ipsa denique domus quam delectet picturis, marmore, laquearibus, columnis, spatiis, cubiculis; et desiderantur talia, sed adhuc ex confusione Babyloniae. Amputa omnia ista desideria, o civis Ierusalem; amputation! si vis rediré, no te delectet captivitas. Sed iam coepisti exire: noli retro respicere, noli remanere in via. Non desunt adhuc hostes qui tibi persuadeant captivitatem et peregrinationem: iam non praevaleant super te sermones iniquorum. Domum Dei desidera, et bona eius domus desidera; sed noli talia, qualia desiderare soles vel in domo tua, vel in domo vicini tui, vel in domo patroni tui. Aliud quiddam est bonum domus illius. Quid opus est ut nos dicamus quae sint bona illius domus? Ipse indicet qui cantat exiens de Babylonia: Replebimur, inquit, in bonis domus tuae. Quae sunt bona ista? Erexeramus fortasse cor ad aurum, ad argentum, et caetera pretiosa: noli talia quaerere; ista premunt, non levant. Hic ergo iam bona illa Ierusalem, bona illa domus Domini, bona illa templi Domini meditemur: quia quae domus Domini, hoc ipsum templum Domini. Replebimur in bonis domus tuae: sanc-

tum templum tuum, mirabile in iustitia. Ista sunt bona domus illius. Non dixit, Templum sanctum tuum, mirabile in columnis, mirabile in marmoribus, mirabile in tectis auratis; sed mirabile in iustitia. Habes foris oculos unde videas marmora et aurum: intus est oculus unde videatur pulchritudo iustitiae. Intus, inquam, est oculus unde videoatur pulchritudo iustitiae. If mile is pulchritudo iustitiae, unde amatur iustus senex? Quid affert in corpore quod oculos delectet? Curva membra, frontem rugatam, caput canis albatum, imbecillitatem undique querelis plenam. Sed forte quia tuos oculos non delectat senex iste decrepitus, aures tuas delectat: quibus vocibus? what did you sing? Etsi forte adolescens bene cantavit, omnia son aetate defecerunt. An forte sonus verborum eius delectat aures tuas, qui verba vix plena enuntiat lapsis dentibus? Tamen si iustus est, si alienum non concupiscit, si de suo quod habet erogat indigentibus, si bene monet, et rectum sapit, si integrate credit, si paratus est pro fide veritatis etiam ipsa confracta membra impendere, multi enim martyres etiam senes; unde illum amamus? quid in eo bonum videmus oculis carnis? Nihil. Quaedam ergo est pulchritudo iustitiae, quam videmus oculo cordis, et amamus, et exardescimus; quam multum dilexerunt homines in ipsis martytibus, cum eorum membra bestiae laniarent. Nonne cum sanguis foedaret omnia, cum morsibus belluinis viscera funderentur, non habebant oculi nisi quod horrerent?

That's also true of the remote. Allegorically, this century is called the sea, bitter with salt and troubled by storms, where men became, through perverse and depraved desires, like fish that devour each other. Behold the treacherous sea, the bitter sea, the sea raging with waves; See what kind of men it is full of. Who does not desire inheritance with the death of others? Who does not want profit at the expense of a third party? How many do not long to rise with the fall of others! How many do not want others to sell their things so they can buy them themselves! How they subjugate each other and, if they can, devour each other, for as the larger fish devours the smaller, so the larger is devoured by another larger! Oh wicked fish! You look for prey in the little one; you become prey to the big one. These things happen every day; they are in sight; We see them, we hate them. Let us not execute them, brothers, because He is the hope of all the ends of the earth. If He were not the hope of the remote sea, He would not have said to His disciples: I will make you fishers of men. Already captured in the sea by the nets of faith, let us rejoice there still swimming within the nets; because this sea is still angry because of the storms, but the nets that captured us will be brought to the shore. The shore is the end of the sea, then the arrival takes place at the end of the world. Meanwhile, brothers, let's live well within the networks; Let's not go outside breaking the net. Many broke networks and created schisms; They came out because they said they could not tolerate the bad fish they caught inside the net, and for this reason they rather became worse fish than those whom they caught.

Praeparans montes in fortitudine sua: non in fortitudine illorum. Praeparavit enim magnos praedicatores, et ipsos appellavit montes; humiles in se, exalted in illo. Praeparans montes in fortitudine sua. Quid dicit unus ex ipsis montibus? Ipsi in nobismetipsis responsum mortis habuimus, ut non fidentes in nobis simus, sed in Deo qui suscitat mortuos (2 Cor 1:9). Qui in se fidit, et in Christo non fidit, non est de his montibus quos ille praeparat in fortitudine sua. Praeparans montes in fortitudine sua, circumcinctus in potentatu. Potentatum intelligo: circumcinctus, quid est? Christum qui in medio ponunt, circumcinctum faciunt, id est undique cinctum. Habemus illum omnes communiter; ideo in medio est: circumcingimus illum omnes qui credimus in illum;

It is not due to our strength, but to his power, that is why he is girded with his power, not our strength. 11 [v. 8-9]. That you move the depths of the sea. Multiplicasti ditare eam. Unde multiplicasti eam ditare?

Eluvius Dei replete is here. Quis est fluvius Dei? Populus Dei. Primus populus repletus est, unde caetera terra rigaretur. Audi illum promittentem aquam: Si quis sitit, veniat et bibé. Qui credit in me, illuminates aquae vivae de ventre eius fluent (lo 7,37 et 38). If it illuminates, et unus fluvius; quia propter unitatem multi unum sunt. Multae Ecclesiae, et una Ecclesia; multi fideles, et una sponsa Christi: sic plana illuminates, et unus fluvius. Crediderunt multi Israelitae, et impleti sunt Spiritu sancto: inde diffusi sunt per Gentes; coeperunt praedicare veritatem, et de fluvio Dei qui impletus est aqua, irrigata est tota terra. Parasti cibum illorum; quia ita est praeparatio tua. Non quia te pro-

This is your preparation. And you prepared it not because those whose sins you forgave deserved you, since their merits were not good, but because of your mercy. Since this is your preparation; For the same reason, you prepared their food. 15 [v. l l ]. It intoxicates its furrows. First draw the furrows that are to be filled. Let the hardness of our hearts open with the grate of the word of God and intoxicate its furrows, multiply its reproduction. That's how we see it. For they believe, and because of those who believe, others also believe, and because of them others believe as well, since it is not enough for a man who has become a believer to win only one. This is how the seed multiplies. Few grains are thrown into the furrow and abundant crops grow. It intoxicates its furrows, multiplies its reproduction; With its drizzles it will be happy at birth. That is, before perhaps being able to receive the torrent of water, it will rejoice at being born with its drizzles; that is, he will rejoice in the drizzle convenient for himself. For the little ones and the weak, since they cannot receive the fullness of the truth, they distill some things from the sacraments. Hear how it distills or drizzles for the little ones when they begin to be born, that is, for those who are not yet capable of receiving the torrent of rain, since they have just been born: I could not, says the Apostle, speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal ones, as to little ones in Christ. By saying, as infants in Christ, he already says that they have been born, but that they are not yet qualified to receive the abundance of wisdom, of which he says: We speak wisdom among the perfect. Rejoice in its showers as you are born and grow; once fortified, he will be able to receive wisdom. The child is fed with milk, and thus becomes suitable for strong delicacies. That is why meruerunt, quibus peccata donasti: merita iliorum mala erant; be your propter mercym mam, quia ita est praeparatio tua, ita parasti cibum illorum. 15 [v. l l ]. Sulcos eius inebria. Fiant ergo primo sulci qui inebrientur: duritia pectoris nostri aperiatur vomere sermonis Dei, Sulcos eius inebria; multiply generations eius. Videmus: credunt, et ex credentibus alii credunt, et ex illis alii credunt; et non sufficit uni homini ut factus ipse fidelis unum lucretur. Sic multiplicatur et semen: pauca grana mittuntur, et segetes exsurgunt. Sulcos eius inebria; multiply generations eius: in stillicidiis suis laetabitur, cum exorietur.

Id est, antequam sit forte idenea capati fluminis, cum exorietur, in stillicidiis suis, id est sibi congruis, laetabitur. Those that are born in the likeness of wheat are properly called tares; Thus we have that the tares are similar to wheat, and oats, and other plants that have the first stem almost completely the same. About the sowing of tares the Lord said this: While men slept, the enemy came and sowed tares again; But when the grass grew and produced fruit, then the tares also appeared. Then the enemy came and sowed tares again. But what did it do to the wheat? The tares do not kill the wheat; In fact, tolerating the tares, the wheat grows. For the Lord himself said to the servants who wanted to uproot it: Let both grow together until the harvest, lest perhaps, wanting to uproot the tares, you uproot the wheat at the same time; When the time of harvest comes, I will say to my reapers: Gather up the tares first and tie them in sheaves to burn them, but put the wheat into the barn. The end of the year is the final harvest of the world. You will bless the crown of the year of your goodness. When you hear the word "crown" understand it as the glory of victory. For this reason the Lord said to his disciples: See that the fields are already ready for harvest, that is, the fields of Judea. Others—he says—worked, and you came in to share the work with them. 1 [v.l]. This psalm is titled For the End, a song of the resurrection psalm. When a psalm is sung and you hear "for the end," understand for Christ; For according to the Apostle, the end of the law is Christ, in order to justice, for every believer. Now you will hear, as soon as the Lord deigns to grant and declare it, how the resurrection is sung here and what resurrection it is about. Christians already know that the resurrection took place in our Head and that it will take place in the members. The head of the Church is Christ, and the members of Christ are the Church. What happened in the head will later be fulfilled in the body. This is our hope; This is why we believe, this is why we continue and remain among the great evil of this world, comforting ourselves with hope before it becomes reality. It will become a reality when, likewise, we are resurrected and, changed into a celestial state, we are made equal to the angels. Who would dare to hope for this if the Truth did not promise it? This promised hope the Jews considered theirs; boasting too much about good and just works, considering that they had received the law, and living according to it, they would obtain here

carnal goods, hoping that they would enjoy them at the resurrection of the dead. That is why the Jews could not respond to the Sadducees, who denied the resurrection of the body, when they proposed the question to them, which they also proposed to the Lord. We know that the Jews could not resolve the question for them, because, when the Lord resolved it, they were amazed. The Sadducees proposed the question about a certain woman who had seven husbands, not at the same time, but each one after the previous one had died. There was a law for the propagation of the people, consisting of that, if someone died without having had children, the brother of the deceased, if he had one, had to take the widow of the deceased as his wife to give succession to his brother. When the question was presented of the woman who had seven consecutive husbands, all dead, and without children, who to fulfill this duty took her brother's widow as his wife, they said, asking: In the resurrection, whose wife will she be? Without a doubt, the Jews would not have tired or given up in the resolution of this question if they had not hoped for themselves in the resurrection such things as they were pursuing in this life. But the Lord, who promised equality with the angels, not the human corruption of the flesh, answers them: You err because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God. In the resurrection, neither men nor women will be married, nor will they die, but they will be equal to the angels of God. He demonstrated, therefore, that where death exists, succession is necessary and that successors should not be sought where there is no death. For this reason he added, they will not die. However, since the Jews retained, even if carnally, the hope of the future resurrection, they were glad at the response rectionem, Iudaei respondé non poterant proponentibus quaestionem, quam Domino proposuerunt iidem Sadducaei. Hinc enim intelligimus eos hanc quaestionem solvere non potuisse, quia Domino solvente mirati sunt. Proponebant ergo Sadducaei quaestionem de quadam mullere, quae habuit septem viros; non simul, sed succedentes sibi. Erat enim hoc legis ad populum propagandum, ut qui forte sine liberis defungeretur, frater eius, si haberet, acciperet uxorem eius, ad suscitandum semen fratri suo (Deut 25,5). Proposita ergo illa mullere, quae habuit septem viros omnes mortuos sine liberis, et ad hoc officium implendum ducentes fratris uxorem, dixerunt quaerentes: In resurrectione cuius eorum erit uxor?

Procul dubio Iudaei non fatiguerentur, non deficerent in this quaestione, si non talia sibi in resurrectione sperarent, qualia agebant in hac vita. Dominus autem aequalitatem Angelorum promittens, non humanom carnis corruptionem, ait illis: Erratis, nescientes Scripturas, ñeque virtutem Dei. In resurrectione enim ñeque cloudnt, ñeque uxores ducent: ñeque enim incipient mori, sed erunt aequales Angelis Dei (Mt 22,23-30), et Le 20,27-36). Demonstravit quod ibi sit necessaria successio, ubi doletur decessio: ibi quia decessores non erunt, nec successores quaerentur. Ad hoc enim subiecit: Non enim incipient mori. Verumtamen quia Iudaei tenebant, etsi carnaliter, spem resurrec-

given to the Sadducees when the dispute with them began over the delicate and obscure question of the resurrection. The Jews expected the resurrection of the dead, and believed that only they would be resurrected to the blessed life because of the works of the law and the justification of the Scriptures, which only they had, and which the Gentiles lacked. Christ was crucified, and blindness partly came to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles had entered (into faith), according to the Apostle. The resurrection of the dead also began to be promised to the Gentiles, who believed in the resurrection of Christ. Hence this psalm is directed, against the presumption and pride of the Jews, in favor of the faith of the Gentiles, called to the same hope of the resurrection. 2. You have already heard, brothers, in some way, the plan of the psalm. On what I said, on what I explained, focus your attention; Don't let any other thoughts take you away from here. It speaks against the presumption of the Jews, who expected the resurrection for themselves alone due to the justice of the law, and yet they crucified Christ, who was resurrected first and who was to have as resurrected members not only the Jews, but all those who were to believe in Him, that is, all the Gentiles. This is where the psalm begins and says: Hail God. Who is it? All the land. Not only Judea. See, brothers, how it recommends the universality of the Church spread throughout the world. Do not feel sorry only for the Jews, who denied this grace to the Gentiles, but weep even more for the heretics. If, then, we have to grieve for those who did not gather, tionis futuree, gavisi sunt responsum esse Sadducaeis, cum quibus illis erat de hac ancipiti et obscura quaestione certamen. Tenebant ergo Iudaei spem resurrectionis mortuorum; et solos se ad beatam vitam resurrections sperabant propter opus Legis, et propter iustificationes Scripturarum, quas habebant soli Iudaei, et Gentes non habebant. Crucifixus est Christus; caecitas ex parte Israel jacta est, ut plenitudo Gentium intraret (Rom 11,25): hoc Apostólo dicente. Coepit etiam Gentibus promitti resurrectio mortuorum, credentibus in Iesum Christum quod resurrexerit. Inde psalmus iste est adversus praesumptionem et superbiam Iudaeorum, pro fide Gentium ad eamdem spem resurrectionis vocatarum. 2. Quodammodo, fratres meí, animum Psalmi audistis.

However, he is judged to have been learned in the law because he was not chosen among the disciples by Him who first chose the foolish things of the world. Yet the Lord bore great testimony of him, saying: Behold a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. Later, the Lord also chose speakers, but they would have been proud if he had not first chosen fishermen. He also chose the rich; But, if he had not first chosen the poor, they would say that they were chosen based on their wealth. Then he elected emperors; But it is better that the emperor, when he comes to Rome, laying down his diadem, weeps at the fisherman's tomb than that the fisherman weeps at the emperor's tomb. God chose the weak in the world to confuse the strong; and he also chose what is ignoble in the world and what is not, as if to undo what is. And what's next? The Apostle concludes: So that no man may boast before the Lord. See how he took our glory to give us glory; He took ours to give us his; He took away the vain to give us the perfect; took away from us the wavering prudentioribus non est approbata: ut quasi desperasse videretur ille, cum audiens dixisset, A Nazareth potest aliquid boni esse? id est, numquid potest? Sic pronouncing quasi desperaret. Sequitur autem ibi, Veni, et vide (lo 1,41-47). Haec verba, id est, Veni, et vide, utramque possunt pronuntiationem sequi. If you say, quasi non credens, A Nazareth potest aliquid boni esse? respondur, Veni, et vide quod non credis.

Rursus si dicas confirms, A Nazareth potest aliquid boni esse; respondur, Veni, et vide quam veré sit bonum quod nuntio a Nazareth; et quam recte credas, veni, et experire. Hinc tamen existimatur doctus ille in Lege Fuisse, quia non est electus inter disciples ab illo qui stulta mundi prius elegit; cum tantum ei perhibuerit testimonium Dominus dices: Ecce veré Israelita, in quo dolus non est. Elegit ergo Dominus postea et oratores; sed illi superbirent, si non prius chooseret piscatores: elegit divítes; sed dicerent merit divitiarum suarum se elect esse, nisi primo elegisset pauperes: elegit imperatores postea; sed melius est ut Romam cum venerit imperator, deposito diademate, ploret ad memoriam piscatoris, quam ut piscator ploret ad memoriam imperatoris. Infirma enim mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortia; et ignobilia mundi elegit, et ea quae non sunt, tanquam a^uae sunt, ut ea quae sunt evacuentur. Et quid sequitur? Conclusit Apostolus: Ut non glorietur coram Deo omnis caro. Videte quemadmodum nobis abstulit gloriam, ut daré glotiam: abstulit nostram, ut daret suam; abstulit inanem, ut daret plenam; abs-

to give us the solid. Our glory is all the stronger and more secure the more it is supported by God. Therefore you should not boast in yourself; The Truth forbade you. What the Truth commanded is what the Apostle says: He who boasts, let him glory in the Lord. Then give glory to his praise. Do not imitate the Jews, who tried to attribute their justification to their own merits and rejected the Gentiles, who approached evangelical grace so that all their sins would be forgiven; as if they had nothing at all that had to be forgiven, therefore already waiting for the salary as if they were good workers. And so, while they were still sick, they believed themselves to be healthy, and from this it came to pass that they were more seriously ill. Because, if they had had a mild illness, they would not have killed the doctor like a frenzy. Give glory to his praise. 5 [v.3). Tell God: How worthy of fear are your works! Why are they worthy of fear and not love? Hear another sentence from the psalmist: Serve God with fear and exalt Him with trembling. And what does this mean? Hear the Apostle: With fear and trembling perfect the work of your salvation. Why with fear and trembling? Listen to the reason below: Because God is the one who works in you out of benevolence, both to will and to act. Therefore, if God works in you, you work well by the grace of God, not by your strength. Then, if you rejoice, fear also; lest what was given to the humble be taken away from the proud. So that you may know that this happened to the Jews because of their own pride, since they believed that they were justified by the works of the law, and therefore they fell, another psalm says: These (contulit nutantem, ut daret solidam. Quanto ergo gloria nostra fortior et firmior, quia in Deo est! Si ergo Deus operatur in te, spelling Dei bene operaris, non viribus tuis. Ergo si gaudes, et time; ne forte quod datum est humili, auferatur superbo. Nam, ut noveritis hoc esse factum de ipsa superbia Iudaeorum, quasi se ex operibus Legis iustificantium, et ideo

They trusted) in chariots, and the former in horses, as if they placed the hope for their uprising in their own strength and means. But we, he says, will be exalted in the name of the Lord our God. These in chariots, those in horses; but we will be exalted in the name of the Lord our God. See how the former boasted in themselves, and the latter in God. So what does the same psalm say? Their feet were tied, and they fell; We, on the other hand, stood up and stood up straight. Hear our Lord Himself saying the same thing: I—he says—came so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may remain blind. Observe, on the one hand, goodness and, on the other, malice. But what is better than Him? Who is more merciful? Who is fairer? Why is it said: Those who do not see, let them see? For kindness. And why do those who see go blind? For the arrogance. Did they see and were they blind? They didn't see, it seemed to them that they saw. For observe, brothers, that when the Jews said, Are we blind?, the Lord said to them: If you were blind, you would have no sin; but as you now say: We see, your sin remains in you. You came to the doctor, and you say what you see? The eye drops are left over; you will always be blind. Recognize yourself blind so that you deserve to be enlightened. Look at the Jews, look at the Gentiles; To some he says: Those who do not see, let them see; and to others: I came so that those who see may become blind. The Jews saw our Lord Jesus Christ in the flesh, the Gentiles did not see him; and behold, those who saw him crucified him and those who did not see him believed. Then what have you done, O Christ!, to the sobercadentium, dicit alius psalmus: Hi in curribus, et hi in equis, quasi in suis quibusdam passibus et instrumentis ad erectionem suam; nos autem, inquit, in nomine Domini Dei nostri magnijicabimur: Hi in curribus, et hi in equis; nos autem in nomine Domini Dei nostri magnijicabimur. Vide quemadmodum illi extollebantur in se; vide quemadmodum isti gloriabantur in Deo. Propterea quid secutum est? lilis obligati sunt pedes, et ceciderunt; nos autem surreximus, et erecti sumus (Ps 19,8.9). Audi ipsum Dominum nostrum hoc idem dicentem: Ego, inquit, veni, ut qui non vident, videant; et qui vident, caed jiant. Vide in a pretty part; in alia quasi malitiam. Sed quid illo melius? quid misericordius? quid iustius? Quare ergo, qui non vident, videant? Propter bonitotem. Quare, et qui vident, caed jiant? Propter elationem. Et veré videbant, et facti sunt caeci?

Non videbant, sed videre sibi videbantur. Nam ecce videte, fratres: cum dicerent ipsi Iudaei, Num sumus caeci? ait Mis Dominus, Si caeci essetis, peccatum non baberetis: moda autem quia dicitis, Videmus, peccatum vestrum in vobis manet (lo 9,39-41). Ad medicum venisti; videre you say? Cessabunt collyria; semper caecus remanebis: confitere te caecum, ut illuminari merearis. Iudaeos attends; attende Gentes. Qui non vident, videant, inquit: ideo veni, ut qui vident, caeci fiant. Ipsum Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum in carne videbant Iudaei; Gentes non videbant: ecce qui viderunt, crucifixerunt; qui non viderunt, crediderunt. Ergo quid fecisti, or Christe,

bios? What did you do to them? We Gentiles see because you deigned for us to see and we are also your members. We see; you hid God and showed man. And why this? So that the blindness of Israel would be carried out and the fullness of the Gentiles would enter. For this you hid God, and presented man to the eyes. They saw and they did not see: they saw what you had received and they did not see what you were; They saw the form of a servant and did not see the form of God. They saw the form of a servant, by which the Father is greater, and they did not see the form of God, by which you now heard: I and the Father are one. They seized what they saw, they crucified what they saw; They insulted him whom they saw and did not know him who was hidden. Listen to the Apostle, who says: If they had known him, they would never have crucified the King of glory. Gentiles who have been called, look at the branches that were broken off by bitterness; you have been grafted by goodness and made partakers of the fatness of the olive tree; do not consider yourself to be more than what you are, that is, do not become arrogant. You do not lead to the root, but it is the one that leads you. Rather tremble when you see the natural branches cut off. The Jews, tracing their origin from the patriarchs, were born of the stock of Abraham. And what does the Apostle say? But you will say: The branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in. Certainly, through infidelity they were broken off. But you—he says—stand by the heh; Don't be conceited, be afraid; because, if God did not forgive the natural branches, he will not forgive you either. Contemplate the broken branches and contemplate yourself grafted. Do not think more of yourself than the broken branches, but say to God: How worthy to be feared are your works! Heradversus superbos? what did you say? Videmus, quia dignitatus es, et membra tua sumus; videmus: abscondisti Deum; obiecisti hominem. Quare hoc? Ut caecitas ex parte Israel ieront, et plenitudo Gentium intraret. Ad hoc abscondisti Deum, et hominem aspectibus obiecisti. Videbant, et non videbant: videbant quod acceperas, et non videbant quod eras: videbant formam setvi, non videbant formam Dei (Phil 2,6.7); formam servi, qua maior est Pater (lo 14,28); non formam Dei, propter quam moda audistis, Ego et Pater unum sumus (Ib. 10,30). Tenuerunt quod videbant, crucifixerunt quod videbant; ínsultaverunt ei quem videbant, non agnoverunt qui latebat. Audi Apostolum dicentem: 5» enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent (1 Cor 2,8).

Ergo Gentes quae vocatae estis, attendite ramos praecisos propter severitatem; You autem insertos propter bonitotem, et participates factos pinguedinis oleae, non altum sapientes; id est non superientes. Non enim tu radicem portas, ait; sed radix te. Magis tetreamini, quia videtis amputates natural bouquets. Iudaei enim per Patriarchas venerunt; of meat Abrahae nati sunt. Et quid ait Apostolus? You say: Fracti sunt rami, ut ego inserar. Bene; propter infidelitatem fracti sunt. Tu autem, inquit, fide stas; noli altum supere, sed time: si enim naturalibus ramis Deus non pepercit, ñeque tibí parcet. Attende ergo ramos fractos, et te insertum: noli extolli super ramos fractos; sed magis dicito Deo, Quam metuenda sunt opera tua! Fratres, si adversus Iudaeos olim praecisos of

hands, if we should not think more highly of ourselves than the Jews who were once cut off from the roots of the patriarchs, but rather fear and say: How worthy of fear are your works!, how much less should we be proud of the recent wounds of those who were cut off! Previously the Jews were broken off and the Gentiles were grafted in. From this graft the heretics broke off; But neither should we be arrogant before these, lest he who pleases to insult those who are cut deserve to be cut off. My brothers, whatever voice you hear in this sense from the bishop, we beg you to disdain it; Those of you who are in the Church do not insult those who are outside it, but rather pray that they may enter. God is powerful to graft them in again. The Apostle said this about the Jews, and this is what happened to them. The Lord was resurrected, and many believed. They did not know him when they crucified him; However, later they believed in Him and such an enormous crime was forgiven. Once the blood of the Lord was shed, the murderers were forgiven, so that I will not call them deicides, because, if they had known Him, they would never have crucified the King of glory. Now, when the blood of the Innocent was shed, the murderers were forgiven, and the same blood that they shed out of folly, they drank out of grace. Tell God, then: How worthy of fear are your works! Why should they be feared? For partial blindness befell Israel until the fullness of the nations came in. O mass of Gentiles! Say to God: How worthy of fear are your works! And rejoice so that you may not fear. Do not boast about the broken branches. Tell God: How worthy of fear are your works! radice Patriarcharum extollere nos non debenmus, sed timere potius, et dicere Deo, Quam timenda sunt opera tua! quanto minus non nos debenmus extollere adversus recentia vulnera praecisionum? Praecisi sunt ante Iudaei, insertae sunt Gentes: de ipsa insertione praecisi sunt haeretici; sed ñeque contra illos nos extollere deben, ne forte praecidi mereatur, quem delectat insultare praecisis. Fratres mei, qualiscumque episcopi vox sonuit vobís, rogamus vos ut caveatis: quicumque in Ecclesia estis, nolite insultare eis qui non sunt intus; sed orate potius ut et ipsi intus sint. Potens est enim Deus iterum inserere illos. De ipsis Iudaeis dixit hoc Apostolus; et factum est in eis.

Resurrexit Dominus, et multi crediderunt: non intellexerunt cum crucifigerent; tamen postea crediderunt in eum, et donatum est eis tam magnum delictum. Fusus Domini sanguis donatus est homicidis, ut non dicam deicidis; quia si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent. Modo homicidis donatus est fusus sanguis innocentis; et ipsum sanguinem quem per insaniam fuderunt, per gratiam biberunt. Diáte ergo Deo: Quam timenda sunt opera tua! Where is the time? Quia caecitas ex parte Israel facía est, ut plenitudo Gentium intraret (Rom 11,17-25) - O Gentium plenitudo, dic Deo, Quam timenda sunt opera tua! et sic gaude ut contremiscas; noli extolli super ramos praecisos. Say Deo: Quam timenda sunt opera tua!

6. In the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you. Your enemies will lie to you, he says, so that your power may be immense. What is this? Listen very carefully. The power of our Lord Jesus Christ was especially manifested in the resurrection, for which this psalm took its title. Resurrected, he did not appear to his enemies, but to his disciples. Crucified, he showed himself to everyone; resurrected, to the faithful to promise the resurrection to the believer and to those who later wanted to believe. Many saints performed untold miracles; none of them, dead, rose again. And those who were resurrected by them were resurrected to die again. Take care of your charity. The Lord commending his works, said: If you do not believe me, believe my works. The past works of the prophets are also recommended; Well, if not all, many are equal and of the same power. The Lord walked on the waters; He also ordered Pedro to walk. Was the Lord not there when the sea parted for Moses and his people to pass through? The Lord himself did these things. He who did these things through his flesh did these things through the flesh of his servants. However, He did not do for His servants, since He did all things, to raise any of those who were dead to eternal life. Therefore, as the Jews could say when the Lord worked miracles, Moses, and Elijah, and Elisha also did these things; and they could say it because they raised the dead and performed many other miracles; Therefore, when asked by the Jews for a sign, recommending the special sign that alone was to take place, he says: This depraved and provoking generation of the 6. In multitudine potentiae tuae mentientur tibi inimici tui. Ad hoc tibi, inquit, mentientur inimici tui, ut Fine sit potentia tua. Quid est hoc? Intentius audite. Potentia Domini nostri Ieusu Christi máxime apparuit in resurrectione, unde psalmus iste titulum accepit. Et resurgens apparuit discipulis suis. Non apparuit inimicis suis, sed discipulis suis (Act 10,41). Crucifixus apparuit omnibus; resurgens fidelibus: ut etiam postea qui vellet crederet, et credenti resurrectio promitteretur. Multi sancti fine miracula fecerunt; nullus ipsorum mortuus resurrexit: quia et qui ab eis resuscitati sunt, morituri resuscitati sunt. Intendat Charitas Vestra. Commendans Dominus operates sua dixit: Operibus credite, si mihi non vultis credere (lo 10.38).

Et commendantur etiam praeterita opera Prophetarum; et si non eadem, tamen fines eadem, fines eiusdem potentiae. Ambulavit Dominus super mare, iussit et Petrum (Mt 14,25.29). Numquid non ibi erat ipse Dominus, quando se divisit mare, ut Moyses cum populo Israel transiret? (Ex 14,21). idem Dominus illa faciebat. Qui fecit ista per carnem suam, ipse illa faciebat per carnem servorum suorum. Illud tamen per servos suos non fecit (nam ipse omnia faciebat), ut aliquis ipsorum mortuus esset, et resurgeret in vitam aeternam. Quia ergo possent dicere Iudaei, cum miracula faceret Dominus, Fecit haec et Moyses, fecit Elias, fecit Elisaeus: possent sibi ista dicere, quia et illi mortuos resuscitaverunt, et plana miracula fecerunt: propterea cum ab illo signum peteretur; proprium signum commendans quod in se solo futurum erat, ait: Generatio ista

God's wrath demands a sign, and no other sign will be given except the sign of Jonah the prophet. Just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the cetacean, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. How was Jonah in the belly of the cetacean? Was he not there to be later returned alive? What the cetacean was for Jonah, this was the abyss of the earth for the Lord. This was the particular sign that recommended, this is the great power. It is a more powerful thing for a dead person to resurrect himself than to not have died. The greatness of the Lord's power, considering that he became man, is manifested in the virtue of the resurrection. This is what the Apostle recommends when he says: Not having my righteousness, which comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ; justice that comes from God founded on faith in order to know Him and the power of His resurrection. It is also recommended elsewhere in this way: And, if he was crucified for weakness, live by the virtue of God. Then as this great power of the Lord is manifested in the resurrection, from which this psalm took its title, what does it mean In the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you but that you understand that your enemies will lie so that you may be crucified and that you are crucified so that you may be resurrected? His lie will serve to highlight your immense power. Why do enemies usually lie? To diminish the power of the one they lie about. For you, he says, the opposite happened. Your power would have appeared lesser if you had not been slandered. prava et amaricans signum quaerit; et signum non dabitur ei, nisi signum lonae prophetae. Sicut enim fuet canvases in ventre ceti tribus diebus, et tribus noctibus; sic erit et filius hominis in corde terrae tribus diebus, et tribus noctibus (Mt 12,39.40). How did you get tarps in ventre ceti? Nonne ut postea vivus evomeretur? Hoc fuet infernus Domino, quod lonae cetus. Hoc signum proprium commendavit; hoc est potentissimura, Potentius est revixisse mortuum, quam non Fuisse mortuum. Magnitudo potentiae Domini secundum quod homo factus est, in virtute resurrectionis apparet. Hanc commendat Apostolus, cum dicit: Non habens meam iustitiam quae ex Lege est; sed eam quae est per fidem Christi, quae est ex Deo iustitia in fide, ad cognoscendum eum, et virtutem resurrectionis eius (Phil 3,9.10). Sic commendatur et alio loco: Et si crucifixus est ex infirmitate, sed vivit in virtute Dei (2 Cor 13,4).

Cum ergo ista magna potentia Domini in resurrectione intelligatur, unde titulum psalmus iste accepit; quid sibi vult, In multitudine potentiae tuae mentientur tibi inimici tui, nisi ut sic intelligas: Ideo tibi mentientur inimici tui ut crucifigaris; ideo crucifigeris ut resurgas? Mendacium ergo illorum ad commendandam tumbam potentiam mam valebit. Quare solent inimici liar? Ut potentiam cuiusque minuant de quo mentiuntur. Tibi, inquit, contra accidit. Nam minus appareret potentia tua, si tibi illi non lyingentur,

7. Also observe in the Gospel the lie of the false witnesses and notice that it is about the resurrection. When it was said to the Lord: What sign do you give us as to why you do these things?, without taking into account what he had said about Jonah, he answered the same thing using another similarity so that you may know that this particular sign is the one that was recommended in a special way (for he said thus: Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up). days? The evangelist, exposing this passage, says: And this Jesus said of the temple of his body. See how, taking the likeness of the body because its flesh was a temple where the divinity resided hidden, he said that he would manifest this power to men. Hence the Jews saw the temple externally, but they did not see the divinity that lived internally. From these words of the Lord, false witnesses concocted the lie that they told against Him; of these precisely for which, speaking of the temple, he declared his future resurrection. When the false witnesses were asked what they had heard him say, they deposed, saying: We have heard him say: I will destroy this temple and in three days I will rebuild it. They had heard it said: In three days I will rebuild it. But they had not heard it said: I will destroy him, but: Destroy. They changed one word and a few letters of it, and it was enough to concoct a false testimony. But whose words do you change, oh human vanity, oh human weakness? You change the word to the immutable Word. You change your word, but do you change the Word of God? Hence it is said in another

place: And iniquity lied to itself. Why did your enemies lie to you or slander you, O Lord, you, whom all the earth exalts? In the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you. They say: I will destroy, when you have said: Destroy. Why did they say that you had said: I will destroy and they did not say what you said: Destroy? In order to defend themselves from this crime, without having room to defend themselves, from the crime of the destruction of the temple, Christ certainly died because he wanted to; However, you killed him. But see that we grant you, O scoundrels!, that He Himself destroyed the temple. For it was said by the Apostle: He loved me and gave himself for me. It was also said of the Father that he did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all. But if the Father gave up the Son and the Son gave up himself, then what did Judas do? The Father did well by giving his Son to death for us; Christ also did good by giving himself for us, but Judas did wrong by giving up the Master out of greed. It is not imputed to the malice of Judas for having given us the benefit of the passion of Christ. He will have the reward of his malice; Christ, the praise of grace. Therefore, He destroyed the temple; The same one who said: I have power to lay down my life and power to take it again; no one will take it from me, but I myself lay it down and take it again. He destroyed the temple by his grace and by your malice. In the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you. See that they lie; see that they are given credit; see that you are oppressed, crucified, abused,

7. Attendite et ipsum mendacium falserum testium in Gospel, et videte quia de resurrectione est. Cura enim Domino dictum esset, Quod signum ostendis nobis, quia ista facis? except eo quod dixerat de lona, ​​per aliam similarityinem hoc ipsum Item dixit, ut noveritís hoc proprium signum máxime commendatum: Solvite templum, inquit, hoc; et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Et Mi dixerunt: Quadraginta et sex annis aedijicatum est templum hoc; et tu in triduo excitabis illud? Et evangelista, quid illud esset exponens: Hoc autem, inquit, dicebat Iesus de temple corporis sui (lo 2,18-21). Ecce have potentiam suam hominibus se demonstraturum dicebat, unde similarityinem de temple dederat, propter carnem suam quae erat templum latentis intus divinitatis. Unde Iudaei templum foris vídebant; numen intus habitans non videbant. Ex istis verbis Domini concinnaverunt falsi testes mendacium, quod contra eum dicerent, ex his ipsis ubi commendavit resurrectionem suamfuturam, loquens de temple. Dixerunt enim falsi testes adversus eum, cum quaereretur ab eis quid illum audissent dixisse: Audivimus eum dicentem, Solvam templum hoc, et post triduum resuscitabo illud (Mt 26,61). Post triduum resuscitabo, audierant: Solvam, non audierant; sed audierant, Solvite. Unum verbum mutaverunt, et paucas litteras, ut falsum testimonium molirentur. Sed cui mutas verbum, o humano vanitas, o humano infirmitas? Verb incommutabili verbum mutas! You mutate your tuum

verbum; numquid mutas Dei Verbum? Unde alio loco dicitur: Et menta est iniquitas sibi (Ps 26,12). Quare ergo tibi mentiti sunt inimici tui, o Domine, cui iubilat omnis terra? In multitudine potentiae tuae mentientur tibi inimici tui. Dicent, Solvam; cum tu dixeris, Solvite. Quare te dixerunt dixisse, Solvam; et non dixerunt quod tu dixisti, Solvite? Ut quasi ipsi se a crimine soluti templi defenderent sine causa. Christus enim, quia voluit, mortuus est: et tamen vos occidistis. Ecce concedimus vobis, or mendacious; ipse solvit templum. Dictum est enim ab Apostólo: Qui me dilexit et tradidit semetipsum pro me (Gal 2,20). Dictum est de Patre: Qui proprio Filio suo non pepercit; sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit illum (Rom 8:32). Si ergo Pater Filium tradidit, et Filius semetipsum tradidit; ludas quid fecit? Pater tradendo Filium ad mortem pro nobis, bene fecit: Christus tradendo seipsum pro nobis, fecit bene: tradendo ludas magistrum pro avaritia sua, fecit male. Non enim quod nobis praestitum est de passione Christi, malitiae Iudae deputabitur: habebit ille mercedem malitiae; Christus laudem gratiae. Prorsus ipse solverit templum; ipse solverit qui dixit: Potestatem habeo ponendi aniínam meam; et potestatem habeo iterum sumendi eam: nemo tollit eam a me; sed ego ipse pono eam a me, et iterum sumo eam (lo 10, 18). These tribulations are simply scourges of the one who corrects so that the sentence of punishment of the one who punishes does not ensue. You placed tribulations on our backs, you placed men on our heads. 17. We went through fire and water. Fire and water; Both things are dangerous in this life. Without a doubt, water quenches fire, and fire dries up water. These two things are the temptations, of which this life abounds. Fire burns, water ruins; Both things must be feared: both the fire of tribulation and the water of destruction. When the things we encounter are anguish and some of what are called misfortunes in this world occur, it is like fire. When prosperous things appear and the abundance of the century surrounds us, it is like water. Go, don't let the fire burn you and the water ruin you. Stand firm before the fire; It's good that you care. As a clay vessel, you are thrown into the furnace of fire so that what has been formed is consolidated. The glass strengthened by fire does not fear water. But, if the glass has not been consolidated or cooked by fire, it is dissolved like earth by water. Don't be in a hurry to go to the water; pass through fire into water so that you may also pass through water. That is why in the sacraments the fire is first applied, catechizing and exorcising. For if not, how is it that many unclean spirits cry, I burn, if this is not fire? After the fire of exorcism we come to baptism so that from the fire we go to water, and from water to rest. What happens in the sacraments, the same happens in the temptations of this world. The first that occurs is the anguish of fear; a Pater est, nunquam sic saevit ut perdat. When you live, if parcit, plus irascitur. Ómnino istae tribulationes flagella sunt corregentis, ne sit sententia punientis. Posuisti tribulationes in dorso nostro: imposuisti homines super capita riostra. 17. Transivimus per ignem et aquam. Ignis et aqua, utrumque periculosum est in hac vita. Certe videtur aqua ignem exstinguere, et ignis videtur aquam siccare. Ita et ipsae temptationes sunt, quibus abundat haec vita. Vide ne te ignis exurat, ne aqua corrumpat.

then the fire; Then, once fear has disappeared, we must fear that worldly happiness will not ruin us.
