a certain acidity that must be tolerated, which is represented by those who gave the baby vinegar. Then, foreshadowing and transforming us into himself, he says: Save me, O God, because the waters have penetrated to my soul. They were able to kill those they pursued, but they had no power to do more. That is why the Lord warned us in advance, saying: Do not fear those who kill the body and have no power to do anything else; fear Him who has power to kill soul and body and throw them into the fires of hell. We despise the smallest things with the greatest fear and we disdain temporal things out of the greatest longing for eternity. In this world, temporal things are sweet, and tribulations are bitter; but who will not drink the cup of temporal tribulations fearing the fire of hell and who will not despise the sweetness of the world coveting the sweetness of eternal life? Then let us cry from here that we may be delivered, lest in afflictions we consent to iniquity and be irreparably absorbed by it. Save me, O God, for the waters have penetrated to my soul, 4 [v. 3]. I am mired in the mud of the deep, and there is no substance. What do you call mud? Perhaps the same ones who persecuted him? Man was made of mud. These, losing justice, became deep mud. Everyone who does not consent to the insinuations of those who persecute him and wish to drag him into iniquity, makes gold from his mud, because he will deserve to convert his mud into celestial nature and become a companion of those of whom the title of the psalm says: In favor of those who will be changed.

But, since these were deep mud, I ran aground in them, that is, they captured me, they prevailed over me, they killed me. Then I got stuck in the mud of the deep, and there is no substance. What does no substance mean? Isn't mud a substance? Or that, running aground, I ceased to be substance? What does it mean I got stuck? Was Christ adhered in this way? Or did it adhere, but not as it is read in the book of Job: The earth was given into the hands of the wicked? Or perhaps he was overwhelmed as to his body, because he could have been captured and crucified? Well, if he had not been fastened with nails, he would not have been crucified. So how is it not substance? Is mud not substance? We will understand, if we can, what no substance means if we first understand what substance is. Riches are called substances. According to this, we say: He has no substance, that is, he has property or he has lost his property. But are we to believe that it was said there is no substance, that is, there is no riches, as if it were now about riches or a question of money? Or perhaps it was said that way because slime was poverty, and it will not be wealth except when we participate in eternity? Then there will be true riches when we lack nothing. It can, therefore, be understood that I am stuck in the mud of the deep, and there is no substance, taking into account the meaning that I have given to the word, as if it were said: I have fallen into poverty. Because later in this psalm it is said: I am poor and afflicted. And the Apostle says: Christ, being rich, became poor for us so that through his poverty you might become rich. Then perhaps the Lord, wanting to recognize

dum, quo ostenduntur qui eum aceto potaverunt (Mt 27,34). Praefigurans ergo, et transformans in se nos ipsos, hoc ait: Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam introierunt aquae usque ad animam meam. Potuerunt qui persecuti sunt etiam occidere; sed amplius quid faciant non habebunt. Praemisit enim exhortationem ipse Dominus dices: Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, et amplius non habent quid faciant; sed eum úmete qui habet potestatem, et corpus et animam occidere in gehenna ignis (Ib. 10,28). Maiore timore minora contemnimus, et maiore aeternitatis cupiditate omnia temporalia fastidimus. Nam hic et deliciae temporalis dulce sunt, et tribulationes temporales amarae sunt: ​​sed quis non bibat tribulationis temporalis poculum, metuens ignem gehennarum; et quis non contemnar dulcedinem saeculi, inhians dulcedini vitae aeternae? Hinc ergo ut liberemur clamemus, ne forte in ptessuris consentiamus iniquitati, et veré irreparabiliter sorbeamur: Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam introierunt aquae usque ad animam meam. 4 [v.5]. Infixus sum in limo projundi, et non est substantia. Quid dicit limum? an ipsos qui persecuti sunt? De limo enim factus est homo (Gen 2:7). Sed isti, cadendo a iustitia, limus profundi facti sunt; quibus persequentibus et ad iniquitatern trahere cupientibus quisquís non consenserit, de limo suo aurum facit. Merebitur enim limus ipsius convertedí in habitudinem caelestem, et socius fieri eorum de quibus dicit titulus Psalmi: Pro bis qui commutabuntur. Isti autem eum limus pro-

fundi essent, haesi in illis; id est tenuerunt me, praevaluetunt mihi, occiderunt me. Infixus ergo sum in limo profundi, et non est substantia. Quid est hoc, non est substantia? Numquidnam ipse limus non est substantia? An, ego inhaerendo factus sum non esse substantia? Quid est ergo, Infixus sum? Numquidnam sic haesit Christus? Aut vero haesit, ac non, sicut dictum est in libro Iob, Tena tradita est in manus impii (Iob 9,24). An secundum corpus infixus est, quia teneri potuit, et ipsam crucifixionem habebat? Nisi enim clavis fixus esset, crucifixus non esset. Unde ergo non est substantia? An limus ille non est substantia? Intelligemus ergo, si potuerimus, quid sit, et non est substantia, si prius intellexerimus quid sit substantia. Substantia quippe dicitur et divitiarum: secundum quam dicimus, Habet substantiam, et, Perdidit substantiam. Sed numquid hoc putabimus hic dictum esse, et non est substantia, id est, non sunt divitiae, quasi modo aliquid de divitiis ageretur, aut aliqua quaestio de divitiis haberetur? An forte quia ille ipse limus paupertas erat, et divitiae non erunt, nisi quando aeternitatis participates effecti fuerimus? Tune sunt enim verae divitiae, quando nobis nihil deerit. Potest etiam secundum huius verbi intellectum accipi sensus iste, ut diceretur, Infixus sum in limo profundi, et non est substantia, id est ad paupertatem perveni. Nam hic dicit: Pauper et dolens ego sum; dicit et Apostolus: Quoniam propter vos pauper factus est, eum dives esset, ut ittius paupertate vos ditaremini (2 Cor 8,9)- Ergo paupertatem

Mendating his poverty, he said: There is no substance. Well, he reached extreme poverty when he took on the form of a servant. What are your riches? Having the form of God and not judging prey is being equal to God. These are immense riches in the extreme. So, where does this poverty originate from? That he emptied himself, taking the day of a servant; and of finding himself in the habit of a man, humbling himself until he became obedient to the point of death, so that for this reason he said: The waters penetrated to my soul. It adds something more than death. What more needs to be added? The ignominy of death. That is why he continues: Until death on a cross. Add poverty! But from here come the immense riches, because just as he was saturated with poverty, so he satisfied us with riches with his poverty. How many riches he has due to his poverty to enrich us! How rich he will make us with his riches if he enriched us with his poverty! 5. I am stuck in the mud of the deep and there is no substance. The word substance also has another meaning, one that expresses that we are what we are. This one is harder to understand even though it is common. But since it is an unusual word, it needs slight consideration and exposition. If you pay attention, perhaps we will not make the effort to try to expose it. The man, the beast, the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, the stone, the air, all are substances in the same thing that they are. Natures are substances. God is a certain substance, because what is not substance is nothing. Substance is a being. Hence in the Catholic faith we thus foresee volens Dominus nobis commendare, fortasse dixerit, non est substantia. Ad summam enim paupertatem pervcnit, quando formam servi induit. Divitiae eius quae sunt? Qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. Hae magnae incomparabilesque divitiae. Unde ergo is paupertas? Quia semetipsum exinanivit formam servi accipiens, in similarityinem hominum factus, et habit inventus ut homo; humiliavit se, factus obediens usque ad mortem: ut diceret, Introierunt aquae usque ad animam meam. Adde super mortem: what amplius additurus is it? Ignominiam mortis. Ideo sequitur: Mortem autem crucis (Phil 2,6.8). Great paupers! Sed hinc erunt magnae divitiae; quia sicut impleta est paupertas eius, ita implebuntur et divitiae nostrae de paupertate ipsius. How many divisions there are, ut de sua paupertate nos divites faceret!

Quales nos factutus est de divitiis suis, quos divites fecit de paupertate sua! 5. Infixus sum in limo profundi, et non est substantia. Intelligitur alio moda substantia, illud quod sumus quidquid sumus. Sed hoc ad intelligendum aliquanto est difficilius, quanquam res usitatae sint: sed quia inusitatum verbum est, indiget commendationis et expositionis aliquantulae; Cui also if you tried fueritis, fortassis in ea non laborabimus. Dicitur homo, dicitur pecus, dicitur tetra, dicitur caelum, dicitur sol, luna, lapis, mare, aer: omnia ista substantiae sunt, eo ipso quo sunt. Naturae ipsae, substantiae dicuntur. Deus est quaedam substantia; nam quod nulla substantia est, nihil omnino est. Substantia ergo aliquid esse

Let us take courage against the poison of some heretics, who say: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one substance. What does it mean they are a single substance? That, for example, if the Father is gold, gold is the Son and gold is the Holy Spirit. What the Father is inasmuch as he is God, this is the Son and the Holy Spirit. To be a Father is not to be what one is (that is, it is not a substance, but rather a relationship), because one is not called Father for oneself, but for the Son; for himself he is God, since, because of what God is, he is substance. And since the Son has the same substance, without a doubt the Son is God. But since what is Father is not a name of substance, but of relation to the Son, that is why we do not say that the Son is Father, just as we say that the Son is God as the Father is. Questions: What is the Father? You are answered: God. Questions: What is the Son? Likewise you are answered: God. Questions unrelated to anything: What is the Father and the Son? In the same way you are answered: God. You have asked about the being of the Father; God, you have been answered. You have asked about the being of the Son; God, was the answer. You have asked about the being of the Father and the Son; Diosyno Dioses, has been the response. No to the park in men; Well, you ask, what is the patriarch Abraham? Man, it is answered, and it is answered taking into account its substance. You ask what his son Isaac is, and the answer is: Man. Of the same substance are Abraham and Isaac. You ask what Abraham and Isaac are, and the answer is not: Man, but: Men. In divine persons it is not like that. For there is such a union of substances that it is not plurality, but unity. If it were said to you: Look, you have told me that the Son is what the Father is; Therefore, the Son is the Father, responds. Unde etiam in Fide catholica, contra venena quorumdam haereticorum sic aedificamur, ut dicamus Patrem, et Filium, et Spiritum sanctum unius esse substantiae. What is it, unius substantiae? Verbi gratia: si aurum est Pater, autum et Filius, autum et Spiritus sanctus. Quidquid est Pater quod Deus est, hoc Filius, hoc Spiritus sanctus. Cum autem Pater est, non illud est quod est.

Pater enim non ad se, sed ad Filium dicitur: ad se autem Deus dicitur. Itaque eo quod Deus est, hoc ipso substantia est. Et quia eiusdem substantiae Filius, procul dubio et Filius Deus. At vero quod Pater est; quia non substantiae nomen est, sed refertur ad Filium, non sic dicimus Filium Patrem esse, quomodo dicimus Filium Deum esse. Quaeris quid sit Pater: responderur, Deus. Quaeris quid sit Filius: responderur, Deus. Quaeris quid sit Patet et Filius: responderur, Deus. From only Patre interrogatus, Deum responds: from only Filio intetrogatus, Deum responds: from utroque interrogatus, non déos, sed Deum responds. Non sicut in hominibus. Quaeris quid sit patet Abraham: responderur, Homo; substantia eius respondertuf. Quaeris quid sit filius eius Isaac: respondertur, Homo; eiusdem substantiae Abraham et Isaac. Quaeris quid sit Abraham et Isaac: non tespondetur, Homo; thirst Homines. Non sic in divinis. Tanta enim ibi est substantiae societas, ut aequalitatem admittat, pluralitatem non admittat. Si ergo tibi dictum fuerit, Cum dicis mihi Filium hoc esse quod Pater est, ptofecto et Filius Patet est; answer-

Rias: As for the substance, I told you that the Son is the same as the Father, not insofar as he relates to another. Listening to himself, he calls himself God; attending to the Father, he is called the Son. Likewise, the Father, considering himself, is God; in relation to the Son, he is Father. The Father, in relation to the Son, is not the Son, and the Son, in relation to the Father, is not the Father. As far as the Father in himself and the Son in himself are concerned, the Father is the same as the Son; that is, God. So what does it mean there is no substance? According to this concept of substance, how can we understand this sentence of the psalm: I am mired in the mire of the deep, and there is no substance? God made man; made a substance; and would that it had remained as God made it! If man had remained as God made him, he would not have bogged down in the deep mud what God made. Finally, since man fell through iniquity from the being in which he was made, and iniquity is not a substance, since it is not a nature created by God, but a perversity that man made, therefore the Son of God came into the mire of the deep and was bogged down, and there was no substance in which he was bogged down, because he was bogged down in the iniquity of man. It got bogged down in the mud of the deep, and there is no substance. All things were made by Him, and without Him nothing was made. All natures were made by Him, but not iniquity, because it was not made. The substances were made by Him and they praise Him. The creation that praises God is commemorated in its entirety by the three young men in the furnace of fire, since the hymn of praise of those who worship God extends from terrestrial creatures to celestial ones or from these to those. No, because you are: Secundum substantiam tibí dixi hoc esse Filium quod Pater est, non secundum id quod ad aliud dicitur. Ad se enim Deus dicitur, ad Patrem Filius dicitur. Rursusque Pater ad se Deus dicitur, ad Filium Pater dicitur. Quod dicitur ad Filium Pater, non est Filius: quod dicitur Filius ad Patrem, non est Pater: quod dicitur ad se Pater, et Filius ad se, hoc est Pater et Filius, id est Deus. Quid est ergo, non est substantia?

Secundum hunc intellectum substantiae, quomodo poterimus intelligere ¡starn Psalmi sententiam: Infixus sitm in limo profundi, et non est substantia? Deus fecit hominem; substantiam fecit: atque utinam maneret in eo quod Deus fecit! Si maneret homo in eo quod Deus fecit, non in illo infixus esset quem Deus genuit. Porro autem quia per iniquitatem homo lapsus est a substantia in qua factus est (iniquitas quippe ipsa non est substantia; non enim iniquitas est natura quam formavit Deus, sed iniquitas est perversitas quam fecit homo): venit Filius Dei ad limum profundi, et infixus est; et non erat substantia in qua infixus est; quia in iniquitate illorum infixus est. Infixus sum in limo profundi, et non est substantia. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil (lo 1,3). Naturae omnes per ipsum factae sunt: ​​iniquitas per ipsum facta non est, quia iniquitas facta non est. Substantiae illae per eum factae sunt quae laudant eum. Universa creature laudans Deum, a tribus pueris on the way commemoratur; et a

creatures have the power to praise, but because all of them, well thought out, excite praise and the heart is directed, when considering creation, to sing a hymn of praise to the Creator. All creatures praise God, but those that He made. Do you perchance notice that in that hymn greed praises God? The serpent praises him, but greed does not praise him. There all the reptiles were named in praise of the Lord, but no vice was named. Vices come from us and come from our will and are not substances. The Lord got stuck in them when he suffered persecution; in the vices of the Jews, but not in the substance of men, which was made by Him. He bogged me down—he says—• in the mud of the deep, and there is no substance. I got bogged down and couldn't find what I did. 6. I have reached the high seas, and the storm submerged me. Let us give thanks to the mercy of the One who reached the high seas and deigned to surrender to be devoured by the marine cetacean, but who was returned on the third day. It reached the high seas, where, having been shipwrecked, we were submerged. There He came, and the storm submerged him, because there He endured the human waves, the storms, the voices of those who said: Crucify, crucify! For when Pilate said: I find in this man no cause for which he should die, the shouting increased, saying: Crucify, crucify! The storm intensified until the one who had come to the high seas was submerged. And the Lord, who not only did not sink when walking on the waters, but did not allow Saint Peter to sink, terrenis ad caelestia, vel a caelestibus ad terrena hymnus Iaudantium Deum pervenit (Dan 3,24-90). Non quo cuneta is habeant sensum laudandi; sed quia cuneta bene cogitata laudem pariunt, et impletur cor consideratione creaturae ad eructandum hymnum Creatori. Laudant omnia Deum, sed quae fecit Deus. Numquid in illo hymno advertistis quod avaritia laudet Deum? Laudat ibi Deum et serpens; avaritia non laudat. Omnia quippe repentia nominata ibi sunt in laude Dei: nominata sunt omnia repentia; sed non sunt ibi nominata aliqua vitia. Vitia enim ex nobis et ex nostra volúntate habemus; et vitia non sunt substantia. In his infixus est Dominus, quando persecutionem passus est; in vitio Iudaeorum, non in substantia hominum quae per illum facta est.

Infixus sum, inquit, in limo profundi, et non est substantia. Infixus sum, et non inveni quod feci. 6. Come in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me. Gratias ipsius misericordiae qui come in altitudinem maris, et glutiri a marine ceto dignitus est: sed evomitus est tertio die (Mt 12:40). Come in altitudinem maris, in qua altitudine nos depressi eramus, in qua altitudine nos naufragium passi eramus: come illuc ipse, et tempestas demersit illum; quia fluctus ibi passus est, ipsos homines; tempestates, voices digontium, Crucifige, crucifige. Dicente Pilate, Non invenio causam ullam in hoc homine quare occidendus sit, invalescebant Voices dicentium, Crucifige, crucifige (lo 19,6). Augebatur tempestas, doñee demergeretur qui venerat in altitudinem maris. Et passus est Dominus Inter manus Iudaeorum, quod non est passus eum super aquas ambularet (Mt 14:25);

He fell into the hands of the Jews. I have come to the high seas, and the storm submerged me, 7 [ v. 4]. I got tired of crying; my jaws became hoarse. Where and when did this happen? Let's ask the Gospel. In this psalm we see the passion of our Lord exposed. We certainly know that he suffered, that the waters penetrated to his soul, since we read and believe that the waters of the people prevailed until they killed him; that he was submerged in the storm, because we know that the sedition prevailed that arose to kill him; but that he became tired shouting and that his jaws became hoarse, not only do we not read it, but we read the opposite, since he did not answer them a word, so that what was said in another psalm could be fulfilled: I became like a man who does not hear and who has no reply in his mouth; and also what was prophesied by Isaiah: He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before the shearer, so he did not open his mouth. If he became like a man who neither hears nor replies, then how did he become tired shouting, and his throat hoarse? Or was he silent because he was hoarse, and then he would have cried out in vain? We do not ignore, as the psalm tells us, the voice that he gave on the cross: O God, my God, why have you abandoned me? But was this voice so loud or so prolonged that it made his throat hoarse? For a long time he cried: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees! Insistently he cried: Woe to the world for scandal! Certainly he cried out as if hoarse, and that is why they did not understand him when the Jews said: What quod non solum ipse passus non erat, sed nec Petrum pati permiserat. Come in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me. 7 [v.4]. Laboravi clamans; raucae factae sunt fauces meae. Hoc ubi? when? Interrogemus Evangelium. Passionem quippe Domini nostri in hoc psalmo cognoscimus.

Et quidem passum eum novimus; intrasse aquas usque ad animam eius, quia populi praevaluerunt usque ad raortem eius, legimus, credimus; tempestate illum demersum esse, quia praevaluit seditio ad eum occidendum, agnoscimus: verum et laborasse eum clando, et raucas factas esse fauces illius, non solum non legimus, sed etiam contra legimus, quia non responderbat eis verbum, ut impleretur quod in alio psalmo dictum est, Factus sum quasi homo non audiens, et non habens in ore suo reiargutiones (Ps 37,15); et quod in Isaia prophetatum est, Sicut ovis ad immolandum ductus est, et sicut agnus coram tondente se, sic non a-peruit os suum (Is 53,7). Si factus est sicut homo non audiens, et non habens in ore suo redargutiones, quomodo laboravit clamans, et raucae factae sunt fauces eius? An ideo iam tune tacebat, quia raucus erat, qui sine causa tantum clamaverat? Et illam quidem eius vocem de psalmo quodam in cruz novimus: Deus, Deas meas, utquid me dereliquisti? (Ps 21,2). Sed quanta illa vox Fuit, aut quam diuturna, ut in ea raucae factae essent fauces eius? Diu clamavit, Vae vobis scribae, et Pharisaei (Mt 23,13.14): diu clamavit, Vae mundo ab scandalis (Ib. 18,7). Et revera quomodo raucus clamabat, et ideo non intelügebatur, quando dicebant Iudaei: Quid est

is that what it says? This speech is hard; who can hear him? We don't know what it says. He pronounced all the words, but for them his throat was hoarse, because they did not understand their voices. I got tired of crying; my jaws became hoarse. 8. My eyes failed waiting for my God. God does not allow this to be taken from the person of the Head. Their eyes did not fail as they waited on their God, on Him in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself and on Him who, being the Word, became flesh and dwelt among us so that not only God would be in him, but that He Himself would be God. Therefore this did not happen in Him; The eyes of our Head did not fail waiting for God, but the eyes of his body, that is, of his members, failed. This voice is from the members, this voice is from the body, not from the Head. How will we find it in his body, in his members? What to say more, what to remember something else? When He suffered, when He died, all the disciples distrusted that He was the Christ. The apostles were defeated by the thief, who believed, when they fainted. He looks at his members with distrust; He sees those two, of whom one of them was Cleopas, whom after the resurrection he found on the road speaking to each other, their eyes being veiled, so they did not recognize him. How could they recognize him by the look of his body when his mind wavered? Something similar to its mind happened to the eyes of the body. They were talking among themselves, and when he asked them what they were talking about, they answered: Are you just a stranger in Jerusalem? Don't you know how Jesus the Nazarene, poquod dicit? Durus est hic sermo; quis potest illum audire? Non scimus quid dicat (lo 6,61, et 16,18). Ule omnia verba dicebat; sed illis raucae fuerunt fauces eius, qui voices eius non intelligebant. Laboravi clamans; raucae factae sunt fauces meae. 8. Defecerunt oculi mei ab sperando in Deum meum. Absit ut hoc de persona capitis accipiatur: absit ut defecerint oculi eius ab sperando in Deum eius, in quo magis Deus erat mundum reconcilians sibi (2 Cor 5,19), et qui Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,14), ut non solum Deus in illo esset, sed etiam ipse Deus esset.

Non ergo ita; non ipsius capitis nostri oculi defecerunt ab sperando in Deum eius; sed defecerunt oculi eius in corpore eius, id est in membris eius. Haec vox membrorum est, haec vox corporis est, non capitis. Quomodo ergo eam in eius corpore membrisque invenimus? Quid aliud dicam? quid aliud commemorem? Quando passus est, quando mortuus est, omnes discipuli desperaverunt quod ipse esset Christus. A latrone Apostoli victi sunt, qui tune credidit, quando illi defecerunt (Luke 23:42). Vide membra eius desperantia; attende duos illos quos post resurrectionem invenit in via colloquentes secum, quorum unus erat Cleophas, quando detinebantur oculi eorum ne eum agnoscerent. Quomodo enim oculis agnoscerent, a quo mente titubarant? Factum erat aliquid in oculis eorum simile mentís ipsorum. Loquebantur enim inter se, et eum ab eo compellarentur unde loquerentur, responderunt: Tu solus peregri-

derous in words and deeds, has he been killed by the elders and chief priests? We hoped that He would redeem Israel. They had waited, but they did not wait. Their eyes died waiting on their God. Then He was transfigured in them saying: My eyes have failed waiting for my God. But he gave them this hope when he offered to feel his scars. When they were touched by Thomas, they restored his lost hope and he exclaimed: My Lord and my God! Your eyes failed waiting for your God; you touched the scars, and found your God; you touched the form of a servant, and recognized your God. To this one, however, the Lord said: Because you saw me you believed; and, foreshadowing us with the word of his mercy, he adds: Blessed are those who do not see and believe. My eyes failed waiting on my God. 9 [v. 5]. Those who hated me without cause multiplied on the hairs of my head. They have multiplied so much that even one of the Twelve joined them. Those who hated me without cause multiplied on the hairs of my head. He compared his enemies to the hairs on his head. No wonder they were worn out when he was crucified at the place of the Skull. Let the members take this voice as their own, learn to be hated without reason. Well, if it is necessary, O Christian, for the world to hate you, why don't you make it hate you without cause, so that in the body of your Lord and in this psalm that speaks of his body you may recognize your voice? When will the world hate you for free? When you do not persecute Him, and yet you are hated for Him. This is being hated

without reason, without cause. It is little that the world hates you without cause; Offer yourself to be hated by returning evils for goods. My enemies were strengthened, and they persecuted me unjustly. What he said before: They multiplied on the hairs of my head, he repeats now when he says: My enemies are strengthened; and what he added previously: Those who hated me without cause, he now says it like this: Those who persecuted me unjustly, because without reason or without cause is the same as unjustly. This is the voice of the martyrs listening to the motive, not the punishment. For it is not glory to suffer persecution, to be arrested, scourged, imprisoned, outlawed, killed; But, when this is suffered for a good cause, it is a glory. Glory is found in the goodness of the cause, not in the acerbity of the penalty. For no matter how great the tortures of the martyrs are, can they be equal to the tortures of all thieves, of all the impious, of all criminals? Well what? Does the world also hate these? He certainly hates them. For they surpass the measure of the common malice of the world and in a certain way are alien to the very society of worldly men by disturbing earthly peace, and for this reason they suffer many evils, and not without reason. Finally, observe the voice of that thief who was hanging on the cross accompanying the Lord, who, upon seeing that the other crucified thief was also insulting the Lord, saying: If you are the Son of God, free yourself from the cross, he rebuked him, saying: You do not fear God, being, however, in the same torment as Him, despite the fact that we are, by the way, precisely due to our crimes. Vedqueno suffered without reason, but through confession he cast out the rottenness and became a saint.

naris in lerusalem? Nescis quae jacta sunt, quomodo lesus Nazarenas, potens in factis et dictis, occisus est a senioribus et principibus sacerdotum? Et nos sperabamus quod ipse erat redempturus Israel (Ib. 24, 13-21). Speraverant, et non sperabant. Defecerunt oculi eorum ab sperando in Deum ipsorum. Ipsos ergo in se transfiguravit saying: Defecerunt oculi mei ab sperando in Deum meum. Hanc spem reddidit, quando palpanda scars obtulit; quas cum tetigisset Thomas, rediit ad spem quam perdiderat, et exclamavit: Dominus meus, et Deus meus. Defecerunt oculi tui ab sperando in Deum tuum: palpasti scars, et invenisti Deum tuum; palpasti formam servi, et cognovisti Dominum tuum. Cui tamen ipse Dominus ait: Quia vidisti credidisti. Et nos praenuntians voce misericordiae suae: Beati, inquit, qui non vident et credunt (lo 20„28.29). 26,14). oderit, ut in corpore Domini tui, et in hoc psalmo de illo praemisso agnoscas vocem tuam? Quomodo fiet ut oderit te mundus gratis?

habearis: hoc est enim gratis, sine causa. Parum sit tibi sine causa odio haberi, insuper et praesta, ut retribuant tibi mala pro bonis. Confortati sunt inimici mei, qui persequuntur me iniuste. Quod dixit, Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei; hoc postea, Confortati sunt inimici mei: et quod primo, qui oderunt me gratis; hoc postea, qui persequuntur me iniuste. Quod ergo gratis, hoc est iniuste. Ipsa est vox martyrum, non in poena, sed in causa. Non persecutionem pati, non teneri, non flagellari, non includi, non proscrib, non occidi laus est; sed habendo causam bonam, ista pati, haec laus est. Laus enim est in causae bonitote, non in poenae acerbitate. Nam quantacumque fuerint supplicia martyrum, numquid aequantur suppliciis omnium latronum, omnium sacrilegorum, omnium sceleratorum? Quid enim, et hos odit mundus? Odit plane. Excedunt enim mundi medietatem amplítudine malitiae, et ab ipsa mundanorum quodammodo hominum societate alieni sunt, infestantes pacem etiam terrenam; et patiuntur fine bad, sed non gratis. Denique vide vocem illius latronis cum Domino in cruz pendentis, cum insultaret ex alia parte unus duorum latronum Domino crucifixo, et diceret, Si Filius Dei es, liberate te: compescuit illum alter, et dixit, Tu non times Deum, vel quia in eadem damnatione positus es? Et nos quidem recte pro factis nostris (Luke 23:39-41). Ecce non gratis: sed confessione effudit ex se saniem, et factus est aptus cibo Domini. Exclusit iniquitatem suam, ac-

peace of the food of the Lord. He cast away his iniquity; He manifested it and found himself free from it. Here are the two thieves; The Lord was also there; they were crucified; also the Lord. The world hated them, but not without reason; He also hated Christ, but without cause: What I did not steal I paid back then. This is the same as free. I did not steal, and I paid; I did not sin, and they tormented me. Only He was like that; He certainly stole nothing. Not only did he not steal, but what he had without having stolen, he nullified in himself to approach us: For he did not consider it a shame to be equal with God, and yet he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. He stole nothing at all. Who stole then? Adam. Who stole first? The one who seduced Adam. How did the devil steal? I will set my throne toward the north and I will be equal to the Most High. He stole what he had not received: see the plunder. The devil usurped what he had not received and lost what he received; and he gave drink from the same cup of his pride to the one who wanted to deceive. Taste, he says, and you will be like gods. They wanted to steal divinity and lost happiness. That one stole and that's why this one pays: I, he says, paid for what I didn't steal. The Lord himself, approaching the passion, speaks in this way in the Gospel: Behold, the prince of this world is coming, that is, the devil, and he will find nothing in me, that is, he will find no cause of death in me; But so that you all know that I do my Father's will, get up and let's get out of here; and he went to passion, to pay for what he had not stolen. What does it mean and will you find nothing in me? No fault. Did the devil lose something from his house? Reveal Christ to the captors: He will find nothing in me. He says that cusavit eam, et caruit ea. Ecce ibi duo latrones, ibi et Dominus; et illi crucifixi, et ille crucifixus: et illos odio habuit mundus, sed non gratis; et illum odio habuit, thirst gratis. Quae non rapui, tune exsolvebam. Hoc is free. Non rapui, et exsolvebam; non peccavi, et poenas ibam. Solus enim ipse talis, ipse veré nihil rapuit. Non solum nihil rapuit, sed etiam quod non de rapiña habebat, hoc se evacuavit, ut ad nos vinoet. Non enim rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo; et tamen semetipsum exinanivit, formam serví accipiens (Phil 2,6.7). Omnino non rapuit. Sed quis rapuit? Adam. Quis rapuit cousin? lile ipse qui seduxit Adam.

Quomodo rapuit diabolus? Ponam sedem meam ad aquilonem, et ero similis Altissimo (Is 14:13). Usurpavit sibi quod non acceperat: ecce rapinam. Usurpavit sibi diabolus quod non acceperat, perdidit quod acceperat; et de ipso calice superbiae suae, ei quem decipere volebat propinavif. Taste, inquit, et eritis sicut dii (Gen 3:5). Rápete voluerutu divinitatem, perdiderunt congratulatem. Ule ergo rapuit, et ideo exsolvit. Ego autem, inquit, quae non rapui, tune exsolvebam. Ipse Dominus propinquans passioni, in Evangelio sic loquitur: Ecce venit princeps huius mundi, id est diabolus, et in me nihil inveniet, id est, quare me occidat non inveniet; sed ut sciant omnes quia voluntatem Patris mei jacio, surgite, eamus (lo 14,30): et iit ad passionem, solvere quod non rapuit. Quid est enim, in me nihil inveniet? Nullam culpam. An aliquid lost

He has stolen nothing in response to sin; He took nothing that was not his; The opposite is typical of plunder, of iniquity. They snatched, yes, to the devil those he had robbed. No one—he says—enters the strong man's house and takes his belongings if he has not first tied up the strong man. He tied up the fort and took his belongings, but he did not steal them, because he answers you: These belongings had disappeared from my great palace; I did not commit theft; I undid him. 10 [v. 6]. Lord, you knew my foolishness. Again he speaks on behalf of the body. For what foolishness is there in Christ? Is He not the strength and wisdom of God? Or does he speak of that need of his, of which the Apostle says: The foolishness of God is wiser than men? You knew my foolishness, that is, this for which those who seemed to be wise mocked me. You knew why it happened: You knew my foolishness. For what is more akin to foolishness than, being in his power to destroy his persecutors with a single word, he nevertheless allows them to seize him, whip him, spit on him, slap him, crown him with thorns and nail him to the cross? This is similar to foolishness; It seems like a foolish thing, but the foolishness of God is wiser than all the wise. Apparently it is a foolish thing, if anyone ignores the common actions of the farmer, to throw grain on the ground. Furthermore, it is mowed with great labor, transported to the threshing floor, threshed, and forked. However, after innumerable dangers from the sky and storms, after so much work on the part of the peasants and so much care on the part of the owners, the clean wheat is put into the granary. Winter comes, and what was clean is taken out of the barn and thrown away; It seems foolish, but the espede domo sua diabolus? Iste discusses kidnappers; nihil apud me inveniet. Tamen nihil rapuisse se dicit, peccatum attendens, nihil usurpasse quod eius non esset; hoc est enim rapinae, hoc iniquitatis: nam ab ipso diabolo extorsit quos ipse rapuerat. fiemo, inquit, in domum fortis intrat, et vasa eius diripit, nisi prius alligaverit fortem (Mt 12:29). Alligavit fortem, et vasa eius diripuit, certe non rapuit; sed respondert tibi: Vasa ista de domo magna mea perierant; non furtum feci, sed furtum recepi. 10 [v.6]. Deus tu scisti imprudentiam meam. Iterum ex ore corporis. Nam quae imprudentia in Christo?

Nonne ipse est Dei Virtus et Dei Sapientia? An illam dicit imprudentiam suam, de qua dicit Apostolus: Stultum Dei sapientius est bominibus? (1 Cor 1:25). Imprudentiam meam: hoc ipsum quod in me irriserunt qui sibi videntur esse sapientes. Tu scisti quare ieront: tu scisti imprudentiam meam. Quid enim tam simile imprudentiae, quam cum haberet in potestate, una voce suos persecutors prosternere, ut pateretur se teneri, flagellari, conspui, colaphizari, spinis coronari, ligno affigi? Imprudentiae simile est; stultum videtur: sed stultum hoc overcome omnes sapientes. Stultum quidem est: sed et granum quando cadit in terram, si nemo sciat consuetudinem agricolarum, stultum videtur. Labore magno metitur, portatur ad aream, tumbatur, ventilatur: post tanta pericula caeli et tempestatum, et labores rustícanorum curamque dominorum, mittitur in horreum frumentum purgatum.

ranza makes it no such thing. Then he did not forgive himself, because the Father did not forgive him, but handed him over for us all. The Apostle also says of Him: He loved me and gave himself for me, because the grain, unless it falls to the ground and dies, does not bear fruit. This is foolishness; but you know her. If the Jews had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory. O God, you knew my foolishness, and my crimes are not hidden from you. This is clearly understood and without a doubt by the members, since Christ had no sin; He bore the sin, but did not commit it. And my crimes are not hidden from you, that is, I manifested all my sins to you and before seeing them in my mouth you saw them in my thoughts; You saw the wounds that you had to heal. But where? Certainly in the body, in the members, in those faithful to whom that member who confessed his sins was attached. And my crimes—he says—are not hidden from you. 11 [v.7]. Let not those who hope in you be ashamed for my sake, O Lord, Lord of hosts! The head speaks again. Do not be ashamed for me, do not be told: Where is he in whom you trusted? Let it not be said to them: Where is he who said to you: Believe in God, and believe also in me? Let not those who hope for you be ashamed of me, O Lord, Lord of hosts! Let not those who seek you be troubled by me, O God of Israel! This can also be understood as being said by the body, but if you do not take his body for one man, because his body does not Venit hiems; et quod purgatum erat, profertur et proiicitur: imprudentia videtur; sed ut non sit imprudentia, spes facit. Non ergo ille pepercit sibi; quia et Pater illi non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit illum (Rom 8:32). Et de ipso, Qui dilexit me, inquit Apostolus, et tradidit seipsum pro me (Gal 2,20): quia granum, nisi ceciderit in terram ut moriatur, jructum, inquit, non reddet (lo 12,24.25). Haec is reckless; sed tu nosti illam: isti autem si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent (1 Cor 2:8). Deus, tu scisti imprudentiam meam; et delicia mea a te non sunt abscondita, Hoc plane, lucide, aperte, quia ex ore corporis intelligendum est. Delicta nulla Christus habuit; Fuit delictorum susceptor, sed non commissor. Et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita: id est, confessus sum tibi omnia delicta mea; et ante os meum vidisti ea in cogitatione mea, vidisti vulnera quae sanares. Are you located?

Utíque in corpore, in membris; in illis fidelibus, unde illi haerebat iam membrum illud quod confitebatur peccata sua. Et delicta, inquit, mea a te non sunt abscondita. 11 [v.7]. Non erubescant in me, q_ui te exspectant, Domine, Domine virtutum. Rursus vox capitis, Non erubescant in me: non dicatur illis, Ubi est de quo praesumebatis? non dicatur illis, Ubi est qui vobis dicebat, Credite in Deum, et in me credite? (14.1). Non erubescant in me, qui te exspectant, Domine, Domine virtutum. Non confundantur super me, qui quaerunt te, Deus Israel. Potest hoc et a corpore intelligi, sed si Corpus eius non unum hominem ponas: quia revera non est unus
Prayer of the vexed people

He is a small member, a single man. His body consists of members. His entire or total body is the entire Church. No wonder the Church says: Let not those who hope in you be ashamed of me, O Lord, Lord of hosts! May I not be afflicted in this way by the persecutors who rise up against me; May it not be trampled in this way by my envious enemies, by the heretical murmurers who departed from me, because they were not mine, since, if they had been mine, they would have, without a doubt, remained with me; May it not be brought down in this way by scandals, so that those who hope in you may be ashamed for my sake, O Lord, Lord of hosts! Let not those who seek you be troubled by me, O God of Israel! 12 [v.8]. For you I endured the affront; Shame covered my face. It is not an extraordinary thing to say I endured, but to say I endured for you. If you endure because you sinned, you endure for yourself, not for God. For what glory, says Saint Peter, is yours, if by sinning you are punished and endure it? But if you endure (reproaches) for having observed the commandment of God, you certainly endure them for God's sake, and your reward will endure forever, because you endured reproaches for God. First He endured them, so that we might learn to endure them. And if the one who had nothing to blame him for endured them, how much more must we endure them, since, if we have no sin of which the enemy accuses us, yet we have another that is justly punished in us? Some individual calls you a thief, and you are not a thief; you hear the affront; But if, nevertheless, you are not a thief, you are not such that you do not have something that displeases God. Therefore, if That homo corpus eius, sed exiguum membrum; Corpus autem ex membris constat. Corpus ergo eius plenum, all Ecclesia. Merit ergo dicit Ecclesia: Non erubescant in me, qui te exspectant, Domine, Domine virtutum. Non sic affligar ab insurgentibus persecutoribus, non sic obterar ab invidentibus inimicis meis, ab oblatrantibus haereticis qui a me exierunt, quia non erant ex me; nam si fuessent ex me, mecum forsitan permansissent (1 lo 2,19). Non sic eorum scandalis premar, ut erubescant in me qui te exspectant, Domine, Domine virtutum. Non confundantur super me, qui quaerunt te, Deus Israel. 12 [v.8]. Quoniam propter te sustinui exprobrationem, operuit irreverentia faciem meam. Nihil magnum est quod dicitur, sustinui; sed quod dicitur, propter te sustinui.

Si enim sustines, quia peccasti; propter te sustines, non propter Deum. Quae enim vobis gloria est, ait Petrus, si peccantes punimini, et suffertis? (1 Petr 2:20). Si autem sustines quia mandatum Dei servasti, I will see propter Deum sustines; et merces tua manet in aeternum, quia propter Deum sustinuisti opprobria. Ideo enim prior ille sustinuit, ut nos sustinere disceremus. Et si ille, qui non habebat quod illi obiiciebatur; quanto magis nos qui, etsi non habemus peccatum quod nobis obiicit inimicus, habemus tamen alterum quod digne in nobis flagelletur? Nescio quis te furem dicit, et non es fut: audis opprobrium; non tamen sic non es fur, ut non sis aliquid quod Deo displicet. Porro S.Ag. 20

who had stolen nothing at all and who with all truth said: Behold, the prince of this world comes, and will find nothing in me, he was called a sinner, wicked, Beelzebub, perverse, will you, slave, bring to evil hearing, according to your merits, what the Lord heard without deserving it? He came to be your model. Almost as if without cause I would have done this if you didn't take advantage. Why did he hear it? So that when you hear it you do not faint. You hear it, and your heart falls to your feet; In vain, therefore, did He hear it, since He did not hear it for Himself, but for you. For you I endured the affront; shamelessness covered my face. Shamelessness—he says—covered my face. What is shamelessness? Don't get confused. In short, it seems like an outrage to say: The man is irreverent, shameless, he has no respect. The great irreverence or shamelessness of man is not to be ashamed. Therefore irreverence is like impudence. It is appropriate for the Christian to have this impudence when he finds himself among men who dislike Christ. If he is ashamed of Christ, he will be blotted out of the book of the living. It is necessary that you do not feel this confusion when you are insulted for Christ; when you are told: You worship the crucified, you worship an evil dead, you worship a slain, if you are ashamed then, you are dead. Heed the sentence of the one who deceives no one: Whoever is ashamed of me before men, I will also be ashamed of him before the angels of God. Then you should ensure that there is impudence in you, do not be ashamed when you hear an insult for Christ; Don't be confused by anything. What do you fear for your forehead, you did not arm it with the sign of the cross. In this, then, consists for you I endured the affront; la dessi ille qui omnino nihil rapuerat, qui verissime dixerat, Ecce venit princeps mundi huius, et in me nihil inveniet, dictus est peccatoi (lo 9,24), dictus est iniquus, dictus est Beelzebub (Mt 10,25), dictus est insanus; tu dedignaris, serve, audire pro meritis tuis, quod Dominus audivit nullis meritis suis? Ule venit ut tibi praeberet exemplum. Quasi gratis hoc fecerit, sic tu non proficis. Quare enim ille audivit, nisi ut tu cum audires non deficeres? Ecce tu audis, et deficis: frustra ergo ille audivit; non enim propter se, sed propter te audivit. Quoniam proper te sustinui exprobrationem, operuit irreverentia faciem meam. Irreverentta, inquit, operuit faciem meam. Irreverentia what is it? I didn't confuse. Denique quasi vitium videtur, cum dicitur: Irreverens homo est. Magna irreverentia hominis, non illum erubescere.

Ergo irreverentia quasi impudentia est. Oportet ut habeat christianus irreverentiam istam, quando venerit inter nomines quibus displicet Christus. Si erubuerit de Christo, delebitur de libro vivostium. Opus est ergo ut habeas irreverentiam, quando tibi de Christo insultatur; quando dicitur, Cultor crucifixi, adotator male mortui, venerator occisi: hic si erubueris, mortuus es. Shame covered my face. For you I endured the insult, and since I was not ashamed of you when I was insulted for you, shamelessness covered my face. 13 [v.9-10]. I became a stranger to my brothers, and a stranger to my mother's children. I have become a stranger to the children of the synagogue. Well, in his country it was said about him: Don't we know that he is the son of Mary and Joseph? And hence it is said in another place: We don't know where this one is from. Then I have become a stranger to my mother's children. They didn't know where I was from, who my meat came from. They did not know me as born of the seed of Abraham; hence my flesh trembled when the servant, placing his hand under the same thigh, swore by the God of heaven. I have become a stranger to my mother's children. And why this? Why didn't they know him? Why did they call him a foreigner? Why did they dare to say: We don't know where he is from? Because the zeal of your house devoured me, that is, because I pursued their iniquities, because I did not patiently endure those I corrected, because in your house I pursued your glory, because I punished the money changers and traffickers in the temple. For this reason it was written: Zeal for your house devours me. This is why he is strange, this is why he is a stranger, this is why we don't know where he is from. They would have known where he was from if they had known what you ordered. If I had found that they observed your commandments, the zeal of your house would not have devoured me. And the insults of those who insult you fell on me. The apostle Saint Paul also used this testimony; It has been read a little; It goes like this: What was previously written was written for our teaching, a rentia faciem meam. Propter te sustinui exprobrationem: et quia non de te erubui, quando mihi propter te insultabatur, operuit irreverentia faciem meam. 13 [v.9-10]. Alienatus factus sum fratribus meis, et bospes filiis matris meae. Filiis Synagogae hospes factus est. In patria quippe ipsius dicebatur: Nonne nos scimus eum esse filium Mariae et loseph? (Luke 4:22). Et unde alio loco: Hunc autem nescimus unde sit? (9.29). Factus ergo sum hospes filiis matris meae. Non scierunt unde sim, de quibus erat caro mea: non me sciebant de femore Abraham natum; unde caro mea oceulta erat, quando sub ipso femore manum servus ponens, iuravit per Deum caeli (Gen 24,9). Hospes factus sum filiis matris meae. Quare hoc? quare non agnoverunt? quare alienum dixerunt? quare ausi sunt dicere: Nescimus unde sit?

Quoniam zelus domus tuae comedit me: id est, quia persecutus sum in lilis iniquitates ipsorum, quia non patienter tuli quos corripui, quia quaesivi gloriam tuam in domo tua, quia flagellavi in Templo male versantes (lo 2,15); ubi etiam positum est, Zelus domus tuae comedit me. "Assaultants, of whom it is said in another psalm: Let not those who provoke God exalt themselves." Then I afflicted my soul with fasting, and it became a reproach to me. It became a disgrace to me not to agree with them, that is, to abstain from them. He who does not consent to those who persuade evil, abstains from them, and for this fast deserves insult; so that he is insulted, because he does not consent to evil. 15 [v. 12]. And I put on sackcloth. We have already spoken something about the hair shirt; hence that of Psalm 34: But I, when they troubled me, put on sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting. And I put on sackcloth, that is, I offered them my flesh, in which they were angry, and I hid my divinity from them. I offered them the sackcloth, which was mortal flesh, so that by the likeness of sin they might condemn sin in the flesh. And I put on sackcloth, and I was for them "in parabolam" (a fable), that is, a ridicule. The saying that expresses the similarity of something if it is spoken of badly is called a parable (fable). For example: Perish like that one. This is a parable, that is, a comparison and likeness of outrage or cursing. Then I was a fable for them. 16 [v. 13]. Those who sat at the door insulted me. At the door, that is, in public. And those who drank wine saluted against me. Do you think, brothers, that this happened only to Christ? This happens to its members every day. When perhaps it is necessary for the servant of God to prohibit drunkenness and dishonesty in some small village where the paamaricantes has not been heard, de quibus alio loco psalmus dicit: Qui amaricant, non exaltentur in semetipsis (Ps 65,7). Ergo, operui in ieiunio animam meam; et factum est mihi in opprobrium. Hoc ipsum mihi in opprobrium factum est, quia non illis consensi, hoc est, ab illis ieiunavi. Qui enim non consentit male suadentibus, ieiunat ab ipsis; et per hoc ieiunium meretur opprobrium, ut ideo illi insultetur, quia non consentit ad malum. 15 [v.12]. Ut posui vestimentum meum saccum. Iam et de sacco aliquid diximus, unde illud est, Ego autem eum mihi molesti essent, induebam me cilicio, et humiliabam in ieiunio animam meam. Posui vestimentum meum saccum: id est, opposui illis, in quam saevirent, carnem meam; occultavi divinitatem meam.

Saccum, quia mortalis caro erat, ut de peccato condemnaret peccatum in catne (Rom 8:3). Et posui vestimentum meum saccum; et factus sum illis in parabolam; id est in irrisionem. Parable dicitut, when datut similarity of aliquo, when of illo male dicitur. Sic Ule, verbi grada, pereat quomodo Ule, parabola est; id is compared et similarity maledicti. Factus ergo sum illis in parabolam. 16 [v.13]. Adversus me insultabant qui sedebant in porta. In porta, mhil aliud quam in publico. And in me psallebant qui bibebant vinum. Putatis hoc, frattes, Christo tantummodo contigisse? Quotidie illi in members eius contingit: quando forte necesse erit servo Dei prohibite ebrietates et luxurias in aliquo vel fundo vel oppido, ubi non auditum fuetit

In front of you praying. In the abundance of your mercy. This is the acceptable time or grace, in the abundance of your mercy. If it were not for the abundance of your mercy, what would we do with the multitude of our iniquities? In the abundance of your mercy. Hear me according to the truth of your health. As he mentioned mercy, now he adds truth, because mercy and truth are all the ways of the Lord. How mercy? Forgiving sins. How true? Giving what was promised. Hear me according to the truth of your health. 18 [v.15]. Get me out of the mud so I don't get bogged down. Ego autem ad te eram. Are you comfortable? Ad you praying. Quando enim malediceris, et quid agas non habes; quando tibí actantur opprobria, et quomodo corrigas eum a quo actantur non invenis, nihil tibi restat nisi orare. Be memento et pro ipso orare. Ego autem oratione mea ad te, Domine. Tempus beneplaciti, Deus. Ecce enim sepelitur granum; exsurget fructus. Tempus beneplaciti, Deus. De hoc tempore et Prophetae said quod commemorat Apostolus: Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis (2 Cor 6,2). tempus beneplaciti, Deus. In multitudine misericordiae tuae. Nam si non esset multitudo misericordiae tuae, quid nos faceremus de multitudine iniquitatis nostrae? In multitudine misericordiae tuae. Exaudi me in veritate salutis tuae. Quia dixit, misericordiae tuae, subiunxit et veritatem; quia mercy et veritas universae viae Domini (Ps 24:10). Quare mercy? Dimittendo peccata. Quare veritas? Reddendo promissa. Exaudi me in veritate salutis tuae. 18 [v.15]. Salvum me jac de luto, ut non inhaeream. De illo de quo supra dixerat: infixus sum in limo profundi, et non est substantia.

from the deep, and there is no substance or consistency. Therefore, since this has already been explained and you understood it well, there is no need to explain what you heard again. Here it says that he must be freed from where he previously said he was stuck. Get me out of the mud so I don't get bogged down. He himself explains this, saying: I will be taken out of those who hated me. Therefore these are the mud in which he was stuck. Perhaps this suggests a doubt. Shortly before he had said: I am bogged down; Now he says: Take me out of the mud so that I don't get stuck, whereas, in accordance with the previous sentence, he should say: Deliver me, by taking me out, from the mud in which I got stuck, without preventing me from getting stuck. Therefore he was troubled in the flesh, not in the spirit. He says this taking into account the weakness of the members. When you are seized by him who forces you to commit iniquity, your body is indeed chained. As for the body, you are mired in the mud of the deep; but as long as you don't consent, you don't get bogged down. If you consent, you get bogged down. Therefore your prayer in these circumstances must consist of asking that your soul not be chained, as your body already is. Be free in the midst of bondage. Let him be brought out from those who hated me and from the depths of the waters. 19 [v.16]. Do not submerge me in the storm of water. I was already submerged, for you said: I have reached the high sea, and you added: and the storm submerged me. He immersed him as to the meat; but now he asks that I not immerse him in the spirit. To those who were told: If you are persecuted in one city, flee to another, this was said so that they would not be bogged down either in the flesh or in the spirit. Well, we should not want to get bogged down in Proinde quia illud expositum bene accepistis, quod hic auditatis expressius non est. Hinc se dicit liberandum, ubi se ante dixit infixum: Salvum me jac de luto, ut non inhaeream. Et exponit hoc ipse: Eruar ex iis qui oderunt me. Ipsi ergo sunt lutum ubi haeseram. Sed hoc strong suggestion. Paulo ante dixerat, Infixus sum; moda dicit, Salvum me fac de luto, ut non inhaeream; cum secundum sententiam priorem debenet dicere: Salvum me fac de luto ubi haeseram, eruendo me, non agendo ut non inhaeream. Ergo haeserat flesh, sed non haeserat spiritu. Dicit hoc ex infirmitate membrorum suorum. Quando forte caperis ab eo qui te premit ad iniquitatem, tenetut quidem corpus tuum; secundum Corpus infixus is in limo profundi: sed quamdiu non consentís, non haesisti; If you consent, haesisti.

Oratio ergo tua ibi sit, ut quomodo iam tenetur corpus tuum, non teneatur et anima tua, sis liber in vinculis. Eruar ex bis qui oderunt me, et de profound aquarum. 19 [v.16]. No» me demergat tempestas aquae. Sed iam demersus erat. Come in altitudinem maris, tu dixisti; et tempestas demersit me, tu dixisti. Demersit secundum carnem, non demergat secundum spiritum. Quibus dictum est, If you persecute fuerint in a civitate, fugite in aliam (Mt 10,23); hoc eis dictum est, ut nec carne haererent, nec spititu. regarding meat, but, as far as we can, we should avoid it. But, if we had become bogged down by falling into the hands of sinners, we are already bogged down in terms of the body, we are already bogged down in the mud of the deep; Therefore, we only have to pray for our soul so that we do not get bogged down, that is, so that we do not consent. Let the storm of water not submerge us, so that we do not go into the depths of the mud. Neither the abyss swallow me nor the pit close its mouth over me. What is this, brothers? What are you praying for? Great is the pit and depth of human iniquity; If anyone has fallen there, he falls into the abyss. But, nevertheless, he is there in such a way that, if he confesses his sins to God, the pit does not close his mouth over him, as it was written in another psalm: From the depths I cried to you, O Lord!; Lord, hear my prayer. If, on the contrary, he executes what Scripture states in another passage: The sinner pays no attention to anything when he has reached the depths of evil, then he closes the pit with his mouth. Why are you closing your mouth? Because the sinner closed his first. He despised the confession; died; What is said elsewhere was fulfilled in him: The confession of the dead perishes as nothing. Brothers, this is to be greatly feared. If you see a man who has committed iniquity, he is submerged in the pit; But if, when manifesting it to him, he said to you: I confess; I have sinned, then the pit has not closed its mouth on him. If he says to you: What evil have I done?, when he defends his sin, the pit closes its mouth on him, and he will have no way to draw him out. Confession spurned, there will be no room for mercy. If you possumus, vitare debenmus. Si vero haeserimus, et in manus peccatorum venerimus, iam corpore haesimus; fixi sumus in limo profundi: restat pro anima deprecan ut non inhaereamus, id est non consentiamus; non nos demergat tempestas aquae, ut eamus in profundum limi. Ñeque absorbat me profundum, ñeque coarctet super me puleus os suum. Quid est hoc, brothers? what deprecatus is this? Magnus est puteus profunditas iniquitatis humanoe: illuc quisque si ceciderit, in altum cadet. Sed tamen ibi positus, si confitetur peccata Deo suo, non super eum claudet puteus os suum: ut est in alio quodam psalmo scriptum, De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine; Domine, exaudi vocem mea-m (Ps 129,1.2).

Si autem factum in illo fuerit quod alia sententia Scripturae dicit, Veccator, cum venerit in profundum malorum, contemnet (Prov 18,3); clausit super eum puteus os suum. Quare clausit os suum? Quia clausit os illius. Perdidit enim confessionem; I will see mortuus est, impletumque in eo est quod alibi dicitur: A mortuo, velut qui non sit, perit confessio (Eccli 17,26). Metuenda is res vehementer, fratres. Si videris hominem fecisse iniquitatem, mersus est in puteum: quando autem illi dixeris iniquitatem ipsius, et dixerit, Veré peccavi, fateor; non super eum clausit puteus os suum: cum autem videris eum dicere, Quid enim mali feci? factus est defender peccati sui; Clausit super eum puteus os suum, qua eruatur non habet. I [v. 17]. Today I have to expose the last part of the psalm that I told you about yesterday. I see that it is time to pay what is due, if prolixity does not also leave us debtors today. Therefore, I warn you and ask you not to expect a prolonged extension of things that are evident. This way we will be able to stop at the points that need requires, and hopefully we will be able to complete what is missing so that on other days we will be debtors for other things and we will equally pay for them! Let's see the things that follow. After having said: Nor let the pit close its mouth over me, our Lord Jesus Christ continues, head and body, crying out in the midst of suffering. Yesterday I reminded your charity of the verse: Nor let the pit close its mouth over me, so that with all our efforts and with the piety of faith we may avoid this curse from coming upon us, for then the pit closes its mouth on man, that is, the depth of iniquity, when man not only lies already immersed in sin, but also when the access or entrance to confession is blocked. man says: I am a sinner, the depth of the well is illuminated by some ray of light. I also reminded you that in certain places you should know that these are the words of the Head that are recorded in this psalm; But those that are said in such a way that they cannot agree with the Head, you must refer to the body. For Christ speaks as if He were one, and truly He is, of whom it is said: There shall be two in one flesh. If they are one flesh, why do you wonder that they are one voice? Now he continues: Hear me, O Lord, for your mercy is kind. Give the reason why he should be heard: because his mercy is benign. But was it not more reasonable for me to say: Hear me, O Lord, so that your mercy may be kind to me? Then why does he say: Hear me, O Lord! - for your mercy is kind? In other words he recommended the kindness of the Lord's mercy coming from his tribulation when he said: Hear me, O Lord, for I am tormented. In truth, he who says: Hear me, O Lord, for I am tormented, gives the reason why he prays to be heard; But for man placed in tribulation it is necessary that God's mercy be benign. Regarding this kindness of God's mercy, hear what Scripture says elsewhere: As rain in drought, so is God's mercy in tribulation. What he calls precious there, he calls benign here. Bread is not pleasant if it does not precede hunger. Therefore, when God allows or causes us to be in some tribulation, even then he is merciful, since he does not deprive us of food, but rather excites desire in us. So what

He says now when exclaiming: Hear me, O Lord! Why is your mercy kind? Do not hesitate to hear me; I am in such tribulation, that your mercy is benign to me. You wanted to help me so that your help would be sweet to me; There is no reason for you to delay your help. My tribulation has reached a certain measure of misfortune; Your mercy comes to execute the work of kindness. Hear me, O Lord, for your mercy is kind. Look upon me according to the multitude of your mercies, not according to the multitude of my sins. 2 [v.18]. Do not turn your face from your child. It is a recommendation of humility to say about your child, that is, your little one, because I no longer have pride due to the exercise of tribulation. Do not turn your face away from your child: this is that precious mercy of God of which he spoke before. For in the next verse he declares what he said: Because I am troubled, hear me quickly. What do you mean by promptly? That you have no reason to defer your help. I am troubled; my affliction has preceded, your mercy follows. 3 [v.19]- Take care of my soul and rescue it: this needs no explanation. Let's see what follows: Because of my enemies, deliver me: this is a request worthy of admiration, of being treated at length and of not skipping over it hastily, but rather of explaining it carefully. Because of my enemies, deliver me. What does it mean because of my enemies, deliver me? So that they may be confused, so that they may be tormented by my deliverance. So what? If there were not those who should be tormented by my liberation-

radiatur aliquo lumine etiam profunditas putei. Sequitur ergo, Inter passiones exclamans Dominus noster Iesus Christus, caput et Corpus; sicut commendavimus, ut quibusdam locis, capitis verba cognoscatis; quae autem dicta fuerint ita ut capiti converté non possint, ad Corpus referatis. Sic enim ioquitur Christus tanquam unus; quia et veré umis de quo dictum est: Erunt duo in carne una (Eph 5,31). If enim in carne una, quid miras quia et in voce una? Sequitur ergo, Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam suavis est misericordia tua. Hanc causam asseruit quare debeat exaudiri, quia suavis est mercy Dei. Nonne magis hoc erat consequens ut diceret, Exaudí me, Domine, ut suavis mihi sit misericordia tua? Quare ergo, Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam suavis est misericordia tua. Suavitatem misericordiae Domini de tribulatione sua commendavit alus quodammodo verbis, cum dixit: Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam tribulor. Revera enim qui dicit, Exaudiri me, Domine, quoniam tribulor, causam dicit quare se exaudiri roget: sed homini in tribulatione pósito, necesse est ut suavis sit misericordia Dei. De hac suavitate misericordiae Dei videte quid alio loco Scriptura dicat: Sicut pluvia in siccitate, ita speciosa est misericordia Dei in tribulatione (Eccli 35,26). Quod ibi ait, speciosa; hoc ait hic, suavis. Nec pañis dulcís esset, nisi fames praecederet. Ergo et quando Dominus permittit aut facit ut in tribulatione aliqua simus, etiam tune misericors est; non enim alimentum subtrahit, sed desiderium movet. Itaque quid ait mode: Exaudi

me, Domine, quoniam suavis est thy mercy? Iam noli differre exauditionem; in tanta tribulatione sum, ut suavis mihi sit misericordia tua. Ad hoc ergo subvenire differebas, ut mihi dulce esset quod subveniebas: iam ergo ultra non est quod differebas; pervenit tribulatio mea ad mensuram certam calamitatis, veniat misericordia tua ad faciendum opus bonitotis. Exaudí me, Domine, quoniam suavis est Misericordia tua. Secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum réspice in me: non secundum multitudinem peccatorum meorum. 2 {v.18]. Ne averías faciem tuam a puero tuo. Et haec humilitatis commendatio est, a puero tuo, id est a parvo; quia iam carui superbia per disciplinam tribulationis: Ne averías faciem tuam a puero tuo. Haec est illa speciosa misericordia Dei quam supra dixit. Nam sequenti versu exponit quod dixit: Quoniam tribudor, velociter exaudí me. What is it, velociter? Iam non est quod differas: tribulor; praecessit afflictio mea, sequatur misericordia tua. 3 [v.19]. Intende animae meae, et redeeme eam. Non indiget expositione: videoamus ergo quod sequitur. Propter inimicos meos erue me. Haec plane miranda petitio est, nec breviter perstringenda, nec cursim transilienda; prorsus miranda: Propter inimicos meos erue me. Quid est, Propter inimicos meos erue me? Ut confundantur, ut crucientur liberatione mea. Quid ergo, si non essent illi qui liberatione mea essent cruciandi, mihi subvenid non debuit? et tune tibi acceptabilis est libera-

tion, should I not help myself, and only then would liberation be acceptable to you when the condemnation of another occurs? Suppose there are no enemies who should be confused or tormented by your deliverance; So would you stay like this? Would you not be delivered? Or was it written to serve your enemies so that they too may be converted for your liberation? But it is to be admired that this contains a reason for supplication. Is the servant of God delivered by his God and Lord in order to profit others? So what would happen if there were no one to benefit from? Should not then the servant of God be delivered? Wherever I turn, now to punishment, now to deliverance from enemies, I see no reason for this supplication: Because of my enemies, deliver me; unless we understand something else; which, when I have to say it with the Lord helping me, He Himself, who dwells in you, will dictate it in you. There is a certain hidden liberation of the saints, and this is carried out for their sake. And there is another public and manifest one; This is carried out in attention of its enemies, either to punish them or to free them. Thus, God did not free the Maccabean brothers from the torture and fire of the persecutors, with whom King Antiochus, being cruel, wanted to take advantage of their mother's love so that, flattering them to preserve their lives, they would give up their purpose and, preferring to live for men, die for God. But that mother, who was no longer similar to Eve, but to Mother Church, whom she had given birth to in pain, with joy saw them die in order to see them alive; and therefore he exhorted them to choose rather to die for the fatherly laws of the Lord, their God, than to live in breaking them. What are we to judge here, brothers, but that they were tatio, cum fuerit alterius damnatio? Ecce non sunt inimici, qui vel confundantur, vel torqueantur de liberatione tua: sic remanebis? will you not liberate? An ad hoc ut valeat inimicis mis, quo possint et ipsi tua liberatione convertedi? Sed et hoc mirum est, si habeat aliquam petitionis causam. Numquid enim ad hoc liberatur servus Dei a Domino Deo suo, ut alii proficiant? Quid, si deessent qui proficerent, ille servus Dei non erat liberandus? Quocumque ergo me convertam, sive ad punitionem, sive ad liberationem inimicorum, non video causam petitionis huius, Propter inimicos meos erue me: nisi aliquid intelligamus, quod cum dixero adiuvante Domino, iudicabit in vobis qui habitat in vobis.

Est quaedam liberatio sanctorum occulta: haec propter ipsos fit. Est quaedam publica et manifesta: haec propter inimicos eorum fit; sive punishing, sive liberating. Nam utique Deus de ignibus persecutoris non liberavit fratres Machabaeos, quibus Antiochus saeviens etiam matrem adhibuit, cuius blanditiis ad amorem vitae converterentur, et amando vivere hominibus, Deo morerentur. At illa mater, iam non Evae, sed matri Ecclesiae similis, quos cum dolore pepererat ut vivos agnosceret, cum gaudio vidit morientes; et ad hoc hortata est ut electrent potius morí pro paternis legibus Domini Dei sui, quam vivere contra eas. Quid hic credituri sumus, fratres, nisi quia liberati sunt? Hidden thirst Fuit.

freed? Their release was hidden. Antiochus, for whom they were martyred, seemed to have done something that dictated, or rather incited, his cruelty. On the contrary, the three young men were publicly and manifestly delivered from the fiery furnace, because their bodies emerged from it unharmed and their liberation was public. Those were secretly crowned, these were evidently delivered; However, all of them were saved. What was the fruit of the liberation of the three young people? Why did their crown dilate? Nebuchadnezzar himself converted to their God; and he praised, because he saved his servants, whom he had despised when he put them in the fiery furnace. There is a hidden liberation and another manifest. The hidden liberation belongs to the soul; manifests it, to the body. The soul is secretly delivered, manifestly the body. Therefore, if this is so, let us recognize the voice of the Lord in this psalm, and then we will say that what he said above belongs to hidden liberation: Take care of my soul and deliver it. Therefore, the liberation of the body is missing. Well then; When He resurrected, and ascended to heaven, and sent the Holy Spirit from there, those who were cruel in His death were converted, believing in Him, and thus, from enemies, they became friends by the grace of Christ, not by their justice. That is why he goes on to say: Because of my enemies, deliver me. Therefore, attend to my ahna refers to hidden liberation, that is, the liberation of the soul. Now deliver me from my enemies, to the manifest, that is, to the liberation of the body. It would be of no use to my enemies if you had only saved my soul; They have to believe that he did something else, that something else was accomplished. What use is there in my sanillorum liberatio: denique ipse Antiochus, a quo occisi sunt, visus est sibi aliquid fecisse quod eius crudelitas dictabat, vel potius incitabat (2 Mach 7). At I see three pueri of the way ignis aperte liberati sunt (Dan 3,49); Quia et corpus eorum erutum est, salus eorum publica Fuit. lili ergo sunt in occulto coronad, isti in aperto liberati; omnes also save. Quis autem fructus liberanis trium puerorum? Quare eorum corona dilata est? Ipse Nebuchodonosor conversus est ad Deum ipsorum, eumque praedicavit, quia eruit servos suos; quem contempserat, cum eos miserat in caminum. Est ergo liberatio occulta; est liberatio manifesta. Liberatio occulta ad animam, liberated manifesta etiam ad corpus pertinet. In occulto enim anima liberatur, in manifesto corpus.

Porro si ita est, in hoc psalmo vocem Domini agnoscamus: ad occultam liberationem pertinet quod supra dixit, lntende animae meae, et redeem eam. Restat corporis liberatio: quia eo resurgente, et in cáelos ascendant, et spiritum sanctum desuper mittente (Act 1,9, et 2,4), conversi sunt ad eius fidem qui in eius morte saevierunt; et ex inimicis amici facti sunt per illius gratíam, non per iustitiam suam. Ideo secutus est: Propter inimicos meos erue me. lntende animae meae; sed hoc in occulto: Propter inimicos autem meos erue et corpus meum. Nihil enim inimicis meis proderit, si solam animam liberaveris: aliquid se egisse, aliquid se implevisse credituri sunt. Quae militas in sanguine meo, dum
