What if I get corrupted? Then attend to my soul and rescue it; You only know this. Then also, because of my enemies, deliver me, so that my flesh may not be corrupted. 4 [v. 20]. You know my disgrace, my confusion and my shame. What is disgrace, confusion and shame? Disgrace is what the enemy throws in your face; confusion, which stings your conscience, and shame, which makes the naive face blush due to the imputation of a false crime. There is no crime, or, if there is, it is not the person who is accused. However, the weakness of the human soul often blushes when a false thing is imputed, not because it was imputed, but because it was believed. All these things occur in the body of the Lord, since confusion could not occur in Christ, since there was no guilt in Him. Christians were blamed for the crime of being Christians. This was a glory, and the brave received it with pleasure; and they received him in such a way that they were not ashamed of the name of their Lord for anything. How could their faces be covered with shame when Paul was in front of them, who said: I am not ashamed of the Gospel, since it is a virtue of God, in order to health, for every believer? Oh Paul, are you not also a worshiper of the Crucified? It is little for me, he says, not to be ashamed of this; In fact, I only glory in what the enemy thinks that makes me blush: It is not for me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified for me, and I for the world. Only disgrace could be blamed on this face, because there could be no confusion in its soul.

healed, no shame in front so free. But as some were blamed for having killed Christ, they were rightly sorry for their evil deed, and they were healthily confused and converted, in such a way that they were able to say: You knew my confusion. You, Lord, not only knew my shame, but also my confusion; and in some also shame, who, although they believe in me, are nevertheless ashamed to confess in public before the wicked, human language being more powerful before them than the divine promise. See them and commend them to God so that he does not leave them like this, but so that by helping them he may perfect them. For a certain man, believing and doubting, said: I believe, Lord; Help my disbelief. In your presence are all those who torment me. Why do I feel the disgrace, why the confusion, why the shame? You know it. Then deliver me because of my enemies, for you know all these things of mine, they do not know them; and since they are in your presence, ignorant of these things, they cannot be confused or corrected unless you clearly deliver me because of my enemies. 5 [v. 21]. Disgrace and misery awaited my heart. What does waited mean? He foresaw these things to happen, he foretold these things as future. He didn't come into the world for anything else. If I had not wanted to die, I would not have wanted to be born either; He performed both for the sake of the resurrection. Two things were known to mankind and one was unknown. We men knew about being born and dying, but we were unaware of being resurrected and living eternally. To let us know what we didn't know

do I descend in corruptionem? (Ps 29,10). Ergo, intende animae meae, et redeem eam; quod tu solus seis: deinde et propter inimicos meos erue me, ut caro mea non videat corruptionem. 4 [v.20]. T» enim cognoscis opprobrium meum, et confusionem meam, et verecundiam meam. What is it, opprobrium? why is he confused? What's true? Opprobrium est quod obiicit inimicus. Confusio est quae motdet conscientiam. Verecundia est quae facit ingenuam border etiam de falsi criminis obiectione erubescere. This is not a crime; aut etsi crime est, non est illius cui obiicitur: sed tamen infíimitas humani animi plerumque verecundatur, etiam cum falsum obiicitur; Non quia obiectum est, sed quia creditum. Omnia haec sunt in corpore Domini. Nam confusion in illo non poterat esse, in quo culpa non inveniebatur. Obiiciebatur crime Christianis, hoc ipsum quod Christiani essent. Illa quidem gloria erat: fortes libenter accipiebant, et sic accipiebant, ut omnino de nomine Domini sui non erubescerent. Operuerat enim irreverentia faciem ipsotum, habentium frontem Pauli dicetis: Non enim. erubesque of Gospel; virtus enim Dei est in salutem omni credenti (Rom 1:16). O Paule, nonne tu es adorator Crucifixi? Parum est, inquit, inde mihi non erubescere; imo hinc solum glorior, unde me putat inimicus erubescere. Mihi enim absit gloriari, nisi in cruz Domini nostri lesu Christi, per quem mihi mnndus crucifixus est, et ego mundo (Gal 6,14). Huic ergo tali fronti opprobrium solum poterat obiici. Nam

nec confusion poterat esse in conscientia iam sanata, nec verecundia in fronte tam libera. Sed cum obiieeretur quibusdam quod Christum interfecerint; merit compuncti sunt bad conscientia, et salubriter confusi atque conversi, ut possent dicere: Tu cognovisti confusionem meam. Tu ergo, Domine, nosti, non solum opprobrium meum, sed et confusionem meam; in quibusdam et verecundiam, qui quamvis in me credant, publice me tamen coram impiis confiteri erubescunt, plus apud se brave lingua humano quam promissione divina. Videte ergo eos: et commendantur tales Deo, non ut sic relinquat, sed ut eos adiuvando perficiat. Dixit enim et quidam credens, et titubans: Credo, Domine; adiuva incredtilitatem meam (Mark 9:23). In conspectu tuo sunt omnes tributantes me. Quare mihi sit opprobrium, tu-nosti; quare confusion, tu nosti; quare verecundia, tu nosti: ergo erue me propter inimicos meos, quia tu nosti ista mea, illi non norunt; ac per hoc, quia ipsi in conspectu tuo sunt, ist nescientes non poterunt vel confundí vel correcti, nisi manifesté me erueris propter inimicos meos. 5 [v.21]. Opprobrium exspectavit cor meum et miscriam. Quid est, exspectavit? Future ista praevidit, future ista praedixit. Non enim venit ad aliud. Si mori nollet, nec nasci vellet: causa resurrectionis utrumque fecit. Duo enim quaedam nobis in genere humano NOTA Erant, unum autem incognitum. Born quippe nomines et mori sciebamus; resurgere et in aeternum vivere nesciebamus. Ut ostenderet nobis quod non nove
Ennarrations on the Psalms

He carried out the two things that we knew. This is what he came to. Disgrace and misery awaited my heart. But whose misery? He expected misery, but rather that of those who crucified and persecuted him; so that misery was found in them, and mercy in Him, since, having compassion on them while hanging on the cross, He said: Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they do. Disgrace and misery awaited my heart; and I hoped that someone would be sad with me, and there was none. So what was the benefit of trusting? That is, what was the benefit of predicting, what was the benefit of saying I came to this? He came to fulfill what I said: I hoped that someone would be sad with me, and there was none; and comforters, and I found them for us, that is, and there were some for us. What he said in the previous verse: I hoped that someone would be sad, he repeats this in the next verse when he says: and comforters. What it states in the previous verse: and there was none, it says in the next one: and I did not find them. Therefore they are not different propositions, but the same previous sentence repeated. If we confirm this ruling, no controversy can arise from it. Didn't his disciples feel sad when he was led to the passion, when he was suspended from the tree, when he died? They were so sad that Mary Magdalene, who was the first to see him resurrected, when joyfully announcing what she had seen, found them crying. The Gospel says these things; It is not my opinion, it is not my conjecture; It is known that they were hurt, it is known that the disciples cried. The women who were not close to Christ also cried when he was taken to the torture, to whom he returned, suscepit duo quae noveramus. Ad hoc ergo venit. Opprobrium exspectavit cor meum et mlseriam. Sed miseriam cuius? Exspectavit enim miseriam, sed magis crucifigentium, magis persequentium; ut in illis esset miseria, in illo miseria. Miseriam quippe illorum miserans etiam pendens in cruz: Pater, inquit, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt (Luke 23,34). Opprobrium exspectavit cor meum et miseriam: et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non Fuit. Quid ergo profuit quia expectavi? hoc est, quid profuit quia praedixi? Quid profuit quia dixi ideo me venisse? Ventum est ut impleretur quod dixi: sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non Fuit; et consolantes, the non inveni; hoc est, non Fuit.

Quod enim superiore versu dixit, Sustinui qui simul contristaretur; hoc sequenti versu, et consolantes. Quod autem superiore versu, et non Fuit; hoc sequenti versu, et non inveni. Ergo non altera subiecta, sed superior repetita sententia est. Quam sententiam si retractemus, quaestio nonnulla poterit oboriri. Numquid enim discipuli eius non sunt contristan, quando ductus est ad passionem, quando ligno suspensus, quando mortuus? Usque adeo contristan, ut illa Maria Magdalene, quae primo eum vidit, gaudens lugentibus nuntiaret quid viderit (lo 20,18, et Me 16,9). Evangelium ista loquitur; non nostra praesumptio, non nostra suspicio est; constat doluisse, constat luxisse disciples. Extraneae mulieres flebant, quando ad passionem ducebatur; ad quas conversus ait:
Prayer of the vexed people

Dose said: Weep for yourselves, but not for me. So how is it that He expected someone to grieve with Him and there was none? We investigate, and we find sad people, sobbing and moaning; Hence this sentence surprises us: I hoped that someone would be sad with me, and there was none; and comforters, and I did not find them. Let us examine more diligently, and we will see that He expected someone to grieve with Him, and there was none. Those of whom we have spoken were carnally saddened by mortal life, which was to be changed with death and restored with the resurrection; That's where that sadness came from. The sadness must have been those who, blind, killed the doctor; who, feverishly, as if frantic, perniciously reviled Him for whom health was offered to them. He wanted to heal, to punish them; hence the doctor's sadness. He inquires to see if he has found a companion for this sadness. He did not say: I waited for someone to grieve, and there was none, but: I waited for someone to grieve with me, that is, for what I was sad, and I did not find it. Saint Peter certainly loved a lot and without hesitation he threw himself into the waters to walk above them, and at the voice of the Lord he was delivered; and when Christ was led to the passion, carried away by the fearlessness of love, he followed him; However, troubled, he denied him three times. What did it come from? Because it seemed like a bad thing to die. He avoided what he thought was evil. What he avoided, this afflicted the Lord. Before, Peter had also said to the Lord: Take such a thought away from you, Lord; God will be kind to you, this will not happen. Then he deserved to be called satan after having heard from the Lord himself: Blessed are you, Simon, son of Jonah. Then in the sadness that the Lord had for those for whom he prayed saying: Flete: be you, nolite me (Luke 23,28). Quomodo ergo sustinuit qui simul contristaretur, et non Fuit? Attendimus, et invenimus tristes, et lugentes, et plangentes; once again look at this sentence: Sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non Fuit; et consolantes, et non inveni. Intendamus diligentius, et videbimus eum sustinuisse qui simul contristaretur, et non Fuisse. Contristabantur enim illi carnaliter de vita mortali, quae mutanda fuet morte, et reparanda resurrectione: hinc erat illa tristitia.

De illis enim esse debuit, qui caeci medicum occiderunt, qui tanquam perniciose febrientes phrenetici, faciebant iniuriam ei a quo illis fuet salus allata. Ule volebat curare, illi saevire: hinc tristitia doctor. Quaere utrum invenerit huius tristitiae comitem. Non enim ait, sustinui qui contristaretur, et non Fuit; sed, qui simul contristaretur, id est, ex ea re, qua ergo, contristaretur, et non inveni. Petrus certe plurimum amavit, et in fluctus calcandos se sine dubitatione proiecit, et ad vocem Domini liberatus est (Mt 14,29-31): et eum ductum ad passionem, amoris audacia consecutus, tamen turbatus, ter negavit. Unde, nisi quia malum illi videbatur morí? Id enim devitabat quod malum putabat. Hoc ergo et in Domino dolebat, quod ipse devitabat. Propterea et ante dixerat, Absit a te, Domine; propitius tibi esto, non fiet istud: quando meruit audire, Satan; posteaquam audierat, Beatas es, Simón Bar lona (Ib. 16,17.22.23).
Ennarrations on the Psalms

Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they do, they did not find any companion. And I hoped that someone would be sad with me, and there was none. There were none at all. And comforters, and I did not find them. Who are the dildos? Those who profit, well, they are the ones who console us, they are the consolation for all the preachers of the truth. 6 [v. 22]. And they gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. The Gospel tells us that this was fulfilled to the letter. But you must know, brothers, that this very thing of not finding comforters, this very thing of not finding anyone who would grieve with me, was my gall, my bitterness, my vinegar: bitterness, because of the affliction; vinegar, due to its old age and rancidity. We read in the Gospel that they certainly offered him gall, but in drink, not in food. However, this is how it should be understood and thus what was predicted here so long before was fulfilled: And they gave me gall for food. Not only in this saying, but also in this fact, we must investigate the mystery; try to find out the secrets; enter, tearing the veil of the temple, into the sanctuary; see the sacrament there or investigate what was said or what was done. They gave me—he says—gall for food. What they gave him was not food, it was drink; But they gave it to him for food, since the Lord had already taken the food and they poured gall into it. He had taken the soft food when he ate the Passover with his disciples. There he offered them the sacrament of his body and blood. In this delicate and sweet meal of the unity of Christ, which the Apostle recommends, saying: As one

bread, so we many are one body; In this pleasant meal, who is it that offers the gall if not the challenger of the Gospel, in the style of those persecutors of Christ? The Jews sinned less by crucifying him who walked on earth than those who despise him who is already seated in heaven. Then what the Jews gave him by giving him food, which he had already taken, to drink that bitter drink, the same thing is done by those who by living badly scandalize the Church. This is done by heretics who irritate God; but they are not conceited in themselves. They throw gall on such pleasant food. But what does the Lord do? He doesn't admit it in his body, in his stomach. Enclosing a mystery, the Lord, when offering him the gall, tasted it or tasted it, but did not want to drink it. If we didn't tolerate them, we wouldn't taste or like them either; but since it is necessary to tolerate them, it is also necessary to like them. But since these cannot form part of the members of Christ, they can be tasted, but they cannot be received into the body. And they gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. I was thirsty, and they gave me vinegar; that is, I desired his faith, and I found his old age or staleness. 7 [v. 23-24]. Let their table become a noose before them. The snare you laid for me by giving me such a drink may serve as a snare for you. Why in front of them? It would have been enough to say: Turn their table into a noose. Such are those who know their iniquity and most obstinately persevere in it; and in such a way they persist in it, that before them it becomes their own bond. They are too perverse; That's why they go down to hell alive. In the end,

Ergo in tristitia quam habebat Dominus de illis pro quibus oravit, Pater, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt, nullum comitem invenit. And he continued who seemed to be contrite, and he was not. Prorsus non Fuit. Et consolantes, et non inveni. Who sunr consolations? Proficient. Ipsi enim nos consolantur, ipsi sunt solatio omnibus praedicatoribus veritatis. 6 [v.22]. Et deierunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto. Factum is quidem ad litteram, et Evangelium hoc nobis indicat. Sed intelligetidum est, fratres, hoc ipsum quod non inveni consolantes, hoc ipsum quod non inveni qui simul contristaretur, hoc Fuit fel meum, hoc mihi amarum, hoc acetum Fuit: amarum propter moerorem, acetum propter eorum vetustatem. Namque legimus illi quidem oblatum fel, sicut Evangelium loquitur (Ib. 27,34); thirst in potum, not in escam. Verumtamen sic accipiendum et impletum quod hic fuet ante praedictum, Dederunt in escam meam fel: et in isto ipso facto, non solum in hoc dicto, mysterium requirere deben, secreta pulsare, velum templi conscissum intrare, videre ibi sacramentum, vel quod ita dictum est, vel quod ita factum est. Dederunt, inquit, in escam meam fel. Non ipsum quod dederunt esca erat; potus enim erat: thirst in escam dederunt; quia iam Dominus escam acceperat, et in ipsam iniectum est fel. Acceperat autem ipse escam suavem, quando pascha manducavit cum discipulis suis: ibi sacramentum sui corporis demonstravit (Luke 22:19). In hanc escam tam dulcem, tam dulcem unitatis Christi, quam commendat Apos-

tolus, they say, Quia unus pañis, unum corpus multi sumus (1 Cor 10:17); in hanc escam suavem quis est qui dat fel, nisi contradictors Evangelii, tanquam illi persecutors Christi? Minus enim peccaverunt ludaei crucifigentes in terra ambulantem, quam qui contemnunt in cáelo sedentem. Quod ergo fecerunt ludaei, ut in escam quam iam acceperat darent bibendum amarum illum potum, hoc faciunt qui male vivirdo scandalum inferunt Ecclesiae: hoc faciunt haeretici amaricantes; sed non exaltentur in semetypsis (Ps 65,7). Dant fel super tam iucundum cibum. Sed quid facit Dominus? Non admittit ad corpus suum. Hoc sacramento ipse Dominus, quando illi obtulerunt fel, gustavit, et noluit bibere (Mt 27:34). Si non eos pateremur, nec omnino gustaremus: quia vero necesse est eos pati, necesse est gustari. Sed quia in mernbris Christi such esse non possunt, gustari possunt, recipi in corpus non possunt. Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto. Sitiebam, et acetum accepi; id est fidem illorum desideravi, et vetustatem inveni. 7 [v.23.24}. Eiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in muscipulam. Qualem muscipulam mihi exhibituerunt, giving mihi talem potum, talis muscipula illis sit. Ouare ergo, coram ipsis? As long as they are not confused and ashamed, they will necessarily defend their actions, it will seem to them that they are something, because they arrest, chain, punish, kill, jump for joy, outrage. Of all these facts they will be confused and ashamed in some time. See that I said, and I will say a thousand times with you, that all those who still jump for joy and discredit and insult the martyrs, will be confused and ashamed, and perhaps sometime within these walls, confused, they will beat their chests. 4 [v. 4]. Let those who harbor evil against me draw back and blush. First the violence of the persecutors appeared, now the hatred of the ill-intentioned remains. Therefore, in the Church there are different times of persecution that follow one another. Violence against the Church took place when the kings were persecuting, and as it had been announced that the kings would persecute and believe, the first was fulfilled, the second was then fulfilled. And what was natural to follow happened; The kings believed and peace was given to the Church, and the Church began to be at the top of esteem even on earth, even in this life. But the roar of the persecutors is not lacking, since they turned their violence into ill will. In those thoughts, as if locked in the abyss, the demon is bound; it roars, but it does not overflow. The title of this psalm is like the sign that is placed on the threshold of the house indicating its destination: For David, of the sons of Jonadab, and of the first who were taken captive. The Jonadab that is made known to us through the prophecy of Jeremiah was a man, who commanded his sons not to drink wine or live in houses, but in tents. By retaining and observing their father's command, the children deserved to be blessed by God. This precept had not been imposed on them by God, but by their father. But they received him as a commandment from their Lord God. Because, if it is true that God had not commanded them not to drink wine and to live in tents, nevertheless, God had commanded the children to obey their parents. Children should not obey their parents only when the parents command their children to do something contrary to what the Lord God commands. And parents should not be angry when God is postponed to them. But, when parents order something that is not against God, they must be heard as if it were God who ordered, since God commanded parents to be obeyed. God blessed the sons of Jonadab for their obedience and set them up as an example to his disobedient people, reproaching him for the fact that the sons of Jonadab had obeyed their father and he did not obey his father.

You carry the earthly body, in which the treasure of God is deposited, something must be feared due to the fragility of the container. Therefore you are my firmness so that I may be strong in this world against all temptations. But if many disturb me, you are my refuge. I will confess my weakness, being timid like the hare, because I am full of thorns like a hedgehog. For in another psalm it is written: The stone is a refuge for hares and hedgehogs. But the stone, says Saint Paul, was Christ, 6 [v. 4]. My God, deliver me from the hands of the sinner. Sinners are generally those among whom this one who is to be freed from captivity suffers; this one who cries: Wretched man I, who will deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through our Lord Jesus Christ. The enemy is within; It is the law that is in the members. There are also enemies outside, so you cry out to Her who shouted: Cleanse me, Lord, from my hidden sins, and forgive your servant from those of others. Then, when it is said above save me, it refers to your internal illness, that is, to your iniquity; to the one by which you are captive; to that by which you belong to the first man, so that you may cry out among the first captives. Now saved from your iniquity, attend to the iniquity of strangers, among whom it is necessary that you live until this life ends. And when will it end? It ends for you (when you die); For the Church it will end at the end of the world. Then this one man who is the unity of Christ breaks out into these cries. It is necessary that many faithful who died are already in the rest that

God offered to the souls of the faithful; but there are still members of Christ here: those who live and those who are later to be born. Then until the end of the world the man who asks to be delivered from his sins and from the law of his members, which opposes the law of the mind, will continue here; Then he will continue shouting among the sins of others, in the midst of which he must live until the end of the world. But you will meet two kinds of sinners; some who received the law and others who did not receive it. The pagans did not receive it; All Jews and Christians received it. Therefore the name of sinner is general: either he is a transgressor of the law, if he received it, or he is only wicked without the law, if he did not receive it. The Apostle speaks of both kinds, and says: Those who sinned without the law will perish without the law, and those who sinned while in the law will be judged by the law. You, who groan between both genders, say to the Lord what you hear in the psalm: My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner. Of what sinner? From the hand of the lawbreaker and the wicked. By transgressing the law, you become wicked, for he who transgresses the law is wicked. Everyone who transgresses the law is wicked, but not every wicked transgresses the law: Where there is no law—says the Apostle—there is no transgression. Those who did not receive the law can be called evil, but not transgressors. Both will be judged on their own merits. But I, who want to be freed from captivity by your grace, cry out to you: Deliver me from the hand of the sinner. What does hand mean? 10 [v. 8]. Fill my mouth with praise singing a hymn to your glory, to your magnificence all day long. What does all day mean? Without intermission. In prosperity, because you console; in adversity, because you correct; before existing, because you created me; later, because you gave me health; when I sinned, because you forgave me; when I repented, because you helped me; having persevered, because you will crown me. So, then, I will fill my mouth with praise singing a hymn to your glory, to your magnificence all day long. 11 [v. 9]. Do not throw me away in the time of old age. You are my hope since youth; Do not forsake me in the time of old age. When will be the time of old age? When my vigor fails, do not forsake me. Here God answers you: Rather, let your strength fail so that my strength may remain in you, so that you can say with the Apostle: When I am weak, then I am powerful. Do not fear being abandoned in weakness, in old age. Well what? Did your Lord not weaken on the cross? Did not the potentates, the strong bulls, move their heads before Him, as before a helpless and defenseless man, a prisoner and dejected, and say: If He is the Son of God, let Him come down from the cross? Was that weakened one abandoned? He preferred not to come down from the cross, so that it would not appear that, showing his power, he was giving in to the offenders. What did he teach you who, hanging on the cross, did not want to come down from it? Patience among outragers and may you be strong in your God. Perhaps it was also said in person of Him: I have been a wonder to many; and you are my powerful helper, personifying him in all matters of faith [v.8]. Repleatur os meum laude, ut hymno dicam gloriam tuam; all die magnificentiam tuam. Quid est, tota die? Sine intermissione. In prosperis, quia consolaris; in adversis, quia corrigis; antequam essem, quia fecisti; cum essem, quia salutem dedisti: cum peccassem, quia ignovisti; cum conversus essem, quia adiuvisti; cum perseverassem, quia coronasti. Ita plane repleatur os meum laude, ut hymno dicam gloriam tuam; all die magnificentiam tuam. 11 [v.9]- Ne proiicias me in tempore senectutis. Spes mea a iuventute mea, ne proiicias me in tempore senectutis. Quod est hoc tempus senectutis? Cum deficiet virtus mea, ne derelinquas me.

Respondet hic tibi Deus: Imo vero deficiat virtus tua, ut in te maneat mea; ut dicas cum Apostólo: Quando infirmor, tune potens sum (2 Cor 12,10). Noli timere ne proiiciaris in infirmitate, in ista senectute. Quid enim, Dominus tuus non est infirmatus in cruz? nonne ante illum, tanquam ante hominem nihil valentem, captivatum et oppressum, caput agitaverunt fortissimi, et tauri pingues, et dixerunt: Si Vilius Dei est, descendat de cruz? (Mt 27,39.40). Numquid ille, quia infirmus erat, desertus est; qui maluit non descendéré de cruz, ne non potentiam ostendisse, sed insultantibus cessisse videretur? queza, not in terms of power; as to how He was transfigured into us, taking our being, not as to what He was when He came down. He became a prodigy for many. Quite the opposite; His strength will be in you when yours fails. 12 [v. 10-11]. Why do I say this? For my enemies spoke against me, and those who were stalking my life deliberated together, saying, God forsook him; Pursue him and arrest him, because there is no one to rescue him. This was said of Christ, who suddenly became weak in the hands of the enemies and was imprisoned as an invalid, despite the fact that by the immense power of his divinity, by which he was equal to the Father, he was raised from the dead. How would they have arrested him if they had not first said in their hearts: God abandoned him? Hence those words he spoke on the cross: My God, my God! Why did you abandon me? Did God then abandon Christ, since God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, and furthermore, Christ being God, and God worthy of being blessed above all factus sum multis, et tu adiulor fortis: ex persona eius secundum infirmitatem, non secundum potestatem; secundum id quod nos in se transfiguraverat, non secundum id quod ipse descenderat. Si ibi erat vetus homo noster, senectus ibi erat; quia vetus, senectus. Tamen quia verum est, Renovabitur sicut aquilae iuventus tua (Ps 102,5); resurrection ipse die tertio, promisit resurrectionem finito saeculo. Iam praecessit caput; membra secutara sunt.

And why did he wish it on those who hate his life? What does it mean to those who hate their life? Those that cause some quarrel. Those who incite quarrels are called inciters. If so, let us guard against those who conspire against our lives. What does it mean that they conspire or incite against our lives? Of confusion and shame: of confusion, due to a bad conscience, and of shame or blushing, considering honor or esteem. Do this to them and they will be good. Don't think he's being cruel. so that God, who had blinded him, would displease him, and thus, displeasing Him, he would prepare his soul to fight against Him. 15 [v.14}. If no one advises you by tormenting you, if no one compels you to displease God in the work you suffer or to hate men, because of which you suffer, your soul is not disturbed, but without disturbance you say what follows: I always hoped in you and I will add something to all your praise. What is this? We should be struck by what is said: I will add something about all your praise. Do you have to make the praise of God more perfect? Is there anything that can be added? If it is absolute praise, what have you to add to it? God is praised in all his good works, in all creation, in the entire plan and constitution of the work, in the government and regime of the centuries, in the ordering of the times, in the greatness of heaven, in the fertility of the earth, in the extension and bounding of the sea, in the germinative power of every creature that is born in every place, in the children of men themselves, in giving the law, in freeing his people from Egyptian captivity and in all his other admirable works. But he had not yet been praised for having resurrected the flesh to eternal life. Therefore the praise that was added here is the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that we may understand, if we want to understand this well, that this added praise is praise above all past praise. You, sinner, who feared that your soul would be troubled, who only hoped in God to deliver you from that first captivity, who did not boast of your righteousness, but of the grace of God, which this psalm recommends, how will you add anything to the praise above all praise of God? I will add, he says. Let's see what it adds. Ad hoc dicebat, ut displiceret illi Deus, qui illum fecerat caecum; et curn illi displiceret, committeretur anima ipsius. 15 [v.14]. Si ergo nemo tibi tabulando persuaserit, nemo extorserit ut tibi displiceat Deus in his quae pateris, aut ut oderis homines per quos pateris, non committitur anima tua; sed securus say quod sequitur: Ego autem semper in te sperabo, et adiiciam super omnem laudem tuam. Quid est hoc? I will move us debt, adiiciam super omnem laudem tuam. Perfectiorem facturus is laudem Dei? est aliquid quod superadiiciatur? si iam omnis illa laus est, tu quid adiecturus est?

Laudatus est Deus in omnibus bonis factis suis, in omni creature sua, in omni institutione rerum omnium, in gubernatione et regimine saeculorum, in ordine tempotum, in eminentia caeli, in fecunditate terrarum, in circumfusione maris, in omni praepollentia nascentis ubique creaturae, in ipsis filiis hominum, in danda lege, in liberandis suis a captivitate Aegyptiorum, et caeteris ómnibus mirabilibus suis: nondum erat laudatus in eo quod suscitavit carnem in vitam aetetnam. Sit ergo is laus adiecta per resurrectionem Domini nostri lesu Christi; ut hic eius vocem intelligamus super omnem laudem praeterítam: sic hoc et recte intelligimus. Quid tu forte peccator, qui timebas committi animam tuam, qui in ipso solo sperabas, ut a prima illa captivitate libetareris, qui de iustitia tua non

You could have uttered all praise, and nothing at all would have seemed to be lacking, because in reality nothing was lacking if you had condemned all the wicked. For the very justice by which sinners are condemned is no small praise of God. This justice would be great praise. You created man, you gave him free will, you placed him in paradise, you imposed a precept on him, you threatened him with death if he broke the command; You failed to do anything for his good, no one could demand that you had done more for him. But he sinned; The human race became a mass of sinners that flooded with sinners; then, if you condemn this mass of iniquity, who will say to you: You acted unjustly? You would be absolutely righteous, and this would also be entirely your praise; But since you delivered even the same sinner by justifying the wicked, I will add something to all your praise. 16 [v.15]. My mouth will publish your righteousness; not mine. Hence I will add something to all your praise, since what I have that is righteous, if I am righteous, is due to your righteousness, which is found in me, not to mine, since you justify the wicked. My mouth will publish your righteousness; all day your health. What does your health mean? (That) health is from the Lord. No one takes advantage of being saved. Health belongs to the Lord. No one is saved by himself; health belongs to God; man's health is vain. (I will announce) Your health all day long, that is, at all times. Something adverse happens, it announces the health of the Lord. Something prosperous happens, it announces the health of the Lord. Do not announce it in prosperity and the streets in the adverpraesumebas, thirst for gratia illius quam commendat hic psalmus; quid, tu adiicies aliquid super omnem laudem Dei? Adiiciam, inquit. Videomus quid adiiciat. Posset esse omnis laus tua, et nihil omnino deesse videretur ad laudem tuam, quia et nihil deesset, si damnares omnes iniquos. Non enim non esset magna laus Dei iustitia ipsa qua iniqui damnantur: magna laus esset. Fecisti hominem, dedisti ei liberum arbitrium, in paradiso collocasti, praeceptum imposuisti, mortem, si praeceptum violat, ius-' tissimam denuntiasti; nihil non fecisti, nemo est qui a te amplius exigat. Peccavit; factum est genus humanum tanquam massa peccatorum, profluens de peccatoribus (Gen 2 et 3); quid ergo, tu si massam istam iniqui taris damnes, quisquam tibi dicet: Iniuste fecisti? Esses plane etiam sic iustus, et omnis esset ista laus tua; sed quia liberasti et ipsum peccatorem iustificando impium, adiiciam super omnem laudem tuam. 16 [v.15].

Os meum enuntiabi iustitiam tuam; all die sdutem tuam. Quid est, salutem tuam? Domini est salus (Ps 3,9). Nemo sibi usurpet quia se salvum facit: Domini est salus. Non se salvum per se quisquam facit: Domini est salus, vana salus hominis (Ps 59,13). Tota die salutem tuam: toto tempore. Aliquid adversi est; praedica salutem Domini: aliquid prosperi est; praedica salutem Domini. Ne praedices in prosperis, et

sity, so that what was said is not fulfilled: all day. The whole day is understood as day with night. When we say, for example: Thirty days passed, don't we also understand the nights? What is said in Genesis? Once the afternoon came and the morning came, they completed a day. Then the total day is completed with its night; but the night serves the day, not the day the night. 1 [v. l]. The title of this psalm is titled For Solomon. In it things are said that cannot suit Solomon, king of Israel according to the flesh, if what the Scripture narrates about him is taken into account; which can perfectly apply to Christ. Hence it is rightly presumed that the name of Solomon was adduced allegorically so that Christ might be understood in him. Solomon certainly means peaceful; Therefore, such a word is adapted in all truth and propriety to Him through whose mediation, leaving enemies, having received the remission of sins, we are reconciled to God. For, being enemies, says the Apostle, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son. He is also the peaceful one who made both things one and who broke down the fence of division, the enmity in the flesh; who nullified the law of the commandments with decrees to create in himself the two in one new man, making peace, and who when he came evangelized peace to those near and to those far away. He himself says in the Gospel: My peace I leave you, my peace I give you. Also by many other testimonies it is demonstrated that the Lord Jesus Christ is peaceful; but not according to the peace that this world knows and seeks, but according to that of which the prophet says: I will give you true joy, peace upon peace; That is to say, to the peace of reconciliation he adds the peace of immortality. because

Nor does the true charity of God reside in him who is ungrateful to the Holy Spirit, through whom his charity is spread in our hearts. And, therefore, these do not belong to the people of God, because they are not poor, of God. On the contrary, the poor of God say: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who proceeds from God, that we may know the things freely given to us by God. From all of this it is deduced that, when in this psalm it is said that God, Father and king, taking into account the sacrament of the taking of man by which the Word became flesh, gives justice to the Son of the king, these rich people do not want justice to be given to them, but believe that they have it for themselves; and thus, not knowing the justice of God and wanting to establish their own, they do not submit to the justice of God. In this way they are not, as I said, poor in God, but rich in themselves, because they are not humble, but proud. But He will come to judge the people of God in righteousness, and the poor of God in judgment; and by this judgment he will separate his

poor, those whom with his poverty he made rich, from the rich themselves. Therefore, the poor people cry to Him and say: Judge me, O God, and discern my cause from the unholy people. 4. Having changed the order of the words in the same verse when he said: O God, yield your judgment to the king, and your justice to the king's son, judge your people in justice, and your poor in judgment, recording in the first part of the verse first the judgment and then the justice, and then writing, in the second, first justice and then judgment, shows that he rather called the judgment justice and that the order in which it is written does not matter when they mean the same thing. It is usually called perverse judgment that is unjust; But we do not usually say unjust or iniquitous justice, because if it is perverse and unjust, it should no longer be called justice. Therefore, writing judgment and repeating this concept under the name of justice, he sufficiently demonstrated that he properly called judgment what is usually called justice, that is, what cannot be understood to have been misjudged. The Lord demonstrated that there can be perverse judgment where he says: Do not judge with partiality, but judge righteous judgment. Here he prohibits the first and commands the second. When he names judgment without any adjective, he wants to always understand just judgment, as he said elsewhere: You have left the most important things in the law: mercy and judgment. And likewise what Jeremiah says: Acquiring wealth not with judgment; It does not say: You acquire wealth with perverse and unjust judgment or without right judgment

iactantia qua putant sibi esse tribuendum, non gtatiae Dei, quod bene vivunt; et ideo iam nec bene vivunt, quantacumque bona opera faceré videantur. De suo quippe habere se putant, et gloriantur quasi non acceperint (1 Cor 4:7): divites sui, non pauperes Dei; abundant sibi, non egentes Deo. Sed ait Apostolus: Si distribuero omnia mea pauperibus, et tradidero corpas meum ut ardeam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest. Tanquam si diceret: Si distribuero omnia mea pauperibus, et pauper Dei non fuero, nihil mihi prodest. Charitas enim non inflatur (1 Cor 13,3.4); nec est vera Dei charitas in eo qui ingratus est sancto Spiritui eius, per quem diffusion in cordibus nostris charitas eius (Rom 5,5). Et ideo such non pertinent ad populum Dei, quia non sunt pauperes Dei. Pauperes quippe Dei dicunt: Nos autem non spiritum huius mundi accepimus, sed Spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quae a Deo donata sunt nobis (1 Cor 2,12). Nam cum et in isto psalmo, propter suscepti hominis sacramentum quo Verbum caro factum est (lo 1,14), dicatur Deo Patri regi, lusútiam tuam da filio regis; nolunt isti sibi dari iustitiam, sed a semetypsis eam habere confidunt. Ignorantes enim Dei iustitiam, et suam volentes constituere, iustitiae Dei non sunt subiecti (Rom 10:3). Non sunt itaque, ut dixi, pauperes Dei, sed divites sui; quia non sunt humiles, sed superbi. Veniet vero ille iudicare populum Dei in iustitia, et pauperes Dei in iudicio: et eo iudicio discernet a divitibus eorum pauperes suos; sed quos paupertate sua fecit divites suos. Clamat e quippe populus pau-

per: ludica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (Ps 42,1). 4. Quod autem mutato verborum ordine, cum prius dixisset, Deus, iudicium tuum regi da, et iustitiam tuam filio regis, prius pones iudicium, deinde iustitiam; prius iustitiam posuit, deinde iudicium, dicens, Indicare populum tuum in iustitia, et pauperes tuos in iudicio; magis ostendit iudicium se appellasse iustitiam, nihil intetesse demonstrans quo ordine ponatur, cum idem significacet. Solet enim dici iudicium pravum quod iniustum est; iustitiam vero iniquam vel iniustam dicere non solemus. Si enim prava, et iniusta erit; nec iustitia iam diganda est. Proinde setting iudicium, atque iustitiae nomine repetendt>; vel setting iustitiam, et eam iudicii nomine repetendo, satis edocet proprie se appellare iudicium quod pro iustitia poni solet, id est, quod in male iudicando intelligi non potest. Ubi enim Dominus dicit, Nolite iudicare personaliter, sed rectum iudicium iudicate (lo 7,24), ostendit esse posse pravum iudicium, cum dicit, Rectum iudicium iudicate: denique illud vetat; hoc praecipit. Cum vero sine ulla adiectione dicit iudicium, continuous iustum vult intelligi; sicut est quod ait: Relinchitis graviora Legis, misericordiam, et iudicium (Mt 23,23). Et illud quod Ieremias dicit: Faciens divitias suas non cum iudicio (Jer 17:11). Non ait, Faciens divitias suas pravo iniustove iudicio, vel non cum iudicio recto aut

and just, but not with judgment, calling judgment him who alone is upright and just. 5 [v. 3]. May the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills receive justice. The mountains are large prominences, the hills are small. Therefore, without a doubt, these are those of whom another psalm speaks: The lesser with the greater, or the small with the great. These mountains leaped for joy like rams, and these hills, like sheep's lambs, when Israel left Egypt, that is, in the liberation of God's people from the bondage of this world. Therefore those who stand out in the Church for eminent holiness are mountains, who are capable of teaching others by speaking, in such a way that they instruct faithfully, and by living, so that they are profitably imitated. The hills are those that obediently imitate the perfection of those. Why will the mountains receive peace, and the hills receive justice? Would it perhaps make no difference if it were said: Let the mountains receive justice for the people, and the hills peace? Justice is necessary between both of them and they both need peace. It could happen that peace was called, by another name, justice, but the true peace is this, not the one established among themselves by the unjust. Or is it to be understood that what is said: The mountains will receive peace, and the hills justice, taking into account the distinction? Those who stand out in the Church must look for peace with vigilant attention, lest by their elevated position, acting with pride, they cause schisms, breaking the unity of the Church. The hills must continue to obey them and imitate them in such a way that Christ will put them off, lest, seduced,

By the vain authority of the evil mountains, since they seem to them to stand out, they are separated from the unity of Christ. That is why it was said: Let the mountains receive peace for the people. So say: Be imitators of me, as I also am imitators of Christ. Say also: Even if I or an angel from heaven evangelizes you outside of what you received, let it be anathema. Also say: Was Paul crucified for you or were you baptized in the name of Paul? Thus receive peace for the people of God, that is, for the poor of God; wishing not to reign for them, but with them. And the hills do not say: I am of Paul, I of Apollo, I of Peter, but let them all cry: I am of Christ. In this consists justice: in not putting the servants before the Lord or equating them and in raising their eyes in such a way to the mountains from where their help comes, that, nevertheless, they do not expect to receive help from the mountains, but from God, who made heaven and earth. 6. It can be understood very well that the mountains receive peace for the people in such a way that we understand by peace the reconciliation by which we are reconciled with God, since the mountains receive it for their people. The Apostle testifies to this: Old things have passed away, behold, they have all become new, and they are all from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation. Here you see how the mountains receive peace for the people. As if God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself; not imputing their crimes to them, but putting in us the word of reconciliation. In whom if not in the mountains

fair; sed, non cum ludido: iudicium non appellans, nisi quod rectum ac iustum est. 5 [v.3]. Suscipiant montes pacem populo, et streets iustitiam. Montes maiores sunt, colles minores. Nimirum ergo hi sunt quos alius habet psalmus: Pusillos cum magnis. Isti quippe montes exsultaverunt sicut arietes, et isti colles sicut agni ovium, in exitu Israel ex Aegypto (Ps 113,13-4.1), id est in populi Dei liberatione ab huius saeculi servitute. Excellenti ergo sanctitate eminentes in Ecclesia, montes sunt; qui idonei sunt et alios docere (2 Tim 2,2), sic loquendo ut fideliter instruantur, sic vivirdo ut salubriter imitentur: colles autem. sunt illorum excellentiam sua obedientia subsequentes. Quare ergo montes pacem, et colles iustitiam? An forte nihil interesset, etiamsi ita diceretur: Suscipiant montes iustitiam populo, et colles pacem? Utrisque enim iustitia, et utrisque pax necessaria est: et fieri potest ut alio nomine pax appellata sit ipsa iustitia; haec est enim vera pax, non qualem iniusti Inter se faciunt. An potius cum distinctione non contemnenda intelligendum est quod ait, Montes pacem, et colles iustitiam? Excellent quippe in Ecclesia, pací debent vigilant intentione consulere; ne propter suos honores superbe agendo schismata faciant, unitatis compage disrupta. Colles autem ita eos imitando et obediendo subsequantur, ut eis Christum anteponant; ne malorum montium, quoniam videntur excellere, vana auctoritate seducti,

be a Christi unitate disruptant. Ideo dictum est: Suscipiant montes pacem populo. Dicant quidem: Imitatores mei estofe, sicut et ego Christi (1 Cor 11,1). Sed rursus dicant: Licet si nos, aut angelus de cáelo vobis annuntiaverit praeterquam quod accepistis, anathema sit (Gal 1,8). Dicant etiam: Numquid Paulus pro vobis crucifixus est, aut in nomine Pauli baptizati est? (1 Cor 1:13). Ita suscipiant pacem populo Dei, id est, pauperibus Dei; non illis, sed cum illis regnare cupientes. lili quoque non dicant, Ego sum Pauli, ego sum Apollo, ego vero Cephae; sed omnes dicant: Ego sum Christi (Ib. 12). Haec est iustitia: non preponere servos Domino, nec aequare; Ita levare oculos in montes unde veniat auxilium sibi, ut tamen auxilium suum non sperent a montibus, sed a Domino qui fecit caelum et terram (Ps 120,1.2). 6. Potest et sic convenientissime intelligi, Suscipiant montes pacem populo, ut pacem intelligamus in reconciliatione qua Deo reconciliamur: montes quippe eam suscipiunt populo eius. Hoc Apostolus ita testatur: Vetera transierunt; ecce jacta sunt nova: omnia autem ex Deo, qui reconciliavit nos sibi per Christum, et dedit nobis ministerium reconciliatiónis. Ecce quomodo suscipiunt montes pacem populo eius. Deus enim erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi; non reputans illis delicia eorum, et ponens in nobis verbum reconciliatinis. In quibus, nisi in montibus qui suscipiunt pacem populo eius? Quocirca legati pacis subsequenter adiun-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

who receive peace for their people? That is why the legates of peace then add and say: For Christ we are ambassadors, and as if God were exhorting for us, we beseech you through Christ to be reconciled to God. The mountains receive this peace for their people, that is, the embassy and the preaching of their peace; and the hills justice, that is, obedience, which constitutes, in men and in every rational creature, the origin of all perfection and justice. In this way we are reminded of the great difference that exists between these two men; that is, between Adam, who was the author of our death, and between Christ, who is the author of our health; For as through the disobedience of one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of one man the many will be made righteous. Then let the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills receive justice, so that, by agreeing in this way, one and the other, what is written may be fulfilled: Justice and peace kissed each other. What other codices record: May the mountains and hills receive peace for the people, I believe that, written like this, the preachers of evangelical peace, both earlier and later, should be understood as mountains and hills. In these codices it continues like this: In justice he will judge the poor of the people. But the codices that write what we stated above enjoy more authority: May the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills receive justice. Some write for your people; others do not say for you, but only for the people. 7 [v. 4]. He will judge the poor of the people and save the children of the poor. It seems to me that they are the same poor gunt, et dicunt: Pro Christo ergo legatione fungimur, tanquam Deo exhortante per nos; obsecramus pro Christo reconciliari Deo (2 Cor 5,17-20).

Hanc pacem suscipiunt montes populo eius, id est, praedicationem legationemque pacis eius: colles autem iustitiam; hoc est obedientiam, quod est in hominibus et in omni rationali creatura omnis iustitiae origo atque perfectio; ita ut duorum hominum, id est, Adam qui Fuit caput moitis nostrae, et Christi qui est caput salutis nostrae, haec commendetur magna distinctio: quia sicut per inobedientiam unius hominis, peccatores constituti sunt multi; ita et per obedientiam unius hominis, iusti constituentur multi (Rom 5,19)- Suscipiant ergo montes pacem populo, et colles iustitiam; ut hoc modo utrisque concordantibus, fiat quod scriptum est, Iustitia et pax osculatae sunt se (Ps 84,11). Quod vero alii codices habent, Suscipiant montes pacem populo, et colles: utrosque praedicatores evangelicae pacis intelligendos puto; sive praecedentes, sive subsequent. In his autem ccdicibus illud sequitur: In iustitia iudicabit pauperes populi. Sed illi magis codices approbantur, qui habent quod supra exposuimus, Suscipiant montes pacem populo, et colles iustitiam. Aliqui autem habent, populo tuo; aliqui non habent tuo, sed tantummodo populo. 7 [v.4]. ludicabit pauperes populi, et safes faciet filios pauperum. Papperes et filii pauperum iidem ipsi mihi videntur; sicut eadem civitas

and the children of the poor, as Zion and the daughter of Zion are the same city. But, if they are to be understood as diverse, then we take the mountains to be poor, and the hills to be the children of the poor, the prophets and the apostles being the poor, and the children of the poor being the children of the prophets and apostles, that is, those who benefit under their authority. What was said above, will judge, and what was added below, will save, is a certain statement of how he will judge. For he will judge to save (the good), that is, to separate them from those whom he must destroy and condemn, to whom he will give health prepared to be revealed in the last time. For these say to him: Do not lose my soul to the wicked; and also: Judge me, O God!, and separate my cause from unholy people. It should be noted that it does not say: He will judge the poor people, but: he will judge the poor of the people. Where previously he said to judge your people in righteousness, and your poor in judgment, he called God's people those who give or ominous his poor; That is to say, there he only dealt with the good ones and those who are on the right side. But since in this world those on the right and those on the left are fed at the same time, who like lambs and goats must be separated at the end, he called the whole group as it is mixed under the name of people. And as the word judgment refers to in a good sense, that is, to save them, that is why it says: he will judge the poor of the people, that is, he will separate to save those who are poor in the people. We already explained above who the poor are. Let us also understand by these the needy. And he will humiliate the slanderer. Here no other is understood as Sion et filia Sion. Si autem distinctius intelligendum est; pauperes accipimus, mountains; Filios autem pauperum, colles: velut Prophetas atque Apostólos, pauperes; Filios autem eorum, id est, qui sub eorum auctoritate proficiunt, filios pauperum. Quod vero supra dictum est, ludicabit, et postea, safes faciet, quaedam velut expositio est quomodo iudicabit. Ad hoc enim judicabit, ut safes faciat, id est, a petdendis damnandisque discernat, quibus donat salutem paratam tevelari in tempore novissimo (1 Petr 1,5).

A talibus quippe illi dicitur, Ne comperdas cum impiis animam meam (Ps 25,9); et, ludica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (Ps 42,1). Considetandum etiam quod non ait, ludicabit pauperem populum; thirst, pauperes populi. Supra enim ubi dixit, ludicare populum tuum in iustitia, et pauperes tuos in iudicio, eumdem dixit populum Dei quos pauperes eius; id est, tantummodo bonds et ad dexteram partem pertinent. Quia vero in hoc saeculo simul dextri sinistrique pascuntur, qui velut agni et haedi in fine separandi sunt (Mt 25,32): totum sicut commixtus est, nomine populi nuncupavit. Et quia iudicium etiam hic in bono ponit, id est, ad safes fazandos; ideo ait, ludicabit pauperes populi: id est, eos ad salutem discernet, qui sunt in populo pauperes. Iam qui sint pauperes supra exposuimus: hos et egenos intelligamus. Et humiliabit calumniatorem. Nulius melius quam diabolus hic calumniator agnoscitur. Eius slander
Ennarrations on the Psalms

Better for a slanderer than the devil. His slander was: Does Job worship God gratuitously? Our Lord Jesus Christ, helping his people with his grace, humbles them, so that they worship God freely, that is, so that they delight in the Lord. It also humiliated him, since, not finding the devil, that is, the prince of this world, anything in Christ, he killed him for the slander of the Jews, whom the slanderer used as his instruments, working in the children of unbelief. It humiliated him because the One whom he had killed rose again, and with death took away from him the kingdom of death, in which he exercised his power in such a way, that by a man whom he deceived he had dragged everyone to condemnation by death. But he was humiliated, because if for the crime of one death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the surpassing power of grace and justice reign in life through the one Jesus Christ, who humiliated the slanderer, who alleged false crimes, perverse judges and false witnesses to condemn him who had been sent. 8 [v.5]. And it will remain in the sun (et permanebit soli) or And it will remain with the sun (permanebit cum solé). Some of our translators judged that what is written simparamenei in Greek should be better translated in this second form. If in Latin it could be expressed with a single verb, we would say compermanebit (will compermane); Therefore, since the sentence could not be expressed in Latin with a single verb or word, it was said Permanebit cum solé (will remain with the sun). Compermanebit soli (will remain with the sun) is the same as permanebit cum solé (will remain with the sun). It is not surprising that per-

May He rise with the sun by whom all things were created and without whom nothing was made; Apart from the fact that this prophecy was recorded against those who think that the Christian religion must remain victorious in this world until a certain time and that it must then cease to exist. Then it will remain with the sun as long as the sun rises and sets; That is, as long as this time lasts, the Church of God will subsist, that is, the body of Christ on earth. What he adds: and before the moon, generations of generations, he could put it this way: and before the sun; that is, and will remain and remained with the sun and before the sun; which would be understood like this: with the times and before the times. What precedes time is eternal, and only that which does not change in any time must be considered truly eternal, as the Word was in the beginning. But he preferred to symbolize the increase and decrease of mortals with the moon. Finally, when he said: Before the moon, wanting, in a certain way, to make known for what cause he recorded the moon, he says: And generations of generations, this is as if he said: Before the moon, that is, before the generations of generations, which pass through the decession and succession of mortals, these being like the waxing and waning of the moon. Therefore, what is better understood by remaining before the moon than by preceding all mortal things by immortality? For the same reason, sitting at the right hand of the Father, with the slanderer already humiliated, can conveniently be taken to remain with the sun. In this way it is understood that the Son is the splendor of the glory of the Father, as if the Father were the sun, and his splendor, the Son. This can be said of the substance

est: Numquid gratis colit lob Deum? (Iob 1,9). Humiliat autem illum Dominus Iesus, gratia sua suos adiuvans, ut gratis Deum colant, id est, delectentur in Domino (Ps 36,4). Humiliavit etiam sic: quia cum in eo diabolus, id est, ptinceps huius mundi nihil invenisset (lo 14,30), occidit per calumnias Iudaeorum; quibus est usus calumniator tanquam vasis suis, operans in filiis diffidentiae (Eph 2,2). Humiliatus est enim, quia ille quem occiderant resurrexit, et regnum abstulit mortis; cuius ille potestatem ita gerebat, ut ex uno homine quem deceperat, omnes per mortem traheret ad condemnationem. Sed humiliatus est; quoniam si ob unius delictum mors regnavit per unum, multo magis qui abundaotiam gratiae et iustitiae accipiunt, in vita regnabunt per unum Iesum Christum (Rom 5:17), qui humiliavit calumniatotem, false crimina, iniquos iudices, false tests, ut eum seguirent immittentem. 8 [v.5]. Et permanebit soli, vel permanebit cum solé, Sic enim melius interpretandum quidam nostri putaverunt, quod in graeco est autnrapo^EvEí. Quod si latine uno verb dici posset, compermanebit digandum esset: ideo quia latine verbum non potest dici; ut saltem sententia exprimeretur, dictum est, permanebit cum solé. Nihil est enim aliud compermanebit soli, quam permanebit cum solé. Quid autem mignum est permanere cum sole ei per quem facta sunt omnia, et sine

quo factum est nihil (lo 1,3); nisi quia haec ptophetia propter eos praemissa est, qui putant religionem nominis christiani usque ad certum tempus in hoc saeculo victuram, et postea nonfuturam? Permanebit ergo cum solé, quamdiu sol oritur et occidit: hoc est, quamdiu tempora ista volvuntur, non deerit Ecclesia Dei, id est, Christi corpus in terris. Quod vero adiungit, Et ante lunam, generationes generationum: potuit dicere, Et ante solem, id est, et cum solé, et ante solem; quod intelligeretur, Et cum temporibus, et ante tempora. Quod ergo tempus antecedit, aeternum est: et hoc veré habendum est aeternum, quod nullo tempore variatur, sicut in principle erat Verbum. Sed per lunam significare maluit increases defectusque mortalium. Denique cum dixisset, ante lunam; volens quodammodo expose pro qua re lunam posuerit, generations, inquit, generationum: tanquam diceret, Ante lunam, id est ante generationes generationum, quae transeünt decessione et successione mortalium, tanquam decrementis incrementisque lunaribus. Ac per hoc quid melius intelligitur permanere ante lunam, nisi omnia mortalia immortalitate praecedere? Quod etiam sic non ¡inconvenienter accipi potest, ut quod iam humiliato calumniatore sedet ad dexteram Patris, hoc sit permanere cum solé. Spiendor enim aeternae gloriae intelligitur Filius (Hebr 1,3); tanquam sol sit Pater, et splendor eius Filius eius; thirst sicut

invisible of the Creator, but not of the visible creature, in which there are celestial bodies; among which the sun stands out, from which this resemblance was taken; and terrestrial, of which the stone, the lion, the lamb, the man who has two sons, etc. are also taken as similarities. Then, the slanderer humiliated, he remains with the sun, because, having defeated the devil by the resurrection, he is seated at the right hand of the Father, where he will no longer die and death will no longer lord it over him from now on. He also remains before the moon, preceding, as the firstborn among the dead, the Church, which passes away due to death and the succession of mortal men. These are the generations of generations. Or is it perhaps understood by generations as those by which we are mortally begotten, and by generations of generations, those by which we are immortally begotten? Then this would be the Church, to which He, being the firstborn from the dead, precedes, remaining before the moon, which is a figure of the Church. Certainly, what is said in Greek geneas geneon was translated by many generationis generationum (from the generation of generations), not generationes; because geneas is an ambiguous case in Greek, and it does not appear clearly whether it is genitive of the singular, tes geneas, namely, huius generationis (of generation), or accusative of the plural, las geneas, that is, has generationes (the generations). Perhaps the previously explained sense was preferred, so that, as if explaining what the moon meant, generations of generations were added (that is, a mutable thing). 9 [v.6].
like rain on fleece,

like drizzle that drips on the earth. He remembered and warned what was done for Judge Gideon, with Christ as his goal. Gideon asked the Lord for a sign, consisting of placing a fleece on the threshing floor and that if it rained it would get wet by itself, leaving the threshing floor dry; He also asked the opposite sign that, when the threshing floor got wet when it rained, only the dry fleece would remain. This symbolized: that the first people of Israel were, like the dry fleece, placed on the threshing floor, that is, in the middle of the globe of the earth. Therefore Christ Himself descended as rain on the fleece while the ground was still dry, and therefore He said: I have not been sent except to the sheep that perished of the house of Israel. From there he chose the mother from whom he was to take the form of a servant in which he appeared to men. From there he chose the disciples, to whom he commanded the same thing, saying to them: Do not go to the way of the Gentiles, nor enter the cities of the Samaritans; Go first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. When he says go first to the sheep; He showed that later, when it was time to rain on the threshing floor, they would also go to the other sheep, which did not come from the ancient people of Israel; of which he says: I have other sheep that are not of this fold; I also have to bring them, so that there is only one flock and one shepherd. Hence the Apostle also says: I say, then, that Christ was a minister of circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises of the patriarchs. In this way the rain descended on the fleece, leaving the threshing floor still dry. But as the Apostle continues and says: But the nations will glorify God for mercy's sake, so that when the time comes, it will be fulfilled.

Ergo humiliato calumniatore permanet cum sole; quia victo diabolo per resurrectionem, sedet ad dexteram Patris (Mark 16,19), ubi iam non morí tur, et mors ei ultra non dominabitur (Rom 6,9). If we read what the prophet says: The people whom I did not know served me and obeyed me by hearsay, we see that, the Jewish nation having been dried up from the grace of Christ, the entire world was flooded among all peoples by clouds full of Christian grace. In other words: he pointed to the same rain when, referring to the earth and not the fleece, he said: Drizzle that drips on the earth. But what is rain if not drops of water that fall to the ground? I believe that the Jewish nation was symbolized under the name of fleece either because it had to be stripped of the authority of teaching, as a sheep is stripped of its woolen fleece, or because it retained in a secret place the same rain, which it did not want to be preached to the foreskin, that is, it did not want to be manifested to the uncircumcised Gentiles. 10 [v. 7]. In his days justice and abundance will be born until the moon disappears. The Greek verb that appears in the codices, antanairece, was translated into Latin as it seemed to each translator: and so, some wrote tollatur (let it be removed); others, auferatur (let it be dissipated), and others, extollatur (let it be lifted up). Those who translated it by tollatur or by auferatur do not completely disagree. Tollatur is used rather, according to custom, to remove something by making it disappear than to make it elevated; and auferatur is almost only used to indicate that it be destroyed, that is, that it ceases to exist; and extollatur, so that it may be raised higher. This last verb, when used in a bad sense, usually means pride, as we see where it is said: Noli extolli in sapientia tua (Do not be conceited in your wisdom). When used in a good sense, it indicates higher honor, as when something is exalted;

Accordingly, it was written in noctibus extollite: In the nights raise your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the Lord. Then, if here we understand that it was said auferatur, what would we express when saying doñee auferatur luna but that it be destroyed in such a way that it does not exist or that it disappears completely? Perhaps he wanted this to be understood, indicating that there will be no more mortality when the last enemy death is destroyed, so that the abundance of peace will last until then so that something coming from the weakness of mortality will not oppose the happiness of the blessed, which will take place in that century of which we have a faithful promise from God through Jesus Christ our Lord, of whom it is said: In his days justice and abundant peace will be born, until, death having been completely conquered and destroyed, it will be all mortality assumed. On the contrary, if the word moon does not symbolize the mortality of the flesh, which the Church is now going through, but rather the Church itself, which remains eternally free from this mortality, in such a way that justice and an abundance of peace will be born in its days until the moon is elevated, as if it were said: In its days justice will be born, which will overcome the contradiction and rebellion of the flesh; and peace will be established, increasing and exceedingly abundant until the moon is lifted up, that is, until the Church is lifted up by the glory of the resurrection, which is to reign with Him who, as the firstborn among the dead, preceded it in this glory, sitting at the right hand of the Father. In this way he (Christ) remains with the sun before the moon, where the moon (that is, the Church) will also be elevated later.

per Piophetam dicit, Populus quem non cognovi servivit mihi: in obauditu auris obedivit mihi (Ps 17,45): videmus iam gratia Christi siccam remansisse gentem Iudaeorum, totumque orbem terrarum in ómnibus gentibus christianae gratiae plenis nubibus complui. Alio quippe verb eamdem pluviam significavit, dicens, Guttae stillantes; non iam super vellus, sed super terram. Quid est enim aliud pluvia quam guttae stillantes? Ideo autem illam gentem velleris nomine mean puto, vel quia exspolianda fuet auctoritate doctrinae, sicut ovis exspoliatur vellere; vel quia in abdito eamdem pluviam detinebat, quam nolebat praeputio praedicari, id est, iticircumcisis gentibus reveali. 10 [v.7]. Orietur in diebus eius iustitia et abundantia pacis, doñee tollatut luna. Id quod dictum est, tollatur, alii interpretati sunt, auferatur: alii vero, extollatur; unum verbum graecum sicut unicuique visum est, transfetentes, quod ibi positum est, ávravmpedr). Sed qui dixerunt, tollatur, et qui dixerunt, auferatur, non usque adeo dissonant. Tollatur enim magis habet consuetudo ita dici, ut auferatur et non sit, quam ita ut altius elevetur; auferatur vero prorsus aliter intelligi non potest, nisi ut periatur, hoc est, ut non sit: extollatur autem nihil nisi ut altius elevetur. Quod quidem cum in malo ponitur, superbiam solet significare; sicuti est: In tua sapientia noli extolli (Eccli 32,6). In bonus autem ad

honorem pertinet broadrem, velut cum aliquid elevatur; sicuti est: In noctibus extollite manus vestras in sancta, et benedicite Dominum (Ps 133,2). Hic ergo si auferatur dictum intellexerimus, quid erit doñee auferatur luna, nisi efficiatur ut non sit? Fortassis enim hoc intelligi voluit, ne ulterius sit mortalitas, quando novissima inimiea destruetur mors (1 Cor 15:26): ut pacis abundantia usque ad hoc perducatur, ne quid resistat felicitati beatorum ex infirmitate mortalitatis; quod erit in iilo saeculo, cuius tenemus fidelem promissionem Dei per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum, de quo dicitur, Orietur in diebus eius iustitia et abundantia pacis: doñee morte omnino devicta atque destructa, omnis mortalitas absumatur. Sin vero vocabulo lunae, non mortalitas carnis per quam nunc transit Ecclesia, sed ipsa omnino Ecclesia significata est, quae permaneat in aeternum, ab hac mortalitate liberata; ita dictum accipiendum est, Orietur in diebus eius iustitia et abundantia pacis, doñee extollatur luna, tanquam diceretur: Orietur in diebus eius iustitia, quae contradictionem ac rebellionem carnis vincat, et fiet pax in tantum crescens et abundans, doñee luna extollatur, id est, elevetur Ecclesia, per gloriam resurrectionis cum illo regnatura, qui eam in hac gloria primogeni tus a mortuis antecessit, ut separet ad dexteram Patris (Mark 16,19); ita cum sole permanens ante lunam, quo postea extolleretur et luna.

11 [v. 8]. And he will rule from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth. This is understood from the one who had previously said: In his days justice and abundance of peace will be born until the moon is raised. If here it is correctly understood, under the name of the moon, symbolized by the Church, it most aptly shows how widely the Church itself had to be spread by saying and will dominate from sea to sea, since the great marque that is called ocean surrounds the earth and, penetrating somewhat between the earth, forms these seas that are known to us and that are furrowed by ships. Therefore, by saying from sea to sea, he declared that he was to dominate from one end of the earth to the other, whose name and power were to be announced and have great effectiveness in all the roundness of the earth. So that sea to sea cannot be understood in any other way, he then added: and from the river to the limits of the roundness of the earth. Then what he says: to the limits of the roundness of the earth, he said previously when writing from sea to sea. From what is now recorded: from the river, he clearly demonstrated where Christ wanted to manifest his power and from where he began to choose disciples; namely, from the Jordan River, where, as the Holy Spirit descended on the Lord who had just been baptized, the voice from heaven sounded, saying: This is my Son, the Beloved. Then, from here, his teaching and the authority of the celestial magisterium begin to expand, extending to the ends of the roundness of the earth as the Gospel of the kingdom is preached throughout the world as a testimony to all people. Then the end will come.

12 [v. 9]. The Ethiopians will fall before Him, and His enemies will lick the earth. Taking the part for the whole, he designated all the nations as the Ethiopians, preferring to name the nation that in a very particular way is found at the ends of the earth. It was said that they will prostrate themselves before Him, manifesting that they will worship Him. But since schisms were to appear in various parts of the earth that would look with evil on the Catholic Church, spread throughout the whole earth, and since the same schisms were to be divided among themselves according to the names of men, and since by loving the men by whom the schisms were established, the glory of Christ, which is spread throughout the whole earth, was to be fought, therefore, after saying: the Ethiopians will fall before Him, he added: and their enemies they will lick the earth; that is, they will love men, depriving Christ of glory, to whom it was said: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; and over all the earth your glory. That is why man deserved to hear: You are earth, and to earth you will go. Therefore, licking this earth, that is, delighting in the vain authority of such men, he opposed the divine word, with which it was prophesied that the Catholic Church was to exist not in one part of the earth, like any schism, but that it was to extend throughout the world, multiplying and growing even to the Ethiopians themselves, that is, to the last and most hidden confines of men. 13 [v. 10-11]. The kings of Tarshish and the Isles will offer him gifts; The kings of Arabia and Sheba will bring him gifts. And all the kings of the earth will worship him and all nations will serve him.

11 [v.8]. Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a lumine usque ad terms orbis terrae. De quo utique dixerat: Orietur in diebus eius iustitia et abundantia pacis, doñee extollatur luna. Si Ecclesia hic recte significatur vocabulo lunae, consequenter ostendit quam late eamdem Ecclesiam fuet diffusurus, cum adiecit: Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare. Mari quippe magno cingitur terra, qui vocatur Oceanus; de quo influit quiddam exiguum in medio terrarum, et facit ista maria nota nobis, quae navigiis frequentantur. Proinde, a mari usque ad mare, a quolibet fine terrae, usque ad quemlibet finem dominaturum dixit, cuius nomen et potestas toto orbe fuerant praedicanda,.multumque valitura. Quod ne aliter posset intelligi, a mari usque ad mare; continuous subiecit, et a flumine usque ad terms orbis terrae. Quod ergo ait, usque ad terms orbis terrae; hoc ante dixerat, a mari usque ad mare. Quod vero never ait, a illumine; evidenter expressit inde voluisse Christum potestatem suam iam commendare, unde et disciples coepit elect you; a flumine scilicet Iordane, ubi super baptizatum Dominum cum descenderet Spiritus sanctus, sonuit vox de cáelo: Hic est Filius meus dilectus (Mt 3,17). Hinc ergo doctrina eius incipiens et magisterii caelestis auctoritas, dilatatur usque ad terms orbis terrae, cum praedicatur Evangelium regni inuniverse orbe, in testimonium omnibus gentibus; et tune veniet finis.

12 [v.9]. Coram illo decident Aethiopes, et inimici eius terram lingent. Per Aethiopes, a parte totum, omnes gentes significavit; eam eligens gentem, quam potissimum nominaret, quae in finibus terrae est. Coram illo procident, dictum est, adorabunt eum. Et quia schismatafutura erant per diverse terrarum loca, quae inviderent Ecclesiae catholicae toto terrarum orbe diffusae; eadem porro schismata per hominum nomina se fuerant divisura, et, homines amando quibus auctoribus scissa sunt, gloriae Christi, quae per omnes terras est, inimicatura: ideo cum dixisset, Coram illo decident Aethiopes; adiunxit, et inimici eius terram lingent; id est, homines amabunt, ut invideant gloriae Christi, cui dictum est, Exaltare super cáelos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua (Ps 107,6). Homo quippe audire meruit: Terra es, et in terram ibis (Gen 3,19). Hanc terram lingendo, id est, talium auctoritate vaniloqua delectati, eos amando, et in suavissimos habendo, contradicunt divinis eloquiis, quibus catholica Ecclesia praenuntiata est, non in aliqua parte terrarumfutura, sicut quaelibet schismata; thirst in universe world fructifying atque crescendo, usque ad ipsos Aethiopes, extremes videlicet et teterrimos hominum, perventura. 13 [v.10-11]. Reges Tharsis et insulae doll offerent; reges Arabum et Saba dona adducent. Et adorabunt eum omnes reges terrae; ownes gente servient ei. Hoc iam non expositorem, sed contemplatorem
