gifts. This does not need an expositor, but an observer; In fact, it is not only seen by the gaze of the joyful faithful, but also by the contemplation of the crying unbelievers. Unless perhaps we should ask why it was said dona adducent (they will bring or lead gifts), since those who can walk are usually led. Are they perhaps sacrificial victims? May God not allow such justice to appear in your days. These gifts that were predicted are to be led, it seems to me that they symbolize the men, whom the royal power leads to the society of the Church of Christ even when the kings who persecute them have presented these gifts ignoring what they did when they sacrificed the holy martyrs. 14 [v.12}. When declaring why kings should give him so much honor and why all nations would serve him, he says: Because he delivered the needy from the powerful and the poor who had no supporter. This poor and needy is the people of those who believe in Him. In this people there are kings who adore Him, because they do not disdain being poor and indigent, that is, of humbly confessing their sins and manifesting that they need the glory and grace of God so that the king, the king's son, can free them from the powerful. The powerful is he who above was called a slanderer, whose strength did not make him powerful to subdue men and hold them in captivity, but the sins of men. But whoever defeated the slanderer and entered the strong man's house to destroy his belongings, having tied him up, this same man freed the poor from the powerful and the poor who had no supporter. This could not be done by anyone's strength, or desiderat; imo non solum laetantium fidelium, sed etiam infidelium gemmentium infertur aspectibus: nisi fortasse quaerendum est quid dictum sit, dona adducent. Ea quippe adduci solent, quae ambulare possunt. Numquidnam ergo de immolandis victimis dici potuit? Absit ut talia oriatur in diebus eius iustitia. Sed ista dona quae adducenda praedicta sunt, homines mihi videntur significare, quos in societatem Ecclesiae Christi regum adducit auctoritas; quamvis reges etiam persequentes dona adduxerint, non scientes quid facerent sanctos martyres immolando. 14 \y.\2\.

Cum vero exposeet causes cur ei tantus honor deferretur a regibus, eique serveretur ab omnibus gentibus: Quia liberavit, inquit, egenum a potent, et pauperem cui non erat adiutor. Iste egenus et pauper, populus est credentium in eum. In hoc populo sunt etiam reges adorantes eum. Non enim egeni esse dedignantur et paupéres, id est humiliter peccata confitentes, et egentes gloria et gratia Dei, ut eos rex ille, filius Regis, liberet a potent. idem quippe est potens, ille qui superius calumniator est dictus: quem potentam ad homines sibi subdendos et in captivitate retinendos non virtus eius fecit, sed humano peccata. idem ipse et fortis est dictus; ideo et hic potens. Sed qui humiliavit calumniatorem, et intravit in domum fortis, ut eo alligato vasa eius diriperet (Mt 12,29), hic liberavit egenum a potent, et pauperem cui non erat adiutor. Non enim hoc efficere potuit vel cuiusquam

of any just man, or of any angel. There being no helper, He came and delivered them. 15 [v. 13]. It will be thought that if man, because of his sins, was held by the devil, perhaps his sins pleased Christ, who freed the helpless from the powerful. There is no such thing. On the contrary, he forgives the poor and the destitute, that is, he forgives the sins of the humble, who does not trust in his merits nor expect health from his strength, but longs for the grace of his Savior because of his destitution. By adding: and he will save the souls of the poor, he recommended both helps of grace: the remission of sins when he says: Verdona to the poor and the destitute, and the participation of justice when he added: and he will save the souls of the poor. No one is able to acquire health by himself, the health that is perfect righteousness, unless the grace of God helps, since the fullness or fulfillment of the law is brought about only by charity, which is not found in us by us, but is infused into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. 16 [v.14}. Redeem their souls from usury and iniquity. What are these usuries if not sins, which are also called debts? I think he called them usury because much greater evil is committed in torture than in sin. For example, the murderer only kills the body of the man, since he cannot harm the soul in any way; However, he throws his own body and soul into hell. Because of this class of despisers of the present mandate and those who mock the future torture, it was said: When I come I will demand with usury. Of this virtus, vel quisquam homo iustus, vel aliquis Angelus. Cum ergo nullus esset adiutor, ipse adveniens safes fecit eos. 15 [v.13]. Occurrebat autem, Si propter peccata homo tenebatur a diabolo, numquidnam Christo qui eruit egenum a potent, peccata placuerunt? Absit: thirst, Parcet ipse inopi et pauperi; Id est, peccata dimittet humili, et non de suis mentís confidenti, aut de sua virtute salutem speranti, sed indigenti gratia Salvatoris sui. Cum autem addidit, at animas pauperum salvas faciet, utrumque adiutorium gratiae commendavit; et quod est in remissíonem peccatorum, cura ait, Parcet pauperi et inopi; et quod est in participatione iustitiae, cum addidit, Et animas pauperum salvas faciet.

Nemo enim sibi est idoneus ad salutem, quae salus est perfection iustitia, nisi Dei adiuvet gratia; quia plenitudo Legis non est nisi charitas, quae non a nobis existit in nobis, sed diffusion in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum qui datus est nobis (Rom 5,5). 16 [v.14]. Ex usuris et iniquitate redeemet animas eorum. Quae sunt istae usurae, nisi peccata, quae etiam debita nominantur? (Mt 6,12). Usuras autem appellatas puto, quia plus mali invenitur in suppliciis, quam commissum est in peccatis. Nam, verbi gratia, cum homicida corpus tantum hominis perimat, animae autem nocere nihil possit; Ipsius et anima et Corpus perditur in gehenna. Propter huiusmodi contemptores praesentis praecepti, et irrisores futuri supplicii dictum est: Ego veniens,

The souls of the poor are freed from usury by the blood that was shed in remission of sins. Redeem usury by forgiving sins, which required greater punishments; redeems from iniquity by helping through grace to work justice. Thus, the two things that were said above are repeated. What was said in the previous verse: Forgive the poor and the needy, is now also said when writing about usury; and what was previously said; and will save the souls of the poor, it seems to have been said here by adding and from iniquity, meaning in both words redeems, since, by forgiving, he redeems from usury, and, by saving souls, he redeems from iniquity. Therefore, as he forgives the poor and the needy and saves the souls of the poor, so he redeems their souls from usury and iniquity. And his name will be honored before them. His name is honored by the receipt of so many benefits who respond that it is just and worthy to give thanks to the Lord, their God. What some codices write: And their name will be honored in their presence, can be understood in this way: that, even when despicable Christians appear in this world, their name is honored in the presence of Him who gave them not to remember their names nor to pronounce them by those who were previously named when they were chained to the superstitions of the Gentiles or were marked with the traces of the demerits of their evils. But now this name (of Christian) is honored in his presence even when it appears despicable to enemies. 17 [v.15]. And he will live and gold from Arabia will be given to him. It would not be said and anyone who could not say this would live, no matter how much tiemcum iisuris demandingem (Ib. 15,27). Ab his usuris redimuntur animae pauperum, sanguine illo qui fusus est in remissionem peccatorum. Redimet ergo ab usuris, remittendo peccata, quae debenbant amplificara supplicia: redimet autem ab iniquitate, adiuvando per gratiam etiam ad faciendam iustitiam. Eadem ¡taque duo repetita sunt quae supra dicta erant. Quod enim supra est, Varcet inopi et pauperi, hoc intelligitur, Ex usuris: quod vero ibi dicit, Et animas pauperum salvas faciet; hoc dictum vídetur, Ex iniquitate: ut redeemet ad utrumque sabaudiatur. Nam parcendo redeemet ab usuris; saved autem faciente redeemet ab iniquitate. Ita, cum parcet pauperi et inopi, et animas pauperum salvas faciet; sic ex usuris et iniquitate redeemet animas eorum. Et honorabile nomen eius coram ipsis.

Dant enim honorem nomini eius pro tantis beneficiis, who will respond dignum et iustum esse gradas ágete Domino Deo suo. Vel quod habent codices aliqui, Et honorabile nomen eorum coram ipso: quia etsi videntur huic saeculo contemptibiles Christiani, nomen eorum coram ipso est honorabile, qui eis illud dedit, iam non memor nominum illorum per labia sua (Ps 15,4), quibus antea vocabantur, cum essent Gentilium superstitionibus obligati, vel suorum malorum meritorum signati vocabulis, antequam essent christiani: quod nomen honorabile est coram ipso, etsi contemptibile videtur inimicis. 17 [v.15]. Et vivet, et dabitur ei de auro Arabiae. Non diceretur,

for he would live on earth, if that life were not recommended in which he will no longer die, and in which he dies it will no longer lord it over him from now on. And for this he who was despised when he died will live, since, as another prophet says, he was only separated from the life of this earth. But what does it mean and will he be given gold from Arabia? If Solomon received gold from there, however, in this psalm this was applied figuratively to another true Solomon, that is, to the true Pacific, since he did not dominate from the river to the ends of the roundness of the earth. Then in this way it was prophesied that the wise men of this world would also believe in Christ. By Arabia we understand the Gentiles; for gold, wisdom, which stands out among all disciplines like gold among other metals. Hence it was written: Receive prudence as silver, and wisdom as purified gold. And they will always ask of Him: what is said in Greek peri autou, some translated as of Him; others, by Himself or by Him. What does it mean about Him if not what we ask when we say your kingdom come to us? The coming of Christ will put the kingdom of God in view of the faithful. It is difficult to understand how it is understood by Him, unless it is said that, when one prays or asks for the Church, one prays for Him, because it is His body, since that great sacrament was understood from the Church and from Christ: They will be two in one flesh. What follows: all day long, that is, at all times I will bless him, is very clear. 18 [v.16].
And there will be support
on the ground, on the tops

Et vivet (de quo enim non posset dici hoc quantulocumque spatio temporis vivosente in hac terra?) nisi illa vita commendaretur, in qua iam non moritur, et mors ei ultra non dominabitur (Rom 6,9). Atque ideo et vivet qui contemptus est moriens: quoniam sicut alius propheta dicit, Tolletur de terra vita eius (Is 53,8; cf. Acts 8,33). Sed quid est, et dabitur ei de auro Arabiae? Nam quod inde aurum etiam ille Salomón accepit, in hoc psalmo figúrate transiectum est in alium verum Salomonem, id est verum pacificum: non enim ille dominatus est a illumine usque ad terms orbis terrae. Sic ergo prophetatum est, etiam sapientes huius mundi in Christo Fuisse credituros. Per Arabiam autem Gentes intelligimus: per aurum sapientiam, quae ita excellit Inter omnes doctrinas, ut aurum inter metalla; unde scriptum est, Acápite prudentiam sicut argentum, et sapientiam sicut aurum probatum (Prov 8,10.11). Et orabunt de ipso semper. Quod habet graecus, TTEPÍ aü-roO, aliqui interpretad sunt, ie ipso; aliqui, pro ipso, sel pro eo. Quid est autem, de ipso, nisi forte quod oramus dicentes: Adveniat regnum tuum? (Mt 6,10). Christi namque adventus praesentabit fidelibus regnum Dei. 1 [v.l]. Hear, hear, dear children of the body of Christ, you who have the Lord, your God, for your hope and do not set your eyes on vanities and false follies. This psalm has by inscription, that is, by title, the following words: The hymns of David, son of Jesse, are finished. Psalm for Asaph. In all the psalms that we have in whose titles the name of David was recorded, son of Jesse was never added except in this one. Which must be believed that it was not done without foundation and in vain, since at all times the Lord admonishes us and incites us to understand the pious propensity of charity. What does it mean that the hymns of David son of Jesse ended? Hymns are praises of God with song; Hymns are songs that contain praises of God. If there is praise and it is not from God, there is no hymn; If there is praise and it is from God and it is not sung, there is no hymn. Therefore, it is necessary for it to be a hymn that it has these three things: praise, God and song. What does it mean the hymns are over? The praises sung to God are over. It seems that something cumbersome and sad has been announced. Whoever sings praises, not only praises, but praises with joy. He who sings praises not only sings, but also loves the one to whom he sings. In praise there is exaltation on the part of the one who praises, and in the song, affection of the lover.

1 [v.l.] The title of this psalm is the following: Of intelligence to Asaph. Asaph is translated in Latin as congregationtio (congregation or meeting); in Greek, for synagogue. Let's see what the synagogue understood. First let us know what the synagogue is, and from here we will understand what the synagogue understood. Every meeting is designated by the generic name of synagogue. Hence the word synagogue can be understood as a gathering of men or animals. But the meeting that is currently being talked about is not about animals, since we hear the word intelligence. Hear what was said of the man who, placed in honor, despised laudes tuas: sed ubi? In atriis filiae Zion; quia praedicatio Dei praeter Ecclesiam inanis est. Parum est laudare Deum, et annuntiare omnes laudes eius: ln atriis filiae Sion annuntia. Ad unitatem tende, noli dividere populum; sed rape ad uaiira, et fac unum. Oblitus sum quamdiu dixi. Iam finito Psalmo, et ex isto odore coniicio me diuturnum habuisse sermonem: sed studiis vestris non sufficio; violenti estis nimis: utinam ista violentia rapiatis regnum caelorum!

Nos autem intelligamiis primitus synagogam; exinde intelligemus quid intellexerit synagoga. As he expected earthly happiness, according to the promises of God referring to the Old Testament, when he saw that the wicked were swimming in it and that those who did not worship God had great preponderance in the riches that he expected to receive from God, when he thought that he was serving God for no reason, his feet wavered; for there it says: Behold the sinners, who abound in riches in the world. Then in vain did I justify my heart? See how his steps almost slipped, so that the soul asks itself: What use was there in serving God? God, since he is happy, who does not serve him? The psalm from which I took this testimony precedes the one we are discussing. 2. In a good situation it happened, but not because of our order, but because of God's economy, that we now heard in the Gospel: The law was given by Moses, but grace and truth were due to Jesus Christ. If we scrutinize the two Testaments, the New and the Old, we see that they do not contain the same sacraments or the same promises; However, they have many of the same precepts. For you shall not kill, you shall not fornicate, you shall not steal; honor your father and mother; You will not bear false witness, you will not covet another's property, you will not desire your neighbor's wife, it was also commanded to us. And whoever does not observe them will go astray and will not be worthy at all to ascend the holy mountain of God, of which it was said: Who will dwell in your tabernacle or who will rest in your holy mountain? The innocent of hands (that is, of works) and the pure of heart. If we examine the precepts, we see that either they are all the same or there are only a few in the Gospel that the prophets did not record. The precepts are the same (in both Testaments); promises and sacraments are different. Let's see why the precepts are the same: because, according to them, we must serve God. The sacraments are different because some are the sacraments that give health and others are those that promise the Savior. The sacraments of the New Testament give health, those of the Old promise the Savior. Having already promised, why should we look for what is promised? You already have the Savior. I say that you already have what was promised, not because we have already received eternal life, but because vino felicem esse quia servio? Ule autem psalmus cuius testimonium produxi, praecedit istum quem nunc in manibus habemus. 2. (Ps 14:1). Innocem manibus, et mundo corde (Ps 23,4). Discussa ergo praecepta, aut omnia eadem inveniuntur, aut vix aliqua in Gospel quae non dicta sint a Prophetis. Christ, whom the prophets announced. The sacraments were changed; Other simpler ones were established, in smaller numbers, healthier, more fertile. Why are the promises different? For the land of Canaan was promised, a fertile land, abundant in fruit, abundant in milk and honey; A temporal kingdom, earthly happiness, a large family, the subjugation of enemies were promised. All these things belong to earthly happiness. But why was it appropriate to promise this first? Because the spiritual is not first, but the animal, and then the spiritual. The first man, who comes from the earth, is earthly; the second, which comes from heaven, is celestial; what is the earthly, such are the earthly, and what is the heavenly, such are the heavenly. Just as we bear the image of the earth, let us bear the image of him who is from heaven. The Old Testament belongs to the image of the land; the New, in the image of the celestial. But so that no one thinks that the earthly man was made by one and the heavenly man by the other, God, showing that he was the creator of both, also wanted to be the author of the two Testaments, promising earthly things in the Old, and heavenly things in the New. But for how long have you been an earthly man? How much do you like earthly things? Perhaps because certain childhood things are given to the child, with which he does not divert his attention from games, should they not be taken out of his hands when he becomes older so that he can dedicate himself to something more useful that suits the adolescent? No doubt you yourself gave your son tentia nuts, habens iam Salvatorem? Hoc dico, teneas promissa, non quod iam acceperimus vitatn aeternam; sed quia iam venerit Christus, qui per Prophetas praenuntiabatur. Mutata sunt Sacramenta; facta sunt faciliora, pauciora, salubriora, feliciora. Promissa quare non eadem? Quia promissa est terra Chanaan, terra copiosa, fructuosa, affluens lacte et melle; promissum regnum temporale, promissa felicitas saeculi, promissa fecunditas filíorum, promissa subiectio inimicorum (Ex 3,8): haec omnia ad terrenam felicitatem pertinent. Sed quare ipsa primo promitti oportebat? Quia "non primo quod spiíituale est, sed quod ánímale; postea", inquit, "spirituale.

being a child, and the book being big. Therefore, because God tore from the hands of his children, through the New Testament, those things that were like children's toys, to give them something more useful when they grew up, it must be thought that He himself did not give them those first ones. 3. Therefore you should not be attached to earthly things even if God gives them. However, because we should not adhere to them, we should not believe that they are given by someone other than God. He gives them; But you should not expect them from Him as if they were the supreme good, since He also gives them to the evil one. If I gave them as the only good, I would not give them to the wicked. But He also wanted to give them to the bad so that the good would learn to obtain from Him something else that He does not give to the bad. Those unfortunate ones who apply themselves to temporal things and do not care about him who made heaven and earth and who gave them earthly goods, and who temporarily delivered them from the captivity of Egypt, and led them through the middle of the Red Sea, and buried in the waters the enemies who pursued them; those, I repeat, who did not worry that he would give them, when they grew up, also the heavenly goods, as he gave them the earth.

Being small, fearing to lose what they had received, they killed the one who gave it to them. We say these things, brothers, so that, as men of the New Testament, you may learn not to attach your hearts to earthly goods. For if those to whom the New Testament had not yet been revealed clung inexcusably to temporal goods, how much more inexcusably do those to whom the heavenly promises have already been revealed in the New Testament pursue earthly things! Remember, brothers, what was said by the persecutors of Christ: If we let him go free, the Romans will come and take away our place and our nation. See how, fearing to lose earthly things, they killed the King of heaven. And what happened to them? They also lost their earthly goods, and where Christ was killed, there they were killed. Not wanting to lose the earth, they killed the Giver of life, and, having been killed, they lost the earth itself, which happened at the same time that they killed him, so that by the same temporal circumstance they would be warned why they suffered these things. For when the city of the Jews was razed, they were celebrating the Passover, and there were many thousands of men who had gathered from the Jewish nation to celebrate the Passover festival. So, God, through the evil ones, but being good; through the unjust, being just, he took revenge on them in such a way that many thousands of Jews died and the city was devastated. This is what Asaph's knowledge laments in this psalm; and in the same cry, as if understanding, he discerns material goods from heavenly ones, distinguishes the Old Testament from the New,

Deus per Novum Testamentum excussit de manibus filiorum, ut aliquid utilius daret grandescentibus, propterea priora illa non ipse dedisse putandus est: ipse utrumque dedit. Sed Lex ipsa per Moysen data est; Gratia et veritas per lesum Christum jacta est (lo 1,17): gratia, quia impletur per charitatem quod per litteram iubebatur; veritas, quia redditur quod promittebatur. Hoc ergo intellexit Asaph iste. Denique omnia quae Iudaeis promissa fuerant, ablata sunt. Ubi est regnum eorum? ubi templum? ubi unctio? ubi priests? Did you help the Prophetae? Ex quo venit qui per Prophetas praedicabatur, in illa gente iam nihil horum est; iam lost terrena, et nondum quaerit caelestia. 3. Inhaerere ergo terrenis, quamvis ea Deus donet, you should not. Verumtamen non quia inhaerere eis non debenmus, alium ea daré, nisi Deum, credere debenmus; ipse ea dat; sed noli pro magno exspectare ab eo bonum, quod dat et non bono. Nam si pro magno ea daret, malis ea non daret. Ideo autem ea voluit daré et malis, ut discant boni aliud ab eo quaerere, quod non dat et malis. lili autem inhaerentes terrenis miseri, et non de illo praesumentes qui fecit caelum et terram, qui eis dedit et ipsa terrena, qui eos etiam temporaliter de Aegypti captivitate liberavit, qui eos per divisum mare duxit, qui eorum inimicos persequentes fluctibus obruit (Ex 14,22.28); non in illo praesumentes qui

daret utique caelestia grandibus, sicut terrena parvulis dedit, unientes will lose quod acceperant, occiderunt qui dederat. Si enim illi inexcusabiliter terrenis inhaeserunt, quibus ipsum Novum Testamentum nondum fuet revelatum; quanto inexcusabilius terrena sectantur, quibus iam promissa caelestia in New Testament revealsa sunt! Nam recolite, fratres mei, quid dictum sit a persequentibus Christum. Si dimiserimus eum, venient Romani, et tollent nobis, et locum, et gentem (lo 11,48). so that you can see why things have to happen, what you have to wait for, what to abandon and which ones you have to adhere to. It begins like this: 4. Oh God, why did you reject us forever? Did you reject forever? He speaks on behalf of the Jewish people, of the congregation that is properly called a synagogue. Oh God, why did you reject us forever? He does not censure, but rather asks: Why? For what reason, for what reason did you do this? What did you do? You rejected us forever. What does forever mean? Maybe until the end of the world. Or perhaps you turned us away from Christ, which is the end for every believer? O God, why then did you reject us forever and did your spirit become angry with the sheep of your flock? Why were you angry with the sheep of your flock if it were not because we adhered to earthly things and did not recognize the shepherd? 5. Remember your congregation that you possessed from the beginning. Could this be the voice of the Gentiles? Did he possess the Gentiles from the beginning? He possessed the seed of Abraham, the people of Israel, according to the flesh, born of the patriarchs, our fathers, of whom we became children, not coming from the flesh, but imitating faith. Your own congregation, the rod of your inheritance, you redeemed. He called the same congregation the rod of inheritance. What sign did he give to Moses when Moses said to him: What sign shall I give them that they may believe that you have sent me? And God said to him: What have you in your hand? This is why the Church was admonished to avoid the beginning or origin of sin. What is the beginning or origin of sin, which is like the head of the serpent? The beginning or origin 15 [v.131- Iam ergo Asaph corrects you ad intellectum; dic nobis qualem salutem operatus est Deus in medio terrae. Cum illa terrena vestra salus eversa est, quid fecit? quid promise? You confirmed in virtute your death. Tanquam gente Iudaeorum velut arida a fluctibus separata, mate in amaritudine sua Gentes erant, terramque illam undique circumluebant: ecce confirmasti in virtute tua mare, et remansit tetra sitiens imbrem tuum. You confirmed in virtute your mare: contrivisti capita draconum in aqua. Draconum capita, daemoniorum superbias, a quibus Gentes possidebantur, contrivisti super aquam; quia eos quos possidebant, tu pet Baptismum liberasti. 16 [v.14]. Quid adhuc post capita draconum? lili enim dtacones habent principern suum, et ipse primus est magnus draco. Et de illo quid fecit qui operatus est salutem in medio terrae?

Audi: Tu confregisti caput draconis. Cuius dtaconis? Intelligimus dtacones omnia daemonia sub diabolo militantia: quem ergo singularem draconem cuius caput confractum est, nisi ipsum diabolum intelligere debenmus? Quid de illo fecit? Tu confregisti caput draconis. Illud est initium peccati. Caput illud est quod accepit maledictum, ut semen Evae observeet caput serpentis (Gen 3:5). Admonita est enim Ecclesia initium peccati devitare. Quod est initium peccati, tanquam caput serpentis? Initium omnis peccati superbia (Eccli 10,15). Conftactum est ergo caput draconis; confracta est

of all sin is pride. Then the head of the dragon was broken, the diabolical pride was pulverized. And what did he who brought about health in the midst of the earth make of him? You gave it to the Ethiopian people as food. What is this? Who are the Ethiopian peoples? All the Gentiles. The Gentiles are admirably personified in the blacks, since the Ethiopians are black. Then the Gentiles were called to faith because they were black; Without a doubt, these were called to faith, for it was said to them: Once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. These were certainly called being black, but not so that they would remain black, since of these the Church is formed, to which it is said: Who is this that ascends whitened? What happened to the black woman? What was written: I am black, but beautiful. And how did they receive this dragon for food? I think more like receiving Christ for food; but to Christ to perfect themselves with Him, to the devil to destroy Him in themselves. Hence that calf whom the disloyal and apostate people worshiped when they claimed the gods of Egypt and rejected the one who freed them from Egyptian servitude, originated that great sacrament. For Moses was so angry against those who honored and worshiped the idol, that, inflamed with zeal for God, he took temporary revenge, frightening them to avoid perpetual death. However, he threw the calf into the fire, destroyed it and reduced it to dust and mixed it with water, which he gave to the people to drink; In this way a great mystery was carried out. O prophetic wrath, O spirit not altered, but enlightened! What did he do? First he throws it into the fire so that it loses the shape of a calf, then he reduces it to dust so that it can be consumed with some diabolical superbia. Et quid de illo fecit, qui operatus est salutem in medio terrae? Dedisti eum in escam populis Acthiopibus. Quid est hoc? How intelligo populos Aethiopes? Quomodo, nisi per hos, omnes Gentes? Et bene per nigros; Aethiopes enim nigri sunt. Ipsi vocantur ad fidem, qui nigri fuerunt; ipsi prorsus, ut dicatut eis: Fuistis enim aliquando tenebrae; nunc autem lux in Domino (Eph 5,8). Ipsi ptotsus vocantur nigri; sed ne remaneant nigri: de bis enim fit Ecclesia, cui dicitur, Quae est ista quae ascendit dealbata? (Song 8,5, sec. LXX). Quid enim de nigra factum est, nisi quod dictum est: Nigra sum, et speciosa? (Song 1,4). Et quomodo acceperunt isti in escam draconem istum?

Puto quia magis Christum acceperunt in escam: sed Christum quo se consummarent; diabolum quem consumerent. Nam inde et vitulus ille quem adoravit populus infidelis, apostata, quaerens déos Aegyptiotum, dimittens eum qui liberavit de servitute Aegyptiorum; unde agitatum est illud magnum sacramentum. Cum enim sic irasceretur Moyses colentibus et adorantibus idolum, et zelo Dei inflammatus vindicatet temporaliter, ut a morte sempiterna devitanda terreret; tamen ipsum caput vituli in ignem misit et exterminavit, comminuit, in aquam sparsit, et dedit populo bibere (Ex 32,1-20): sic factum est magnum sacramentum. O ita prophetica, et animus non tnrbatus, sed illuminatus! Quid egit? Mitte in

little by little. He throws it into the water in powder form and gives it to the people to drink. What does this mean? That the worshipers of the devil had become the body of him, just as those who recognize Christ become the body of Christ, so that it is said of them: You are the body and members of Christ. The demon's body was to be consumed, and consumed by the Israelites. The apostles were from that town, the first Church was from them. Peter had to be told about the Gentiles: Kill and eat. What does kill and eat mean? Kill what they are and make them what you are. Therefore kill and eat; For the same reason, spray and drink; Both things occurred in the same mystery, since it was certainly and without a doubt appropriate that the body that belonged to the devil, by believing, should become that of Christ. Thus the devil was consumed or destroyed by losing his own members. This was also foreshadowed in Moses' serpent. Because, when the magicians threw their staffs at Pharaoh's feet, they became dragons, just like Moses' staff, but Moses' staff devoured the staffs, turned into dragons, of all those magicians. Therefore, it must be understood that this is also now done with the body of the devil, since, when it was devoured by the Gentiles who believed in Christ, it became food for the Ethiopian peoples. It can also be understood: You gave him food to the Ethiopian people, who now all bite him. How do they bite you? Vituperating, calling names, criticizing; in the style that was said, prohibiting strictly, but, nevertheless, with complete clarity: If you bite and devour one another, see that you are not consumed by one another. What does it mean you bite and devour each other? You litigate, you dis-

you blame each other, you blame each other for your shortcomings. Then see now how the devil is consumed by these bites. Who is there, even if he is a pagan, who, being angry with his servant, does not call him satan? Observe how the devil is given for food. The Christian says this, the Jew says it, the pagan says it; He adores him, and yet he curses him. 17 [v. 15]. Let's look at the remaining things. Brothers, I beg you to attend. They are heard with great pleasure, because they have already been heard throughout the entire globe of the earth. When these things were announced, they did not exist, because then they were promised, not given; But now, how they move the spirit when we see that the things that we read announced in the Scriptures have been carried out in the world! Let's see what that one who already understood Asaph did, since he worked health in the middle of the land. You caused fountains and torrents to gush forth so that, flowing with the liquor of wisdom, the riches of faith would sprinkle the salvation of the Gentiles and convert all the unbelievers by this irrigation into the sweetness of faith. You made fountains and torrents gush forth. Perhaps fountains and torrents are different things here; Perhaps they are the same thing, because perhaps the sources would have been so copious that they would have formed rivers. You made fountains and torrents gush forth. If we consider that fountains and torrents are different, in some the word of God generates a fountain of water that springs to eternal life; In others, hearing this word, but not receiving it in such a way that they live well, yet, by not giving rest to the tongue, it becomes a torrent. Streams that do not carry water at all times are properly called torrents. Rivers are sometimes also figuratively called torrents;

ignem, ut prius confundatur forma ipsa; minutatim comminue, ut paulatim consumatur; mitte in aquam, da populo bibere. Quid est hoc, nisi quia adoratores diaboli Corpus ipsius facti erant? Quomodo agnoscentes Christum, fiunt Corpus Christi, ut eis dicatur: Vos autem estis corpus Christi et memha (1 Cor 12,27). Corpus diaboli consumandum erat, et hoc ab Israelitis consumandum. Ex illo enim populo Apostoli; ex illo prima Ecclesia. Et dictum erat Petro de Gentibus: Macta et manduca (Acts 10,13). Quid est, Macta et manduca? Occide quod sunt, et fac quod es. Hac, Macta et manduca; hac, Comminue et bibe: utrumque tamen in eodem sacramento; quia oportebat utique, et sine dubitatione oportebat, ut corpus quod erat diaboli, credendo transiret in Corpus Christi. Sic diabolus consumitur amissis membris suis. Hoc figuratum est et in serpente Moysi. Nam fecerunt magi similiter, proiectisque virgis suis exhibituerunt dracones; sed draco Moysi omnium illorum magorum virgas absorbuit (Ex 7:12). Intelligatur ergo et moda corpus diaboli: hoc fit; devoratur a Gentibus quae crediderunt, factus est esca populis Aethiopibus. Ilhd quoque intelligi potest, dedisti eum escam populis Aethiopibus: quia nunc eum omnes mordent. Quid es mordent Rebuking, blaming, accusing. comeditis invicem? Litigatis eum invicem, detrahitis invicem, opprobria obiicitis invicem. Attendite ergo nunc his morsibus I consumed diabolum. Quis non iratus servo suo, etiam paganus, dicat illi: Satan? Vide diabolum datum in escam. Hoc dicit Christianus, hoc dicit ludaeus, hoc dicit Paganus; ipsum adorat, et de ipso maledicit. 17 [v.15]. Videoamus ergo reliqua. Fratres, obsecro, intendite: eum magna voluptate audiuntur, quia audita etiam in orbe terrarum cognoscuntur. Haec quando dicebantur, non fuerunt; quia tune promittebantur, non reddebantur; I never see that voluptate afficimur, eum ea quae praedicta legimus ia libro, compleri videmus in mundo! Videamus quid fecerit, quem iam intelligit Asaph, quod operatus est salutem in medio terrae. You disrupt fonts and torrents: ut manarent liquorem sapientiae, ut manarent divitias fidei, ut irrigarent salsitatem Gentium, ut omnes infideles in fide dulcedinem sua irrigatione converterent. Disrupisti fontes et torrentes. Forte discretum est; strong unum est, quia fontes tam largi fuerunt ut illuminate facerent. You disrupted fonts and torrents. Si autem ad discretionem: in allus fit verbum Dei fons aquae salientis in vitam aetemam (lo 4,14); alii autem audientes verbum, et non sic habentes ut bene vivant, tamen non tacentes lingua, torrentes fiunt. Thus it was said: They will be drunk with the abundance of your house and you will give them to drink from the torrent of your delights; and yet this torrent will never dry up. Streams that do not carry water during the summer are properly called torrents, even though their channels fill and flow with the winter waters. When you see a believing man who must persevere to the end, who must not abandon God in temptation, who endures all discomforts for the sake of the truth, not for the sake of falsehood and error; Where do you think such vigor comes from if it is not from the word that constituted in him the source of water that leaps to eternal life? Another, on the contrary, receives the word, preaches, does not remain silent, runs, but the summer tests whether it is a fountain or a torrent. However, both water the earth through Him who wrought health in the midst of the earth. Let the fountains flow, let the torrents flow. You made torrents and fountains gush forth. 18. You dried up the rivers of Ethan. This is why we see that he makes fountains and torrents gush out and dries up rivers, so that the waters may flow there and dry up here. It dries up, he says, the rivers of Ethan. What does Ethan mean? It is a Hebrew word. What does it mean? Strong, robust. Who is this strong and sturdy one of whom God dries up the rivers? Who but that same dragon? No one enters the fort's house to destroy his trousseau if he has not first tied it to the fort. He is the strong one who, boasting of his power, abandoned God; He is the mighty one who said: I will set my throne on the north side and I will be like the Most High. From this same glass of pernicious strength He gave man drink. Those who thought they would be gods wanted to be strong.

eating the forbidden fruit. Made strong Adam is mocked: Behold Adam, who became like us. The Jews also became strong by boasting of their justice, because, ignoring the justice of God and trying to establish their own as strong, they did not submit to the justice of God. See how the man's strength became indigestible, leaving him sick, poor, isolated in the distance, with his head down, not daring to raise his eyes to heaven, beating his chest and saying: Lord, have mercy on me, a sinner. He is already sick, he already confesses his illness; It is not strong, it is dry land; water yourself with fountains and torrents. Those who boast of their strength are still strong. Let your rivers dry up; Let not the doctrine of the Gentiles, of the haruspices, of the soothsayers, of the magical arts progress, since the rivers of the fort have dried up. You dried up Ethan's rivers. Let that doctrine dry up and let our minds be flooded with the truth of the Gospel. 19 [v. 16]. Yours is the day and yours is the night. Who is ignorant of this, since He made all things, since by the Word they were all made? The same one who brought about health in the middle of the earth was told: Yours is the day and yours is the night. Here we must understand something that refers to the health that was wrought in the midst of the earth. Yours is the day. Who are these? The spiritual ones. And yours is the night; These are the carnal ones. Yours is the day and yours is the night. Let the spiritual speak spiritual things to the spiritual, for it was said: Combining spiritual things, we speak wisdom with the perfect. This sa-

Sed torrentes proprie dicuntur fluvii qui aestate deficiunt, aquis autem hiemalibus inundantur et currunt. Vides ergo hominem bene fidelem, perseveraturum usque in iinem, non relicturum Deum in omni temptatione; pro veritate, non pro falsitate et errore, omnes molestas sustinentem: hic unde sic viget, nisi quia verbum factum est in eo jons aquae salientis in vitam aetemam? Alius autem accipit verbum; Praedicat, non tacet, currit: sed aestas probat fontem aut torrentem. Tamen ex utroque rigetur terra, ab eo qui operatus est salutem in medio terrae; exundent fontes, current torrents: You disrupted fonts and torrents. 18. Your syccaiti flows Etham. Hac rumpit fontes et torrentes, hac siccat fluvios, ut inde currant aquae, et hinc aquae siccentur. Fluvios, inquit, Etham. Who is Ethan? Verbum enim hebraeum est. What does Etham interpret? Fortis, robustus. Quis est iste fortis et robustus, cuius fluvios siccat Deus? Quis, nisi ille ipse draco? Nemo enim intrat in domum fortis, ut vasa Ulitis diripiat, nisi prius alligaverit fortem (Mt 12:29). Ipse est fortis, de virtute sua praesumens, et Deum deserens; ipse est fortis, qui ait: Ponam scdem meam ad aquilonem, et ero iimilis Altissimo (Is 14,13). De ipso cauce perversae fortitudinis homini

propinavit. Fortes esse voluerunt, qui se déos futures de cibo vetito crediderunt. Factus est Adam fortis cui insultaretur: Ecce factus est Adam tanquam unas ex nobis (Gen 3,5.6.22). Fortes et Iudaei de iustitia sua ptaesumentes: Ignorantes enim Dei iustitiam, et suam iustitiam quaerentes constituere, tanquam fortes, iustitiae Dei non sunt subiecti (Rom 10,3). Videte hominem digessisse fortitudinem suam, et remansisse infirmum, inopem, longe stantem, nec oculos ad caelum levare audentem; sed percutientem pectus suum, et dicentem: Domine, propitius esto mihi peccitori (Lk 18:13). Iam infirmus est, iam infirmitatem confitetur; non est fortis: arid terra est; governs fontibus and torrentibus. lili adhuc fortes sunt, qui de virtute sua praesumunt. Siccentur illuminates eorum: non proficiant doctrinae gentium, haruspicum, mathematicorum, magicae artes; quoniam siccati sunt fluvii Fortis: Tu siccasti fluvios Etham. (1,3). lili ipsi qui operatus est salutem in medio terrae, illi dicitur: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox. Biduria is not yet perceived by the carnal, since it is said to them: I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal ones. Therefore when the spiritual ones speak to the spiritual ones, one day he speaks to another day; But since the same carnals do not remain silent about the faith of Jesus Christ crucified that children can perceive, one night announces to another night science. Yours is the day and yours is the night. To you belong the spiritual, and also the carnal; You illuminate some with immutable wisdom and truth; You console others with the manifestation of the flesh, like the moon that attenuates the darkness of the night. Yours is the day and yours is the night. Do you want to know the day? See it if you can; Elevate your mind as much as possible. Let's see if you belong to the day, let's see if your gaze no longer blinks. Can you understand what you heard now from the Gospel: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God? You don't know how to think except in the words that sound and pass. Can you already perceive the Word or the Verb, not the sound, but God? Here you heard: And the Word was God. You think of these words: All things were made by Him; and by Him those who speak were also made. What quality is this Verboo Word? Oh carnal! Do you perceive it? Reply. Do you perceive it? You don't perceive it; You still belong to the night, you need the moon so that you do not die in the darkness. Indeed, certain sinners bent the bow to shoot the upright in heart on the dark moon. Therefore, the flesh of Christ was darkened when it was taken down from the cross and placed in the tomb. Those who killed him outraged him. He had barely risen yet, and the upright disciples of heart, inter-perfect chimur, were shot with arrows (1 Cor 2:13.6). Nondum capiunt istam sapientiam carnales: Non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus (Ib. 3,1). Ergo cum spirituales spiritualibus loquuntur, Dies diei eructat verbum: cum vero et ipsi carnales non tacent fidem crucifixi Christi, quam possunt capere parvi, Nox nocti annuntiat scientiam (Ps 18,3). Tuus est dies, et tua est nox. Ad te pertinent spirituales, ad te pertinent carnales: illos illustras incommutabili sapientia et veritate; illos consolaris carnis manifestatione, tanquam luna consolans noctem. Tuus est ¿ies, et tua est nox. Vis audire diem? Vide si capis; erect quantum potes mentem tuam.

1 [v.l]. This psalm offers the medicine of humility to the swelling of pride and comforts the humble with hope. Do this so that no one vainly boasts of himself or the humble mistrusts the Lord. There is a ratified, sure, fixed, unalterable, faithful, and suspicionless promise from God that comforts the troubled. All human life on earth is, as it is written, a continuous test. And the prosperous one should not be chosen and only the adverse one avoided, but both must be carefully guarded against: the former, so that it does not ruin; this, so that it does not depress; so that any man, in whatever state he may be in this life, should have no other comfort but God, nor any other joy but his promises. This life, no matter how much happiness it is flooded with, deceives many; God to no one. Therefore, as for every man who converts to God, the delight is changed, the pleasures are changed, since they are not taken away, but are changed, for the same reason, we still do not actually possess all our pleasures in this life; but the same hope is so certain that it must take precedence over all the pleasures of this world, as it is written: Delight yourself in the Lord. Then they will proclaim what we know from the book of Wisdom, for when they see the glory of the saints, of those who, being in the world, were humbled and endured it; Of those who, upon being exalted, did not agree to such exaltation, they will say: These are the ones we once held as a derision. Then, likewise, they will exclaim: What did pride profit us? And the boasting of riches, what did it bring us? All these things passed away like a shadow. Because they boasted about corruptible things, their hope faded. On the contrary, our hope will then become reality. So that the promise of God remains complete, firm and secure in

We said from the heart with faith: Do not destroy to the end. There is no need to fear that any of the potentates will annul the promises of God. He will not nullify them, because he is true; the potentates have no power to annul them. Then let us be sure of his promises and declare now how the psalm begins. 2 [v.2]. We will confess to you, oh God! We will confess you and invoke your name. Do not invoke him before confessing; confess and invoke. You call the one you call to yourself. Well, what is invoking? Call to yourself. If it is invoked for you, that is, if it is called to you, who does it approach? It doesn't come close to being arrogant. Without a doubt He is very high; the proud cannot touch him. To reach all the highest things we climb up, and, if we still cannot reach them, we look for some artifact or some ladder so that, perched, we can reach what is high. The opposite happens with God; He is most high, and is reached by the humble. It was written: The Lord is close to those who broke his heart. The brokenness of the heart is piety, it is humility. He who is grieved is angry with himself, angry with himself, to have God favorable; He becomes a judge of himself to have God as his defender. Invoked God, he comes. Who is it coming to? Not to the arrogant. Hear another testimony: The Lord is exalted and looks at lowly things and knows high things from afar. The Lord is exalted, and looks at humble things not from afar; However, he knows the highs from afar. And so that the proud do not rejoice in impunity because it was said that he regards humble things as if they were enormous.

See what you must do; because, if he knows, he does not forgive. Better is he who forgives than he who knows. What is forgiveness but not knowing? What does it mean not to know? Do not warn. Since the warning is also a rebuke, it is often said that it is typical of the one who punishes. Hear what he who prays for forgiveness says: Turn your face from my sins. What should you do if he has turned his face away from you? It is a disastrous thing, and it must be feared that it will abandon you. On the other hand, if God does not turn away his face, he warns. That is why it is said in a psalm: Turn your face from my sins; and in another: Do not turn your face from me. There he is told: Take away my sins; here: Don't take him away from me. Then confess and invoke. Confessing cleanses the temple where the one invoked must come. Confess and invoke. psalm that admonishes you: Confess the Lord, for he is good. What does it mean because it's good? Why are you afraid to confess? It is good, forgive the one who confesses. Confession makes us humble; Draw near to the humble, you, O God, who turn away from the proud. Scripture teaches us in many places that the repetition of a sentence is its strengthening. Hence the Lord says: Truly, truly; and also in some psalms: So be it, so be it. To make the matter known it was enough to have said once: So be it; but he added another one to confirm or consolidate what was expressed. You know that Pharaoh, king of Egypt, while Joseph was already imprisoned there for the love of purity, had a dream known to all of us, consisting of seeing seven fat cows, which were devoured by seven thin ones, and seven thick ears of corn, which were devoured by seven other empty ears. How did José interpret him? If you remember, these two dreams are one. What has been seen has only one meaning, José tells him, but having seen it duplicated serves as confirmation. I said this so that you do not judge that the repetition of holy words is due to the desire for loquacity. Frequently, repetition has the force of confirmation in Holy Scripture: My heart is prepared, O God!; my heart is prepared; and in another place: Wait in the Lord and act manfully; and be comforted mino, quoniam bonus est (Ps 105,1, et 106,1). Quid est, quoniam bonus est? Quid timetis confit? bonus est; ignoscit confitenti. Exhausimus corda nostra confessione; terruisti, mundasti. Confessio nos humiles facit, propinqua humilibus, qui recedis ab excelsis. Firmamentum autem esse sententiae in repetitione, multis Scripturarum locis docemur. Inde est quod Dominus ait, Amen, amen (lo 1,51).

So that you may know what two people are like and at the same time, through the union of marriage, one, only one speaks in Isaiah and says: As a husband, he girded me with a mitre, and as a wife, he adorned me with a garment. She was called a husband in attention to the head, and a wife in attention to the body. Speak, therefore, one; Let us hear him and also speak with him. Let us be his members so that this voice can be ours too. I will tell, he says, all your wonders. Christ preaches himself, he also preaches in his already existing members to attract others, so that those who were not yet come closer and join his members, through whom the Gospel was preached; and thus a single body is formed under a single head, with one spirit and one life. 5 [v.3}. And what does it say? When I take the time, I will judge the justices. When will he judge justice? When the time had come. It's not time yet. By virtue of the grace of his mercy, he first announces justice and then judges it. For, if he wanted to judge before announcing, who would be worthy of being delivered, who would be found worthy of being acquitted? Therefore now is the time of preaching: I will narrate—he says—all your wonders. Listen to the narrator, listen to the crier, because, if you do not listen, when the time has come, I will judge loquantur, Christus loquitur: loquitur ex persona capitis, loquitur ex persona corporis. Sed quid dictum est? Erunt duo in carne una. Sacramenlum hoc magnum est; ego, inquit, dico, in Christo et in Ecclesia (Gen 2,24, et Eph 5,31.32). Et ipse in Gospel: Igitur iam non duo, sed una caro (Mt 19,6). Nam ut noveritis has duas quodammodo esse personas, et rursus unam copulatione coniugii, tanquam unus loquitur apud Isaiam, et dicit: Sicut sponso alligavit mihi mitram, et sicut sponsam induit me ornamento (Is 61,10). Sponsum se dixit ex capite, sponsam ex corpore. Loquitur ergo unus; audiamus enim, et in eo nos quoque loquamur: simus membra eius, ut haec vox et nostra esse possit. Enarrabo, inquit, omnia mirabilia tua.

Evangelizat Christus seipsum, evangelizat se etiam in membris suis iam existentibus, ut et alios adducat, et accessant qui non-eront, et copulentur membris eius, per quae membra eius praedicatum est Evangelium; et fiat unum corpus sub uno capite, in uno spiritu, in una vita. 5 [v.3]- Et quid ait? Cuín accepero, inquit, tempus ego iustitias iudicabo. When do you judicabit iustitias? Cum acceperit tempus. Nondum est ipsum tempus. Gratias misericordiae eius: prius praedicat iustitias, et sic iudicat iustitias. Nam si ante vellet iudicare quam praedicare, quis inveniretur liberandus? quis absolvendus occurreret? Modo ergo praedicationis tempus est: Narraba, inquit, omnia mirabilia tua. Audi narrantem, audi praedicantem; nam si contempseris, Cum accepero tempus, inquit, ego iustitias iudicabo. In another psalm it is written: I will sing to you, O Lord, mercy and judgment. Mercy and judgment: first mercy, then judgment; Through mercy sins are forgiven, through judgment they are punished. Don't you want to fear the avenger of sins? To me to the condoner; Do not reject him, do not get conceited, do not say: I have nothing to forgive me for, then listen to what follows: When I take the time, I will judge the justices. Did Christ take the time? Did the Son of God take the time? The Son of God did not take time, the Son of man took him. But, nevertheless, He Himself is the Son of God, by whom we were created, and the Son of man, by whom we were rescued. When He took the man, He was not taken. Having changed man for the better, He was by no means worse, for he did not cease to be what he was, but took on what he was not. What was it? Subsisting in the form of God, he did not consider it predatory to be equal to God; They are words of the Apostle. And what did he take? He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. When he took the form of a servant, he took time. Did it change? Did it decrease? Did he get exhausted? Did it deteriorate? No, by the way. Well then, what does it mean that he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant? It was said that He annihilated Himself by taking what was inferior to Him, not lowering Himself by making Himself equal to it. Then, brothers, what does it mean when the time takes, I will judge the righteousness? Who took time as the son of man and who governs time as the Son of God. Hear how he took the time to judge, since he is the son of man: it is said

in the Gospel that the Father gave him power to judge, because he is the son of man. Since he is the Son of God, he never received the power to judge, because he never lacked it. As the son of man, he took the time to be born, to suffer, to die, to be resurrected and to ascend to heaven as well as to come and judge. These things are said about Him, and also about His body, since He will not judge without His members, since in the Gospel it is written: And you will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel. Then the total Christ speaks, that is, the head and body of his saints (by saying): When the time takes, I will judge the righteousness. 6 [v. 4]. Now what's next? The earth slipped. If the earth slipped, what was it due to sins? Sins are called crimes because delinquere (to commit a crime) is like slipping quodam liquido (a certain liquid) from the stability, the firmness of virtue and justice. All sin by the desire for lower things. Just as man is strengthened by the love of superiors, so he fades or slides and liquefies by the desire of inferiors. The merciful giver, the condoner of sins and yet not yet the recipient of torture, paying attention to this flow of things, which is due to the sins of men, says: The earth and all the inhabitants of it slipped away. Certainly the earth slipped on all its inhabitants. This is, therefore, an explanation, not an addition. It is as if you were asking: How does the earth slide? Was its foundation taken away and something buried in it through a crack? There is no such thing, but he called all his mo -

Misericordiam et iudicium: misericordiam mode, postea iudicium; in qua mercy peccata donantur, in quo iudicio peccata puniuntur. Vis non timere peccatorum punitorem? Ama donatorem; noli respuere, noli te extollere, noli dicere, Non habeo quod mihi donet; audi enim quod sequitur: Cum accepero tempus, ego iustitias iudicabo. Accept tempus Christus? accepit tempus Filius Dei? Filius Dei non accepit tempus; sed Filius hominis accepit tempus. idem ipse autem et Filius Dei per quem facti sumus, et Filius hominis per quem refecti sumus. Homine assumpto, ipse non assumptus; nomine mutato in melius, nullo moda ipse in deterius commutatus, non destitit esse quod erat, sed accepit quod non erat. What was it? Cum in forma Dei esset, non rapiñara arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo: Apostoli verba sunt. Et quid accepit? Sed semetipsum exinanivit, formam serví accipiens (Phil 2,6.7). Sicut formam servi accepit, ita et tempus accepit. Demutatus est ergo? deminutus est? exilior redditus? in default lapses? absit. Quid ergo semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens? Exinanisse se dictus is accipindo inferiorem, non degenerando ab aequalí. Ergo, fratres, quid est loe, Cum accepero tempus, ego iustitias iudicabo? Accepit tempus ut Filius hominis; gubernat tempora ut Filius Dei. Audi quia ut Filius hominis accepit tempus iudicandi. Dicit in Gospel: Dedil ei

potestatem iudicii faciendi, quoniam Filius hominis est (lo 5,27). Secundum quod Filius Dei, nunquam accepit potestatem iudicandi; quia nunquam caruit potestate iudicandi: secundum quod Filius hominis, accepit tempus sicut nascendi et patiendi, sicut moriendi et resurgendi et ascendendi, ita veniendi et iudicandi. Dicit in illo ista et Corpus eius; non enim sine illis iudicabit: dicit quippe in Gospel, Sedebitis super iuoiecim sedes, indicantes kuoáecim tribes Israel (Mt 19,28). Ergo totus Christus dicit, id est caput et corpus in sanctis, Cum accepero tempus, ego iustitias iudicabo. 6 [v.4]. Auto mode what? Earth defluxit. Si defluxit terra, unde fluxit nisi peccatis? Ideo et delicta dicuntur. Delinquere est, tanquam de liquid quodam defluete a stabilitate firmamenti virtutis atque iustitiae. Cupiditate enim inferiorum quisque peccat: sicut roboratur chántate superiorum, sic deficit, et quasi liquescit cupiditate inferiorum. Hunc fluxum rerum in peccatis hominum attendens donator misericors, donator peccatorum, nondum exactor suppliciorum, attendit et ait: Defluxit terra, et omnes inhabitantes in en. Ipsa utique terra defluxit in habitantibus se. Expositio est consequens, non additio. Tanquam if you say: How to defluxit terra? subtracta sunt fundament, et aliquid in ea hiatu quodam demersum est? Quod dico terram, omnes inhabitantes in ea. Inveni, inquit, terram peccatricem; et quid feci? Ego confirmed eius columns.

rators. I found, he says, a sinful land. And what did I do? I consolidated its columns. What columns did he strengthen? He calls the apostles columns, because that is how the apostle Saint Paul calls his co-apostles, who were considered columns. And how would they have been pillars if they had not been established by Him? In a certain earthquake these same columns also staggered, because in the passion of the Lord all the apostles distrusted. But those columns that faltered in the passion of the Lord were consolidated with the resurrection. The foundation of the building, Christ, cried out through its columns, and in all these columns (or apostles) the architect cried out. One of these columns was the apostle Saint Paul when he said: Do you want to have proof of him who speaks in me? The one who speaks in me is Christ. Then I—he says—established the pillars of the earth; I resurrected; I demonstrated that death should not be feared and I showed those who fear that not even the body itself perishes in those who die. The wounds frightened them, the scars strengthened them. Our Lord Jesus Christ could have been resurrected without scars. What extraordinary power does he need who restored the union of his body to such great integrity to appear without any trace of past wounds? He had the power to restore him from there without scars, but he wanted to have them to consolidate the tottering columns with them. 7 [v.5]. We have already heard, brothers, that he is not always silent. Let's hear what he said through these columns. Then about the chalice of pure wine filled with mixture in the hand of the Lord, as soon as God gives me to understand, I will tell your charity what seems to me, without closing your ears to other expositors who may tell you something better, because another more exact meaning can be found, since the darkness of the Scripture is such that it is difficult for it to have only one meaning, and, therefore, we should not envy the most intelligent nor despair like little ones. However, any meaning that emerges must conform to the rule of faith. Therefore, the chalice of pure wine filled with mixture seems to me to be the law that was given to the Jews and all the Scripture that is called the Old Testament, in which the set of all the sentences is found, because there the New Testament is hidden as among the dregs of the corporal sacraments. The circumcision of the flesh is a reality and figure of a great sacrament in which the circumcision of the heart is understood; The temple of Jerusalem is a reality and figure of another great sacrament: the body of Christ; The promised land represents the kingdom of heaven; The sacrifice of animal victims contains a great sacrament, since in all those sacrifices that unique sacrifice and that unique victim of the cross, Christ, was symbolized, since, instead of all the ancient sacrifices, we have only one, since those prefigured this one, that is, this one was symbolized by

those. Those people received the law; He received just and good commandments. For what is more just than that you will not kill, you will not fornicate, you will not steal, you will not bear false witness; honor your father and mother; You will not covet other people's goods, you will not desire your neighbor's wife; Will you worship one God and serve Him alone? All these things belong to wine. All those other carnal things settled in the Jews, so that, remaining with them, all spiritual knowledge would emanate from there. Being the cup in the Lord's hand means being in his power; To be full of pure wine is to be full of the sincere law, and to be mixed is to have the dregs of these carnal sacraments. All that people, taking into account the number of the twelve sons of Jacob, were made up of as many tribes. The various parts or groupings of peoples are called tribes. But since no land was given to the priests who served the temple and it was appropriate that the entire land of promise be divided into twelve tribes, by excepting from the distribution of the land a tribe of great dignity, that of Levi, which was the priestly one, there would be eleven left if the twelve had not been completed with the adoption of two sons of Joseph. Notice how this happened. Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob and

He was the one whom his brothers sold to be taken to Egypt. There, in reward for his chastity, he was elevated to excellent dignity, with God assisting him in all his actions. In Egypt he received his brothers, by whom he was sold; and also to their father, because suffering from hunger they went down to Egypt in search of food. Joseph had two sons: Ephraim and Manasseh. When Jacob died, in bequeathing his will, he counted these two grandsons in the number of his children, saying to his son Joseph: The other children that are born to you will be yours; These are mine, and they will divide the land with their brothers. The land of promise had not yet been given or divided, but Jacob spoke in spirit, prophesying. Adding the two sons of Joseph, they were completed, surpassing the twelve tribes, since there are now thirteen. Instead of one from Joseph, two were added, and thus thirteen were constituted. But except for the tribe of Levi, a tribe of priests, who served the temple and lived off the tithes of all the other tribes among whom the land was divided, twelve remained. Among these twelve tribes was that of Judah, from which the kings came. However, the first king, Saul, was from another tribe (Benjamin), but he was disapproved for being a bad king. Then David, of the tribe of Judah, was made king; and their descendants, coming from the same tribe, were already kings.
