Esurire in pauperibus voluit, who dives in cáelo est; et tu dubitas homo daré homini, cum scias te Christo daré quod das, a quo accepisti quidquid das! Sed illi dormiemnt somnum suum, et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis. 10 [v.7]. Ab increpatione tua, Deus Jacob, dormitaverunt omnes qui ascenderunt equos. Who sunt, who ascendunt equos? Qui humiles esse noluerunt. Non in equis sedere peccatum est; sed cervicem potestatis contra Deum erigere, et putare se in aliquo honore esse. Quia dives es, ascendisti; inctepat Deus, et dormís. Magna ira increpantis, magna ira! attendat Charitas Vestra rem tremendousm. rebuked strepi-
Triumphant song after victory

scary thing. The threat carries with it a roar; The noise or the roar usually wakes up men. So heavy is the voice of the rebuking God, who says: At your threat, O God of Jacob, all those who rode on horses fell asleep. See with what sleep Pharaoh fell asleep, who mounted his horses; Well, it did not awaken in his heart, because, due to the threat, it had hardened him. Hardness of heart is numbing. I beg you, brothers, to notice how those sleep who, with the Gospel resounding throughout the world in the amens and hallelujahs, still do not want to detest their old life and wake up to the new. Judea kept the Scripture; It is now known throughout the entire world. In that one nation it was previously said that the only God who made heaven and earth must be honored and adored; now be silent. Jesus Christ was resurrected, he was insulted on the cross, but his same cross, on which he was mocked, is already engraved on the foreheads of kings. And they still sleep! Brothers, great is the wrath of God. In a better way we have heard Him who says: Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you. But who hears them? Those who did not ride horses. Who are those who didn't ride horses? Those who do not boast or pride themselves in their dignity and power. At your threat, O God of Jacob, those who rode on horses fell asleep. 11 [v. 8]. You are terrible; and who will resist you because of your anger? Now they sleep without feeling the angry one, because he became angry so that they would sleep. Those who do not feel him asleep now will finally feel him awake, because he will appear as judge of the living and tum habet; strepitus expergisci solet faceré homines. Tantum pondus est increpantis Dei, ut diceret: Ab increpatione tua Deus lacob, dormitaverunt omnes qui ascenderunt equos. Ecce quo somno dormitavit ille Pharao qui ascendebat equos (Ex 14,8): non enim vigilavit in corde, quia de increpatione durum cor habebat. Duritia enim cordis, obdormitio est. I pray you, fratres mei, videte quomodo dormiunt, qui sonante Gospel, et Amen, et Alleluia per totum otbem terrarum, adhuc vitam veterem nolunt damnare, et in novam evigilare.

Erat Scriptura Dei in Iudaea; moda per totum orbem cantatur: in illa una gente dicebatur Deus unus qui fecit omnia, esse adorandus et colendus; ubi tacetur mode: Christus resurrected? irrisus in cruz, ipsam cruze suam in qua irrisus gst iam fixit in frontibus regum; et adhuc dormitur! Magna ira Dei, brothers! Melius nos audimus eum qui dicit: Surge qui dormís, et exsurge a mortuis; et illuminabit te Christus (Eph 5,14). Sed qui illum audiunt? Qui non ascendant equos. Who sunt who non ascendant equos? Qui non se actant et extollunt, quasi in honoribus et potestatibus suis. Ab increpatione tua, Deus lacob, dormitaverunt qui ascenderunt equos. 11 [v.8]. Your terribilis is; et quis resistet tibi tune ab ira tua? Modo dormiunt, et iratum non sentiunt; sed ut dorment iratus est. Mode quod sleepers non sentiunt, in fine sentient: apparebit enim
Ennarrations on the Psalms

dead: And then who will resist you because of your anger? Now they speak whatever they want, argue against God and say: Who are Christians? Who is Christ? How simple are those who believe what they do not see and abandon the delights they see, pursuing the faith of the things that are hidden from their eyes! You are asleep and you bleat. Speak against God as much as you can. How long, Lord, will they continue to be sinners, how long will sinners continue to boast, how long will they utter iniquity? When will everyone shut up? When they enter within themselves, when they repress the teeth with which they now bite us, with which now, as Christians, they tear us apart, insulting us and reviling the lives of the saints. They will reconsider within themselves when what is said in the book of Wisdom happens to them: that, sorrowful and anguished at seeing the glory of the many, entering within themselves, they will say: These are those whom we once mocked. Oh you who slept with deep sleep! Now you are certainly awake and you find nothing in your hands. Now you see how those whom you despised as poor people have their hands full of the glory of God. Tell yourselves when you no longer oppose the wrath of God with action, with detraction, with word and with thought, since He was clearly presented to you whom you judged worthy of ridicule when it was announced to you that He would come. And what will you say? We erred from the path of truth and the light of justice did not illuminate us nor did the sun rise for us. How could the sun of justice rise for the sleeping, since they fell asleep before the wrath and threat of God? Perhaps they will say this to themselves: I hope iudex vivorum et mortuorum; et quis resistet tibi tune ab ira tua? Modo enim loquuntur quod volunt, et disputant contra Deum, et dicunt: Qui sunt Christiani? Who is Christus? aut quales inepti qui credunt quod non vident, et dimittunt delicias quas vident, et sequuntur fidem rerum quae oculis ipsorum non exhibitionntur? Dormitis, et balatis; loquimini adversus Deum quantum potestis. Usquequo peccatores, Domine, usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur? responder, et loquentur iniquitartem? (Ps 93.3). Quando autem nemo responder, et nemo loquitur, nisi quando se in se convertat? When in se convertent dentes quibus moda nos rodunt, quibus nos discerpunt itridendo Christianos, et reprehendendo yitam sanctorum?

Tune se in se convertent, cum illis eveniet quod dicitur in libro Sapientiae, Dicent inter se, poenitentiam agents, et per anguishm spiritus gementes: cum viderint gloriam sanctorum, tune dicent, Hi sunt quos aliquando habuimus in risum. O qui multum dormistis! certe iam evigilatis, et in vestris manibus nihil invenitis. Videtis quomodo plenas habeant manus gloria Dei, quos tanquam pauperes irrisistis. Dicite ergo tune vobis, quando non resistitis irae Dei; non manu, nec lingua, nec verb, nec cogitatione: apparebit enim vobis manifestus, quem irridendum putastis, cum vobis venturus nuntiaretur. Et quid dicent? Ergo erravimus a via veritatis, et iustitiae lumen non
Triumphant song after victory

We would not have gotten on the horse!, and then they themselves will accuse their horses (their arrogance). You hear them calling their horses on which they fell asleep: We departed, the Scripture says they will say, from the path of truth and the light of justice did not illuminate us nor did the sun rise for us. What good did pride do for us? And what good did the boasting of riches bring us? All these things vanished like a shadow. Then you were awake for some time. But it would have been better if you had not mounted the horse so that you would not have slept when you should have been awake, and thus you would have heard the voice of Christ and Christ himself would have enlightened you. You are terrible; and who will resist you then because of your anger? What will happen then? 12 [v.9]. You sent judgment from heaven, and the earth trembled and was still. She who is now disturbed, she who now speaks, will tremble and be still at last. It would be better for him to calm down now to finally enjoy himself. 13 [v.10]. The earth shook and became still. When? As God rises up in judgment to save all the meek in heart. Who are the meek at heart? Those who, stamping their horses, did not mount them, but in humility confessed their sins. To save all the meek at heart. 14 [v. l l ]. Because the thought of man will confess or praise you and the residue of thought will celebrate you solemnities. There is a first thought and subsequent residues of thought. What is the first thought? He by whom luxit nobis, et sol non ortus est nobis. Quomodo iustitiae sol oriretur dormientibus? Sed ab ira et increpatione eius dormiunt. Hoc forte dicturus est, Et non ascenderem equum: et tune ipsi equos suos aecusabunt. Listen to the accusantes equos suos in quibus dormierunt: Ergo erravimus, inquit Scriptura, a via veritatis, et iustitiae lumen non luxit nobis, et sol non ortus est nobis. Quid nobis profuit superbia? et divitiarum iactantia quid contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia tanquam umbra (Sap 5,3.6.8.9). Ergo vigilasti aliquando. Sed melius equum non ascenderes, ut tune non dormitares, quando vigilare debuisti; et audires vocem Christi, et illuminaret te Christus. Your terribilis is; et quis resistet tibi tune ab ira tua? Quid enim erit tune? 12 [v.9]- De cáelo iaculatus is iudicium: terra tremuit, et quievit. Quae moda se turbat, quae moda loquitur, timere habet in fine et quiescere. Melius mode quiesceret, ut in fine gauderet. 13 [v.10]. Terra tremuit, et quievit. When?

Cum exurgeret in iudicium Deus, ut safes faceret omnes mites corde. Who sunt mites corde? Qui frementes equos non ascenderunt, sed in humilitate sua peccata confessi sunt. Ut safe faceret omnes mites corde. 14 [v.ll]. Quoniam cogitatio bominis confitebitur tibi, et relice cogitationis solemnia celebrabunt tibi. Prima, cogitatio; posterior, relice cogitationis. Quae est cogitatio prima? Unde incipimus: bona illa cogitatio, unde incipies confiteri. Confessio adiungit nos Christo. Iam
Ennarrations on the Psalms

we begin; that good thought for which we begin to confess or praise. Confession unites us to Christ. For the same confession, that is, the first thought, works in us the remaining thoughts, and these same subsequent thoughts will celebrate solemnities for you. The first thought of man will confess you, and the rest will celebrate you solemnities. What is the thought that you will confess? He who condemns the past life, who dislikes what was, in order to be in this way what he was not; This is the first thought. But since you must separate yourself from sins by confessing to God with the first thought, so that you do not forget that you were a sinner, for the same reason that you were a sinner you celebrate solemnities to God. You should still know that the first thought carries with it the confession and turning away from the past life; But, if you have forgotten the sins from which you were freed, you do not give thanks to the Deliverer and you do not celebrate solemnities to your God. Here is the first penitent thought of the apostle Saul already made Paul. Hearing the voice from heaven when he persecuted Christ and became enraged against the Christians and intended to capture them wherever he found them to kill them; Upon hearing, I repeat, the voice of heaven, which said to him: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?, surrounded by light and blind, as for the body, so that he could see inside, he formulated the first thought of obedience, because when he heard: I am Jesus of the Nazarene, the One whom you persecute, he exclaimed: Lord, what do you want me to do? This is a penitent thought, since he already calls the one he persecuted Lord. How will the solemnities celebrate the residue of thought? You heard it in Saint Paul when the Apostle himself was read: Remember that Christ, from the livero confessio ipsa, id est prima cogitatio, facit in nobis relics cogitationis; et ipsae relics cogitationis solemnia celebrabunt tibi. Cogitatio hominis confitebitur tibi, et relice cogitationis solemnia celebrabunt tibi. Quae est cogitatio quae confitebitur? Quae damnat vitam priorem, cui displicet quod erat, ut sit quod non erat, ipsa est prima cogitatio. Sed quia sic tú recedere a peccatis, prima cogitatione confessus Deo, ut non tibi recedat de memoria quia peccator Fuisti, per hoc quod peccator Fuisti, solemnia celebras Deo. Adhuc intelligendum est.

Prima cogitatio confessionem habet, et recessionem a vetere vita: sed si oblitus fueris a quibus peccatis liberatus sis, non agis gratias liberatori, et non celebras solemnia Deo tuo. Ecce prima cogitatio confitens Sauli apostoli, iam Pauli, qui primo Saulus fuet; quando audivit vocem de cáelo, cum persequeretur Christum, et fureret in Christianos, et vellet ut ubicumque inventions adduceret necandos, audivit vocem de cáelo, Saule, Saule, quid persequeris me? et circumfulsus lumine, facta sibi caecitate in oculis, ut intus videret, emisit primam cogitationem obedientiae; cum audiret, Ego sum lesus Nazarenas, quem tu persequeris, Domine, ait, quid me Mes faceré? (Acts 9,45). Haec est cogitatio confitens; iam Dominum appellat quem persequebatur. Quomodo relicie cogitationis solemnia celebrabunt, in Paulo audistis, cum ipse Apostolus
Triumphant song after victory

name of David, rose from the dead, according to my Gospel. What does remember mean? Do not forget the thought for which you first confessed and the remaining thoughts also remain in your memory. See how the same Apostle repeats in another place what was given to him: First, he says, I was a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and an evildoer. He who says I was first a blasphemer, is he still a blasphemer? In order not to be blasphemous, the first penitent thought took place, but to commemorate what was given to him, the remaining thoughts for which he celebrated the solemnities remained. 15. Indeed, my brothers, see here that Christ renewed us, forgave us all our sins and we are transformed. If we forget what has been given to us and by whom, we forget the gift of the Savior. So that we do not forget the gift of the Savior, does not Christ sacrifice himself daily for us? Christ sacrificed himself for us once when we believed; then the first penitent thought took place, but now the remaining thoughts when we remember who is to come to us and what he is to give us. Through these same second thoughts, that is, through this memory, Christ immolates himself in us in such a way as if he who renewed us by his first grace renewed us daily. The Lord already renewed us in baptism, and we were made new men, rejoicing in hope to be endured in tribulation. However, we must not forget what was granted to us. And if now your first thought no longer exists, which existed before (for your prilegeretur: Memor esto Christum lesum resurrexisse a mortuis ex semine David, secundum Evangelium meum (2 Tim 2,8). est, Idem Paulus apostolus alio loco: Qui prius, inquit, fue blasphemus, et persecutor, et iniuriosus (1 Tim 1,13). cogitationis erant, per ipsas relics cogitationis solemnia celebrabat. 15. Etenim, fratres mei, ecce innovavit nos Christus; nonne quotidie nobis Christus immolatur?

Et semel nobis Christus immolatus est, cum credidimus; tune Fuit cogitatio: moda autem relice cogitationis sunt, cum meminimus quis ad nos venerit, et quid nobis donaverit; ex ipsis reliquiis cogitationis, id est ex ipsa memoria, quotidie nobis sic immolatur, quasi quotidie nos innovet qui prima gratia sua nos innovavit. Iam enim innovavit nos Dominus in Baptism, et facti sumus novi nomines; in spe quidem gaudentes, ut in tribulatione simus patientes (Rom 12,12): tamen non debent de memoria nostra recedere quid nobis praestitum sit. Et yes way
Ennarrations on the Psalms

first thought consisted of turning away from sin, and now you are not turning away, but then you turned away), the subsequent thoughts exist so that the one who healed is not forgotten. If you forget that you were hurt, subsequent thoughts will not exist in you. What do you think David said? See that he speaks in person about everyone. Saint David sinned gravely. The prophet Nathan was sent to him and rebuked him. Then he confessed and said: I sinned. This was the first thought of the man who confesses. The thought of man will confess you. What were the remaining thoughts? He declares them when he says: And my sin is always before me. What was the first thought? The one who had to turn away from sin. If he has already turned away from sin, how is it that his sin is always before him if it is not because that thought passed away, but the remaining thoughts celebrate the solemnities? Then let us remember, dear brothers; I beg you. Whoever has been freed from sin remembers what it was; let the remaining thoughts remain in it. You will lead another to be healed if you remember that you were also healed. Let each one remember what he was and see if he is no longer, and then he will help him who still is what he is no longer. But, if he boasts of his own merits and rejects sinners as unworthy and becomes cruel without compassion, he mounted the horse, be careful not to fall asleep, because those who mounted horses fell asleep. Has he already left the horse, has he humiliated himself? Don't get back on the horse again, that is, don't get arrogant again. This will happen to him if the remaining thoughts celebrate solemnities to God. non est cogitatio tua quae Fuit (etenim prima cogitatio fuít recedere a peccato; moda autem non recedis, sed tune recessisti): sint relice cogitationis, ne excidat a memoria quia sanavit. Vulnus te habuisse si oblitus fueris, non tibí erunt relice cogitationis. Quid enim putatis dixisse David? Ecce ex omnium persona loquitur. Peccavit David sanctus graviter; missus est ad illud Nathan propheta, et corripuit illum: et confessus est, et dixit, Peccavi (2 Reg 12,13). Haec fuet prima cogitatio confitentis: Cogitatio hominis confitebitur tibi. What were the relics of cogitationis? Quando ait: Et peccatum meum ante me est semper (Ps 50,5). Quae Fuit ergo prima cogitatio? Ut recederet a peccato.

Et si iam recessit a peccato, quomodo peccatum illius ante illum est semper, nisi quia cogitatio illa transitiit, sed relice cogitationis solemnia celebrant? Meminerimus ergo, fratres charissimi, rogamus vos: quisquís liberaras est a peccato, meminerit quid Fuit; sint in illo relicie cogitationis. Tune enim portat alium sanandurn, si se meminerit esse sanatum. Ergo unusquisque recordetur quid Fuit, et utrum iam non sit; et tune subveniet ei qui adhuc est quod ille iam non est. Si autem iactat se quasi de meritis suis, et repellit tanquam indignos peccatores, et sine mercy saevit; equum ascendit, videat ne dormiat: dormitaverunt enim quid ascenderunt equos. Iam tune resign equum; humiliavit se: non iterum ascendat equum, id est, non se rursus erigat in superbiam. Unde illi hoc fit? Si relice cogitationis solemnia celebrent Deo.
Triumphant song after victory

16 [v.12]. Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord, our God. Each one makes the vows they can and fulfills them. So that it does not happen that you promise and do not fulfill it, each one promises what he can and fulfills it. Do not be lazy in making vows, because you do not have to fulfill them with your strength. You will faint if you boast about yourself. If you trust in Him to whom you promise, promise, for you will surely keep it. Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord, our God. What vows should we all make commonly? Believe in god; expect eternal life from Him; live well according to the ordinary Christian norm. There is a certain common standard for everyone; for example, do not steal; However, continence is not commanded, nor is marriage, but everyone is equally commanded not to commit adultery, everyone is ordered not to get drunk, so the soul is drowned and the temple of God is destroyed. It is also commanded to all equally not to be arrogant, not to kill, not to hate one's brother, not to plot someone's downfall. This we must all promise. There are other promises particular to each individual; For example: a man promises conjugal chastity to God so as not to know another woman outside of his own; Likewise, a woman also promises not to meet another man other than her own. Others, having already tried the union, promise to renounce it from now on; These promise something more than the first. Others promise virginity from their earliest age in order to abstain from everything that those who tried it abandon; These promise a lot. Others promise to make a guesthouse of their house for all the saints who come to it; They promise a lot. Others promise to leave all their possessions 16 [v.12]. Vovete, et reddite Domino Deo nostro. Quisque quod potest voveat, et reddat. Ne voveatis, et non reddatis; sed quisque quod potest voveat, et reddat. Non sitis pigri ad vovendum; non enim viribus vestris implebitis. Deficietis, si de vobis praesumitis; si autem de illo cui vovetis, vovete, secuti reddetis. Vovete, et reddite Domino Deo nostro. Omnes communiter quid debenmus vovere? Credere in illum, sperare ab ¡lio vitam aeternam, bene vivere secundum communem modum. Est enim quidam modus communis omnibus.

Furtum non faceré, non castimoniali praecipitur, et nuptae non praecipitur: adulterium non faceré, omnibus praecipitur: non amare vinolentiam, qua ingurgitatur anima, et corrumpit in se templum Dei, omnibus aequaliter praecipitur; non superbire, omnibus aequaliter praecipitur: non hominem occidere, non odisse fratrem, non adversus aliquem tenere perniciem, omnibus in commune praecipitur. Hoc totum omnes vovere debenmus. Sunt etiam vote propria sinngulorum: alius vovet Deo castitatem coniugalem, ut praeter uxorem suam non noverit aliam; sic et femina, ut praeter virum suum non noyerit alium. Alli etiam vovent, ctsi expetti tale coniugium, ultra nihil tale pati, nihil tale concupiscere aut sustinere: et ipsi voverunt aliquid maius quam illi. Alli virginitatem ipsain ab ineunte aetate vovent, ut nihil tale vel experiantur, quale illi experti reliquerunt: et isti voverunt purimum. Alii vovent domum suam esse hospitalem ómnibus sanctis advenientibus:
Ennarrations on the Psalms
Triumphant song after victory

and, distributing them among the poor, live a common life in the company of the saints; They promise a lot. Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord, your God. Everyone promises what they want, but pay attention to what they promise. Anyone who promises God, if he then looks back, does wrong. For example: a nun wants to get married; what do you want? What a maiden. What do you want? What his mother wanted. Did he want something bad? Bad at all. Because? Because he had made a vow to the Lord his God. And what does the apostle Saint Paul say about these? Even though he tells young widows, in the First Epistle to Timothy, to marry if they wish, in another place he writes: Nevertheless, they will be happier, in my opinion, if they remain that way. In this he shows that they will be happier if they remain widowed, but he does not condemn them if they want to get married. But what about some young widows who promised and then failed to deliver? These have a sentence of condemnation, because they broke the first heh. What does it mean they broke or annulled the first heh? They promised and did not deliver. No brother who has retired to the monastery says: I am leaving it, because those who are in the monastery are not the only ones who will obtain the kingdom of heaven and those who are not in it will not belong to God. To him the answer is: What you say is true, but they did not promise; you promised, you looked back. As the Lord threatens the day of judgment, what does he say? Remember Lot's wife. He said it to everyone. What did Lot's wife do? She was delivered from Sodom and, being on the road, she looked back, and wherever she looked, she remained. It was with-

poured into a pillar of salt so that men can be seasoned by contemplating it. Have courage; do not be rude; Do not look back, lest, by setting a bad example, you become a pillar of salt and harm others. Also now we say this to certain brothers of ours whom we have observed how to falter in their good purpose. Do you want to be just like that? We put before their eyes some who looked back. They are bitter in themselves, but they season others when they are remembered, so that, having their punishment, they do not look back. Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord, our God, because that woman of Lot concerns us all. Does a married woman want to marry? He looked back from the state he was in. Does the widow who had promised to stay that way want to get married? She wanted what is allowed to someone who marries, but it is no longer allowed to her, because from her state she looked back. The virgin is already a nun, she has consecrated herself to God, she has all the other virtues that adorn virginity itself, and without which virginity is disformed; But what will happen if it is immaculate in body and depraved in mind? What did I say? What will happen if no one rapes her, but perhaps she is drunk, arrogant, quarrelsome, talkative? (You must know) that God condemns all of this. If he had married before promising, he would not be condemnable. But he chose something better, he left aside what he was allowed, and now he becomes arrogant and commits many illegal actions! I say that it is allowed to marry before promising; becoming arrogant is never allowed. Oh virgin of God, you did not want to get married, which was permitted, and you became conceited, which is prohibited. Better is a humble virgin than a humble married woman.

magnum votum vovent. AIÍus vovet reünquere omnia sua distribuenda pauperibus, et iré in communem vitam, in societatem sanctorum: magnum votum vovet. Vovete, et reddite Domino Deo nostro. Quisque quod vovere voluerit voveat: illud attendat, ut quod voverit reddat. Ünusquisque Deo quod vovet, si respicit retrorsum, malum est. Nescio quae castimonialis cloude voluit: quid voluit? Quod et virgo quaelibet. Quid voluit? Quod et matei ipsius. Aliquid mali voluit? Mali planned. Quare? Quia iam voverat Domino Deo suo. Quid enim dixit de talibus apostolus Paulus? Cum dicat viduas adolescentulas cloudre si velint (1 Tira 5,14), sed tamen ait quodam loco: Beatior autem erit, si sic permanserit secundum meurn consilium (1 Cor 7,40). Ostendit beatiorem, si sic permanserit; non tamen damnandam, si cloude voluerit. Quid autem ait de quibusdam quae voverunt, et non reddiderunt? Habentes, inquit, damnationem, quia primam fidem irritam fecerunt (1 Tim 5:12). Quid est, primam fidem irritam fecerunt? Voverunt, et non reddiderunt. Nemo ergo positus in monastery frater dicat: Recedo de monastery, ñeque enim soli qui sunt in monastery perventuri sunt ad regnum caelorum, et illi qui ibi non sunt ad Deum non pertinent. Respondetur ei: Sed illi non voverunt; your vovisti, your retro respexisti. De die iudicii cum Dominus minaretur, quid ait? Rementote uxoris Lot (Luke 17:32). Bus dixit. Quid enim fecit uxor Lot? Liberata est a Sodomis, et in via posita retrorsum respexit: ubi respexit, ibi remansit. Facta est autem statua salis

(Gen 19:26), ut illius contemplatione condiantur homines; cor habeant, non sint fatui, non retro respiciant, ne malum exemplum dantes, ipsi remaneant, et alios condiant.
